title: Jim Harbaugh hopes to rebound from first 0-2 start as a head coach
summary: It was a bad weekend for the Brothers Harbaugh at SoFi Stadium.
full_text: ''' It was a bad weekend for the Brothers Harbaugh at SoFi Stadium. On Monday night, John lost his game and his quarterback. One day earlier, Jim's Chargers joined the 1926 Racine Tornadoes in losing back-to-back home games who won fewer than 20 percent of their games in the prior season. The Chargers emerged from what were, on paper, two winnable games with an 0-2 record. For Jim Harbaugh, it's the first time he has ever started 0-2 as a head coach, at the college or pro level. Although the 2026 start is depressing, it's impressive that he went 22 seasons without losing two straight games to open a campaign. The run includes three years at the University of San Diego, four at Stanford, four with the 49ers, nine at Michigan, and his first two with the Chargers. That won't make him feel much better about the current predicament, especially with a four-game gauntlet before the Chargers' Week 7 bye (at Bills, at Seahawks, Broncos, at Chiefs). Jim needs to dig deep into the bag of Jack Harbaugh motivational quotes to turn this one around. The fact that Sunday's game is regarded as a trap game for the Bills shows how quickly the L.A. program has crumbled. The Chargers have now lost five in a row dating back to 2025, and they haven't scored 17 or more points in any of them. If something doesn't change, changes could be coming after the dust settles on the next four weekends and the Chargers get extra time to figure things out before facing the Rams, Texans, and Ravens.
author: Mike Florio

title: UNC chancellor on Bill Belichick: "Support comes with expectations"
summary: Internal turmoil at the North Carolina football program brought down G.M.
full_text: Internal turmoil at the North Carolina football program brought down G.M. Michael Lombardi and defensive coordinator Steve Belichick. Head coach Bill Belichick remains. Earlier this week UNC chancellor Lee Roberts addressed the investigation that prompted the resignation of Bill Belichick's consigliere and his son. "Coach Belichick continues to have our support, the support of the administration and of the board [of trustees]," Roberts said Thursday, via Brad Crawford of CBS Sports. "He understands that that support comes with expectations around conduct and behavior . Nobody understands that better than coach Belichick." As to Lombardi and Steve Belichick, the conduct and behavior apparently fell short of the standard. Given their proximity to the head coach, that's problematic. "We're continuing to put in place policies and training and monitoring to make sure that the standards we expect of the football program are being adhered to," Roberts said. The message is clear. The powers-that-be have their eyes on Bill Belichick. And if they can pin something/anything to him, they can escape the Belichick experiment without owing him a buyout. North Carolina is off this weekend. The 2-1 Tar Heels host Notre Dame next weekend.
author: Mike Florio

title: Deion Sanders on Travis Hunter's usage: "I have no idea what's going on"
summary: Back in May, Colorado coach Deion Sanders expressed disappointment that he hadn't heard from the Jaguars regarding how to coach, and how to deploy, cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter.
full_text: Back in May, Colorado coach Deion Sanders expressed disappointment that he hadn’t heard from the Jaguars regarding how to coach, and how to deploy, cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter. Two games into Hunter's second NFL season, Coach Prime remains perplexed about Hunter's workload. "I don't ask questions because I'm not there," Sanders said recently on his CBS Colorado show. "I don't know what transpires when we're not looking. I have no idea what’s going on . I know who he was and who he is right now. I know what he's capable of. I do know that." In Week 1, Hunter got four snaps on offense and 29 on defense. He had one catch for eight yards. In Week 2, Hunter had six snaps on offense and 37 on defense. He wasn't targeted in the Jacksonville passing game. The lack of usage for a player who entered the league with the promise of being the first true full-time two-way player since Chuck Bednarik has sparked plenty of questions. Earlier this week, coach Liam Coen said the team will be looking at giving him more reps this week, on both sides of the ball. Asked on Friday whether Hunter has spoken to coaches about the rotation at cornerback this week, Hunter opted for discretion. "I'm gonna leave that up to the coaches to answer," Hunter said. " That ain’t for me to answer ." In an appearance on The Pivot podcast before the start of the regular season, Hunter reiterated his belief that he can reach his full potential as a cornerback and as a receiver. Ryan Clark told Hunter that he could be a Hall of Fame cornerback or a Pro Bowl-caliber receiver . But Clark's implicit message was clear — it's impossible to be both. How can Hunter accomplish it? "Work ethic," Hunter said. "We all get the same 24 hours." Channing Crowder pressed Hunter on his effort to use that 24 hours to do both at the highest possible level. "The numbers don't work out," Crowder said. "If I'm trying to be the best — how are you gonna be the best, if you ain't trying to be the best? If you ain't trying to compete and do the best to be the best? So my main focus is be the best. So I'm gonna do everything I can do to be the best. I don't want to be the best at one position. There's a lot of people that's the best at one position. Ain't nobody yet been the best at both, full-time." For now, Hunter has played on a part-time basis on defense, with cameo appearances on offense. What's his preference? "I like doing both," Hunter said. "And I cannot sit on the sideline. I don't think nobody's noticed that yet. I hate the sidelines. I do not wanna sit there. I can't sit there and just watch football. I've got to be on the field." Clark pointed out that 52 other guys spend time on the sidelines. "That's their problem," Hunter said. He was smiling when he said it, but there's no escaping his point. Hunter still wants to play on a full-time basis on both sides of the ball. But he's playing so little on each side of the ball that the snaps don't add up to the amount of time he'd be getting if he played all snaps on offense or all snaps on defense. It's still not clear what the Jaguars are doing with the player whom they moved up from No. 5 to No. 2 in the draft to get, with the justification that they'd be getting two players in one. At some point, the idea of a two-way player has yielded to the reality that, as Crowder said, the numbers don't work out. It's too hard to be fully and completely prepared to perform at a high level on both offense and defense. And it's almost as if the Jaguars want Hunter to come to the conclusion on his own that he'll accept playing one side of the ball or the other in order to get a full-time workload at one speciic position. Still, if the Jaguars weren't prepared to let Hunter do what he clearly wants to do (and he surely made his point clear to them before the draft), why did they give up so much to make him the second overall pick in the draft? That's the most confounding aspect of this. Everyone knew Hunter wanted to play both ways. The decision to trade up to get Hunter sent a message that the Jaguars were on board with that approach. The numbers, to date, paint a far different picture.
author: Mike Florio

title: Titans-Giants tickets are available for as little as $17
summary: Two months ago, the price point for a ticket for a specific event at MetLife Stadium landed as high as $39,704.
full_text: '' Two months ago, the price point for a ticket for a specific event at MetLife Stadium landed as high as $39,704 . On Sunday, it will be considerably cheaper to get in to the building. At TickPick, the get-in price for Titans-Giants is as low as $17. At Ticketmaster, the league's official reselling partner (by the way, it's amazing how many previously seedy and illegal businesses became respectable and legitimate once corporate America figured out how to profit from them), there are plenty of tickets at $20 or $21. There are good reasons for the football game to be viewed as far less desirable to attend than the World Cup Final. First, the Giants have lost their starting quarterback for the season. (Yes, Jaxson Dart supposedly could return for the postseason. But if they manage to get that far without him, why bring him back when he hasn't played in months?) Second, the Titans aren't exactly a road draw. Third, and perhaps most importantly, it's a bad weather weekend in New Jersey, thanks to a nor'easter that will bring plenty of rain and wind to the region. But if you're willing to brave the elements and you're willing to answer Cam Skattebo’s call and you've got a portrait of Andrew Jackson burning a hole in your pocket, you can go to the game.
author: Mike Florio

title: Seven teams face an 0-3 hole — and only seven 0-3 teams have ever made the playoffs
summary: Eight teams entered Week 3 at 0-2.
full_text: Eight teams entered Week 3 at 0-2. One of them — the Falcons — avoided an 0-3 start. For the others, it becomes imperative to avoid starting the year with three straight losses. In NFL history, only seven teams have made the playoffs after starting 0-3. The group includes the 2025 Texans, the 2018 Texans, the 1998 Bills, the 1995 Lions, the 1992 Chargers, the 1982 Buccaneers, and the 1981 Jets. Only the '92 Chargers made it to the postseason after starting 0-4. It's easier now than it once was, thanks to 17 regular-season games and seven playoff spots per conference. It's still not easy. For starters, plenty of teams that start 0-3 do so for a very good reason — they're not very good. Those that are have a reduced margin for error over the final 14 games. This year, one game features two 0-2 teams: the Texans at the Colts. The other winless teams are the Dolphins, the Titans, the Chargers, the Commanders, and the Buccaneers.
author: Mike Florio

title: Brian Daboll downplays revenge as motivation for Titans-Giants game
summary: Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll will be coaching against the team that fired him when he faces the Giants on Sunday.
full_text: '' Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll will be coaching against the team that fired him when he faces the Giants on Sunday. He says that's not particularly important. Daboll, who was hired as Giants head coach in 2022 and fired last year, said he can set aside any emotions associated with facing his former team and just focus on doing his job. "I've faced a lot of former teams before," Daboll said. "It's a one-week season every week, so you've got to put everything you got into it. You've got to get ready for scheme, new coordinators on their end, different players. As simple as it sounds, that's what it is every week in the National Football League. I have a ton of respect for the people in that organization. Very grateful for the opportunity the Mara family and Tisch family gave me. From top down to the bottom, really good people in that building. But it's about getting the players ready for a game. I've been on a number of teams that played my former teams before. But the focus is on our players." Daboll also downplayed any idea that he has an advantage because he knows the players on the Giants, noting that they're a different team this year than they were last year. Daboll is treating Sunday like he'd treat any other game.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Commanders announce Marcus Mariota will be a team captain for the rest of the season
summary: Mariota will start in place of the injured Jayden Daniels on Sunday against the Seahawks.
full_text: Marcus Mariota will be the Commanders' starting quarterback for whatever games Jayden Daniels misses with his left elbow injury. And Mariota and Daniels will both be team captains for the rest of the season. Commanders coach Dan Quinn announced on Friday that the five Commanders who were chosen as team captains before the season got together and decided they want Mariota to be a captain, not just while he's the starting quarterback but also when he returns to the No. 2 job when Daniels returns. "I thought it was such a cool thing: The captains huddled up with me earlier in week and said, 'We'd like to make Marcus our sixth captain,'" Quinn said. "I thought, What a great tribute of brotherhood of those guys asking. They were all as on board as you could imagine. I thought it was awesome, too. What a great example of teammate and leadership." The Commanders say Mariota's status as captain for the rest of the season is not an indication that he'll be starting for long, as the team expects Daniels to be back soon. But even if Mariota spends most of the season on the bench, he'll have the captain's C on his jersey. In addition to Mariota and Daniels, the Commanders' captains are wide receiver Terry McLaurin, linebacker Frankie Luvu, safety Jeremy Reaves and punter Tress Way.
author: Michael David Smith

title: After Week 2 stinger, Saquon Barkley vows to be "fearless"
summary: Barkley missed much of Sunday's game after injury.
full_text: A stinger grossly shortened Eagles running back Saquon Barkley's day against the Titans in Week 2. As a Week 3 Monday night game against the Bears looms, Barkley is undeterred — but also cognizant of the situation. " I’ve had a history of [stingers] before ," Barkley said Friday, via Tim McManus of ESPN. "This is the first bad one I had in a long time. It's also like a wake-up call to me. I've been super active focusing on my lower body and longevity of my career. I probably wasn't as great as I needed to be with my neck stability and strengthening my neck. So it's putting that within my routine and having that as part of my process and kind of the same way I attack everything from head to toe, do the same thing with my neck. "It's good to have an MRI knowing it's nothing, hopefully, God willing, where I worry about my career and I can just go out there and play free." The injury happened on the first play from scrimmage at Tennessee. Barkley later returned wearing a neck collar, but he finished the day with only four carries for nine yards and one catch for 11 yards. Barkley was limited in practice on Thursday. He fully participated on Friday. Will the injury affect him on Monday? "I don't think so," Barkley said. "That's why I'm rehabbing my ass off, to get it as strong as it needs to be. I feel like I'm in a really good spot. I know they wouldn't let me go out there if I wasn't able to do it. "I'm going to let the game come, and I'm going to go out there and play fearless, don't worry about." The Eagles are 2-0 after narrow wins against the overmatched Commanders and Titans. Philly may be facing a third-string quarterback in Chicago on Monday night, giving the Eagles a golden opportunity to move to 3-0.
author: Mike Florio

title: Tim Tebow pauses his relationship with Life Surge after Pablo Torre investigation
summary: Pablo Torre is a troublemaker.
full_text: Pablo Torre is a troublemaker. In the best way possible. A recent episode of Pablo Torre Finds Out explored the entity known as Life Surge, which allegedly has preyed on Christians who attend events featuring speakers like former NFL quarterback Tim Tebow in an effort to get them to plunk down cash to sign up for classes on how to make money. It was enough to get Tebow to suspend his dealings with Life Surge. “ The allegations are extremely, extremely serious ,” Tebow told reporters on Friday, "and it’s something that we take very serious. And so for us, we’re having our team do an investigation but also pausing our relationship 'til we can learn more about the facts to be able to understand more.” Tebow was asked whether he knew about the situation before Torre's investigation. “Honestly, I was at a anti-human trafficking conference yesterday, and the team shared with me when we were leaving as we were flying to Alabama for [an] event,” Tebow said. “And kind of caught off guard with some of it, and I think that’s why we’re trying to understand more of the facts to really learn it.” That's hardly a clear and unequivocal denial. Regardless, Torre's investigation put just enough of a spotlight on the situation to get Tebow to back away, regardless of what he knew or should have known before Torre pulled the curtain back on Life Surge. It's possible the group duped Tebow in the same way it allegedly duped those who attended the events at which Tebow spoke. Historically, plenty of Christians have had their strong beliefs leveraged into plenty of money for charlatans who regard intense faith as an opportunity to make easy money.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bud Light leans in to fines for beer celebrations
summary: The Church Lady has commandeered the league office.
full_text: '' The Church Lady has commandeered the league office. And the league's official beer sponsor has taken full advantage of it. Three different fines issued were this week to players who mimed the consumption of a beverage that the NFL presumed to be beer. Bud Light, which reportedly pays the NFL $250 million per year , has leaned in to the league's crackdown. Tweeted the Bud Light official account: " $37,384 in the jar … how many beers will that buy for everybody this weekend?" That highly-specific amount represents the exact sum of the fines imposed on 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk ($14,926), Colts guard Matt Goncalves ($8,847), and Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson ($13,611). Meanwhile, and as Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News notes, the Cowboys have Miller Lite logos all over the backdrop for their press conferences in Brazil, where they'll be playing the Ravens this weekend. It's all ridiculously hypocritical for the NFL. But the league doesn't care. For the NFL, it's do as we say, not as we brew.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bears ST coach says Eagles are violating intent of the rule by using holder on kickoffs
summary: Last week, the Eagles used a holder on their kickoffs so that the ball could be placed at an angle that affected the trajectory of the ball and made it harder for the returner to field.
full_text: Last week, the Eagles used a holder on their kickoffs so that the ball could be placed at an angle that affected the trajectory of the ball and made it harder for the returner to field. This week, the Bears are preparing to face the Eagles on Monday night, and Bears special teams coordinator Richard Hightower says he doesn't think the Eagles should be able to do that. Hightower, who was one of the special teams coaches who was involved in adopting the NFL's "dynamic" kickoff, said permitting a 12th player on the field to hold the ball was intended to be for windy conditions with the ball in a tee, and not for what the Eagles are doing. "Two years we talked about it, where you could use a holder," Hightower said. "It evolved to weather-related only. This past year it changed to you can use it at any time. But . . . the intent of the rule is the ball is supposed to be in a tee when you have a holder out there. It's not to be used like you've seen it used here lately." Hightower said there was a conference call with special teams coaches scheduled to discuss the matter. "We're all getting together on that shortly and we hope to get that fixed and corrected within the language of everything done in the rulebook," Hightower said. Hightower said he believes the NFL could make a change now requiring that the ball is placed in a tee if there's a holder on a kickoff, and that the change wouldn't need to wait until the offseason. "That's the intent of the rule and what we want to have happen, so that's the way it should be, and that's the way we'd like it going forward," Hightower said. There's precedent for the NFL making such a change during the season: In 2022, the Raiders were using a holder on kickoffs to place the ball on top of the tee, rather than in the tee, something the NFL initially allowed — only to change course during the season and ban it . Hightower wants to see the NFL do the same thing with the Eagles' tactic.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Josh Allen is having a historic start to the season
summary: Bills quarterback Josh Allen has gotten off to a great start in 2026.
full_text: ''' Bills quarterback Josh Allen has gotten off to a great start in 2026. He's already made a little history — and he could make some more. Per NBC Sports research, Allen is one of only three players with nine or more total touchdowns and no turnovers in the first two games of the season. The others — Patrick Mahomes in 2018 and Peyton Manning in 2013 — won the NFL MVP award that same year. With at least two touchdowns and no turnovers against the Chargers on Sunday, Allen would join Mahomes as the only players with 11 or more touchdowns and no turnovers through three games. (Mahomes had 13 touchdowns and no turnovers through three games in 2018.) And there's more. Allen has had two straight games with four or more touchdowns and no interceptions. If he does it again on Sunday, he'll tie five players for the longest streak in league history: Matthew Stafford in 2025, Allen in 2024, Lamar Jackson in 2019, Drew Brees in 2018, and Russell Wilson in 2015. Finally, Allen has had two straight games with two rushing touchdowns. Only three players have done that in the first three games of the season: Priest Holmes in 2003, Stephen Davis in 1999, and Jim Brown in 1958. Allen would trade it all for a 3-0 start, for the third straight season. And to extend Buffalo's home record to 19-2 over the past 21 games.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Shanahan on Nick Bosa's injury: I know he's bummed, but he'll be back
summary: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed defensive end Nick Bosa will miss multiple weeks after injuring his calf before Thursday's practice.
full_text: '' 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed defensive end Nick Bosa will miss multiple weeks after injuring his calf before Thursday's practice. "We can't say exactly, but I'm guessing around a few weeks ," Shanahan said of Bosa's timeline, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com. The 49ers ruled out Bosa and rookie defensive end Romello Height (hand surgery) for Sunday's game against the Cardinals. They have been hit hard by injuries in the defensive line. Defensive tackle C.J. West (knee), defensive end Sam Okuayinonu (foot) and defensive tackle Alfred Collins (patellar tendon) are on injured reserve. Rookie defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. has a high-ankle sprain that will keep him out multiple weeks. "Losing Bosa was rough yesterday," Shanahan said. "I mean, losing six out of the 10 D-linemen in the last two weeks that have made our team is a little unusual. I don't think I've been a part of that, so that has been different." Bosa returned from a torn ACL in his right knee and played 70 snaps over the first two games. He injured his knee in Week 3 last season, almost exactly a year ago, in a game against the Cardinals. It is unclear whether Bosa injured his right calf, as Shanahan said he wasn't sure. Bosa was warming up before the walkthrough when he injured his calf. "I know he's bummed out, but he'll be back," Shanahan said. The 49ers are still deciding whether to place Bosa on injured reserve. Only eight players can return from IR during the season, and the team already has several players on IR who it plans to return to the roster. "He's right there at that point, along with a couple of other guys that are all in the same boat," Shanahan said. "Because of the number we have on [injured reserve], we won't be able to do all of them. So we've got to decide, and we're just trying to guess which ones will go longer, which ones have the chances of being sooner, and it's just a guess. "They're all really in the same boat, so we've got to decide that by tomorrow."
author: Charean Williams

title: Saquon Barkley back to full participation, Hollywood Brown doesn't practice
summary: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said that he expects to be good to go for Monday night's game against the Bears and Friday's injury report shows that he's on track to play.
full_text: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said that he expects to be good to go for Monday night's game against the Bears and Friday's injury report shows that he's on track to play. Barkley was up to full participation after getting in a limited session on Thursday. Barkley suffered a stinger in last Sunday's win over the Titans. Wide receiver Hollywood Brown (ankle) was added to the injury report on Friday and he did not practice. Tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) remained out of practice. Running back Tank Bigsby (abdomen), running back Will Shipley (foot), and wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) were limited after missing Thursday's practice. Linebacker Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) was also limited while defensive tackle Jalen Carter (wrist), safety Andrew Mukuba (knee), and guard Tyler Steen (shoulder) were full participants.
author: Josh Alper

title: 49ers WR Mike Evans is questionable with a hip injury
summary: 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans returned to practice Friday, but he is questionable to play Sunday.
full_text: '' 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans returned to practice Friday, but he is questionable to play Sunday. Evans' hip injury kept him out of practice on Wednesday and Thursday. He has nine catches for 103 yards and a touchdown in two games. Evans missed nine games in 2025 and three games the previous season after sitting out only nine games over his first 10 seasons. The 49ers ruled out defensive end Nick Bosa (knee/calf), defensive end Romello Height (hand), wide receiver Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and defensive tackle James Thompson (ankle). Bosa injured a calf muscle during Thursday's practice, and he is expected to miss multiple weeks. Height underwent hand surgery this week, and Robinson and Thompson have high-ankle sprains that could keep them out multiple weeks.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bills sign WR Greg Dortch to active roster, place DB Jordan Hancock on IR
summary: The Bills have signed wide receiver Greg Dortch to the active roster from the practice squad, the team announced Friday.
full_text: ''' The Bills have signed wide receiver Greg Dortch to the active roster from the practice squad, the team announced Friday. In a corresponding move, the Bills placed defensive back Jordan Hancock on injured reserve. Hancock missed Thursday and Friday's practice due to a hamstring injury. He played 13 defensive snaps and 42 on special teams in the first two games and totaled five tackles. The Bills elevated Dortch for the first two games. He returned five punts for 46 yards (9.2 avg.) and five kicks for 133 (26.6 avg). He has played four offensive snaps and 18 on special teams.
author: Charean Williams

title: Titans RB Tony Pollard has no injury designation, but RB Tyjae Spears is questionable
summary: Titans running back Tony Pollard (ankle) had a second consecutive limited practice Friday after missing Wednesday.
full_text: '' Titans running back Tony Pollard (ankle) had a second consecutive limited practice Friday after missing Wednesday. Pollard, though, did not receive an injury designation for Sunday. That is good news for the Titans because running back Tyjae Spears (ankle) is questionable to play. Spears returned to practice Friday on a limited basis. Rookie running back Nick Singleton made his regular-season debut in Week 2 and could see more work this week because of Pollard and Spears' injuries. " He’s doing a really good job ," Titans coach Robert Saleh said Friday, via Jim Wyatt of the team website. "He's probably 50-50 on the read [on his runs], but to be expected from a young buck. So, hopefully we get him a couple more. But overall I think he's going to be a good back, he's going in the right direction." Singleton, selected in the fifth round out of Penn State, carried the ball four times for 10 yards against the Eagles. The Titans also list cornerback Cor'Dale Flott (quad) as questionable after he had three limited practices this week.
author: Charean Williams

title: LT Josh Simmons out, CB Mansoor Delane set to play for Chiefs-Dolphins
summary: The Chiefs are once again set to start undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson at left tackle.
full_text: The Chiefs are once again set to start undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson at left tackle. Kansas City officially ruled out Josh Simmons on Friday with his back injury. Simmons did not practice all week as he continues to recover. While head coach Andy Reid said in his Friday press conference that defensive back Chamarri Conner won’t play, he is officially doubtful for the contest after he was a limited participant in Friday’s practice. But cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) is off the injury report and set to play. He was a full participant in practice all week. Delane was available on an emergency basis for last week’s game against the Colts after aggravating his shoulder during the Week 1 win over the Broncos. Defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah (quad), linebacker Jeff Bassa (shoulder), defensive back Jadon Canady (knee), linebacker Jack Cochrane (calf), defensive back Jaden Hicks (biceps), defensive tackle Chris Jones (calf), receiver Rashee Rice (knee), cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (knee), and quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee) are all officially off the injury report and set to play.
author: Myles Simmons

title: WR Zay Flowers questionable, OT Ronnie Stanley out for Ravens
summary: Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers returned to Friday's practice as a limited participant.
full_text: Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers returned to Friday's practice as a limited participant. The team lists him as questionable to play Sunday. He did not play in Week 2 after having a limited practice last Friday, so it remains to be seen whether he will play. Flowers caught five passes for 150 yards and a touchdown in the season opener. The Ravens ruled out Ronnie Stanley despite coach Jesse Minter saying earlier in the day that the offensive tackle would be a game-time decision. Stanley did not practice this week because of a toe injury. Defensive lineman Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) and linebacker Teddye Buchanan (knee) will make their 2026 debuts against the Cowboys. Neither player has a designation after full practices all week. Outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson (finger) returned to full participation Friday, and he also does not have a designation.
author: Charean Williams

title: J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey on track to play Sunday night
summary: The Broncos have good news and bad news at running back on their final injury report ahead of Sunday night's game against the Rams.
full_text: The Broncos have good news and bad news at running back on their final injury report ahead of Sunday night's game against the Rams. J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey are on the good news side. Dobbins (hip) and Harvey (hamstring) were both full practice participants the last two days and they do not have injury designations for Sunday. Harvey missed last Sunday's win over Jacksonville and Dobbins was injured during the game. The bad news involves rookie Jonah Coleman. He missed practice all week with an ankle injury and has been ruled out. Wide receiver Marvin Mims (foot) was limited in practice and is questionable to play after missing last week's win.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sam Darnold is set to start for the Seahawks
summary: Darnold has no injury designation for Sunday's game.
full_text: ' Sam Darnold is ready to return to action for the Seahawks. Darnold missed last Sunday's win over the Cardinals with the glute injury that knocked him out of the season opener, but he returned to full practice on Thursday and is off the injury report entirely on Friday. Head coach Mike Macdonald called Darnold "ready to go" in his Friday press conference, so Drew Lock will move back to the bench after helping the team to two victories. The news is not as good on the defensive side of the ball. Safeties Julian Love (calf) and Ty Okada (hamstring) have been ruled out. Love was added to the injury report when he missed practice on Thursday while Okada has yet to play this season. Defensive tackle Brandon Pili (concussion) is considered questionable for Sunday's road game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dre'Mont Jones out, Craig Woodson and Eli Raridon questionable for Week 3
summary: The Patriots will officially be without one of their key defenders on Sunday.
full_text: The Patriots will officially be without one of their key defenders on Sunday. New England has ruled out linebacker Dre'Mont Jones for the Week 3 matchup against Jacksonville. Jones did not practice all week with a shoulder injury. Linebacker Quintayvious Hutchins (knee) was also ruled out for the contest. Safety Craig Woodson (shoulder) and tight end Eli Raridon (thigh) are both questionable for the game. Raridon was limited on Wednesday and didn’t practice on Thursday or Friday. Woodson went the other way, not practicing on Wednesday or Thursday while being limited on Friday. Safety Brenden Schooler (back) was limited all week as he returns from the NFI list. Offensive tackle Morgan Moses (foot), offensive tackle Dametrious Crownover (knee), cornerback Carlton Davis (neck), and fullback Reggie Gilliam (knee) are all off the injury report and are set to play.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jets list Adonai Mitchell, Joseph Ossai as questionable
summary: The Jets aren't ready to make a call on wide receiver Adonai Mitchell's availability for Sunday's game against the Lions.
full_text: '' The Jets aren't ready to make a call on wide receiver Adonai Mitchell's availability for Sunday's game against the Lions. Mitchell was added to the injury report with a finger injury on Thursday and he was limited in practice for the second straight day on Friday. The team has listed him as questionable for the game. Linebacker Joseph Ossai (foot) is also listed as questionable. Ossai did not play in the first two games, so this weekend would mark his Jets debut. The Jets ruled safety Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin), tight end Mason Taylor (thumb), and linebacker Kiko Mauigoa (quad) out for this week. Running back Kene Nwangwu (back) is listed as doubtful.
author: Josh Alper

title: Texans rule out Jadeveon Clowney, Nico Collins
summary: The Texans ruled out five players for Sunday's game against the Colts.
full_text: The Texans ruled out five players for Sunday's game against the Colts. Houston won't have defensive end Jadeveon Clowney (knee), wide receiver Nico Collins (hamstring), linebacker Jake Hummel (groin), offensive guard Ed Ingram (groin) and safety M.J. Stewart (knee). Clowney, Collins, Hummel and Ingram did not practice this week. Stewart was a limited participant on Wednesday and Friday but missed Thursday's work to rehab. Offensive tackle Trent Brown (knee/wrist) returned to full participation on Friday, but the Texans still list him as questionable. Collins, the team's top wideout, injured his hamstring in practice last week and missed the Week 2 loss to the Bengals. Clowney has a bone bruise that will keep him out a second consecutive week.
author: Charean Williams

title: Giants list Brian Burns as questionable
summary: Word this week was that Giants linebacker Brian Burns would miss time with the ankle injury he suffered in Week 2, but the Giants have not ruled him out for Sunday's game against the Titans.
full_text: '' Word this week was that Giants linebacker Brian Burns would miss time with the ankle injury he suffered in Week 2, but the Giants have not ruled him out for Sunday's game against the Titans. Burns is listed as questionable despite missing practice all three days this week. The report and the lack of practice time suggest Burns will need more time before he's able to play, but final word on his status won't come until closer to kickoff. Left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin) returned to practice Friday and has no injury designation. Cornerback Deonte Banks (calf) and safety Tyler Nubin (calf) join Burns with questionable designations on the team's final injury report.
author: Josh Alper

title: Joey Porter Jr. questionable after another limited practice
summary: Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. hasn't played this season.
full_text: Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. hasn't played this season. It remains to be seen when he will play this season. Porter is questionable, with the Steelers listing the reason as not-injury-related/conditioning. In the first two weeks, he was also listed with a back injury. Porter was limited in Friday's practice, and he has yet to fully participate this season. Porter said earlier this week he " definitely " sees himself playing at some point this season. He is earning $3.924 million in 2026, the final year of his rookie deal, after not receiving his desired long-term deal. The Steelers' team policy is not to negotiate once the season starts. The Steelers ruled out running back Rico Dowdle (toe) and offensive guard Gennings Dunker (knee). Wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (foot), running back Jaylen Warren (shoulder) and cornerback Jamel Dean (ankle) are questionable. All three were limited practice participants again on Friday.
author: Charean Williams

title: Charvarius Ward questionable, Ashton Dulin out for Colts-Texans
summary: The Colts are listing one of their defensive starters as questionable, but it appears he's trending in the right direction to play on Sunday against the Texans.
full_text: The Colts are listing one of their defensive starters as questionable, but it appears he's trending in the right direction to play on Sunday against the Texans. Cornerback Charvarius Ward is questionable for Week 3 with his groin injury. Ward did not practice on Wednesday. He was limited on Thursday and a full participant on Friday. “[Ward] had a good day of work today, and then we'll see how he feels tomorrow,” head coach Shane Steichen said Friday, via transcript from the team. “But I think he's in a good place right now.” Additionally, the Colts are listing Ashton Dulin (ankle) as out. Alec Pierce (heel) is also out, but he’s set to be placed on injured reserve — the Colts just haven’t made that official quite yet. Cornerback Sauce Gardner (rib), guard Matt Goncalves (foot), and receiver Laquon Treadwell (shoulder) are all off the injury report and are set to play.
author: Myles Simmons

title: JC Tretter: Field condition in Brazil "reinforces" NFLPA concerns about international games
summary: Sunday's game between the Ravens and Cowboys in Brazil will be played on a grass field that likely will not look great on TV.
full_text: Sunday's game between the Ravens and Cowboys in Brazil will be played on a grass field that likely will not look great on TV. It also will present challenges for the players, especially when it comes to wearing the right cleats. NFL Players Association executive director JC Tretter has weighed in on the issue. And he has pointed to the obvious red flag regarding the general field quality at stadiums that rarely host NFL games. "There have been a lot of questions about the field surface in Brazil, and I wanted to provide the NFLPA’s perspective," Tretter said in a lengthy message posted on Twitter . "Our number one priority is the health and safety of our players. The concern heading into this week was that the field would be loose, patchy, and lead to excessive slipping. Those conditions are generally more of a playability and performance issue than a significant injury concern. "But safety isn't the only standard. Players should be able to perform at the level they expect of themselves and that fans expect from them. A thin, slick field may not present the same risks as a surface with too much traction, but it still affects performance and the quality of the game. "We've been in regular communication with the league about the field. Both the NFLPA's and the league's field experts have been on the ground in Brazil for days, monitoring conditions and working to make the surface as safe and playable as possible for Sunday. "Based on our experts' assessment, the field needed better traction and stability. They recommended reinforced stitching to help the surface hold together and brought in equipment to reinforce as much of the field as possible before the game. Our experts will remain engaged and continue evaluating conditions through kickoff. "The work happening this week also highlights two larger issues. "First, we need field standards that account for both safety and performance. The NFL, NFLPA, and our field and engineering experts spend a lot of time working on these issues, and we've made progress. But we're not where we need to be yet. We can't have surfaces that melt players' cleats, like we saw in Nashville last week. We can't have frozen fields that create unnecessary risks. The best athletes in the world should be playing on surfaces that meet the same standard of excellence we expect from them every week. "Second, this reinforces one of our concerns about international expansion. Two of the three games played in Brazil have had field-related issues. That's not a coincidence. This time of year makes it extremely challenging to maintain the kind of grass surface we expect at the NFL level. "Our guys are exceptional at what they do, and I'm confident they'll put on a terrific game in Rio this week. They always do. But we owe it to them to provide the best possible opportunity to succeed. Players can overcome a lot. But they shouldn't have to overcome the field. "The NFL has been clear they want to continue to grow the game internationally. However, growth alone cannot be the goal. The goal has to be growing the game while maintaining the standards our players deserve. If we can't do both, then we need to make different decisions." The problem is that the NFL has already made the decision to expand the slate of international games from 10 per year to 16. As to field quality, it would be better to have a team or two based in other countries, since that would give the league a reason to ensure that the field will be good enough for all 10 home games played there. For now, the league intends to, in theory, have every team play one international game per year. And while the NFLPA isn't required to agree to that term in the next Collective Bargaining Agreement, the league will surely lock out the players until they agree to both 18 regular-season games and 16 annual international games. The best the players can do is negotiate the best concessions in exchange. Field quality shouldn't be a concession. The league's desire to save money and to expand revenue potential for non-football events has contributed to the current number of artificial fields. The issue is different as to international games; cities need to be selected with the quality of the games to be played there as one of the top priorities. In Brazil, it clearly is not.
author: Mike Florio

title: Caleb Williams, Tyson Bagent out of practice Friday
summary: Case Keenum remains on track to be the Bears' starting quarterback against the Eagles on Monday night.
full_text: Case Keenum remains on track to be the Bears' starting quarterback against the Eagles on Monday night. The Bears practiced without both Caleb Williams (hamstring) and Tyson Bagent (concussion) on Friday. The two players were estimated as non-participants on Thursday as well. Williams's injury is not believed to be a major one, but head coach Ben Johnson said he was week-to-week and the lack of practice time suggests that he'll miss at least one game before being in position to return. Kicker Cairo Santos (hip) and offensive lineman Joe Thuney (rest) also sat out practice on Friday. Linebacker Noah Sewell (Achilles), cornerback Tyrique Stevenson (hamstring), and defensive lineman Shemar Turner (knee) were limited participants while defensive lineman Grady Jarrett (rest) and running back Kyle Monangai (knee) fully participated in practice.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ravens WR Zay Flowers returns to practice Friday
summary: Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers returned to practice Friday, participating in individual drills.
full_text: Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers returned to practice Friday, participating in individual drills. The Ravens' practice report is not out yet, so his participation level and status for the Week 3 game against the Cowboys will be revealed later today. Flowers missed practice earlier in the week, while rehabbing his hamstring injury. He did not play in Week 2 after having a limited practice last Friday, so his availability for Sunday's game in Brazil still seems iffy. Coach Jesse Minter was more optimistic but less specific about Flowers and defensive lineman Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) than he was about offensive tackle Ronnie Stanley, according to Jonas Shaffer of the Baltimore Banner . Stanley did not practice this week because of a toe injury. Minter said the Ravens will wait until pregame warmups to decide if Stanley can play. Stanley started last week's game but was replaced by Carson Vinson in the fourth quarter.
author: Charean Williams

title: NFL injury report for Week 3: Updates on Puka Nacua, Sam Darnold, Nick Bosa, Joey Porter and more
summary: Every team's final injury report and game statuses for Week 3
full_text:
Per usual, there are a slew of notable injuries to monitor ahead of this weekend's games. Fortunately for you, we're keeping track of every team's final injury report, which you can find below.
News broke about several injured players before today's injury reports were released. Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will play this weekend for the first time after he sustained a glute injury during the early portions of Seattle's Week 1 win over the Patriots.
Rams wideout Puka Nacua (hip/groin) will be listed as doubtful for Sunday night's showdown against the Broncos in Denver. 49ers pass rusher Nick Bosa is expected to miss a few weeks after he pulled his calf during Thursday's practice. Jaxson Dart , who sustained a season-ending knee injury during Monday night's loss to the Rams, reportedly underwent surgery on Friday. His recovery timeline is 4-6 months.
Below is a rundown of every team's final injury report of the week. Be sure to monitor this page throughout the evening as we will be providing updates as soon as they are available.
Chargers : G Kayode Awosika (fibula), TE Charlie Kolar (forearm), DB Elijah Molden (hamstring), G/T Trey Pipkins III, WR Brenen Thompson (quadricep), DL Dalvin Tomlinson (hamstring) OUT; QB Trey Lance (groin), CB Rodney Shelley (hamstring) QUESTIONABLE Bills : DB Jordan Hancock (hamstring), DL T.J. Sanders (illness) OUT; WR Keon Coleman (ankle), WR DJ Moore (shoulder), DL Ed Oliver (hip), G Ar'maj Reed-Adams (elbow) QUESTIONABLE
Lance was a late addition to the injury report. The Chargers can promote DJ Uiagalelei from the practice squad if Lance is unable to play. Jim Harbaugh said that Trevor Penning will start at left guard in place of Awosika.
For the Bills, coach Joe Brady said that Coleman and Moore will be game-time decisions after being limited participants on Friday.
"I'm going to give them all the way through till game time," Brady said . "And I have confidence in them. When they're ready to go, they'll be ready to go."
Panthers : LB Devin Lloyd (calf), LB Claudin Cherelus (shoulder), S Nick Scott (rib) OUT; WR Jalen Coker (ankle), WR Xavier Legette (knee) QUESTIONABLE Browns : OL Teven Jenkins (back) OUT; CB Tyson Campbell (ankle, hip, knee), S Grant Delpit (shoulder) QUESTIONABLE
The Panthers were hit hard on both sides of the ball this week. Lloyd won NFC Defensive Player of the Week after registering nine tackles, a sack, two interceptions (one returned for a touchdown) and three pass breakups. He did not practice at all this week. Dave Canales said Coker should be good to go -- he didn't practice Thursday but logged limited practices on Wednesday and Friday -- and Legette will be a game-time decision.
The Browns will be without Jenkins for the third straight week, but coach Todd Monken said he's hopeful both Campbell and Delpit can play. Both were limited in practice all week. Campbell was listed as questionable (ankle) last week but played; he picked up the hip injury earlier this week and the knee injury on Friday.
Jets : S Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin), LB Kiko Mauigoa (quad), TE Mason Taylor (thumb) OUT; RB Kene Nwangwu (back) DOUBTFUL; WR Adonai Mitchell (finger), EDGE Joseph Ossai (foot) QUESTIONABLE Lions : G Ben Bartch (foot), S Thomas Harper (ankle) OUT
Ossai is trending upwards as he was a full participant on Friday. Mitchell was limited on Thursday and Friday.
Along with Harper, the Lions will also be without Avonte Maddox , who sustained a season-ending injury during Detroit's Week 2 loss in Buffalo. The injuries to Maddox and Harper will give Christian Izien , Jalen Mills and Bishop Fitzgerald more opportunities to make plays in the Lions' secondary.
Texans : WR Nico Collins (hamstring), DB M.J. Stewart (knee), LB Jake Hummel (groin), G Ed Ingram (groin), EDGE Jadeveon Clowney (knee) OUT; OT Trent Brown (knee/wrist) QUESTIONABLE Colts : WR Ashton Dulin (ankle), WR Alec Pierce (heel) OUT; CB Charvarius Ward Sr. (groin) QUESTIONABLE
It's another lengthy injury list for the Texans, with no absence looming larger than Collins'. The Texans managed just six points last week with Collins out, and tight end Dalton Schultz (140 yards) was the only player with more than 37 yards receiving. Ingram being out and Brown being questionable means an already-struggling offensive line could be down more bodies, too, though Brown at least logged a full practice Friday.
As expected, Pierce will miss this game after he prematurely exited the Colts' Week 2 loss to the Chiefs. The arrow is up for Ward, who was fully engaged on Friday.
Patriots : LB Quintayvious Hutchins (knee), LB Dre'Mont Jones (shoulder) OUT; TE Eli Raridon (thigh), S Craig Woodson (shoulder) QUESTIONABLE Jaguars : DT Albert Regis (elbow) DOUBTFUL
Raridon didn't practice the past two days after being limited on Wednesday. Woodson was limited on Friday after not practicing the previous two days.
New England will face a familiar face in former Patriot Jakobi Meyers , who was taken off the injury report after dealing with a thumb injury.
Chiefs : T Josh Simmons (back) OUT; DB Chamarri Conner (knee) DOUBTFUL Dolphins : EDGE Rob Beal Jr. (hamstring), WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) OUT; RB Jaylen Wright (stinger/foot) DOUBTFUL; CB JuJu Brents (knee), WR Ryan Miller (hip/back) QUESTIONABLE
Conner was limited during each of this week's practices. For the Dolphins, Brents and Miller were full participants on Friday.
Titans : CB Cor'Dale Flott (quad), RB Tyjae Spears (ankle) QUESTIONABLE Giants : OLB Brian Burns (ankle), CB Deonte Banks (calf), S Tyler Nubin (calf) QUESTIONABLE
Flott was questionable all week, while Spears was limited on Friday after not practicing the previous two days. Fellow running back Tony Pollard (ankle) will play after being limited the past two days.
For the Giants, Burns didn't practice all week, while Banks and Nubin were limited throughout the week.
Bengals : WR Andrei Iosivas (thumb) OUT; DT B.J. Hill (Achilles) DOUBTFUL Steelers : G Gennings Dunker (knee), RB Rico Dowdle (toe) OUT; WR Michael Pittman Jr. (foot), CB Joey Porter Jr . (NIR/conditioning), RB Jaylen Warren (shoulder), CB Jamel Dean (ankle) QUESTIONABLE
Cincinnati has only two players on its injury report, but they're both significant. Hill's absence would leave the Bengals with less depth in the middle of their defensive line. Iosivas' absence will likely lead to more targets for running backs Chase Brown , Samaje Perine (who caught three touchdowns in Pittsburgh back in 2022) and tight end Mike Gesicki .
The Steelers removed the back ailment from Porter's injury label this week. Porter, who unsuccessfully held in this summer in the hope of getting a new contract, was non-committal when asked about his status for Sunday. Pittsburgh will also have to scramble if Warren can't play. With Dowdle already out, Travis Homer would likely be promoted from the practice squad if Warren is inactive.
Seahawks : S Julian Love (calf), S Ty Okada (hamstring) OUT; DT Brandon Pili QUESTIONABLE Commanders : G Sam Cosmi (concussion/throat), S Nick Cross (illness), QB Jayden Daniels (left elbow), LB Frankie Luvu (groin), TE Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) OUT
AJ Finley will replace Love in the starting lineup on Friday. Along with Darnold, the Seahawks will also have rookie running back Jadarian Price , who left last week's win over the Cardinals early after injuring his chest. Price was a full participant on Friday.
Daniels is among the large contingent of injured Commanders who won't play on Sunday. Daniels will be replaced by Marcus Mariota , who has played well when given the opportunity since coming to Washington in 2024. During his time in D.C., Mariota has thrown 15 touchdowns against seven interceptions and has completed 64.1 percent of his passes.
Cardinals : S Dadrion Taylor (back) OUT; DL Roy Lopez (groin), CB Max Melton (toe) QUESTIONABLE 49ers : James Thompson (ankle), WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle), DL Romello Height (hand) EDGE Nick Bosa (calf) OUT; WR Mike Evans (hip)…

title: NFL Week 3 picks, best bets: Broncos upset Rams, Bills rout Chargers
summary: Jordan Dajani gives his picks for Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season
full_text:
Week 2 in the NFL was a weird one. We went from shootouts and fun in Week 1 to low-scoring games and injuries. Weather robbed us of a fun matchup in Chicago between the Bears and Minnesota Vikings , then Jaxson Dart's injury robbed us of what could have been a fun Monday night showdown between the New York Giants and Los Angeles Rams . Overall, not a great week for football fans.
As for our picks, we went 7-9 against the spread and 2-3 on best bets. We cashed on the San Francisco 49ers blowing out the Miami Dolphins and the New York Jets keeping things close with the Green Bay Packers , but somehow were on the wrong side of Tennessee Titans vs. Philadelphia Eagles and Baker Mayfield getting beat by the Cleveland Browns . Mayfield is now 0-2 against his former team.
Here's a look at what I'm thinking this week. As always, credit to the CBS Sports research team for making me sound smart.
Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
Top five picks ATS record: 5-5 Overall ATS record: 15-17 Straight-up record: 19-13
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ )
This is a sort of a "put my money where my mouth is" situation. I'm not very concerned that the Houston Texans have started 0-2. For one, they had to play Josh Allen and Joe Burrow . Secondly, DeMeco Ryans has started 0-2 in three out of his four seasons as head coach. Yet, he's finished with double-digit wins every year.
Still, I agree it's worrisome that this Texans defense hasn't looked stout and that the offense couldn't find the end zone at all last week against the Cincinnati Bengals . Not having Nico Collins really hurts, but I still like this Houston team more than its rival here.
The Indianapolis Colts kept up with the Kansas City Chiefs last week, but I couldn't get over how bad this defense was. The Colts are just the third team in NFL history to allow 500 yards of total offense in each of their first two games, joining the 1967 Falcons and the 2016 Raiders . They rank dead last in total defense, passing defense and scoring defense. Plus, Daniel Jones isn't going to have Alec Pierce to throw to! Houston is 13-1 SU and 10-3-1 ATS in its last 14 road divisional games. I'll call my shot here and take the Texans.
The pick: Texans -1.5 Projected score: Texans 27-21
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
What can you say about the Los Angeles Chargers ? They are the first team ever to start 0-2 with both losses coming to 14-loss teams from the previous season. Everyone wants to talk about Justin Herbert , but I'm watching his receivers either drop balls or give them to the wrong team — or straight-up switch their allegiances, play defense and stop their teammates from catching them.
There are very real people out there who are very actually blaming Justin Herbert for this incompletion. This is a great throw. It's just a really stupid tight end. pic.twitter.com/nPfIoP3VR3
I agree Herbert hasn't been good. Yes, it's true he's not Josh Allen. He can't power otherwise bad or average teams to wins by himself. But if you want to blame the quarterback for all the Chargers' issues, then you're simply not watching.
When I watch Chargers tape, I get frightened by the defense. They aren't really generating pressure, and there have been multiple blown coverages. Even when the Chargers stick to their assignments, it doesn't really matter. Some of the throws Kirk Cousins was making last week were offensive.
There's almost an arrogance with these. "I don't trust you guys to stop this, so I'm just going to trust my receivers."
Kirk Cousins throwing yolo no-look balls to Tre Tucker 40 yards down the field pic.twitter.com/MmncVyz03d
Not sure how many football fans know Cody White but Kirk Cousins sure trusts him! pic.twitter.com/hdGnT5mrHL
Okay, that was kind of a rant, but all that to say is that I don't trust the Chargers to cover against the best team in football in their first road game of the year. Herbert is having to answer tough questions from reporters, the Buffalo Bills had a long week to prepare for this game, and the fan base is still riding high after that successful home opener vs. the Detroit Lions . There is going to be a packed house to watch the Bills debut the ugliest uniforms of all time.
Coming 🔜 to Highmark Stadium. @JoshAllenQB | #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/TIKFsiORzb
The pick: Bills -7 Projected score: Bills 29-17
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
I've become a Jets merchant, cashing on them in both Week 1 and Week 2. Now I'm flipping on them, because how they lost last week to the Packers was embarrassing.
Aaron Glenn was content to let Jordan Love have the final play of a tie game instead of taking a timeout and giving his offense a final chance. And I'm not so sure he remembered the rules for overtime, since he elected to take the ball first and promptly go three-and-out. C'mon, man.
It's true that the Lions' defense is once again going to stop them from contending for a Super Bowl , but Jared Goff should get back two of his starting offensive linemen this week, and the offense as a whole is still electric. Jahmyr Gibbs has racked up 299 total yards and three touchdowns this season, while Amon-Ra St. Brown became the first player to catch two touchdowns in a team's first two games of a season since Rob Gronkowski in 2021.
Quite simply, the Lions are going to outscore the Jets. And I want to see Dan Campbell take some anger out on his former defensive coordinator after getting embarrassed on a national stage last Thursday night. The Lions are 11-1 SU and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 home games following a loss, so Campbell usually comes through.
The pick: Lions -6.5 Projected score: Lions 28-16
Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET (NBC, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
I would argue that the Denver Broncos looked like the worst team in football in Week 1. Week 2 was a different story.
The Broncos defeated the Jacksonville Jaguars , 20-13, after trailing by 10 points in the second half. Trevor Lawrence and his Jags were dominant in Week 1 vs. Cleveland, but the only thing that was dominant this past Sunday was the Broncos' defensive front vs. the Jaguars' offensive line.
It took longer than expected, but Davis Webb and Bo Nix finally found a rhythm. Jaylen Waddle carried the passing game with 138 yards on eight receptions, and you started to see glimpses of why people think Denver could be a Super Bowl contender. After all, they came one Nix injury away from making the big game last February.
As for the Rams, they danced all over the lifeless Giants, who had the collective air knocked out of them when Jaxson Dart went down with his knee injury. How much stock are we supposed to put into that game? I guess we learned Davante Adams is still a good wide receiver? He'll have to be a star again on Sunday night, because I'm not sure Puka Nacua will suit up with his hip/groin issue.
I'm calling the upset here. Nix has this weird thing when it comes to beating teams in the NFC. He's 9-0 in his past nine games against NFC opponents and has scored 23 total touchdowns, with just two turnovers and a 104.2 passer rating in those contests. This is a redemption opportunity for Denver after that season opener in Kansas City that was a borderline FCC violation.
The pick: Broncos +2.5 Projected score: Broncos 26-24
Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET (ESPN, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
I don't understand this line, but I'll bite. It's Jalen Hurts vs. a 38-year-old Case Keenum who hasn't started since 2023. Caleb Williams is sidelined with his hamstring injury, and Tyson Bagent is working through concussion protocol, so here comes the former University of Houston quarterback who led the NCAA in passing yards and passing touchdowns TWICE back in the day.
Keenum is 30-36 as a starting quarterback, and his last completion of 20+ air yards came in 2019 with Washington! Expect Ben Johnson to run the ball plenty, which could work since Chicago owns the No. 1 rushing offense in the NFL through Week 2 with 212.5 rushing…
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Why Patriots QB coach uses chicken wings to motivate Drake Maye
summary: There are apparently a lot of similarities between playing QB and eating a chicken wing
full_text:
There is a myriad of ways to motivate athletes, from inspirational sports movies to bulletin board material. The Patriots , however, have found a unique way to motivate quarterback Drake Maye .
Ashton Grant, the Patriots quarterbacks coach, recently acknowledged that Drake is his own biggest critic. But while that might be true, Grant has found a creative metaphor that has further helped Maye in his pursuit of excellence — chicken wings.
"He's someone that wants to chase perfection, and I think that is good," Grant said . "And try to feed into that a little bit because there's always a little bit more meat on the bone.
"You know, we joke around with like chicken wings, and if you guys ever eat wings ... people throw them away, and there's a little bit of meat left. I try to show pictures of bare bones of the meat just to be like, there's always more for us to do. You know, whether it be with our details, techniques, our fundamentals, our communication, our operation. We're constantly chasing the best version of ourselves, and I'm happy that he's someone that likes to do that."
Maye is coming off a 2025 campaign that saw a Super Bowl appearance and a runner-up finish in the NFL MVP race. However, his 2026 start has been much slower. He has just one touchdown and 386 passing yards to go along with four interceptions. Those four turnovers rank 31st in the league, while he ranks 25th in passing yards. He and the Patriots face the Jacksonville Jaguars in Florida this weekend.
Anyone who has eaten a chicken wing knows exactly what Grant is talking about. While it's relatively easy to get most of the meat off the bone, it takes a little more time and effort to polish it off. Because of that, most people tend to leave some meat on the bone (which is crazy given how much chicken wings can cost these days).
While you might not think so at first, a chicken wing is a pretty good metaphor for playing quarterback at a high level. What oftentimes separates the good from the great to the truly elite quarterbacks in the NFL are the ones who put in a little more time and effort. It's safe to say that Maye's work ethic has helped him enjoy early success in New England.
Fortunately for Grant, he won't have to look very far to find good chicken wings in Week 4, when the Patriots head to Buffalo to take on the Bills .

title: NFL likely to shut down rulebook loophole Eagles have been exploiting for the past two weeks
summary: Philadelphia and other teams have added a 12th man on kickoffs to hold the ball on the ground
full_text:
For the past two weeks, several teams have been taking advantage of a loophole in the NFL rulebook, but that likely won't be happening much longer. It looks like the league is thinking about shutting it down.
The rulebook is kind of ambiguous about whether teams can use a holder WITHOUT a tee on a normal kickoff, so the Eagles have been taking advantage of that. In their Week 2 win over the Titans , the Eagles sent out punter Braden Mann to serve as the holder for Jake Elliott on kickoffs. The Eagles were trying to make it easier for Elliott to kick a "Dirty ball," which is essentially a low knuckleball that can be difficult to field.
To make Elliott's job easier, the Eagles had Mann hold the football ON THE GROUND at Elliott's preferred angle.
Smart loophole? #Eagles had holder Braden Mann on the field as a 12th man for all but one of Jake Elliott's kickoffs last week. It's legal under the new kickoff rules, as long as the holder runs off the field after the kick. In this case, it wasn't because of wind. It was to… pic.twitter.com/JFU1Z7lH9f
The Falcons also used this strategy in their Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
When the NFL made the switch over to the dynamic kickoff in 2024, the league added a rule that permitted teams to use a 12th player on the field , but only in one specific situation. It has to be a holder for kickoffs during windy games or in situations where the ball won't stay on the tee. The holder then has to run off the field immediately.
Here's what the rulebook says about using a holder:
"If Team A is using a designated holder, the designated holder may be the 12th person on the field when the ball is kicked for a kickoff or safety kick," the rulebook states. "But he is a non-player, must leave the field on his team's sideline with the kicking tee immediately after the ball is kicked, and is also subject to the rules of non-player conduct in accordance with Rule 13.
Now this is where things get ambiguous. The rulebook states that you can use a holder at any time, but it doesn't necessarily say anything about whether you have to use a tee.
"During a free kick, the kicking team may use a manufactured tee designed to hold the ball no more than one inch from the ground and approved by the League," the rulebook says. "During a kickoff or safety kick, the kicking team may also use a designated holder to hold the ball."
The team "may" use a manufactured tee. It doesn't say they have to use one.
According to Bears special teams coordinator Richard Hightower, using a holder and having him place the ball directly on the ground goes against the spirit of the kickoff rule. During a meeting with reporters on Friday ( via ESPN ), he said the rule will be corrected and that if a holder is used, he'll have to place the ball on a tee.
Basically, the Eagles will still be able to use a holder, but they won't be allowed to place the ball on the ground. Under the current rules, if a team attempts an onside kick, they can place the ball directly on the ground, and that part of the rule won't change.
The Eagles can keep doing what they've been doing until the league changes the rule, but if that doesn't happen soon, you could see other teams start copying Philadelphia's strategy.

title: Giants-Titans weather: MetLife Stadium conditions expected to be rainy and windy for Week 3 game
summary: Here's how wind and rain could impact Sunday's game between New York and Tennessee
full_text:
If you're going to the Giants-Titans game at MetLife this weekend, pack some rain gear. Severe weather is hitting the Northeast this weekend and East Rutherford is expected to be impacted.
Heavy rain and winds are coming through the state this weekend, with precipitation in the area expected to start at 10 p.m. on Friday night, according to weather.com.
When the game kicks off at 1 p.m. ET, the high will be 62 degrees, with an 83% chance of rain. The north wind will be around 18 mph and the gusts could get up to 41 mph. There is a wind advisory until Sunday at 6 a.m. ET.

title: What is Puka Nacua's status for Rams' Week 3 showdown at Broncos?
summary: Nacua missed Week 2 with a hip injury and is struggling to get healthy
full_text:
Rams coach Sean McVay said star wide receiver Puka Nacua (hip) won't practice Friday and will be listed as doubtful for Los Angeles' "Sunday Night Football" showdown against the Broncos , according to ESPN's Sarah Barshop . Including Friday's absence, Nacua will not practice this week. He also didn't practice last week before not playing against the Giants .
In more positive news for the 2025 receiving leader, McVay said if Nacua doesn't play Sunday, he will be back for Week 4 against the Eagles , barring a setback.
Though Nacua's injury is officially listed as a hip ailment, he reported groin soreness last week. McVay has maintained Nacua is not dealing with a hernia but said it "can almost be like pre-hernia is what he's feeling" and wants to err on the side of caution.
Should Nacua not play Sunday, it'd be his second consecutive game missed. With Nacua out in Week 2, Davante Adams exploded for eight catches, 195 yards and two touchdowns, while tight end Terrance Ferguson notched six catches for 54 yards and a touchdown.
Nacua, 25, led the NFL with 129 receptions last year, racking up 1,715 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. His 107.2 receiving yards per game also led the NFL. He was a first-team All-Pro and finished third in Offensive Player of the Year voting.
He had five catches for 74 yards in Los Angeles' Week 1 loss to the 49ers in Australia.
Adams showed he can still take over a game, but that came against the injury-riddled Giants' secondary. Can he duplicate it against the Broncos' excellent one, led by 2024 Defensive Player of the Year Patrick Surtain? Part of what makes the Rams' offense so good at full strength is that Adams often draws opponents' second-best cornerback. As for the wide receivers behind Adams, it's slim pickings. Konata Mumpfield actually led all Los Angeles wide receivers with 42 snaps in Week 2; Adams had 38, and Xavier Smith had 25.
Of course, if there's anyone built to deal with a shortage of wideouts, it's Los Angeles. The Rams led the NFL with 331 plays with three or more tight ends on the field last year, more than double the second-most team. They already have a league-leading 51 such plays this season.
Ferguson could again see a big role. He's a talented pass catcher with the speed to stretch the field. He played 35 offensive snaps last week, second behind Colby Parkinson (42) among tight ends. Davis Allen played 31 snaps, and Tyler Higbee played 16. Overall, Los Angeles played 32 snaps with three or more tight ends on the field.
No matter the solution, Nacua's absence hurts. A lot. The Broncos have a terrific defense that returned to form in a 20-13 Week 2 win over the Jaguars after an uncharacteristically poor Week 1 against the Chiefs . Nacua is a rare combination of size, physicality, speed and contested catch ability. He can line up outside and in the slot, allowing McVay to unlock his entire playbook.
Last year, the Rams averaged 6.8 yards per play with Nacua on the field compared to 5.0 with him off the field.
Nacua isn't the only Rams star to hit the injury report after Week 1. Myles Garrett underwent knee surgery and landed on IR after the opener. Starting safety Kam Kinchens didn't play in Week 2, either.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Bengals' Joe Flacco sets record straight on trade rumors to Giants after Jaxson Dart injury
summary: What the veteran backup said about his name being attached to speculation
full_text:
With six NFL franchises facing quarterback dilemmas in Week 3 following significant injuries, proven backups have become immediate trade rumor fodder across the league. Jaxson Dart's knee injury with the New York Giants immediately summoned speculation involving Joe Flacco and whether the Cincinnati Bengals would be willing to part with their seasoned No. 2.
Jameis Winston is New York's new starter and struggled in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, completing just 11-of-27 passes for 111 yards and an interception.
Flacco was uninterested in discussing his ties to New York — as a former three-year Jet — or talk linking him to a possible trade destination with the Giants.
"It's obviously not real and not true," Flacco told The Cincinnati Enquirer late Thursday ." "But it was good enough to get people like certain friends of mine to get them to text me, 'hey, I'll see you in New York.' I was like, 'no, guys, you won't, that's not true.'"
Much like the San Francisco 49ers planning to keep their No. 2 Mac Jones in the wake of several quarterback injuries around the NFL, it's unlikely the Bengals would be willing to depart from Flacco.
He's a proven veteran behind Joe Burrow and signed a one-year free agent deal in March with the Bengals worth $9 million total incentives as an emergency depth chart option. Flacco's coming off his first Pro Bowl nod and garnered respect from Bengals coach Zac Taylor last season after filling in admirably for Burrow over nine games with 1,664 yards passing, 13 touchdowns and four interceptions.
"I just get a kick out of it," Flacco said of trade rumors. "I haven't really given it too much thought at this point."
Five days after the Bengals traded for Flacco last season, he started a game against the Green Bay Packers and floored Taylor with his poise and knowledge of the game.
"It was never lost on us how impressive that was," Taylor said during training camp this summer . "That's a big reason we brought him back."
Flacco's immediate fit in Taylor's offensive scheme made it a no-brainer to invest in the 41-year-old signal caller for another season in 2026. And given Burrow's injury history, Cincinnati feels good about its decision.
Currently first in the AFC North as the division's lone unbeaten, the Bengals (2-0) play the Pittsburgh Steelers on the road this weekend at 1 p.m. on Sunday inside Acrisure Stadium on CBS.

title: 49ers' Nick Bosa will reportedly miss multiple weeks, IR placement not likely due to limited space
summary: Bosa did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa suffered a calf injury during practice this week and is expected to miss multiple weeks, per the NFL Network . The report states he will be out this week against the Arizona Cardinals after not practicing on Wednesday or Thursday.
The 49ers are reportedly "leaning towards" not putting him on injured reserve due to limited space. Only eight players can return from injured reserve, so the 49ers will need to be strategic with who they place on the list.
If he is placed on IR, he would miss a minimum of four games, per league policy. The team's next four games are against the Cardinals, Denver Broncos , Seattle Seahawks and Washington Commanders .
The 49ers have not been lucky when it comes to injuries, and this is yet another blow to their roster. If Bosa does miss significant time, the team may have to dip into other places to find a DE. Keion White and Khalid Kareem are the two healthy defensive ends and will need to step up in Bosa's absence.
Defensive end Sam Okuayinonu (foot) is on IR, but could return this season, while Mikail Kamara (knee) will be sidelined for the remainder of the year. Mykel Williams is on the PUP list as he continues to rehab a torn ACL he suffered last year and can return in Week 5 at the earliest. Romello Height (hand) is questionable this week, but did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday. Defensive tackle James Thompson Jr . (ankle) was also sidelined for two days of practice this week.
Defensive lineman Alfred Collins is out for the year with a torn patellar tendon and fellow DL Andrew Farmer II is also done for the season with a back injury. Defensive tackle CJ West (knee) is another player on IR.
On Wednesday, the 49ers signed defensive linemen Naquan Jones and Viliami Fehoko Jr. to the practice squad. On Saturday, they promoted defensive lineman Ogbo Okoronkwo to the active roster.
Bosa suffered a torn ACL during Week 3 of last season, ending his 2025 campaign. The Pro Bowler has started both games so far this year for the 49ers and has seven combined tackles, with three solo, two tackles for a loss and one quarterback hit.
Bosa has spent his entire career with the 49ers, beginning his NFL journey in 2019 as a second overall pick. His resume includes Defensive Rookie of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year, first-team All-Pro and five Pro Bowl honors.
In eight seasons, he has 285 total tackles with 64.5 sacks, 13 forced fumbles, five fumble recoveries, and two interceptions in 87 games, 85 of which were starts.
