title: AFC North Preview, Week 3: Bengals and Steelers battle in first divisional matchup
summary: Week 2 of the regular season saw movement across the AFC North standings. The Bengals were the only team to win for a second straight, giving them early sole possession atop the division. The Ravens and Steelers each fell to 1-1, while the Browns’ victory on Sunday brought to them to .500. Let’s preview how […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 16: Ja'Marr Chase #1 of the Cincinnati Bengals attempts to complete a catch against Jalen Ramsey #5 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during an NFL football game at Acrisure Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 2 of the regular season saw movement across the AFC North standings. The Bengals were the only team to win for a second straight, giving them early sole possession atop the division. The Ravens and Steelers each fell to 1-1, while the Browns’ victory on Sunday brought to them to .500. Let’s preview how Week 3 is stacking up for every team in the AFC North. Updated Standings: Cincinnati Bengals 2-0 Baltimore Ravens 1-1 Pittsburgh Steelers 1-1 Cleveland Browns 1-1 Cleveland Browns Matchup: vs. Carolina Panthers, 1:00pm EST The Browns earned a surprising upset victory in Tampa Bay last week, defeating the Buccaneers 23-19. After a long weather delay in the fourth quarter, Cleveland’s defense closed out the game with a two-minute stand in the end zone. Deshaun Watson had his best performance in recent memory and retained his grasp on the starting quarterback job heading into Week 3, where the Browns will host the Panthers in their home opener. Carolina has been an offensive revelation to begin the season, scoring 71 points through two games. They’re 1-1 after a 31-point beatdown on the Atlanta Falcons in Week 2. The Browns’ defense had a much better showing against the Buccaneers than they did versus the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1, but the Panthers will present a challenge. Bryce Young is red-hot at quarterback having thrown six touchdowns and over 600 passing yards with just one interception thus far. How the Browns’ cornerbacks fare against wide receivers Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan will be a big factor. Coker is questionable to play with an ankle injury, which would be a big hit to the Panthers’ offense if he can’t suit up. On the other side of the ball, Watson will look to build off a successful outing against a vulnerable Panthers’ defense. While Carolina allowed only three points last week, they were steamrolled in the season opener for 59 points against the Chicago Bears. The Browns have still yet to establish an effective run game with Quinshon Judkins through two weeks, which should be a priority in this matchup. Rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston will look to continue making big plays through the air. He has seven catches for 154 yards and two touchdowns. Cincinnati Bengals Matchup: @ Pittsburgh Steelers, 1:00pm EST The Bengals are off to a successful 2-0 start after a 14-point victory over the Houston Texans last week, where their defense showed continued encouraging signs. While the Bengals didn’t force any turnovers, they allowed just six points while racking up four sacks, seven quarterback hits and eight pass breakups. Newcomers Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen were disruptive on the defensive line and helped shut down the Texans’ running game. On the flip side, the Bengals were outgained by over 100 total yards, gained only 12 first downs and averaged 4.5 yards per play. Against the Steelers this Sunday, the Bengals will look to find more offensive rhythm and consistency. Pittsburgh’s defense is always dangerous of making game-changing plays, especially in an unpredictable division matchup setting. Look for the Bengals to try to establish the run still with Chase Brown and utilize a quick-passing strategy to neutralize the Steelers’ pass rush. Brown has received 36 carries through two weeks but averaged only 3.8 yards per carry. This profiles as a favorable contest for the Bengals’ defense once again. Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers’ offense have struggled through two games. Cincinnati’s pass rush could wreak havoc against a largely immobile quarterback. The Steelers may be due to connect on some big plays and find more success running the ball, though, so the Bengals will still need to be on their A game. Pittsburgh Steelers Matchup: vs. Cincinnati Bengals, 1:00pm EST The aforementioned Steelers will host the Bengals for their second home game of the season. The Steelers were defeated soundly by the New England Patriots last week, 20-3, which dropped them to 1-1. Pittsburgh’s offensive struggles continued as they converted 16 first downs, were unsuccessful on 83% of third down tries and gained 235 yards of total offense. Pass protection (four sacks, seven quarterback hits) and running the ball were issues, as was a lack of explosive plays through the air. No pass-catcher had more than 35 yards for the Steelers. Against the Bengals, the Steelers will need do a better job of giving Rodgers protection under center. The Bengals have displayed a disruptive pass rush through two games and will challenge the Steelers’ offensive line. They also badly need to find more effectiveness in the run game. They may be without the services of Rico Dowdle in this game as he deals with a toe injury, meaning Jaylen Warren will get a large workload. Wide receiver D.K. Metcalf is in dire need of a breakthrough performance after a rough start to the season (eight catches for 67 yards on 19 targets). Defensively, the Steelers will have their work cut out for them against a talented Bengals’ offense. Their biggest advantage lies up front, where they should be able to create some pressure on Joe Burrow. Pittsburgh’s defense has held up well through two games but the Bengals will present the most talent they’ve faced thus far. In order for them to score enough points to win, they may need a couple of key takeaways and possible a defensive touchdown, like they got in Week 1. Baltimore Ravens Matchup: @ Dallas Cowboys, 4:25pm EST (Brazil) The Ravens are set to do battle against the Cowboys this week in a much-anticipated international matchup in Brazil. After a disappointing upset loss in Week 2, the Ravens will be looking to quickly turn the page. The Ravens suffered another blown lead at home to the New Orleans Saints and were outscored 15-0 in the fourth quarter, leading to a seven-point defeat. While they are technically the road team in this game, it’s essentially a neutral site — one where field playing conditions have been a topic of concern in recent days. Dallas will present a tough task for the Ravens’ defense. They are loaded with playmakers highlighted by one of the league’s top wide receiver duos in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. How well Nate Wiggins, Marlon Humphrey and company fare in these matchups with the Cowboys’ wideouts will be a huge factor in this game. The Ravens struggled with missed tackles last week and could not get off the field on third down enough. They will need to tighten up these areas against a high-powered Cowboys offense. Lamar Jackson may be without the services of Zay Flowers (hamstring) once again, whose absence has been clearly felt over the last six quarters of play. Rashod Bateman and Mark Andrews will likely be relied on heavily again in the passing game. The Cowboys’ defense has been a sieve through two games and they’ll be missing several starters due to injury. If the Ravens’ pass protection can hold up against Quinnen Williams and others, they should be able to score a good amount of points. Baltimore’s offensive line has been one of the league’s worst in pass protection through games and have struggled on the interior.

title: The under-looked cause to the Ravens’ 1-1 start
summary: Much has been made of yet another Ravens’ fourth quarter collapse during their loss to the Saints in Week 2. “It was the defense’s fault!” or “it was Declan Doyle’s fault!” have been reccuring phrases from fans. While we are all quick to scapegoat, there is actually a much simpler issue that, if fixed, would […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Head Coach Jesse Minter of the Baltimore Ravens looks on against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Much has been made of yet another Ravens’ fourth quarter collapse during their loss to the Saints in Week 2. “It was the defense’s fault!” or “it was Declan Doyle’s fault!” have been reccuring phrases from fans. While we are all quick to scapegoat, there is actually a much simpler issue that, if fixed, would have the Ravens sitting at the top of the NFL standings — penalties. Not just any type of penalties, though, but specifically ones that absolutely kill drives and positive plays. Through two weeks, the Ravens have lost -11.0 EPA on the penalties themselves, second-most in the NFL behind only the Carolin Panthers. That number undersells the damage, though. It only captures what happened on the flag, not what the flag took away. Add in the value of the plays those penalties erased and the picture gets worse. The Ravens’ nullified plays were worth a combined +9.2 EPA, by far the most in the league. Baltimore isn’t getting flagged for holding on a stuffed run or an incomplete pass. It’s having productive plays called back again and again: a Ja’Kobi Lane touchdown, a 19-yard catch by Rashod Bateman, an 11-yard grab by Mark Andrews, a Lamar Jackson first down scramble. Combine the two, and the Ravens’ total penalty cost comes to -20.1 EPA, just a hair behind Carolina’s -20.2. Unfortunately, there’s more . . . most offenses make back some of what they lose by drawing flags from opposing defenses. The Panthers have recovered +3.1 EPA that way, and Minnesota and Buffalo have each gained more than +19. Baltimore has gained, drum roll . . . zero. The Ravens are the only offense in the league without a single accepted defensive penalty. That leaves Baltimore with a net offensive penalty EPA of -20.1, the worst mark in the NFL. No team has lost more to penalties on offense, and no team has gotten less back. Then, you factor in some of the questionable calls at the end of the Saints game – that’s really when I started scratching my head. Is it possible that the Ravens are only committing offensive penalties on very successful plays, and the opposing defense hasn’t committed a penalty? A number of the team’s offensive penalties have certainly been valid but there are some that haven’t been. Chris Moore’s holding penalty last week and John Simpson’s “chop block” in Week 1 were highly questionable. The opposing team hasn’t been the victim of any of these 50/50 calls — especially on plays that yield very positive results. Obviously, you would surmise that these penalties are in-part leading to some of these eventually negated plays, but the Ravens have also generated explosive plays without them, so that doesn’t seem valid. These penalties had a major swing factor against the Saints, especially the ones in the 3rd quarter, which led to them losing ~5 expected points. The Ravens had reached the Saints 28 yard line, but were backed all the way up by penalties, resulting in a field goal. They were moving the ball effortlessly and would have probably scored a touchdown. For some quick back of hand math, the Ravens lost by seven points. If those flags did not occur, they should have theoretically been in position to win or tie the game at the end with a field goal – at the very least. Obviously, none of this really matters now and the result is the result. However, the Ravens clearly need to clean up this penalty mess. It’s costing them big time and while part of this is on the Ravens technique, you would clearly expect some of the penalty luck to naturally start swinging in their favor soon. Two weeks isn’t a large sample size but at this pace, they are on track to shatter the NFL record for the most net expected points lost to penalties on offense. What does all this mean? Yes, the Ravens need to clean some things up – but I have a feeling some good luck might be coming their way. They are currently on pace to quadruple the NFL record for net penalty EPA lost on offense, and that probably won’t continue.
author: Stephen Bopst

title: Ravens vs Saints Rookie Report
summary: The Ravens’ 2026 rookie class suffered their first NFL loss in the home opener against the New Orleans Saints in Week 2. Let’s see how the rookies did in the game. OG Vega Ioane After a strong NFL debut in Week 1, Ioane had a much rougher time in Week 2. Ioane was charted with […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Chandler Rivers #29 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts as he runs against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Ravens’ 2026 rookie class suffered their first NFL loss in the home opener against the New Orleans Saints in Week 2. Let’s see how the rookies did in the game. OG Vega Ioane After a strong NFL debut in Week 1, Ioane had a much rougher time in Week 2. Ioane was charted with four pressures on 40 pass-blocking snaps according to PFF. The Saints countered the new Ravens under-center offense with a lot of A-gap blitzes and Ioane, paired with center Jovaughn Gywn, struggled to sort through the noise. PFF also gave him a low run-blocking grade, but the Ravens ran the ball effectively on Sunday, with clips showing Ioane moving bodies, so I’m not buying into that grade as much. While many, myself included, touted Ioane as one of the most NFL-ready prospects in the draft with an All-Pro ceiling, he’s still just a rookie in his second start next to a first-time starter at center. I’m not discouraged. His Week 1 performance was great, and I’ll buy we see more games like that than this one. DE Zion Young Young had an up-and-down day against New Orleans. He continued to flash that raw strength that is the cornerstone of his game, which gave him one pressure on seven pass-rush snaps according to PFF rate, with a 16.3% win rate. He graded out fairly well in pass rush (63.1), run defense (68.7), and special teams (72.6). That being said, Young had two noticeable mistakes on Sunday. First, on the Saints’ first scoring drive, Tyler Shough absolutely shook Young out of his cleats on what should have been an easy tackle for loss that could have helped force a longer field goal attempt. Then, after the Ravens responded to that field goal with their own touchdown and should have been going into halftime with a 14-3 lead, Young failed to keep contain with Malaki Starks on the kick return right before halftime, which allowed the Saints to tag on another three. These aren’t massive mistakes and most rookies do make them, but they were impactful and it’s the little details that can win or lose you a game. Otherwise, I think Young has been as advertised — a guy who’s been able to knock linemen back with his incredible play strength and push the pocket. WR Elijah Sarratt After being specifically mentioned by the coaching staff before the game against New Orleans as a guy who could find rhythm with Zay Flowers and Ja’Kobi Lane down, Sarratt got the game-day activation after being a healthy scratch Week 1. Sarratt then proceeded to get zero snaps on offense or special teams. This is frustrating, considering the Ravens did lose and how much they’ve struggled on offense since Flowers went down. Sarratt’s steady hands should be utilized. TE Matt Hibner and TE Josh Cuevas I wouldn’t normally put two rookies together, but that’s how little they were both used in this one. Neither tight end saw a target, and they played a combined 24 snaps total against the Saints. Hibner ran 10 routes according to TruMedia and earned a 57.8 run-blocking grade on nine blocking snaps, per PFF. Cuevas ran four routes and had a run-blocking grade of 59.7 on one snap. I specifically mentioned Hibner a couple of times leading up to the game, as I would have liked to have seen him get targets. Fellow tight end Mark Andrews was effective in his safety valve role but didn’t offer much downfield or after the catch. Hibner seems to be a guy who could become an explosive tight end receiving option for this team but hasn’t received much a chance. We’ll have to see if his role gets bigger as the Ravens continue to navigate operating without Flowers and Lane. CB Chandler Rivers After being a healthy scratch Week 1, Rivers got the activation against the Saints following T.J. Tampa’s move to IR. Rivers immediately factored into the rotation, out-snapping both Chido Awuzie and Keyon Martin. Rivers flashed throughout the day in coverage, limiting yards after the catch and being a solid tackler — something the rest of the Ravens’ defense struggled with against the Saints. Coming out of the draft, some of the best things scouted from Rivers were his physicality despite his smaller stature, play recognition and IQ, and how well he got downhill to bust screens and on blitzes. That was exactly what he showed in this game, especially on his tackle for loss in the red zone, where he immediately eliminated an Alvin Kamara designed touch out near the boundary. Expect Rivers to keep his playing time in a secondary that’s still looking to find its footing. P Ryan Eckley After a great Week 1 where all three of his punts pinned the Colts inside the 20, Eckley’s day against the Saints was less banner-worthy. Eckley only averaged 41.3 yards on his three punts, and none were even caught inside of the 20. With Flowers’ absence continuing to linger, this Ravens team might need to lean on its defense for some wins. That starts with Eckley giving opposing teams a long field to drive on. He’ll need to be better moving forward. Wide receiver Ja’Kobi Lane and running back Adam Randall remain on injured reserve, with defensive tackle Rayshaun Benny on the practice squad.

title: Buffalo Bills sign WR from practice squad, place DB on injured reserve
summary: Edit: The Bills did not elevate Dortch from the practice squad. They signed him from the practice squad. There’s a difference. Therefore, he has only been elevated twice. He still has one elevation remaining. Smart roster-management decision by the Bills here. Three games in, and the Buffalo Bills have already utilized all of their allotted […]
full_text: Edit: The Bills did not elevate Dortch from the practice squad. They signed him from the practice squad. There’s a difference. Therefore, he has only been elevated twice. He still has one elevation remaining. Smart roster-management decision by the Bills here. Three games in, and the Buffalo Bills have already utilized all of their allotted practice-squad elevations for wide receiver Greg Dortch. The veteran receiver — and Bills primary punt returner — has been called up for Sunday’s Week 3 game against the Chargers. Roster move: Signed WR Greg Dortch from the practice squad. Placed DB Jordan Hancock on Injured Reserve — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) September 25, 2026 As for Hancock, he was limited on Wednesday then didn’t practice the rest of the week, which hints at a practice-related ailment. Now he’ll miss at least four games with that hamstring injury. After a stellar summer and outstanding preseason, Hancock missed the season-opening win over the Texans played on 13 snaps against the Lions. And he was active with five tackles including one stop. Buffalo will have another roster decision to make after this week, when the suspension is over for defensive lineman Phidarian Mathis. I wonder if Dortch will get his first target as a member of the Bills on Sunday, with D.J. Moore and Keon Coleman both carrying questionable designations into this game against the Chargers.

title: 5 Buffalo Bills to watch vs. Los Angeles Chargers
summary: The Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Chargers are set to square off this weekend in a matchup of old AFL foes on totally different paths in 2026. The Bills are riding an offensive hot streak so far, sprinting out to a 2-0 start thanks in part to an NFL-leading 38.5 points per game. The Chargers, […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Chargers are set to square off this weekend in a matchup of old AFL foes on totally different paths in 2026. The Bills are riding an offensive hot streak so far, sprinting out to a 2-0 start thanks in part to an NFL-leading 38.5 points per game. The Chargers, meanwhile, have struggled to find rhythm on offense, dropping both of their games so far by the same score, 26-14. With the New England Patriots coming to town next week, this week’s matchup has all the makings of the quintessential trap game. The Chargers desperately need to avoid an 0-3 start, while the Bills will be plenty motivated to stay on top of what should be a very competitive AFC playoff picture as the fall turns to winter. This week’s edition of “five players to watch” has us taking some liberties. We really have four players and an entire chunk of the defense to discuss this week, and while those may be the ones we’ve chosen, they aren’t the only keys to victory for the Bills this week. Without further ado, here are five Bills—and then some—to watch this week. _____________________________________________________________________________ WR Khalil Shakir DJ Moore showed out in his Week One debut with the team. Keon Coleman picked up the slack in Week Two when Moore went down with an injury. Given that both Moore (shoulder) and Coleman (ankle) are dealing with injuries this week, there is some level of uncertainty as to what Buffalo’s receiver group will look like on Sunday. Moore has already said that he’ll play, as he termed his injury a matter of pain tolerance, but Coleman has yet to practice this week. If we assume that Moore will suit up, albeit in a limited capacity, and Coleman will sit, that means that Buffalo will need No. 10 to step up. Shakir has put together two modest games, combining for seven catches and 88 yards on 12 targets. All of those numbers trail tight end Dalton Kincaid, and he’s behind Kincaid and Moore in receiving yards. If there were ever a day to wager that Shakir will see an uptick in targets, this is the one, as Los Angeles enters play ranked No. 28 in passing defense with a nickel corner in Tarheeb Still that can be beaten by strong slot play. WR Joshua Palmer Speaking of wideouts who might see more targets this week, the former Charger could be in line for some more work if Moore is limited and Coleman is out. Palmer has made the most of his five targets this season, catching two long touchdown passes—a 34-yard strike to win the game against the Houston Texans and a 43-yard hookup to give the Bills a two-score lead against the Detroit Lions. While Palmer has been boom-or-bust, he’s only played 35% of the team’s offensive snaps this year. I’d expect a slight increase this week, and the Bills might look to extend his season-opening touchdown streak given that he’s playing against his old team. DL DeWayne Carter Whether Ed Oliver plays or not, I’m interested in seeing whether Carter can continue his solid level of play. Admittedly, I thought he was going to be a late-summer cut after a poor first season and a second year spent on injured reserve thanks to an Achilles tear; however, Carter has come in and proven to be a valuable part of the defensive line rotation so far. Sure, he’s only made three tackles on 49 defensive snaps, but at his position, it’s about doing the dirty work to ensure that the players at the next level of the defense have room to make plays. Buffalo’s run defense looks to be much improved this season in the early going, and Carter has contributed positively to that improvement. Hopefully, he can rotate in with Oliver this weekend, but if Ed can’t go, Carter has proven that he can pick up the slack. CB Christian Benford Yes, I’m looking at him again. It hasn’t been a great start for Buffalo’s top corner, which is something that we said last season, as well. Does it just take Benford some time to settle into a new year? Or, is the switch to Jim Leonhard’s defensive scheme forcing Benford to play in a way that isn’t his strength? The Chargers’ offense has struggled mightily, but they have some talented receivers, including Quentin Johnson and Ladd McConkey. McConkey, in particular, is someone who could give Benford trouble, as he can line up in the slot or outside, and he relies more on his twitchy route-running and quickness than he does straight-line speed. I’m interested to see how Buffalo defends the pass this week, and I’m looking for big improvements after a mini-bye to self-scout. Part of that improvement involves Benford playing up to his standard. Coverage and Communication Okay, maybe this is a bit of a cop-out, but I really want to see improvement from the entire back-end of the Buffalo defense in both coverage and communication. Truthfully, I think that most of the problems with the latter are a result of the former, and with time, these are issues that will resolve as the players gain more familiarity in the new scheme. As much as the Chargers have struggled on offense, they have talented personnel. Justin Herbert is a good NFL quarterback. Omarion Hampton is a solid NFL running back. We’ve already mentioned some of the talent at receiver, as well. Injury issues on the offensive line should allow Buffalo’s pass rush to thrive, which is something that the team has already experienced this year; if the rush and coverage can finally start to marry, then Buffalo’s defense could take a giant leap forward. I don’t expect perfection, but I’d like to see fewer coverage breakdowns this week. Make the Chargers’ pass-catchers win as a result of winning the physical matchup rather than giving them free space as a result of mental mistakes. One of Buffalo’s defensive backs needs to make a play on the ball, and my proverbial money is on second-year man Maxwell Hairston pulling in the team’s first interception of 2026 this week.

title: Bills vs. Chargers predictions: Buffalo’s offense may dominate in Week 3
summary: The Buffalo Bills are on a heater right now, with quarterback Josh Allen playing incredible football at a clip that has him as the current odds-on favorite to win NFL MVP honors for the 2026 NFL season. Now 2-0 and with impressive offensive showings against both the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions, the Bills are […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: James Cook III #4 of the Buffalo Bills runs with the football during the second half of the NFL game against the Detroit Lions at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills are on a heater right now, with quarterback Josh Allen playing incredible football at a clip that has him as the current odds-on favorite to win NFL MVP honors for the 2026 NFL season. Now 2-0 and with impressive offensive showings against both the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions, the Bills are set to welcome the woebegone Los Angeles Chargers to cozy Highmark Stadium. Things could get out of hand quickly if recent game history is an indication. Will Buffalo’s offense continue its dominant ways in Week 3? It’s trending that way, especially if Allen, running back James Cook III, and tight end Dalton Kincaid continue playing elite football. Many consider this a trap game for the Bills given the situation. However, Buffalo is a much better team than either the Arizona Cardinals or Las Vegas Raiders, which both defeated the Chargers by identical 26-14 scores. That said, Buffalo has its own less-than-ideal identical pair from its first two wins: the defense gave up 31 points in each matchup. Will current trends prevail or is Buffalo headed for a trap? Below, we dive into a few bold predictions for Bills vs. Chargers in Week 3 using data and odds courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook . Josh Allen features early and often Week 3 Through two games, Josh Allen has nine total touchdowns, which includes five passing scores. He’s off to a land-speed-record pace this season, but is it sustainable? It should be at least through Week 3 thanks to a reeling Chargers team. Los Angeles has given up a combined 46-of-66 for 530 yards with four touchdowns and one interception to quarterbacks Jacoby Brissett and Kurt Cousins. I like Allen to surpass that two-game average of 265 yards and two passing touchdowns, perhaps even besting the 23-of-33 pass/attempts average. As of publishing, FanDuel Sportsbook lists Allen’s passing yards total at over 238.5 (-115)/under 238.5 (-115). That over feels like a given this week. Yes, simply picking Allen to surpass what are essentially two-game average marks against LAC isn’t a bold prediction. Instead, I like the odds of Allen throwing for north of 300 yards (+350 at FanDuel), with at least three passing touchdowns (+250 at FanDuel) and at no less than one rushing score (anytime -140 | +450 to score 2+ at FanDuel). I also think Allen will again claim the game’s first score (not a passing TD) as a rusher with a tone-setting touchdown (+550 at FanDuel). Despite the potential for wide receivers DJ Moore and Keon Coleman to both sit out Week 3, there will be plenty of touchdown options, all of whom Allen is well-versed with at wide receiver, tight end, and running back. that includes the expected return of dynamic dual-threat running back Ty Johnson, who’s proven to be a third-down specialist as a receiver. If Buffalo wins the coin toss, look for them to take the ball on offense again — perhaps a nod to the ‘90s Super Bowl Bills teams that sought to bury opponents with an early lead. Head coach Joe Brady has decided to let Josh cook early this season, and it’s worked with aplomb. Expect to see Allen featured early and often in Week 3. Dalton Kincaid dominates in Week 3 You might not see this as a bold prediction, especially if Moore and Coleman are sidelined, however Buffalo does have numerous, sometimes overlooked, options to play a featured role as receiver. Week 1, Dalton Kincaid was second on the team in targets (6), co-led the team in catches (5), and led all pass catchers in yards with 130 through the air. Kincaid followed that up with a Week 2 performance featuring seven catches on eight targets for 95 yards — all three serving as team leads — plus his first touchdown of the 2026 season. In Week 3, Kincaid should feast again as a receiver. Kincaid has the fifth-best odds as a touchdown scorer (non-passing), with anytime odds of +185 at FanDuel. Concerning receiving yards, Kincaid’s O/U with FanDuel sits at O 56.6 (-114)/U 56.5 (-114). It would be far more shocking to seem him flirt with that under. I’d roll with the odds that Kincaid surpasses 100 yards in Week 3 (+470 at FanDuel) and 7+ receptions (+400 at FanDuel). As a deep threat, Kincaid has been a serious problem for defenses of late. In fact, as of publishing, Kincaid has the best odds through FanDuel of hauling in a 15+ yard reception (-550), a 20+ yard reception (-210), and a 30+ yard reception (+190). So far this season, when you think of Kincaid, you envision long receptions downfield no matter who’s covering him. James Cook 1st RB to humble LAC in 2026 There’s been a lot of forgettable football out of the Chargers through two losses, but their rushing defense has been fairly stout. Games against the Raiders’ Ashton Jeanty (21 carries, 48 yards; 4 catches, 15 yards) and Cardinals RB1A Tyler Allgeier (17 carries, 61 yards; 2 catches, 9 yards) and rookie RB1B Jeremiyah Love (11 carries, 41 yards, 1 TD; 2 catches 9 yards) prove that Los Angeles’ front seven is serious about stopping the run. That’s good defense against very capable backs, however, James Cook is on a different level as the reigning NFL rushing champ. Still a somewhat overlooked player in the league, Cook has had a decent start to his 2026 season. I expect him to get plenty of touches in Week 3, which should lead to a bunch of yards and a score or two as one of the most dynamic dual-threats in today’s game. Cook is a featured back, but someone who has seen his workload reduced simply due to the team’s third-down preference to roll with Ty Johnson. As mentioned earlier, Johnson should be back this weekend. Will that eat into Cook’s snap count and, ultimately, his touches? I see a lot of that depending on how diverse a game plan the offense deploys for Cook against LA. Cook seems primed for an explosion of offense on Sunday, perhaps totaling a new season high in carries. Interestingly, Cook has the current best odds with FanDuel of scoring 2+ touchdowns (+310), which sounds like others also believe he’s going to be a big part of Sunday’s game. To that end, Cook also has the most favorable odds of scoring a touchdown at any point in the first half (+135 at FanDuel) and also the second half (+160 at FanDuel). Like many of his teammates, it’s true that Cook could head to the sideline early if Buffalo builds a huge lead in the second half. I’m still willing to bet that he gets a lot of run on Sunday, in an effort to really test how good the Chargers are at stopping the ground game. Remember, Cook is always one cut away from a house call, which means he gets top billing as the favorite to finish with the most rushing yards (-185 at FanDuel). Is it too bold to say that Cook should flirt with 90+ rushing yards (+132 at FanDuel) against the Chargers? Again, one carry always has the potential to get Cook better than halfway there. Fair warning: As of publishing, Cook sits at O/U 79.4 total rushing yards (-114). Los Angeles’ run defense is not to be so easily dismissed. Pointing back to the RB receiving stats above, the Chargers are also equally adept at keeping backs in check as a pass-catching threat. Currently through FanDuel, as a receiver Cook is O 1.5 (-154)/U 1.5 (+116) for receptions and O/U 10.5 (-114) for receiving yards. Do you like the odds that one screen pass goes the distance? Maybe you also like the odds that Cook accumulates 50+ receiving yards (+1280 at FanDuel). The trick on Sunday comes if Brady and Allen find a better path toward utilizing Cook as a receiver. All told, I say Cook bests FanDuel’s current projection for his combined rushing and receiving yards at O/U 94.5 (-114). Think you’ve got what it takes to make a play with the Buffalo Bills in 2026? Head over to FanDuel Sportsbook now to put it to…

title: If Buffalo Bills want to explore a Marvin Harrison Jr. trade, they should have the inside scoop on him
summary: Are the Buffalo Bills going to trade for Marvin Harrison Jr.? Heck, none of us know if the Cardinals are even going to be willing to trade him, and at this juncture, we certainly have been given no indication by the Bills — or any NFL insiders — that a trade is being explored. Speaking […]
full_text: Are the Buffalo Bills going to trade for Marvin Harrison Jr.? Heck, none of us know if the Cardinals are even going to be willing to trade him, and at this juncture, we certainly have been given no indication by the Bills — or any NFL insiders — that a trade is being explored. Speaking of exploring, if you’re even mildly intrigued by this idea — or totally despise the thought of it — I highly encourage you to read Matt Byham’s thorough breakdown of the pros and cons of it all . As Harrison Jr. trade speculation percolates, and it feels like it will, as any of it pertains to the Bills, it’ll be critical to remember the Bills should already have plenty of intel this young wideout. Why? Buffalo’s new receivers coach, Drew Terrell, was the pass game coordinator and receivers coach in Arizona the past three seasons, two of which of course correspond with the beginning of Harrison Jr.‘s NFL career with the Cardinals. A former receiver himself, who’s only 35 years old, Terrell started in the NFL in 2018 with the Panthers as a quality control coach and spent 2020-2022 with the Commanders as an assistant receivers coach and the regular wide receiver coach in the 2021 and 2022 campaigns. Of course, Harrison Jr. hasn’t appeared on special teams, but the Bills’ special teams coach Jeff Rodgers was in Arizona from 2019-2025 coaching special teams and with the title of assistant head coach, so he’d clearly know Harrison Jr. reasonably well too. And we have no idea what Terrell and Rodgers think of Harrison Jr., but their close knowledge of the young wideout may either be what spurs the Bills into action on the trade front or provides the inside info to the front office that keeps the Bills away.
author: Chris Trapasso

title: Buffalo Bills may have firepower to trade for Marvin Harrison Jr.
summary: Imagine a Buffalo Bills offense featuring wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., the fourth-overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. A few years ago, that’s all anyone in Bills Mafia could talk about as the team looked to transition away from mercurial wide receiver Stefon Diggs. Harrison presents a divisive conversation on several fronts at the […]
full_text: Imagine a Buffalo Bills offense featuring wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., the fourth-overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. A few years ago, that’s all anyone in Bills Mafia could talk about as the team looked to transition away from mercurial wide receiver Stefon Diggs. Harrison presents a divisive conversation on several fronts at the moment, but it’s not a conversation to be ignored. ESPN insider Dan Graziano reported this week that league executives “are wondering whether the Arizona Cardinals could explore trading 2024 No. 4 pick Marvin Harrison Jr. ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.” What if the Buffalo Bills pulled off a trade for the embattled Harrison — might it come to pass that the Cardinals decide compensation is better than potential? What would a deal involve for such a high-profile player? It might not take as much firepower as you think. It’s possible the Bills could put together a package including a fifth-round pick and a player that brings Harrison to One Bills Drive. The Cardinals would need to replace Harrison’s snaps, so players currently part of Buffalo’s 53-man roster who might be exposed to such a trade include wide receivers Keon Coleman and Joshua Palmer. Trading Coleman opens up a roster spot for Harrison, which includes renewed opportunity to contribute meaningfully on offense, and earn the contract extension he desires. If instead it’s Palmer who’s traded, the Bills are probably looking for Coleman and Harrison to bring the best out of one another in a battle for playing time and that extension either could be signed to as early as the 2027 NFL season. Remember, Harrison and Coleman were both selected in the same draft, and each will demand consideration for a contract extension in due time. If we believe that such a trade is possible, we must also consider the pluses and minuses, of which there are many. Why the Bills should make a trade for Marvin Harrison Jr. The 2023 Fred Biletnikoff Award winner was once consider the best receiver in all of football. His college production had people talking about Harrison on the same level with current NFL greats and even some all-time Pro Football Hall of Fame wide receivers. The son of one such great, Harrison was considered a generational, can’t-miss prospect, which sent draftniks into a frenzy imagining what he’d bring to an offense. Then reality dealt him a side quest. Harrison’s potential remains sky-high with many, but he’s yet to show the sort of consistency needed to invest heavily in his future with any offense. It’s a tale familiar to anyone familiar with football and the NFL Draft: X player has a 50/50 shot at succeeding or fizzling out, regardless of that can’t-miss potential. To this point, it’s clear that Harrison hasn’t lived up to the hype or his draft status. He looks disinterested, lost, and incapable of making even the most routine of plays for Arizona’s offense. That, alone, might give one reason for pause before saying he deserves a shot over someone else currently in the Bills’ system. In his defense, if so deserved here, Harrison has become an afterthought in the Cardinals’ offensive plans. Through two games in 2026, he’s been targeted just three times, making one reception for 33 yards. In contrast, Palmer, as Buffalo’s fourth or fifth option at times, has made two catches (5 targets) for 77 yards, with both going for touchdowns. Meanwhile, Coleman has caught all seven of his targets for 64 yards, with four of those catches giving Buffalo’s offense a first down. Yet neither Coleman nor Palmer bring the sort of potential found with Harrison. If you believe that still exists, then it seems wise for the Bills to at least explore trade discussions. Like Coleman, Harrison is a young player on a rookie contract. As the son of a former NFL all-time great, it’s easy to fall in love with the younger Harrison’s potential. At his best, Harrison would bring elite play to Buffalo’s wide receivers room. Pairing him with wide receivers DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir, plus tight end Dalton Kincaid — Josh Allen would have a fantasy roster of starting pass catchers at his disposal. It feels like a low-risk move to bring in a player the football world fell in love with before he ever caught a professional pass. It’s perhaps a situation made more enticing if the Bills face injury concerns at wide receiver. Right now, both Coleman (ankle) and Moore (AC joint sprain) are questionable to play in Week 3. Certainly, there’s no trade on the immediate horizon such that it helps Buffalo in Week 3. Arizona has until the league’s November 10 trade deadline to explore their options. Harrison’s value has never been lower, and the Cardinals may want to do some damage control before entertaining any trade offers. If that’s not true, and they’re willing to listen at this point, however, it’s an idea worth embracing. You can bet on it that president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane has already been on the phone. Even though Beane values draft picks, almost no potential selection carries the cachet that brackets Harrison as a former top-five-selected player. While this may not be the soundest of business logic, successfully trading for Harrison also keeps him away from other teams — namely potential playoff rivals. What T.J. Houshmandzadeh had to say in support of Marvin Harrison Jr. There’s a lot of warranted criticism of Harrison at this stage, and he has little other than himself to blame. However, football is a team game and Harrison’s teammates directly impact his production and success or failure to thrive. Consider the comments former NFL wide receiver T.J. Houshmandzadeh made about Harrison in a recent featured appearance with “ Speakeasy ”: “Number one: LaFleur, he ain’t f’ing with Marvin Harrison. When you say ‘oh we also have Trey McBride, who’s one of the best underneath guys and there’s only 60 to 65 plays a game you gotta run. When you value somebody, those words don’t even come out your mouth. So that right there tells me he does not value Marvin Harrison as a football player. Marvin Harrison knows that, and this is why we see this. The routes, half speed, his running style ain’t no different. He, (he’s not) trying, because he feels like ‘I’m not gettin’ the ball anyway.’ And this is where… I don’t know how often he talks to senior about this — this is where he has to understand this is making him look bad. Because, everybody else is watching this. And so, your time with the Cardinals is done. They done paid Trey McBride, they done paid Michael Wilson. You are now the third option. If that. You the fourth option in the offense because it’s Trey McBride, it’s Mike Wilson, then it’s Jeremiah Love. Then you. So, you’re gettin’ the crumbs. When we eat, you the runt of the litter. You get what we leave, the leftovers.” “And so, my advice to Marvin Harrison Jr. would be this: Go all out. Show everybody that this shit really matters to you; that you can create separation; that you can get off — even if you don’t get the ball, they gonna see you’re creating separation. They, the other teams. Your time in Arizona, from that, that quote, it’s over. It’s done. When he was at Ohio State, there (were) actual people that thought he was the best receiver in football. And when I say football, I meant all — literally, people were saying Marvin Harrison Jr. is the best receiver in football. They weren’t just talking college. And so there’s still some people out there that believe, if they get him in their system, he’ll be alright. And I actually do believe if he got into a different system he’d be fine. He’s scarred in Arizona. They’ve never really had a (quarterback) — it ain’t like his rookie year he was terrible. He had a solid rookie season. Whatever has happened from that point until now, mentally, it’s a wrap in Arizona. This dude literally is jogging routes… like they’re run plays. Like, they’re pass plays and he’s making ‘em look like runs. And so that tells me he’s…

title: Buffalo Bills need to make Ty Johnson serious part of run game to keep offense humming and help James Cook
summary: Ty Johnson is probably going to make his 2026 debut in this new Buffalo Bills offense on Sunday against the Chargers, and I’m eager to see how much he’s utilized. The do-everything scatback has repeatedly been called the best third-down back in the NFL by Josh Allen during his time in Buffalo, yet he hardly […]
full_text: Ty Johnson is probably going to make his 2026 debut in this new Buffalo Bills offense on Sunday against the Chargers, and I’m eager to see how much he’s utilized. The do-everything scatback has repeatedly been called the best third-down back in the NFL by Josh Allen during his time in Buffalo, yet he hardly was a part of the offense the past three seasons. Take 2025 for example. Johnson toted the rock 50 times across 17 games — essentially an average of three carries per game — the highest total to date of his time with the Bills. He also caught 24 passes, which equated to 1.4 receptions per contest. Before the season, I wrote on my belief that Johnson should become Buffalo’s clear RB2, not Ray Davis. That piece was centered on my thought that Johnson is simply a better overall runner with more versatility. I’m now pushing for a larger role for Johnson because of what it’d do for the lightening of James Cook’s workload. Cook has 34 carries through two games, and for as much as I understand how silly an on-pace figure is this early in a season, I must reference one here. The Bills superstar runner is on pace for 289 carries this season after he had 309 attempts during the regular season and 39 more during Buffalo’s playoff run a season ago. If all of his touches are counted, Cook had 298 of them in 2024 and 385 last year. Those are some sizable numbers. Now, as I pointed out before the season, Cook is incredibly low mileage for a now 28 year old feature back . He entered the 2026 season with only 948 career carries (counting playoffs). For perspective, his brother Dalvin had 1,409 total carries by the end of his Age 28 season. The “RB cliff” we always hear about it is right around 1,500-1,800 rushing attempts. The Bills should do everything in their power to prolong the time it takes for Cook to get to that cliff, right? And, yes, sample size — but Johnson has averaged 6.8 yards per touch in his time with the Bills (which is more than a full yard more than Cook to date). With Johnson presumably fully healthy now, the Bills should start to move him into a a more substantial RB2 role. Even after missing two games to begin the 2026 campaign, Johnson should set career highs in carries and receptions this season. I think it’d be the best for the offense as a whole — because of Johnson’s skill and versatility — and keep Cook fresh.
author: Chris Trapasso

title: Chargers set to be vulnerable at safety vs. Buffalo Bills in Week 3
summary: The Chargers have a clear weak spot on their defense ahead of Week 3’s trip to Orchard Park that the Buffalo Bills need to exploit early and often. Safety. OK, yes, technically, Derwin James is a safety. He’s not super exploitable. But in actuality, he’s an extra linebacker or slot defender. In fact, James has […]
full_text: The Chargers have a clear weak spot on their defense ahead of Week 3’s trip to Orchard Park that the Buffalo Bills need to exploit early and often. Safety. OK, yes, technically, Derwin James is a safety. He’s not super exploitable. But in actuality, he’s an extra linebacker or slot defender. In fact, James has aligned in those roles on 93 of his 120 snaps through two games. I’m talking deep safeties. Veteran Elijah Molden has been DNP for the first two practices with a hamstring injury. He’s looking unlikely to play on Sunday. That will leave 34-year-old Tony Jefferson, who’s always been good and remains pretty darn steady, second-year pro R.J. Mickens, and rookie Genesis Smith. Jefferson, as the clear elder-statesman of the group, could possess some stabilizing influence over his fellow youngsters. And Mickens was far from dreadful as a rookie. He had two interceptions and two pass breakups on 353 snaps last season. Genesis Smith was freak tester at the combine — 42.5” vertical at 6’2” and 202 pounds — but has a ways to go as an all-around defender. He’s played 63 snaps through the first two contests of his rookie and has allowed five catches for 89 yards with a touchdown and one pass breakup on seven targets in his coverage area. The 21 year old has six tackles without missing one to date. There’s certainly upside to this fourth-rounder’s game. But the combination of Smith and Mickens — along with Jefferson — make the Chargers safety trio quite vulnerable ahead of this Week 3 matchup against the Bills. Could the youngsters make a few plays? Sure. And Jefferson is still holding his own in his mid-30s. Nonetheless, Buffalo needs to prioritize repeatedly challenging that trio throughout this game.

title: Buffalo Bills milestones in reach against Los Angeles Chargers
summary: Two weeks down, and we already need the eraser.  Some of the numbers we have been watching since Week 1 are gone. James Cook caught Joe Cribbs — and passed him. Joe Brady has already done something no other Bills head coach has done. And Josh Allen keeps climbing a list that, quite frankly, has […]
full_text: Two weeks down, and we already need the eraser. Some of the numbers we have been watching since Week 1 are gone. James Cook caught Joe Cribbs — and passed him. Joe Brady has already done something no other Bills head coach has done. And Josh Allen keeps climbing a list that, quite frankly, has an awful lot of running backs on it for a quarterback to be hanging around. Now the Los Angeles Chargers are coming to Buffalo, and we have a few more numbers within reach. Each week, we’ll open the Buffalo Record Book to four chapters: Sure Things, A Good Bet, Not Impossible, and Superhuman. Some weeks, we will have an entry in every chapter. Other weeks, we may be more selective. This week, we have something for all four. ______________________________________________________________________ WEEK 3 — September 27, 2026 ______________________________________________________________________ Chapter 1: Sure Things • Khalil Shakir receptions: Shakir caught three passes against Detroit, bringing his career total to 204. That moved him past Robert Woods and into a tie with former Bills tight end Jay Riemersma on Buffalo’s all-time receptions list. One catch Sunday gives Shakir 205 and 17th place all to himself. The human pinball has caught at least one pass in every game he has played since Week 18 of the 2022 season, so we’re feeling pretty comfortable putting this one here. Of course, now that I said that out loud, you can blame me if Allen throws to literally everyone else. ______________________________________________________________________ Chapter 2: A Good Bet • Dawson Knox receptions: Knox caught two passes against Detroit, bringing his career total to 232. That leaves him one behind Cole Beasley, who caught 233 passes during his four seasons in Buffalo. One catch Sunday ties Beasley. Two moves Knox past him on Buffalo’s all-time receptions list. Last week we called two Knox catches a good bet, and he gave us exactly two. Same assignment this week, Dawson. • Josh Allen keeps chasing running backs: Allen scored two more rushing touchdowns against Detroit, bringing his career total to 83 and tying Hall of Fame running back Jim Taylor for 18th on the NFL’s all-time list. One rushing touchdown Sunday moves Allen past Taylor. Two would give him 85 and tie former Bills running back Marshawn Lynch. Again, completely normal quarterback stuff. ______________________________________________________________________ Chapter 3: Not Impossible • Dawson Knox touchdown catches: We finally got some movement here. Knox caught his 28th career touchdown against Detroit, pulling him even with Stevie Johnson and Gabe Davis on Buffalo’s all-time list. One more would give Knox 29, move him past both, and tie Jerry Butler. Apparently, complaining last week that Allen was throwing touchdowns to everyone except Knox worked. You’re welcome. • Joe Brady goes for 3-0: Brady became the first head coach in Bills history to win each of his first two regular-season games when Buffalo beat Detroit. Now he has a chance to put his name on a much shorter NFL list. With a win Sunday, Brady would become the fifth-youngest head coach in NFL history to begin his career 3-0. Brady turned 37 this week. Josh McDaniels and John Madden were 33 when they did it, while Bill Cowher and Mike Tomlin were 35. We put Brady’s first win in this chapter because calling it anything stronger felt like a good way to upset the football gods. No reason to start tempting fate now. ______________________________________________________________________ Chapter 4: Superhuman • James Cook rushing yards: Look who’s back. Cook escaped this chapter last week when his target dropped from 187 yards to 130. Then he ran for 135 against Detroit, passed Joe Cribbs, and moved into fifth place on the Bills’ all-time rushing list with 4,451 career yards. His next target happens to be his own quarterback. Allen enters Sunday fourth on Buffalo’s career rushing list with 4,813 yards. That means Cook would need 363 yards against the Chargers to pass him – and that’s only if Allen doesn’t move the target (which we all know he will). For a little perspective, the NFL single-game rushing record is Adrian Peterson’s 296 yards. Cook would need to break the NFL record by 67 yards Sunday to catch Allen. Welcome back to Superhuman, Chef. ______________________________________________________________________ Two weeks into this thing, we have already crossed a couple of names out, moved a few numbers around, and watched at least one entry jump from Superhuman to the record book. Now we get another Sunday to see what needs ink, what stays in pencil, and what we’ll have to do the math on again next week. At this rate, we might be doing a lot more erasing before the season is over.

full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Devin Lloyd #55 and Jean Phillips #5 of the Carolina Panthers react to a sack during an NFL football game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images Things seem to be looking up for the Carolina Panthers and quarterback Bryce Young. One dominant defensive performance and two excellent offensives ones have given us more good football to start a season than we have seen in years. This week’s opponents, the Cleveland Browns, are a similarly long suffering team who may have a shot at relevancy this year. When I say similarly long suffering, I mean they are the fourth and third losingest teams in the NFL over the ten seasons prior to this one. They may not be the Jets, but the Browns have the reputation of a team you’re supposed to beat if you’re supposed to be any good at football. FanDuel agrees, holding the Panthers as -2.5 favorites over the Browns. That spread has held steady since odds opened a week ago. Our staff are a little more bullish, predicting an average 10.6 point victory for the Panthers. That’s probably overkill, but it feels good to see people being positive again so we’re going to let it go for now. Staff predictions for Week 3 Walker Clement Panthers 31, Browns 24 – Devin Lloyd would have kept the Browns from scoring this much, but Young still proves to be in command of the better offense. Jonathan DeLong Panthers 31, Browns 14 – I kinda believe the Panthers are actually good, or at least good enough to handle teams that are supposed to be as bad as the Browns. Brian Beversluis Panthers 13, Browns 6 – Panthers win a defensive slugfest. Daniel Belton Panthers 24, Browns 13 – Bryce Young and the offense come back down to Earth a bit, but the defense holds against another subpar quarterback. Eric Buchanan Panthers 24, Browns 13 – With back-to-back road games where the opposing QB gets booed off the field, the Panthers score 14 points off turnovers to seal the win.

title: Panthers Injury Report & Transactions – Week 3
summary: The Carolina Panthers front office is busy throughout the season with transactions, roster moves, and injury updates. Here’s what’s happening at Mint Street this week. Injuries As the Panthers look to go 2-1 on the season as they prepare to face the Cleveland Browns, health is going to play a major factor. Here’s the summary […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - AUGUST 28: Isaiah Simmons #27 of the Carolina Panthers looks on before a preseason game against the Houston Texans at Bank of America Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers front office is busy throughout the season with transactions, roster moves, and injury updates. Here’s what’s happening at Mint Street this week. Injuries As the Panthers look to go 2-1 on the season as they prepare to face the Cleveland Browns, health is going to play a major factor. Here’s the summary for Sunday: Out: Linebacker Devin Lloyd, linebacker Claudin Cherelus, safety Nick Scott Questionable: Wide receivers Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette Now, the good news on Coker and Legette is they were both limited participants in Friday’s practice. Here’s to hoping both of the Panthers’ young wide receivers can see the field on Sunday. But the three defensive players who are out for Sunday is going to make things very, very hard on that side of the ball. Losing Devin Lloyd, in particular, is a massive loss. Transactions The Panthers have been active on the transactions front this week. Here are the most noteworthy moves. Placed running back Jonathon Brooks on Injured Reserve The injury-prone young running back just can’t catch a break when it comes to his health. The 2024 second round pick will miss at least six weeks after having surgery to repair a core muscle. He has appeared in just five games over three seasons. Signed safety Isaiah Simmons to the active roster from the practice squad Originally the No. 8 overall pick in the 2020 draft, he spent his first three seasons with the Arizona Cardinals and racked up 258 tackles, 7.5 sacks, seven forced fumbles, and four interceptions. But Simmons was a “tweener” and when the Cardinals hired a new coaching staff, they didn’t view him as a fit at either linebacker or safety. He was traded to the New York Giants in 2023 and had 71 tackles over two seasons as an occasional fill-in starter. Last year he was signed to the Panthers practice squad then appeared in five games for Carolina in 2025 with two tackles. He played one defensive snap and 87 on special teams. He continues to yo-yo between the Panthers practice squad and active roster this year. In 2026 he has appeared in both of Carolina’s games, playing five defensive snaps and 49 on special teams. Signed wide receiver Ihmir Smith-Marsette to the practice squad Smith-Marsette’s name probably rings a bell for some Panthers fans. He spent the 2023 season in Carolina and was the team’s primary punt returner, averaging 8.7 yards per return and taking one to the house. He also contributed eight receptions for 51 yards plus eight carries for 74 yards and a touchdown. Smith-Marsette was a fifth-round pick by the Vikings in 2021 and has bounced around several teams. In 2024 he was the Giants’ punt returner and also returned 11 kickoffs, including taking one back for a touchdown. The Giants released him during final roster cuts in 2025 and he didn’t latch on with any other team last year. He gives the Panthers another potential option in the return game following the recent release of Jimmy Horn Jr. Signed linebacker Maema Njongmeta to the practice squad Njongmeta began his career in 2024 as an undrafted free agent with the Cincinnati Bengals and had 13 tackles and two fumble recoveries in 17 games, playing mostly special teams. Last year the Panthers claimed him off the Bengals’ practice squad and he appeared in 15 games for Carolina in 2025 with 10 tackles as a special teams mainstay. This year he was waived at final roster cuts, but the Panthers have now added him back to the practice squad.

title: Brian Answers: Bryce Young & Brad Idzik evolution, Bobby Okereke surprise, and more!
summary: Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! We got the Browns on deck on Sunday coming off a fantastic and complete win last week. The rose colored glasses are on, and hopefully don’t drop off any time soon. So I’m going to answer all of your […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 21: Offensive coordinator Brad Idzik of the Carolina Panthers takes the field prior to the preseason game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Field on August 21, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! We got the Browns on deck on Sunday coming off a fantastic and complete win last week. The rose colored glasses are on, and hopefully don’t drop off any time soon. So I’m going to answer all of your questions from the week, let’s dive right in! Forager: Continuing with the optimism and believing the Panthers have their franchise quarterback (I’ll let you pick if it’s Bryce or Haynes :-)), and that they will be picking 32nd in next year’s draft, what position or positions would be on the table for that pick? Seeing the success Waller is having, maybe a pass-catching TE? Possibly an OG for salary cap concerns? Another edge rusher because injuries seem to love this position? Its hard to say at this point, but the Panthers definitely seem to prioritize the trenches on both sides of the ball. Depending on where they pick, a center or a guard would make a lot of sense. I can’t imagine they’ll hang on to both Robert Hunt and Damien Lewis as their cap hits get larger. They could again aim for another tackle since Taylor Moton, Ikem Ekwonu, and Rasheed Walker could all be out the door next off-season depending on circumstance. EDGE rusher is always a thought since this defense tends to rotate them in quite often. I could even see an interior linebacker as a longer term answer to pair with Devin Lloyd. Bobby Okereke has been playing well, but I think he’s more of a stop gap option for the team. Brice Guild: Brian, I know all the talk is about the play of Lloyd and he has been fun to watch but my biggest surprise has been Okereke. He seems faster and more versatile then I expected. He seems to already, in this new to him defense, playing quick and effective. Is it just a good scheme match that is allowing him to play faster then last year? What is your expectations for the development of the chemistry between Lloyd and him and their ceiling together as a interior LB pairing. I think Okereke is definitely a good scheme fit for what Carolina wants out of their interior linebackers, guys who can aggressively pursue the rush and maintain integrity in zone coverage schemes in the pass. I think they’ve developed relatively good chemistry but we’ve also seen both sides of the extremes as far as offenses they’ve faced are concerned. The Bears blew up this defense and the Falcons could barely move the ball without hurting themselves. Let’s see what it looks like in 4-5 weeks for a better answer. TXPanther: The Panthers hiring Darrell Bevell as associate HC/offensive specialist flew under the radar for most of us… could he be the answer to why the offense looks to have taken a step? I absolutely think it helped quite a bit. Between hiring the guy that Dave Canales and Brad Idzik cut their teeth under in Seattle, and Dave Canales handing the reigns off to Idzik with Bevell there to support him, I could totally see Bevell being a bigger reason than people realize in this offense being so effective all of a sudden. Both Canales and Idzik call plays that are likely largely based on what they learned during their time serving underneath him. WanderingJanusz: Is Nic Scourton the Kelvin Benjamin of 2026? I’m not ready to award this team with the energy of the 2015 Panthers just two weeks into the season. They are 1-1, so they’d have to win every game left in the regular season to match that energy. That said, it is interesting how Ejiro Evero is deploying his defense now that the pass rush isn’t going to passively generate pressure like they would have (in theory) with a fully healthy Scourton in the rotation. He blitzed a lot last week. @WTMealey: Amongst their peers who would rank higher BY vs QBs Canales vs HCs DM vs GMs Idzik vs OCs Meaning if Bryce is top 15 QB but DM is top 5 GM he ranks higher I would say Dan Morgan vs General Managers, basically because he has two whole offseasons under his belt where many pundits said it was some of the best drafting and maneuvering in free agency they had seen. Right now, Canales, Bryce Young, and Idzik are all kind of starting on new footing. So I’m going with Dan Morgan. Gunnercrf: How about that lead block by Moehrig on that pick six?! That was so hype he pancaked the guy so bad at the endzone he woke up in a Denny’s. Love seeing defensive players lead blocking for their teammates. While Tre’Von Moehrig isn’t a traditional safety by any means, he absolutely brings the physicality on just about every play he can. I very much enjoy watching him play. Kind of reminds me of Chris Harris with how he hits at times. SmoothC: How different would the ATL game be if they had a QB above the level of a moldy pumpkin? The defense still allowed 160 yards rushing. Taking your starters out in the 4th quarter during a blowout win doesn’t help the rushing numbers in a vacuum. They very much held the Falcons and especially Bijan Robinson in check when it mattered. SnarkyComet: Brian, curious on your take of a segment on Rich Eisen’s Overreaction Monday (On a Tuesday) this week where it was proposed that Bryce could wind up in the top 5 passers in the NFL this season. Eisen quickly said it wasn’t an overreaction and that he’s been playing great, but he wants to see how Bryce will do against this Browns defense. Crazy talk or is there something there? Based on two games worth of information to digest, no it isn’t crazy. Is it objectively an overreaction? Yes, I would say so. Carolina has a lot of good teams on their schedule this season and much better defenses ahead. Combine that with the general wear and tear of the long NFL season likely causing some important starters to miss at least some time, and teams getting more film on Brad Idzik’s tendencies as a play caller, and things could absolutely slow down. But Bryce has built a case so far that he could and should be in that conversation. JakeNCVA: At least twice this summer (once by me), you were asked if we expected the playcalling to be much different under Idzik than it was under Canales. And if I remember correctly the short answer was no, not really. We have seen the offense be better so far than it was most of the time last season. Well to be more precise, we have seen the passing game be better. Some people are attributing this to Idzik calling for more passes down the field. But that would mean that last season Canales called pass plays that were designed dump offs at the LOS at least half of the time while still sending receivers downfield. Through two games the Panthers offense is averaging almost 40 drop backs at game to around 20 running plays. Yes there have been increased targets to the tight ends in both games – something I imagine Canales and Idzik planned on doing in the offseason. As some of your CSR counterparts have said — it appears the game has slowed down for Bryce. Canales said “Bryce has taken advantage of the looks he has gotten”. Is it really the play calling or more like both Bryce Young and the receivers have both improved this season. I’ll be happy to get my receipts for not being correct necessarily in my prediction. However, I do think its a combination of Brad Idzik encouraging more aggression and Bryce Young simply being way more comfortable and confident. They were running similar down field concepts in 2025, and sometimes Bryce just didn’t throw them and elected to play it safe. But by the same token, I don’t know how much Canales was gearing him towards playing it more safe than letting it rip. We certainly saw Bryce let it rip at times in 2025, but he’s been really dealing the ball. I almost feel like we’re seeing an evolution of Canales’s game plans with some higher urgency to score…
author: Brian Beversluis

title: Panthers vs Browns: Matchups to watch
summary: The Carolina Panthers bounced back from a big home loss to the Chicago Bears at home to notch a big win over the Atlanta Falcons on the road. They swept the matchups we highlighted in this space last week, particularly with the linebackers coming to play against Bijan Robinson (even though Robinson did manage a […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 29: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns reacts in the third quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on September 29, 2024 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers bounced back from a big home loss to the Chicago Bears at home to notch a big win over the Atlanta Falcons on the road. They swept the matchups we highlighted in this space last week, particularly with the linebackers coming to play against Bijan Robinson (even though Robinson did manage a decent amount of rushing yards). Winning all the key matchups like that is an easy way to beat your opponent be 31 points. The Panthers will try to get a similar result in another road game, this time against the Cleveland Browns. Jaelan Phillips vs Tytus Howard The Browns traded for Howard in the offseason to try to solidify a leaky offensive line. He hasn’t provided a great return on that investment yet. The Browns as a team have yielded seven sacks through two weeks, and all but one of them has come from an edge rusher (shoutout former Panther A’Shawn Robinson for the other). A fair amount of that is on DeShaun Watson for holding the ball too long, but still, it’s an opportunity for Phillips to make it three straight games with a sack to start his tenure in Carolina. Howard has had some struggles in pass protection, so it’s a matchup the Panthers will be looking for Phillips to win. Howard has been decent in the run game, but he’s been just about the only Browns lineman that can boast that, and if Phillips can hold up there, the front should be able to keep the Browns woeful run game in check. Jaycee Horn/Mike Jackson vs Denzel Boston The safeties may have a role to play here as well, but the corners will get the bulk of the responsibility for covering the Browns rookie wide receiver. Boston has caught touchdown passes of over 40 yards in each of the first two games of the season. The Browns have not been good from play to play and drive to drive, so it’s paramount that the Panthers don’t let them off the hook with any big plays over the top. Now that it’s worked a couple of times, Watson will surely be hunting more deep looks to Boston in this one. Panthers interior offensive line vs Mason Graham The Browns have four sacks through two games. Two are from Mason Graham, and the other two are from safeties Grant Delpit and Ronnie Hickman. The rest of the Browns pass rush has been underwhelming so far (though there’s always a chance that Jared Verse wakes up). Based on the first two weeks, if the interior can hold up against Graham any blitzers from the secondary, the offensive line should be able to give Bryce Young time to find his targets. Cleveland Browns fans vs DeShaun Watson Browns fans have made it no secret that they’re not happy about their controversial quarterback getting paid tens of millions dollars per year to barely play and then play poorly when he does play. And Watson has not been shy about his frustration with people who are unhappy that he’s been a terrible quarterback while also allegedly being a terrible person. Shame on them, right? Well this will be Watson’s first regular season game in front of the home crowd. The Browns are coming off a win, and Watson played reasonably well in that win. It’ll be interesting to see if Browns fans will send more vitriol his way or if one decent performance in a win is enough to call off the dogs for the time being. Either way, if the Panthers defense can jump on Watson early and cause some poor offensive possessions, it’s very likely the crowd is going to turn on the home team and create a lot of strife.

title: Chicago Bears Week 3 Flashbacks: Minnesota Miracle, Windy City Flyer, and More
summary: It’s week 3, and as always, we have some hallmark games from the past to uncover! 1.) 1985, Bears @ Vikings: McMahon’s Miracle in Minny The 1985 Bears season is filled with memorable moments, but one of the first came on a Thursday night in Minnesota. Jim McMahon was dealing with back spasms and an […]
full_text: CHICAGO - SEPTEMBER 27: Devin Hester #23 of the Chicago Bears returns a punt 62-yards for a touchdown in the fourth quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Soldier Field on September 27, 2010 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Jonathan Daniel/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s week 3, and as always, we have some hallmark games from the past to uncover! 1.) 1985, Bears @ Vikings: McMahon’s Miracle in Minny The 1985 Bears season is filled with memorable moments, but one of the first came on a Thursday night in Minnesota. Jim McMahon was dealing with back spasms and an infection in his right leg, leaving Steve Fuller to start with Chicago looking to improve to 3-0. The offense struggled without McMahon, and midway through the third quarter the Bears found themselves trailing 17-9. Mike Ditka finally turned to his injured quarterback. McMahon’s first pass went 70 yards for a touchdown to Willie Gault. His second went 25 yards to Dennis McKinnon for another score. Seven pass attempts into his night, McMahon connected with McKinnon again for a 43-yard touchdown. Just like that, a 17-9 deficit had become a 30-17 Bears lead. McMahon finished 8-of-15 for 236 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, while Gault recorded 146 receiving yards and McKinnon added 133 yards and two scores. Chicago held on for a 33-24 win. The victory moved the Bears to 3-0 on their way to a 15-1 season and, eventually, a dominant run through the playoffs and a Super Bowl XX championship. Before all of that, though, an injured Jim McMahon came off the bench and completely flipped a game in a matter of minutes. 2.) 2010, Bears vs. Packers: Devin Hester is still ridiculous By 2010, the NFL had learned a pretty simple lesson when it came to Devin Hester. Don’t kick him the football. Hester entered Chicago’s Monday Night Football matchup with Green Bay without a return touchdown in nearly three years. With both teams sitting at 2-0, the Packers built a 10-0 lead before Jay Cutler found Greg Olsen late in the first half to get Chicago back into the game. The Bears still trailed 10-7 entering the fourth quarter. Then Hester finally broke through. He fielded a punt and raced 62 yards for a touchdown, giving Chicago its first lead of the night and recording his first return score since 2007. Green Bay answered and retook the lead, but Robbie Gould tied the game at 17 before the Bears defense came up with one more opportunity. Brian Urlacher stripped James Jones late in the fourth quarter, with Tim Jennings recovering the fumble in Green Bay territory. Gould eventually drilled a 19-yard field goal with four seconds remaining to give Chicago a 20-17 victory. The Packers did plenty to hurt themselves, committing a franchise-record 18 penalties for 152 yards, but the lasting image from the night was Hester looking like the most dangerous return man in football once again. Chicago improved to 3-0 and eventually finished the season 11-5, winning the NFC North and reaching the NFC Championship Game. For one night at Soldier Field, the formula was pretty simple. Give Devin Hester the football and see what happens. 3.) 2013, Bears @ Steelers: The defense takes over For years, Chicago’s defense had built its identity around one thing. Taking the football away. That trend continued into Marc Trestman’s first season as head coach, and Week 3 against the Steelers was one of the best examples. The Bears jumped out to a 17-0 lead, helped by a D.J. Williams strip-sack that set up an early touchdown. Then the defense started scoring points of its own. Major Wright intercepted Ben Roethlisberger and returned it 38 yards for a touchdown, giving Chicago a 24-3 advantage. Pittsburgh battled all the way back, eventually cutting the lead to 27-23 in the fourth quarter behind 406 passing yards from Roethlisberger and 196 receiving yards from Antonio Brown. Chicago finally answered with a Jay Cutler touchdown pass to Earl Bennett. 𝐒𝐞𝐩𝐭𝐞𝐦𝐛𝐞𝐫 𝟐𝟐, 𝟐𝟎𝟏𝟑 The Bears put up 𝐅𝐎𝐑𝐓𝐘 against the Steelers in Pittsburgh on SNF! @JayHasTweets with the truck stick 😤 pic.twitter.com/kbZ5lIB2SV — This Day in Chicago Sports (@ChiSportsDay) September 22, 2021 Then the defense put the game away. Lance Briggs knocked the ball free while sacking Roethlisberger, and Julius Peppers picked it up and rumbled 42 yards for another Bears defensive touchdown. Chicago left Pittsburgh with a 40-23 victory and a 3-0 record. The final numbers tell the story. Pittsburgh outgained the Bears 459-258, but Chicago forced five turnovers, committed none and scored 23 points off Pittsburgh giveaways. It may not have been the cleanest win, but it was a familiar formula for Bears fans. Gary Baugher Jr. is a second year contributor to WCG, bringing football insight backed by over 16 years of experience in organized football and more than 30 years as a passionate fan of the game. You can follow him on Twitter at @iamcogs .
