title: Bears vs. Eagles: Keys for a Chicago victory
summary: The Chicago Bears make their first primetime appearance of the season this week against the Philadelphia Eagles. Unfortunately, they will likely be starting their third-string quarterback and they’re home underdogs. Things aren’t looking great for the Bears, but they still have a lot going for them, too. Case Keenum might be the most capable third-stringer […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Kyle Monangai #25 of the Chicago Bears runs the ball against the Minnesota Vikings during the third quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears make their first primetime appearance of the season this week against the Philadelphia Eagles. Unfortunately, they will likely be starting their third-string quarterback and they’re home underdogs. Things aren’t looking great for the Bears, but they still have a lot going for them, too. Case Keenum might be the most capable third-stringer in the league. They have a head coach who can scheme up points against anyone and with seemingly any personnel…as long as it isn’t raining. We rounded up some of our staff to get their keys for a Chicago Bears victory. Sam: Use the ground game and turn this into a grind-it-out game. Case Keenum can be a good game manager, play within the offense and keep the ball out of harm’s way. If the defense gives him a big play opportunity, he should be able to take it. Hopefully, some of the defensive play we saw against Minnesota can carry over. Contiaining the Eagles’ run game is going to be key, but so is shutting down Devonta Smith. Donald: Keys to the game: run, run, and run some more. Assuming it is Keenum at QB, nothing would take pressure off of him like a successful run game. That keyed the Bears victory over the Eagles last year and it can do it again. Second, limit turnovers. Case needs to play within himself. Take the safe play and lean on the run game. On defense, contain Hurts. He doesn’t run as much as he used to but it is still a big factor for the Eagles in sustaining drives. And finally, the Bears have to stop the run. Keeping Saquon off the stat sheet is the best path to securing a W. Lester: Regardless of the QB, the Bears should run the ball 30+ times this week, and they need to stick with the hot hand. I’d expect the backs to get plenty of use in the passing game too, whether that be in the flat, of by leaking though the line of scrimmage over the middle. Gary: POUND. THE. ROCK. We need to see a repeat performance from last season if we want to have the best chance of winning. Establishing the run game will allow whoever is under center to take advantage of play-action when needed for easy underneath completions. Defensively we have to maintain deep discipline, make the Eagles work for it through the ground game and short level passing. Josh: The last time the Bears beat the Eagles, it was behind the strength of the running game. That needs to hold up, while the defense needs to limit Hurts. What do you think it will take for the Bears to beat the Eagles on Monday?

title: Eagles at Bears Q&A: Can Ben Johnson best Vic Fangio?
summary: The Chicago Bears welcome the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football for the first of several Chicago Bears primetime games in 2026. The Bears will almost certainly be without star quarterback Caleb Williams, and there isn’t even certainty whether it will be Tyson Bagent (concussion) or Case Keenum starting for the Bears on Monday. The […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 28: Cole Kmet #85 of the Chicago Bears celebrates after scoring a 28 yard touchdown against Reed Blankenship #32 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the fourth quarter in the game at Lincoln Financial Field on November 28, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears welcome the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football for the first of several Chicago Bears primetime games in 2026. The Bears will almost certainly be without star quarterback Caleb Williams, and there isn’t even certainty whether it will be Tyson Bagent (concussion) or Case Keenum starting for the Bears on Monday. The Bears have several things in flux, but what situation are the 2-0 Philadelphia Eagles in? To find out more about their opponent, we sat down with Brandon Gowton from Bleeding Green Nation, SB Nation’s Eagles site, to find out a little bit more about what the Bears are going up against on Monday. Here’s that conversation: 1. The Eagles definitely didn’t feel like the Eagles as the season concluded last year, and while they are 2-0 this year, it’s by a combined 6 points by 2 of the worst teams in the league. Are the Eagles back, or is this still a team that’s not quite firing on all cylinders? It’s weird because, while you’re right to point out that the overall results haven’t been overly impressive, Jalen Hurts is playing some of the best football of his career. And it’s always easier to feel optimistic about your favorite team’s outlook when the quarterback is looking good. The offense as a whole has been uneven. They’ve been really bad on early downs, which is a reflection of their struggles to run the ball efficiently. The offensive line isn’t what it used to be when Saquon Barkley ran all over the NFL in 2024. Despite these struggles, the Eagles have thus far insisted on running into a brick wall over and over, which has created long third downs. Fortunately, Hurts has been able to bail the offense out in these situations. He’s really hard to carry the offense. But that’s obviously not a sustainable approach over the course of the season. Vic Fangio’s defense hasn’t been quite as good as expected yet. It’s a high bar to clear based on the success we’ve seen over the past two seasons. Perhaps it’ll take a little more time for them to fully click. I’m still bullish about their outlook. All told, they’ve looked like an average team so far. But, given their sustained success over an extended period of time, they deserve more benefit of the doubt than some other teams. It’s reasonable to believe that they can play better. 2. I’m going to go back to last year because they are my questions, and you have to answer them. The Black Friday game last year, Bears fans felt like that was the Bears coming-out party where they officially announced to the league that they are for real. But the commentary on that game, at least nationally, was a lot of “The Eagles stink.” It certainly felt like that was the game where the Eagles weren’t the same anymore at that point. Do you feel that was the Bears doing or an Eagles implosion? I’m a big “more than one thing can be true” guy. The Bears deserve a lot of credit for coming into Philly and bullying the Birds. They pushed this defense around and ran all over them to a tune of 281 yards on the ground. It wasn’t just a matter of the Eagles falling off. Fangio’s defense allowed just 107.2 rushing yards per game over the next six weeks after facing Chicago. I do think it’s fair to point out that Jalen Carter was shut down for a three-game stint due to a shoulder procedure after having an uncharacteristically bad game against the Bears. But he could very well be less than 100% for this week’s game since he’s now playing with a cast on his hand. Last year’s loss to the Bears is something I definitely expect Eagles coaches and players to have on their minds ahead of Monday night’s game. I find it hard to believe Fangio isn’t showing this year’s team film from that game and calling out their toughness. I think the Eagles are going to want to wash the bad taste out of their mouth and put forth a stronger effort this time around. 3. Where are Eagles fans with Jalen Hurts? This is a Super Bowl-winning quarterback, but from afar, it doesn’t seem like he’s winning any popularity contests in Philadelphia. What’s the confidence level in Hurts leading this team moving forward? Hard not to feel really encouraged about Hurts’ outlook after the first two weeks of this season. He’s been their best player so far. As noted above, he’s really had to bail out an offense that’s been running the ball way too often for how bad they are at it. It’s not fair for the Eagles to continue to expect Hurts to do the heavy lifting in this regard. They need to set up better for success. But it’s been nice to see that he’s been able to carry the team while they’ve needed him to do it. If Hurts continues on his current trajectory, he’ll easily earn a new contract extension after this season (if not sooner). 4. I have to ask about the Chicago Bears fan-favorite defensive coordinator, Vic Fangio. How has the Eagles defense looked so far this year? Who is a player or two that you think could be a thorn in Ben Johnson’s side on Monday? The Eagles’ defense hasn’t lived up to lofty expectations thus far. Entering the season, we were talking about this being one of the very best units in the NFL, if not THE best. This isn’t to suggest the defense has been bad. The Eagles have allowed fewer than 300 yards in each of their first two games for the first time since 1995. But they’ve yet to come up with a takeaway, and they haven’t been quite as dominant as expected. The defensive line in particular needs to play better. Jalen Carter has made some important plays through two games, but he hasn’t been the total game wrecker the Eagles paid him to be. It doesn’t help that he has to play with a cast on his hand after getting injured in Week 1. The edge rushers also really need to come alive. Through two games, the Eagles are the NFL’s slowest team when it comes to generating pressure on a given play. Jalen Hurts showed a lot of promise this summer, but the hype hasn’t fully translated over to the regular season games yet. Nolan Smith has done some nice things but hasn’t popped in a major way. The Eagles might get Jonathan Greenard, who I imagine Bears fans are familiar with from his time with the Vikings, back for Monday’s game. That would be big. But Fangio said he’s nowhere near ready to play the number of snaps the Eagles would normally rely on him for. I do think there’s hope for his pass rush. Perhaps I’m too forgiving, but I do think there have been some unusual circumstances for them through two games. They were forced to do more of a mush rush in Week 1 to keep Jayden Daniels contained, which they accomplished. Then they played in extremely hot conditions in Week 2, with the heat index on the Titans’ turf field reaching temperatures of over 150 degrees! Assuming Case Keenum is starting for the Bears on Monday, I think the pass rush will be able to get after him more than they got after Daniels and Cam Ward. Oh, I wrote all of this and didn’t even directly answer the second part of your question. I’d keep an eye out for Riq Woolen. He’s off to a really good start this season, and he has the ability to make plays. I could see him coming up with a pick, especially as the Bears probably look to avoid throwing Quinyon Mitchell’s way. 5. The Eagles currently sit as a 4.5-point favorite. How do you see this one playing out on Monday night? The Eagles are 0-2 against the spread so far this season. I could see them failing to cover again as the Bears’ rushing attack keeps Chicago in it. But ultimately I think Keenum, who hasn’t even played since 2023, will have some struggles as a passer, assuming he gets the start. I expect Fangio’s defense to play well enough to get the job done. And I’m not…
author: Bill Zimmerman

title: Do you trust Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum more against the Eagles?
summary: The Chicago Bears have a big matchup on Monday Night Football, taking on the Philadelphia Eagles. If the Bears lose, they’ll fall below .500 for the first time in a year. It’s only game three, but obviously, everyone would like to see the Bears get back on track after a tough loss in week two […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 29: Case Keenum #11 of the Chicago Bears drops back to pass during the second half of the Week 3 preseason game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears have a big matchup on Monday Night Football, taking on the Philadelphia Eagles. If the Bears lose, they’ll fall below .500 for the first time in a year. It’s only game three, but obviously, everyone would like to see the Bears get back on track after a tough loss in week two against the Minnesota Vikings. Caleb Williams was knocked out of the game, and Ben Johnson has said that he is week-to-week, but almost everyone is certain that he will miss the Eagles game. If he does, that means it will either be Tyson Bagent, if he can clear concussion protocol, or Case Keenum, the veteran QB who has been mostly considered an assistant QB coach in a Bears uniform. Bagent has the youth; Keenum has the veteran experience (but is it too much experience, if you know what I mean). Who do you trust more against the Eagles: Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum? I think the easy answer without thinking would be Tyson Bagent. But this Eagles defense is led by the great Vic Fangio, and we know that Vic has the ability to put inexperienced QBs in a blender. Would the Bears be better off with Keenum, who happens to be 3-0 career against Fangio (albeit when he was much younger), who can read a defense as well as anybody in the league and make snap decisions with the football? Answer: This one, for me, is really difficult to answer. I think the idea of Keenum makes a ton of sense to go up against the Eagles and Fangio. He is a statue back there, but he can stand and deliver. The question is, who is Case Keenum at this point? In the preseason, Keenum was outstanding (as he was in the 2025 preseason as well). Keenum was 25 of 40 for 354 yards, 2 TDs, and 0 INTs. That’s good enough for a 107.7 rating. However, we have to take into account that he was going up against 3rd-stringers. Keenum hasn’t thrown a ball in the regular season since 2023, and in his final four years where he played (2020-2023), the numbers were poor. He threw just 140 attempts over those 4 years and had a yards-per-attempt average under 6. He also had as many INTs as TDs (4 each). So we have to ask ourselves: with Keenum, are we getting the guy who can operate Ben Johnson’s system brilliantly in the preseason, or are we getting the washed QB that looked terrible in his last few regular-season games? While I’ve been leaning towards Keenum for most of this week, I think, in the end, Bagent, if he can play, makes more sense. Bagent also operates Johnson’s system well in the preseason, and his arrow is pointing up, not down. If it’s Keenum, I don’t think it’s a huge difference. If we ranked QBs on a scale of 1 to 10 to face Philly and Caleb is a 10, I think Bagent is a 6 and Keenum is a 5. I think the way Garrett Bradbury is playing with those Eagles DTs, I would rather have a more mobile QB in Bagent because I think the Bears will give up a little pressure. So while I will have almost as much confidence in Keenum as I would with Bagent, I think I lean just a little bit on the Bagent side. What do you say, Bears fans? Would you rather see Bagent or Keenum out there against the Eagles? Sound off in the comments section!
author: Bill Zimmerman

title: Chicago Bears Big Play Breakdowns from Week 2
summary: Week 2 brought 8 more explosive plays. Wait – eight?! That can’t be right; let me go back and…yeah, eight. It’s honestly unbelievable the Chicago Bears didn’t win this one, but a fumble at the goal line and the Williams injury, combined with the constant rain, conspired to leave the Bears with only three points […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Kyle Monangai #25 of the Chicago Bears runs with the ball during the third quarter of the game against the Minnesota Vikings at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 2 brought 8 more explosive plays. Wait – eight?! That can’t be right; let me go back and…yeah, eight. It’s honestly unbelievable the Chicago Bears didn’t win this one, but a fumble at the goal line and the Williams injury, combined with the constant rain, conspired to leave the Bears with only three points for their efforts. However, there was still some good stuff, particularly in the run game, as this 2026 Bears squad starts to figure out who they are going to be this year. Explosive Play 2.1 – Q1 10:26, 2nd and 3 from the Chicago 38. Caleb Williams aborted snap, recovered at Chicago 36 by Williams, run up the middle for 17 yards. Obviously an incredibly creative play call by Johnson to put the ball on the ground and just have Caleb run up the middle for an explosive play… Okay, maybe we should’ve known this one was going to be weird. Busted play, quarterback is talented enough to make it a chunk gain instead of a disaster. Caleb Williams drops the snap, recovers, and picks up 17 yards MINvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/awjnArPfjv — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 Explosive Play 2.2 – Q3 14:50, 2nd and 10 from the Chicago 35. D’Andre Swift off left tackle for 12 yards. The Bears come out in 12 personnel with Kmet attached on the right and Loveland attached on the left side of the line. Rome and Kalif Raymond line up stacked to the left of Loveland. At the snap, Raymond drags across to the right in what looks like a potential play action pass dump off option for a future play. Braxton and Loveland do enough to stalemate their defender and Thuney works up to the second level to get a hat on his assignment. Swift finds the space off the left tackle (hat tip to Rome for hanging with his defender) and with a little stutter step makes the safety miss in the hole, gaining another 6-7 before running out of bounds. Well blocked but Swift’s missed tackle takes it from a nice run to set up a third and short to a fresh set of downs. Explosive Play 2.3 – Q3 14:10, 2nd and 10 from the Chicago 47. Caleb Williams scrambles up the middle for 11 yards. It goes down as an explosive play as it is a run play once Caleb decides to tuck it and go. This was his second of three explosive runs on the day and the first off a scramble. A good decision to go after working through his progression and he knew where the sticks were to keep this drive going early in the third by taking contact and pushing through for the first. It’s the second explosive run of the series. Explosive Play 2.4 – Q3 13:28, 1st and 10 from the Minnesota 42. Kyle Monangai off right end for 15 yard gain. The third explosive run of the drive and the first for Monangai. This is one of those runs where you look back and think…why did he not have 30 carries in this one? The Bears use 12 personnel here, with both Loveland and Kmet on the right hand side of the line with Odunze split out wide. Monangai runs through contact trying to poke out the ball around the line of scrimmage and bursts through the hole before dragging the corner for about six additional yards and another set of downs. Explosive Play 2.5 – Q3 12:14, 2nd and 6 from the Minnesota 23. Kyle Monangai off right guard for 12 yards. The fourth explosive run on the drive and the second for Monangai. Just two plays after the 15 yarder, the Bears use Cole Kmet as a full back and line up in the I-formation. Blocking action moves to the right with Kmet filling the edge defender on the left. Monangai starts the action to the right and makes a cut back to the middle of the field. He’s untouched for ten yards before falling forward for a couple extra. Well blocked here by the Bears. Unbelievably, the four explosive runs on the same drive would not lead to points as D’Andre Swift would fumble at the one a few plays later. Explosive Play 2.6 – Q3 5:19, 3rd and 6 from the Chicago 17. Caleb Williams scrambles off left end for 10 yards. It’s not worth spending a ton of time breaking down scrambles but again I think this is an aspect of Caleb’s game that we can appreciate him flexing when needed. The concern with the hamstring injury going forward is if he’ll feel comfortable running and if so, will he be able to shift into high gear. Anyway, love the spin move here and my mind automatically added a Chris Berman sound effect when he did it. First down with a spin 👀 MINvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/yL3Bljcwxk — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 Explosive Play 2.7 – Q4 11:43, 3rd and 7 from the Chicago 36. Caleb Williams passes short left to D’Andre Swift for 32 yards. A well-timed screen on 3rd down here. It’s a nice play design with a WR screen set up on the right side, where Caleb gives a pump fake, before coming back to Swift on the left side. Swift has a couple of blockers who don’t really impact the play here. He is able to make the first defender miss at the sticks before breaking away from a second defender who goes for the strip. He’s not quite able to run away from the third defender before being taken down for a monster gain. The play design earned the first but Swift again took it from a nice play to an explosive. Big catch-and-run for D'Andre Swift! MINvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2Pcqvzgkg3 — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 Explosive Play 2.8 – Q4 0:38, 2nd and 10 from the Minnesota 41. Tyson Bagent completes pass deep right to Rome Odunze for 21 yards. This is a nice route from Rome in the waning seconds of the game. Bagent is a little late getting this one out and the velocity of the pass allows the defender to recover. Rome does a nice job bringing in the football against his body, fighting through the contact, and getting out of bounds to stop the clock. We know that Bagent’s arm strength isn’t going to be able to deliver a ball at pace in this situation so he’ll need to deliver that one in the future a touch quicker. Nice play overall from Rome knowing the situation and fighting to move forward to stop the clock. A running clock there would’ve shorted the Bears multiple shots to the end zone. 2026 Explosive Play Count: D’Andre Swift 4, Kyle Monangai 4, Caleb Williams 4, Rome Odunze 2, and one each for Kalif Raymond, Luther Burden, and Cole Kmet. What was your favorite explosive play from the opener? There’s something beautiful about Kyle Monangai dragging defenders – he’s got my vote for the week.

title: Dexter Lawrence is adding, among many things, personality to the Bengals defense
summary: Zac Taylor is in a unique position. He’s the head coach of the Bengals and their offensive play-caller. In his position, Taylor, like a CEO, is also in charge of managing this team’s personalities. Most of those personalities have been on offense in Taylor’s tenure. Now, the defense has some. Not only is the Bengals’ […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - SEPTEMBER 20: Cornerback Dax Hill #23 of the Cincinnati Bengals and defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II #97 of the Cincinnati Bengals have fun during warmups before the NFL football game between the Houston Texans and Cincinnati Bengals on September 20, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Zac Taylor is in a unique position. He’s the head coach of the Bengals and their offensive play-caller. In his position, Taylor, like a CEO, is also in charge of managing this team’s personalities. Most of those personalities have been on offense in Taylor’s tenure. Now, the defense has some. Not only is the Bengals’ defense revived. It has personality , especially up front and with Dexter Lawrence. Lawrence is the tone-setter of the Bengals’ defense. That comes in the form of on-field production, but it also comes with having a little fun on the field trash-talking. “He just loves it. I think he’s contributed to the personality of our defense,” Taylor said after Friday’s practice. “Not only are they talented and confident, and playing with this really good chemistry, but they’ve got a really big personality as a whole, and he’s obviously a big part of this, and that’s what’s fun.” Lawrence was mic’d up during the Bengals’ 20-6 win over the Houston Texans in Week 2. It was incredible to listen to, with Lawrence demonstrating elite trash-talking abilities. It’s something we haven’t really seen from a Bengals’ defense in quite some time. The S.W.A.T. Team had personality back in the 80s, but Bengals’ defenses since really haven’t it… until now. “With the mic’d up stuff, everybody gets to see kind of what we see from him, (defensive tackle) Jonathan Allen, and everybody kind of combining together,” Taylor said. “And it probably gets a couple of the other guys out of their shell a little bit.” Don’t be surprised if you see other mic’d-up segments and soundbites from the Bengals or NFL Films showcasing Lawrence and the Bengals’ defensive line trash-talking their opponents. The Bengals’ defensive line is getting a lot of attention. They have talented players, but they also have players with personalities.

title: Orlando Brown Jr. believes the 2026 Bengals are a Super Bowl team
summary: The expectations and pressure were at an all-time high for the Cincinnati Bengals entering the 2026 season after missing the playoffs for three straight years. full_text: CINCINNATI, CA - SEPTEMBER 14: Orlando Brown #75 of the Cincinnati Bengals stands on field prior to the first half of an NFL game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Paycor Stadium on September 14, 2025 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The expectations and pressure were at an all-time high for the Cincinnati Bengals entering the 2026 season after missing the playoffs for three straight years. Although it is still incredibly early, the Bengals’ revamped roster has shown up and executed at a winning level. The Bengals are 2-0 with a healthy Joe Burrow for the first time in the Zac Taylor era, and the defense has been lights out through the first two weeks. One of the biggest reasons for the early success is the new additions on the defensive side that are not only veterans but also Super Bowl champions. The front office brought in Boye Mafe and Bryan Cook, two guys that have won Super Bowls at their previous stops in the NFL. The Bengals also have another guy on the roster who has Super Bowl experience as well, and that is left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. Brown recently had an interview with Casino.org and shared that he believes this is a Super Bowl-caliber roster and a roster that is even better than the one he was a part of on the Chiefs. “To be honest, this is nothing like I’ve ever been a part of,” Brown said. “We are very unique in so many different ways when I look at our offense, defense, and special teams units. I’ve never been a part of anything like this.” As I said earlier in the article, the expectations are at an all-time high this season, and it is clear the players on the roster feel the exact same way.

title: Tee Higgins speaks out on celebration fine from NFL
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are off to a red-hot 2-0 start and will look to add a third win on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The defense has been lights out for the Bengals, but the offense has been slow to get fully going. Despite the offense not being up to par, the unit has done […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - SEPTEMBER 13: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins #5 reacts after a first down in a game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Cincinnati Bengals on September 13, 2026, at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Jeff Moreland/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals are off to a red-hot 2-0 start and will look to add a third win on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers . The defense has been lights out for the Bengals, but the offense has been slow to get fully going. Despite the offense not being up to par, the unit has done enough to win games, and that is all that matters. Tee Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase have done what they always do through the first two weeks, but they have been doing a celebration after each first down/touchdown that has caught the eyes of Bengals fans… Well, that celebration has officially come to an end after the two of them were fined by the NFL for nearly $90,000. Each fine is $14,926, so Higgins must now pay $59,704 total. Chase received two separate fines totaling $29,852, bringing the total fine for the star wideouts to $89,556. Higgins recently appeared on the Kay Adams Show and defended himself. “I’m a fan of WWE, the people’s elbow, and we just threw in a first down celebration with it,” Higgins explained. “Unfortunately, we did get the letter. Everybody on the internet is making it seem like something that it isn’t.” Chase also shared his thoughts on the fines during his weekly press conference. “I think this is where the superstars have to get in with the NFLPA and fight for our money. I can’t really do much about it. We could complain. I don’t even think we can tweet about it because we get fined for tweeting about it. So, it’s really like players have to keep their mouths shut and deal with it. But we’ve got to have a superstar in the NFLPA to do something about it. Help us along the way.” The celebration was fun for a few weeks, but Tee says they will have a new one for Sunday. Don't blame the NFL for Chase & Tee Higgins NFL fine…blame TWITTER! We gotta be better. pic.twitter.com/R3JvdegIAI — Kay Adams (@heykayadams) September 24, 2026

full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are set to kick off AFC North play in Week 3 against the Pittsburgh Steelers . Dexter Lawrence, Johnathan Allen, Boye Mafe, and Bryan Cook are a few of the new additions that have stepped in and made a jaw-dropping impact on a defense that was unwatchable in 2025. The Bengals defense has been lights out through the first two weeks, but all the new faces will be getting a taste of AFC North football for the first time on Sunday. Cook, who grew up in Mount Healthy and played college football at Cincinnati, was asked about the upcoming showdown with the Steelers, and he delivered one of my favorite quotes of all time from a Bengals player. “Being a fan, being a kid growing up, you hear the stories, you can see it on the field. Now, I’m actually in the fight. It’s a gift and an honor, but I’m ready to get to work and see it for myself. Since I was a kid, I’m from Cincy, and my jersey says Cincinnati on it. So every game is personal a little bit, but this game definitely has a little more juice to it,” said Cook. "My jersey says Cincinnati. So, every game is personal for me. But, this game definitely has more juice." Bryan Cook is pumped for his first game against the Steelers with Cincinnati on his chest. #Bengals @FOX19 pic.twitter.com/W7oGWRCEUE — Jeremy Rauch (@FOX19Jeremy) September 24, 2026 The former Bearcats standout is clearly the perfect culture fit for this locker room, and that quote alone should have every Bengals fan ready to run through a brick wall. The Bengals have the opportunity to start 3-0 on Sunday but will need to take care of business against one of their biggest rivals and a team that is searching for a big win.

title: 4 key matchups to watch for in Bengals vs. Steelers
summary: Round 1 of Bengals vs. Steelers is on deck this Sunday in the Steel City, so here are four key matchups to watch for if Cincinnati is going to pull out the victory for a 3-0 start. Dexter Lawrence vs. Spencer Anderson Lawrence has been feasting regardless of who he is going up against through […]
full_text: Round 1 of Bengals vs. Steelers is on deck this Sunday in the Steel City, so here are four key matchups to watch for if Cincinnati is going to pull out the victory for a 3-0 start. Dexter Lawrence vs. Spencer Anderson Lawrence has been feasting regardless of who he is going up against through the first two weeks of the season. On Sunday, he will be matched up at times against Steelers right guard Spencer Anderson. The Steelers will give Anderson plenty of help, as will all teams facing off against Sexy Dexy. Anderson has been a weakness through the first two weeks. So even when it is Jonathan Allen, TJ Slaton, Kris Jenkins Jr., or any other defensive tackle for the Bengals, Anderson will be having his hands full once again. According to PFF, Anderson has a 42.6 pass blocking grade through the first two games. He has been credited with allowing 4 pressures and 1 sack. With the Bengals defense coming off of a 41-pressure performance, this could be a long day for Spencer Anderson, or whoever the Steelers decide to play at right guard this week. Amarius Mims and Orlando Brown Jr. vs. TJ Watt, Alex Highsmith, Nick Herbig, and Jack Sawyer Amarius Mims has been one of the best offensive tackles through the first two weeks of the season. He has not been credited with allowing a pressure in his first two games, even after facing off against one of the best pass rush tandems in the league with Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter in Houston last week. Another tough test awaits him with TJ Watt. Watt has been one of the best pass rushers in the league over the last ten years. This year has been no different. Watt has accumulated 3.5 sacks through his first 2 games. While he’s a great player, I have the utmost faith that Amarius Mims can hold his own when facing Watt. Mims played really well against Watt overall during last season, and looks even better this year. Watt has been moving around the defense more to start the season, so Orlando Brown Jr. will also be tasked with facing off against Watt. Orlando Brown Jr. allowed three sacks during the week two game against Houston. They will need a better performance when Brown Jr. is going up against TJ Watt than what we saw when he was tasked with facing Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter. The other edge rushers for the Steelers are no slouches either, with Alex Highsmith, Nick Herbig, and Jack Sawyer all able to generate pressure at a high rate. Highsmith has 3 sacks of his own through the first two games of the season. Mims and Orlando Brown Jr. against the Steelers’ pass rushers will go a long way in determining the outcome of this one. Amarius Mims took a big jump last year in his second season with the Bengals. The potential is there for an All-Pro season in 2026. pic.twitter.com/vakbfmkAr5 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) July 21, 2026 Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins vs. Jamel Dean and Asante Samuel Jr. or Joey Porter Jr. Joey Porter Jr. has yet to play this season for the Pittsburgh Steelers at corner. He has been in a contract dispute with the organization, and Coach Mike McCarthy said he had a setback with a back injury in practice last week. Whatever the real issue is there, this is another week his status remains up in the air for playing. That puts even more emphasis on Jamel Dean and Asante Samuel Jr. to face off against Chase and Higgins on Sunday. Even if Porter Jr. plays, I am not sure he will be full-go. It also wouldn’t be surprising if this is another week he just doesn’t play at all. Tee Higgins had 5 catches for 95 yards during the week two victory in Houston. Chase added 7 receptions for 75 yards with two touchdowns on the day. Meanwhile, Dean gave up 4 receptions on 6 targets, or a 66.7% completion rate against New England. Samuel gave up 4 receptions on 5 targets, for an 80% completion rate against him. The Patriots were without their top receiver, AJ Brown, during the game, yet still pulled out a 20-3 victory over Pittsburgh. This could be a big week for the Bengals receivers in Pittsburgh. DK Metcalf vs. DJ Turner Metcalf has not had a hot start to his 2026 season. Metcalf has been targeted 19 times through two games, but has just 8 receptions for 67 yards, and has yet to find the end zone this year. The Bengals will be hoping to keep him in check again on Sunday. DJ Turner played Metcalf tough last year, and that was part of his breakout into becoming one of the top young corners in the league. Turner had an 81.9 coverage grade during week two against Houston. He was sticky in coverage with great physicality. What Turner hasn’t done yet this season is get an interception. He would love to end up with one similar to what he pulled off against Pittsburgh last season. Maybe even one that doesn’t have quite the difficulty level of ripping the ball out of his hands, while somehow staying in bounds with possession of the ball. That time DJ Turner just ripped the ball away from DK Metcalf 🔥 pic.twitter.com/ANdOLKYofn — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) July 30, 2026

title: Browns: Grinding on defense, running the ball, and booing the QB
summary: The Cleveland Browns calmed the storm surrounding the team with last week’s victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.  The defense stepped up when it mattered in the fourth quarter, stopping the Buccaneers on their final drive. The run game was still a mess – just 1.9 yards per carry – but quarterback Deshaun Watson made […]
full_text: (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns calmed the storm surrounding the team with last week’s victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The defense stepped up when it mattered in the fourth quarter, stopping the Buccaneers on their final drive. The run game was still a mess – just 1.9 yards per carry – but quarterback Deshaun Watson made up for it by not being a complete disaster, which has to be labeled as a positive. Speaking of Watson, he made good use of his playmakers, as 16 of his 24 completions went to Denzel Boston, Harold Fannin Jr., and KC Concepcion. That is a solid plan for a quarterback who, to use a once-unpopular phrase for a Cleveland quarterback, clearly has “diminishing skills” since arriving in town. Cleveland opens the home portion of its schedule on Sunday when they host the Carolina Panthers, who come to town with a surprisingly effective offense that is averaging 35.5 points a game with quarterback Bryce Young running the show. There is no such thing as an easy day at work for the Browns, especially if the defense can’t keep the Panthers out of the end zone, so here are a few takeaways from the coaches about the upcoming game. The grind is real on defense. Carolina is averaging 312.5 passing yards and has 10 pass plays of 20 or more yards, which is the second most in the league. Cleveland will counter with a defense that has not allowed a 300-yard passer in 47 consecutive games, but one that has also been burned by the big play (six completions of 20 yards or more) through the first two games. If the Browns are to contain Carolina’s offense, they need to keep grinding, according to defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg : “I think everybody’s got to have a foundation, right? And for us, our defensive foundation is heart, mind, fist. And I’ve talked about it, and the heart and the fist were there, and we made a commitment to constantly improving the mind, coaches and players. And when you can look in the mirror and say, I can do better, it’s week to week, whether you get your ass kicked or whether you have a win. “It’s about all of us working our asses off each week, grinding, making this Thursday better than last Thursday, making this meeting that we’re coming up to better than the last meeting, getting this game better than the last game. And it’s about our style of play and the level of execution. That’s the truth about the way this league goes. It’s such a marathon, and we’re in week three of that marathon right now, and our whole goal is to play better than we did last week and hopefully do enough to help the Browns win.” When will the run game take off? Cleveland averaged a workable four yards per carry against Jacksonville in Week 1 before bottoming out in Week 2 against the Buccaneers. Watson is the team’s leading rusher, which is completely unsustainable, while No. 1 running back Quinshon Judkins is averaging just 2.3 yards per carry. With nothing really working, offensive coordinator Travis Switzer said he is looking at every aspect of the run game for answers : “The first two weeks, we’re not where we want to be, so we’re looking at everything that goes into that, and everyone involved. I have to look at it schematically. Certainly, there was a play too, from the game the other day where I’m looking at it like, you know what, I didn’t put us in a great position there. And then we’re looking at just the execution of it by all parties, right, the blockers and the fundamentals and the things that we’re working at up there, the runners and just trusting their eyes and seeing it. But yeah, we’re looking at all parts of that. “But certainly, we’re going to have to run the ball into loaded boxes at times. If you want to be a dominant team and a good running team, you’re going to have to do that. So, yeah, there are different things schematically you can do, whether it’s different run schemes, whether it’s opening it up, whether it’s using the quarterback like we’ve been talking about, there’s different things you can do there, but we’re going to need to run the ball into those looks.” To boo or not to boo. That is the question. Sunday will mark Deshaun Watson’s first start in a regular-season game in front of the home fans since October 20, 2024, the day he suffered the first of two Achilles tendon injuries. There has been a lot of talk about how the home fans will greet Watson when he hits the field for the first offensive play, and how he will react to the response if it is a negative one. The surest way to avoid any unpleasantries, or at least limit them, is to simply play well. And after his performance against Tampa, Watson’s confidence should be on the way up, according to head coach Todd Monken : “He’s had his best week (of practice), you know, he really has. And I think that’s been building; I think that’s been building from becoming the starter after the first week being disappointed and the second half that he played last week. And I think, I mean, you’d have to speak to him, but I think his confidence should be at an all-time high, you know, and the excitement of an opportunity, a third opportunity to continue to just grow and develop as a player. Because again, he’s just scratching the surface, the last couple of days, couple weeks.” The Browns and Panthers kick off Sunday at 1 p.m. from Huntington Bank Field. full_text: The future of the Cleveland Browns defensive line after the trade of DE Myles Garrett has been all about DE Jared Verse and DT Mason Graham . Verse, as the key part of the Garrett deal , needs to have a big Week 3 after a disappointing start to his Browns career. Graham has two sacks this year and has continued his development from his rookie year. DT Mike Hall Jr. could take the group to the next level. Hall, who has played some defensive end as well, was Cleveland’s second-round pick in 2024 . Hall has dealt with injuries that limited him to 17 games in his first two seasons. His 2.5 sacks are disappointing given his draft position, but production for interior defenders does not always lead to sacks. In 2026, Hall has shown flashes of disruption while playing in close to 50% of the team’s defensive snaps: If #Browns DT Mike Hall can string together more performances like the one Sunday against the #Buccaneers , they have a fun, young defensive interior. pic.twitter.com/1QZgSbxGNN — Josh Edwards (@EdwardsCBS) September 25, 2026 The above play is a great example of an impact play that doesn’t show up in the stat sheet. Former Browns OL LeCharles Bentley also noted : Mike Hall is another player whose impact will not be fully explained by the box score. Hall was a difference-maker Sunday. His superpower is his get-off. Bentley showed this example of Hall’s quickness off the snap: With Cleveland’s edge rushers struggling to get pressure, Hall and Graham can get penetration up the middle can create quicker disruptions for opposing offenses. While good pass rushers are rarer from the inside, penetration up the middle can have an even bigger impact on both the run and pass games. Hall’s development, even if it doesn’t show up in the box score, can help make up for the loss of Garrett and give Verse and company a better chance to make an impact from the outside. title: Browns legend Brian Brennan talks to DBN before his Legends induction in Week 3
summary: For the Cleveland Browns, Week 3 is shaping up to be a big one on the sidelines, and a chance to be an exciting one on the field. Three former Browns will be inducted into the Browns Legends club: WR Brian Brennan, OL Alex Mack, and OL Lou Rymkus. On top of that, Cleveland welcomed […]
full_text: For the Cleveland Browns, Week 3 is shaping up to be a big one on the sidelines, and a chance to be an exciting one on the field . Three former Browns will be inducted into the Browns Legends club : WR Brian Brennan , OL Alex Mack , and OL Lou Rymkus . On top of that, Cleveland welcomed back RB Nick Chubb , who signed a one-day contract and will be honored during Sunday’s contest . Brennan, one of my (Jared) favorite players growing up , spoke with our Barry Shuck in advance of his induction into the Browns Legends this weekend Q1: Take us back to the phone call from the Browns about you being inducted into the Browns Legends A1: I have been working out of my residence lately here in Cleveland. And I was working at my desk when JW Johnson, who is the president of the Haslem sports group, called. I thought we were going to catch up on the assistance he needed with alumni. We never made it that far. He surprised me that I would be inducted into the 2026 class of the legends. I was surprised, overwhelmed, and grateful. And I told him that I loved being a Cleveland Brown. That era in which I played had so much success and great players on the roster. To be included as part of that meant a lot to me. Q2: Who was the first person you told? A2: My wife. We’ve been married 42 years. She has been there for all the successes and all the struggles I’ve had as a person, a player, and as post career. Any success I’ve had, she was a part of. As soon as I got the call, I hung up, and I called her. Q3: Playing in an actual NFL game must’ve been the easy part after practicing against Frank Minnifield and Hanford Dixon. Every day, how did these two guys impact your growth as a receiver at this level? A3: We had a really strong receiver group with Webster Slaughter, Clarence Weathers, Reggie Langhorne, and myself. We were a tight-knit group. We had to battle every day against Frank and Hanford. We challenged them as much as they challenged us. I learned a lot about getting off the line of scrimmage, which was so prevalent when I played. Working against those two helped all of us against game opponents. We saw elite defensive back play every day. Q4: In your entire career, you played with a lot of great quarterbacks, including Boomer Esiason with Cincy and under exceptional coaching. If you could suit up for one more game, pick a quarterback and a coach. A4: Bernie Kosar and a combination of Marty Schottenheimer and Lindy Infante. Both I loved. Bernie was a student of the game, and he was great with the football; we had great chemistry, we trusted each other, and he was just so smart in the position. He was one of the first pioneers to consistently use audibles that other quarterbacks got a reputation for using, like Peyton Manning. Marty was a great defensive coach, while Infante was an offensive mind like no other that has never gotten the credit he deserves. Q5: You are not an Ohio native, although you played for both the Browns and later the Bengals. After you hung up your cleats, you decided to stay in the Cleveland area with KeyBank, although they had offices in New York, Connecticut, Alaska, and Colorado. Yet you decided to stay in the Cleveland area. Why? A5: I had success in culture as a Brown. The culture at KeyBank is very solid. To win in the challenging financial arena is part of that culture. And the headquarters is located in Cleveland. I was happy being in Cleveland, love the area, and thought I knew the people. So I felt comfortable around the character of the people here. Q6: There were plenty of NFL receivers who were a lot taller than you, had more weight, faster than you, and drafted higher than in Round 4. Are you the poster child for perseverance in pro football? A6: There are a lot of people who aren’t the prototypical player at their positions. I felt I was always a great athlete and could still play today if I was in shape. I was the 11th or 12th receiver drafted in 1984. Receiver Irving Fryar was the number one overall pick and caught more passes than me, and that was it. I always thought I had the ability, and I’m glad the Browns saw it. Q7: What does it mean for you to be included in the legends? A7:The Browns are now putting me in a high place of team achievement. I am grateful and as a player have no choice but to be overwhelmed at how they view my playing career while in Cleveland. To be included as part of this means a lot to me.

summary: A win can be the medicine fans need to get re-invested in the product. full_text: A win can be the medicine fans need to get re-invested in the product. After last week’s fan confidence in the direction of the team had dipped to 21%, after the Browns’ win over the Buccaneers, fan confidence increased by 39 percentage points up to 60%. That’s a new season high. Panthers fans are not lacking confidence either, as 90% of fans are confident in the direction of their team. Having QB Bryce Young looking good no doubt contributes to that high percentage, since both teams are 1-1. What about this week’s game, though? We asked one question, and it focused on what Browns fans expect the outcome of this Sunday’s game against the Panthers will be. Overall, 57% of Browns fans think the Browns will win, with most of those fans projecting a close win. 25% of fans think the Panthers will edge out a victory, while 18% of fans think last week’s game by the Browns was a mirage and that Carolina will dominate their way to victory. We’ll see how things pan out. If QB Deshaun Watson had played poorly against the Buccaneers and Cleveland had dropped to 0-2, you can believe that the pitchforks would be out if he was starting under those circumstances. In that case, people thought QB Shedeur Sanders would have to start. But the script has changed, for at least a week. Because after that performance by Watson, there’s no defendable reason to now bench him. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 2.5 point underdogs against the Panthers this week, with the over/under being 41.5.

title: Browns vs. Panthers predictions: How will the fans treat Deshaun Watson at home?
summary: This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns take on the Carolina Panthers. Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. We Can Actually Dig in Now One game can make a world of a difference. The Browns looked completely unprepared in Week 1 […]
full_text: This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns take on the Carolina Panthers. Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. We Can Actually Dig in Now One game can make a world of a difference. The Browns looked completely unprepared in Week 1 against the Jaguars, and then looked much better in Week 2 against the Buccaneers, pulling off a road victory. It’s great to get a win, even though the pessimistic side of me (which doesn’t creep in very often) is wondering to myself, “Hmmm, maybe the Buccaneers were just one of the worst teams in football.” Nonetheless, we now have at least two games worth of statistical rankings for all 32 teams in the NFL, which gives us the opportunity to zone in on teams’ strengths and weaknesses a bit more. The big thing we want to focus on this week is the Browns’ run game vs. the Panthers’ run defense, which we also talked about earlier in the week . After two games, the Browns have the 31st ranked rushing offense in the NFL, averaging 65.5 yards and 2.91 yards per carry. Most of the positive yards have come on the ground via QB Deshaun Watson , not RB Quinshon Judkins . The Panthers’ run defense ranks dead last in the NFL through two games, allowing 224 yards rushing per game, and an average of 6.31 yards per carry. Their defenders up front haven’t been this bad against the run in the past, so it’s possible they get their act together. Something has to give, though. My instincts tell me that it’s easier for a bad run defense to find success against a bad run offense, as opposed to the other way around. One area that Cleveland found success with in the second half last week to mitigate their lack of a run game was finding those quick completions on early downs to set up 3rd-and-short situations. I feel like, if a team can use the short passing game to essentially serve the purpose of the ground game, then don’t force anything. Still, it would be a big boost to the offense — which has otherwise shown some promise — to have the running game become a factor. Flipping the Script Speaking of something having to give, what about the Browns’ pass defense against the Panthers’ pass offense? Cleveland has their consecutive games streak going of not allowing a 300+ yard passer. Through two games, they’ve allowed 245 and 182 yards, with the secondary looking much sharper last week. QB Bryce Young has thrown for 361 and 287 yards over his first two games, and 3 touchdown passes in each game. He also has a completion of 50+ yards in each of the games. Young has been getting his young wide receivers involved early and often. Jalen Coker , who was undrafted in 2024, has 16 catches for 204 yards and 2 touchdowns. Tetairoa McMillan , who was the 8th overall pick last year, has 10 catches for 176 yards. Xavier Legette , who was the 32nd pick in 2024, had 2 catches for 64 yards last week. Carolina has stacked the wide receiver position, and it’s paying off. Darren Waller is also a red zone threat for the team. After coming out of retirement last year, he’s gotten more up-to-speed with the Panthers as he rested much of the offseason. If all they need him for is to be a big target for Young down in scoring range, he’s off to a great start, having two touchdown grabs a week ago. Shifting focus to the Browns, obviously, Deshaun Watson is coming off his best game as a member of the Browns. He looked comfortable in Week 2, and led a couple of scoring drives in the second half. The two road games are over, though, and now he plays in front of his home crowd. It’s rare that you have to question whether a home crowd will be ‘good’ for a player or not. Watson still clearly thinks about those boos or the reaction he gets, even if he tries to play it off a bit now. I did like his answer this week, when asked about the fans: “I mean, yeah, the biggest thing is, I don’t never try to go at war with the fans, so the biggest thing is just, ready for support, ready to feel their energy, ready to get this big dub for the city of Cleveland, and continue this great feeling that we have this week. So that’s my motto, is just keep pushing forward, finding ways to win on Sunday to take advantage of the opposing team and get a W.” We’ve seen Mason Graham step up two weeks in a row, and I thought Carson Schwesinger had more of an impact in Week 2. We are still waiting for Jared Verse to get more comfortable in the defense, and the top player who could use a better performance defensively right now is Ronnie Hickman , in my opinion. Other things to watch on defense: Maliek Collins or Mike Hall playing at a higher level would give a big boost to the consistency of the defensive front. Myles Harden had a big game last week. Injury-wise, questions about the health of Tyson Campbell and Grant Delpit are at the forefront. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 2.5 point underdogs against the Panthers. The over/under is 41.5. Quick Hitters Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg gave an explanation on how you adjust your defensive gameplan from week-to-week, to keep teams guessing: “Tony, the truth is, and I learned this from Coach (Joe) Gibbs, it is a week to week. The game plan, the scheme, it’s about all of us working our asses off each week out, grinding, making this Thursday better than last Thursday, making this meeting that we’re coming up to better than the last meeting, getting this game better than the last game. Whatever the game plan is and what are the executions? Getting that better than last week. And it’s about our style of play and the level of execution. That’s the truth to the way this league goes. It’s such a marathon, and we’re in week three of that marathon right now, and our whole goal is to play better than we did last week and hopefully do enough to help the Browns win.” Offensive coordinator Travis Switzer talked about how close the team is in getting the run game to click: “Yeah, I mean, this is a week-to-week league and just look around. Chicago goes from scoring 59 to 3. So, I don’t know about how close, I just know that every week we’re attacking it. And certainly, after last week, and really the first two weeks, we’re not where we want to be there, so we’re looking at everything that goes into that, and everyone involved. I have to look at it schematically, certainly there was a play too, from the game the other day where I’m looking at it like, you know what, I didn’t put us in a great position there. And then we’re looking at just the execution of it by all parties, right, the blockers and the fundamentals and the things that we’re working at up there, the runners and just trusting their eyes and seeing it. But yeah, we’re looking at all parts of that. As far as how close, we’re going to get better. I know that we believe in what we do and we believe in our players, so we know we’re going to get there. But it’s a week-to-week league anyway. Even if we turn around miraculously and we run it great this week, it doesn’t mean anything for the next week, right? We have to reload every week. It’s a week-to-week league.” Special teams coordinator Byron Storer was asked about DE Sam Williams playing gunner: “You look back at Sam Williams’ career at Dallas, and he played out there, I played against him out there, actually, so I’m well aware of his ability to play gunner outside. And that’s the thing with a man of his size, you’re like, I would love for him to play in the box and be a guard or a tackle or a wing. But there’s also that ability to go out there and be a gunner outside with four-five speed and just dominate a corner in front of you too. And his mindset is too, he’s like, ‘coach, I can play gunner.’ And I said, ‘you know what, that’s probably the quickest way for you to get on the field right now.’ So, we took advantage of the opportunity.” Here are predictions from multiple staff members at DBN: Predictions Chris Pokorny: “What are the true colors of the…

full_text: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns open the home portion of the 2026 NFL schedule on Sunday when they welcome the Carolina Panthers to downtown Cleveland. The Browns are coming off an exciting win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a game where quarterback Deshaun Watson, dare we say, looked like a competent NFL quarterback. Carolina, on the other hand, is riding an unexpected offensive explosion behind quarterback Bryce Young that has the Panthers averaging 35.5 points per game. By comparison, the Browns have not broken the 30-point mark since Week 7 of last season. It’s the Browns vs. the Panthers in Watson’s first regular-season start in front of the home fans in almost two years, and the first visit by Carolina in almost eight years. Here is everything you need to know about the game. Game Info Records: Cleveland is 1-1. Carolina is 1-1. Kickoff: 1 p.m. Stadium: Huntington Bank Field, Cleveland. TV: FOX Announcers: Chris Myers, Mark Schlereth, and Jen Hale (sideline reporter) Radio: 850 ESPN Cleveland, 92.3 The Fan WKRK, 98.5 WNCX, 1300 AM La Mega (Español) Announcers: Andrew Siciliano, Nathan Zegura, and Je’Rod Cherry (sidelines) Last meeting: The Browns won the last meeting, 26-24, in Week 1 of the 2022 season. First meeting: The Panthers won the first meeting, 31-17, on November 21, 1999. All-time series: Carolina leads the all-time series, 4-3, but the Browns have won the last two meetings in Cleveland. Weather: 67 degrees and mostly cloudy, with no chance of rain. Winds from the north at 13 mph. ( weather.com ) HOME OPENER = ORANGE PANTS 🔥 @RiddellSports | #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/6SwRqudFfs — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 24, 2026 Uniform: The Browns will be wearing their Sunday best, with brown uniforms and orange pants. Injury report: Browns – Out: Offensive guard Teven Jenkins (back). Questionable: Cornerback Tyson Campbell (ankle/hip) and safety Grant Delpit (shoulder). Panthers – Out: Linebacker Claudin Cherelus (shoulder), safey Nick Scott (ribs), and linebacker Devin Lloy (calf). Questionable: Wide receiver Jalen Coker (ankle) and wide receiver Xavier Legette (knee). The line: Browns +2.5 points, with an over/under of 41.5 points, per FanDuel . News & Notes The Browns come into the game ranked No. 31 in rushing with 131 rushing yards. Carolina are last in rushing defense, having allowed 448 rushing yards. Cleveland has not allowed a 300-yard passer for 47 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the league. The Panthers are averaging 312.5 passing yards and are second in the league in pass plays of 20 or more yards. Carolina quarterback Bryce Young has thrown three touchdown passes in each of the first two games of the season. Cleveland will induct Alex Mack, Brian Brennan, and Lou Rymkus as the 2026 Class of Browns Legends on Sunday. Cleveland wide receiver Denzel Boston is just the second player in franchise history to have a receiving touchdown in each of his first two games, joining Andre’ Davis (2002) and Bobby Mitchell (1958). Boston is leading all NFL rookies in receiving yards (154), while wide receiver KC Concepcion leads all rookies with 10 receptions. Carolina are tops in the league with six takeaways. Defensive tackle Mason Graham is tied for the league lead in sacks for defensive tackles with two. Cleveland kicker Andre Szmyt has converted 18 consecutive field goal attempts, dating back to last season. title: 3 X-Factors for the upcoming Panthers-Browns home opener
summary: The Cleveland Browns look to capitalize on their momentum after their upset win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as the team prepares for their home opener against another NFC South opponent in the Carolina Panthers. The Panthers, who are coming off a thrashing of the Atlanta Falcons, will look to build their own momentum and […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns look to capitalize on their momentum after their upset win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as the team prepares for their home opener against another NFC South opponent in the Carolina Panthers . The Panthers, who are coming off a thrashing of the Atlanta Falcons, will look to build their own momentum and take advantage of an uncertain NFC South. Here are the 3 X-factors for the Panthers vs. Browns in Week 2: Browns defensive line vs Panthers offensive line The trenches will once again be an emphasis on Sunday. Carolina’s offensive line is a work in progress. Cleveland’s defensive line is a work in progress. Something has to give. As for the Panthers, they are missing key starters in Ikem Ekwonu and Taylor Moton but it’s hard to gauge how good their offensive line is considering how they haven’t played a competent pass rush. For the Browns, their pass rush hasn’t materialized the way fans expected it to, but there are a lot of moving parts. Defensive end Jared Verse has gotten off to a slow start , but defensive tackle Mason Graham has quietly emerged as the best defensive lineman on the team. For either team to have a chance to win this game, it will be determined in the trenches. Will the Browns running game materialize? In terms of the offense, the one part of the Cleveland offense that has struggled is the running game . The Browns are ranked towards the bottom in every run metric, but context is key when describing this current run game. Entirely new offensive line from last season Learning a new scheme in terms of the run game One of the many reasons why the Browns running game has struggled is because teams are stacking the box; Cleveland faced a stacked box 30% of the time last week against Tampa Bay. Carolina’s run defense ranks 16th in rushing defense success rate early on this year. For the Browns offense to have some form of a chance, the run game has to be established. Deshaun and the fans It’s a topic of discussion, so let’s discuss. The last time Deshaun Watson played in front of the Browns fans, he was booed. Granted, it was a preseason game, but it was clear Watson was affected by it from his post-game comments. How does Watson prepare to play in front of a fanbase that doesn’t particularly care for him? How will he look if the team goes 3-and-out on their first drive? If the Cleveland offense is humming, the fans will be rocking, which will have the positive impact a great fanbase can give a team. Watson played well last week against the Buccaneers, but the Panthers defense will provide a different challenge. For Watson, he just has to block out the noise and play efficient football. It seems like a tall task for Watson to do considering how he hasn’t done it consistently, but he has an opportunity to redeem himself (in some way) by playing competent football for another week. The fans are going to be critical regardless; it’s up to Watson to just block out the noise and play. What do you think the X-Factors for Week 3’s Browns vs. Panthers matchup will be? title: Cowboys vs. Ravens: Matchups to watch in Week 3
summary: Both the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens hit the road this week, traveling all the way to Brazil for this Week 3 matchup. full_text: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images | Getty Images Both the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens hit the road this week, traveling all the way to Brazil for this Week 3 matchup. Although they are thousand miles from home, this is technically a home game for America’s Team, but we shouldn’t expect any kind of home field advantage. It could be quite the opposite with questionable field conditions. Anyway you want to look at a this is a tough matchup for the Cowboys. The Ravens are one of the better teams in the league despite losing to the Saints a week ago. This is a game chock-full of matchups that could sway the outcome of the game one way or another. Below we discuss which ones we will be watching closely. Cowboys’ run defense vs. Ravens’ rushing attack The Cowboys made an effort to improve their run defense this offseason by bringing in Christian Parker and outside players to help, but as of yet there hasn’t been any sign things have changed. In fact, they are still currently one of the worst against the run in the league, allowing 173.5 yards per game, ranking 30 th in the league. That doesn’t exactly inspire much confidence they’ll be able to contain Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry this week. They both headline the fifth-ranked rushing attack so far this year and are averaging 83.5 rushing yards per game. WR CeeDee Lamb vs. Ravens’ CBs CeeDee Lamb is coming off a huge game last week against the Commanders and will certainly demand attention from the Ravens cornerbacks in this Week 3 matchup. The last time these two teams played No. 88 had just four catches for 67 yards with no touchdowns and a fumble. This time around Baltimore can’t focus the majority of their attention on him though with George Pickens having to be factored in. Moving Lamb around could create favorable matchups for him or provide one-on-one opportunities for Pickens. It could be a win-win. Cowboys’ pass rush vs. Ravens’ OL This is a matchup that could heavily favor the Cowboys considering the Ravens OL is currently allowing a 44% pressure rate through the first two weeks, ranking third-worst in the NFL. The interior of their OL is particularly vulnerable after letting All-Pro C Tyler Linderbaum walk in free agency. Neither Kenny Clark or Quinnen Williams have played up to their typical standards so far, but could both excel in this matchup. And, Donovan Ezeiruaku and Malachi Lawrence could find some success as tackle Ronnie Stanley will be out.

full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have played two games so far this season and things have obviously gone several different directions. NFL seasons are long though, and ultimately we are likely in store for things that we can’t even conceive at this point. Different players will cycle through the team. It is quite possible that someone who isn’t even on the roster right now will log snaps for the organization before the season is over. That is the way that football works. Of course, that also means that the Cowboys could cycle through players who are deeper down their roster. One of the most discussed throughout all of training camp is wide receiver Camden Brown. Brown is the latest point of undrafted free agency success for the Cowboys. Time will tell whether or not he reaches the same heights that some of the greatest UDFAs in team history like Tony Romo, Miles Austin, and Dan Bailey did, but with his entire career in front of him that story remains unwritten. Camden has shared in his time with the Cowboys that his driving force, his “4TheWhy” as he has put it, is his late sister Kaden Storm Brown. Camden has mentioned at many different turns how her memory inspires him each and every day. We obviously root for every player on the Cowboys, but some players have stories that stand out a little bit more. Camden certainly qualifies as one of those. Time will tell how much Camden does or does not get involved his rookie season, but it stands to reason that if his number is called he will be ready.

title: Cowboys vs. Ravens predictions: Despite getting outplayed, Dallas wins
summary: We’re back for another round of weekly predictions. This time it is for the Dallas Cowboys game against the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil. Last week we did pretty well as Dak Prescott did indeed ‘go off’ in the game to the tune of four touchdowns and no interceptions. We also predicted Jake Ferguson would catch […]
full_text: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images | Getty Images We’re back for another round of weekly predictions. This time it is for the Dallas Cowboys game against the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil. Last week we did pretty well as Dak Prescott did indeed ‘go off’ in the game to the tune of four touchdowns and no interceptions. We also predicted Jake Ferguson would catch two touchdowns and he did exactly that. The Quinnen Williams prediction, unfortunately, did not come through. The field in Brazil has been a major talking point and we’re going to follow that line into our predictions. The Cowboys are the designated home team for the game, but they are 3.5-point underdogs according to our friends at FanDuel. The over/under is 52.5 points. On to the predictions. Derrick Henry goes for 150 yards rushing The Cowboys have yet to get control of the line of scrimmage from a defensive standpoint this season. The move to Christian Parker’s new scheme has helped in some areas, but stopping the run is still a weak point. Kenny Clark and Quinnen Williams haven’t played up to the standards they have set previously. Now they have to face Derrick Henry and Lamar Jackson. The Ravens have seen the film, so they are going to pound the line of scrimmage with their battering ram, Derrick Henry. It probably will not go well for Dallas. The prediction is that Henry will top 150 yards rushing in this game while collecting one rushing touchdown. The field costs one big play The field in Brazil has received a ton of attention as the soccer team that normally plays there has complained about the footing. There have also been a lot of rain over the last month on the field, leaving it’s condition in doubt. The NFL is trying to say there is no problem, but where there is this much smoke there is usually fire. The prediction is that somewhere along the way, a big play will happen, or get ruined, because of footing on the field. A wide receiver will slip while wide open, a defender will lose their footing before they can make a touchdown-saving tackle. Or maybe a quarterback falls while trying to avoid a crucial sack on a third down. Something will happen. The Cowboys win on turnovers The Cowboys won’t dominate the game, in fact, when the stats are compiled at the end it will look like a Ravens win. Except for turnovers. The Cowboys defense has been very good about punching the football loose, although they haven’t got as many recoveries as we would like. This time they get a couple of fumble recoveries, and they pick off a Lamar Jackson pass. They will get outplayed, but will capitalize on turnovers to get a close win. title: Cowboys need to find a way to get the running game going
summary: The Dallas Cowboys had the league’s number two offense in 2025. A huge reason is because they were able to be highly productive passing and running the ball. They finished second in passing yards per game and ninth in rushing, with the latter being spearheaded by Javonte Williams and his 1,201 yards, which ranked ninth […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys had the league’s number two offense in 2025. A huge reason is because they were able to be highly productive passing and running the ball. They finished second in passing yards per game and ninth in rushing, with the latter being spearheaded by Javonte Williams and his 1,201 yards, which ranked ninth overall. As is always the case when Dak Prescott is healthy at the quarterback position, the Cowboys are expected to be one of the NFL’s better offenses again this season. However, in the first two games, the Cowboys are averaging just 67.5 yards a game on the ground. Specifically, Williams has just 71 yards on 24 carries, which is just 2.96 yards per attempt. That simply won’t cut it. Prescott is one of the top quarterbacks in the league. With that said, neither he, or any quarterback, can be asked to solely carry the load for an offense. Defenses are too good in the NFL for opposing offenses to be one-dimensional. It may work here and there depending on the opponent, but for the duration of a 17-game season, it’s a recipe for disaster. It’s not like the Cowboys don’t have enough talent in their running back room to be productive. Williams proved a season ago that he can carry significant load, and Emari Demercado showed during his three seasons with the Arizona Cardinals that he can add another layer to a rushing attack. Plus, Hunter Luepke is capable of doing some things, and the Cowboys also recently added Tyler Goodson from the Atlanta Falcons practice squad. It’s time for offensive coordinator Klayton Adams to get back to the drawing board and figure out what’s not working and get it corrected. That will be a tough task against the Baltimore Ravens this Sunday in Brazil as their defense is only allowing up 83.5 yards per game so far. The last thing the Cowboys want to do is to have quick drives on offense and give the ball back to Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry with short fields to score, especially since their defense is still figuring things out under first-year coordinator Christian Parker. Do you think the Cowboys can get their run game going this week?

Offensive impact player – WR George Pickens George Pickens hasn’t exactly been lighting up the stat sheet through the first two weeks of the 2026 NFL season. After some uncharacteristic dropped passes in the season opener against the Giants, he’s only managed to catch a total of nine passes for 68 yards into games so far this year. As a former division rival, Pickens knows all about the Ravens and has been productive against them in the past. Now with the Cowboys, that knowledge should pay dividends this week, especially since more attention could be paid to CeeDee Lamb after his big game last week against the Commanders. Defensive impact player – DT Quinnen Williams Much like George Pickens, Quinnen Williams hasn’t exactly been living up to everyone’s expectations through the first two weeks of the 2026 NFL season. Some have started questioning his fit in Christian Parker’s scheme, while others wonder whether or not he is fully healthy. The interior of their OL is particularly vulnerable after letting All-Pro C Tyler Lindnerbaum walk in free agency. Add it all up and this creates a favorable matchup for No. 92 to be an absolute menace as both the run defender and pass rusher against both RB Derrick Henry and QB Lamar Jackson this week.
