title: Cowboys vs Ravens: 3 causes for concern in Brazil
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are back in action on Sunday as they travel to Brazil to square off with the Baltimore Ravens. Despite losing to the New Orleans Saints just a week ago, the Ravens are one of the AFC’s best teams, so the Cowboys will have their work cut out for them. Before the two […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys are back in action on Sunday as they travel to Brazil to square off with the Baltimore Ravens. Despite losing to the New Orleans Saints just a week ago, the Ravens are one of the AFC’s best teams, so the Cowboys will have their work cut out for them. Before the two teams square off down in South America, here are three causes for concern in this matchup. 1) Baltimore’s Rushing Attack Two games into the 2026 regular season, Dallas’ defense has been dreadful against the run. The Cowboys have allowed the third-most rushing yards (347) and fifth-worst Y/A (5.0), along with the third-worst defensive rush success rate (48.3%). It hasn’t just been traditional running backs who have caused Dallas trouble on the ground; they’ve also allowed opposing quarterbacks to run wild. In their two games, the Cowboys have allowed 126 rushing yards to opposing QBs on 19 rush attempts, an average of 6.6 Y/A. If that trend continues this week, the Cowboys will have no shot at walking out of Brazil with a win. You could argue the Ravens have the best rushing attack in the league. Both Derrick Henry and Lamar Jackson are premier rushing threats, and their complementary style of power and speed makes them a perfect duo. Both players have gotten off to excellent starts this season. Henry is second in the league with 212 rushing yards, averaging over five yards (5.3) per carry, and leads all running backs with four rushing touchdowns. While Jackson has done plenty of damage through the air, he’s also been very effective on the ground, rushing for 74 yards on 11 carries, an average of 7.4 Y/A, to go with a rushing touchdown. This will be by far Dallas’ toughest test so far this season. With how bad the Cowboys have been against the run, Baltimore will almost certainly lean into a run-heavy game plan. If Dallas does not have an answer and fix their run defense fast, it’s going to be a long day. 2) Trey Hendrickson and the Ravens’ pass rush The biggest roster move Baltimore made this offseason was signing veteran edge Trey Hendrickson to upgrade their pass rush. Two games into the season, the move has paid off as the Ravens have been able to get after the quarterback at a good rate. Led by Hendrickson, Baltimore has recorded 39 total pressures, 23 hurries, and five sacks in their two contests. Last week against the Saints, Hendrickson himself recorded six total pressures and four hurries with an impressive 14.0 PRP, via Pro Football Focus . The Cowboys offensive line played much better in pass protection last week against the Commanders, allowing just eight pressures and one sack. They’ll need to replicate this performance and not their Week 1 outing against the Giants on Sunday if they want to keep Dak Prescott upright and move the ball consistently down the field. 3) Conditions of the field at Maracanã Stadium A hot topic the past week or so has been the conditions of the field at Maracanã Stadium, where the Cowboys and Ravens will play on Sunday. According to Yahoo Sports, members of the home soccer team, CR Flamengo, have criticized the playing surface sighting that it may be unsafe. Multiple reports over the weekend raised concerns about the field conditions at Maracaña Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, where the Ravens are scheduled to take on the Cowboys next Sunday in Week 3. Members of CR Flamengo, the home soccer team, have criticized the playing… pic.twitter.com/0vREGq1Qgb — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) September 22, 2026 Cowboys’ owner Jerry Jones was asked about the field conditions earlier this week and said the field conditions are not concerning to him at this time. Jerry Jones to @1053thefan on the state of the field at the Maracana: “I’m comfortable that the field will be ready for us. They’ve had lot of rain down there but the conditions there are not concerning to me right now. It’s realistic we can have a good game on the field.” — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) September 22, 2026 While it may not be concerning to Jones, it’s fair to worry about what things could look like on Sunday.

title: Cowboys defensive front needs best game of season vs. Ravens
summary: Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer takes his team to Rio de Janeiro in his second season with a 1-1 record through two games. How can the Cowboys get an early statement win to string together two in a row after beating the Commanders, against a Ravens team coming off a home loss to the […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer takes his team to Rio de Janeiro in his second season with a 1-1 record through two games. How can the Cowboys get an early statement win to string together two in a row after beating the Commanders, against a Ravens team coming off a home loss to the Saints? What is the biggest challenge the Ravens present to the Cowboys to right their ship under first-year HC Jesse Minter? Let’s take a closer look. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the Baltimore Ravens if… they win on early downs on both sides of the ball. So much of the buildup for this matchup between a Cowboys team that was second in the NFL in points scored in week two, and a Ravens team that was second in week one (behind only the Bears’ scoreboard-breaking 59 points) has been about the skill players and big-play potential from both quarterbacks. No matter how good these groups are, games are still won and lost at the line of scrimmage, and this is where the Cowboys will need to put together their most complete game of the season. Starting with the Dallas defense against the Baltimore offense, the Cowboys will be facing a mobile quarterback for the second week in a row in Lamar Jackson. They’ll also be depleted in the secondary without Cobie Durant and P.J. Locke against Rashod Bateman, Devontez Walker, Chris Moore, and Mark Andrews. This is a game where the Cowboys defensive front needs to make their money, particularly the interior tackles that have yet to make as big of a splash as expected through two games. The Ravens offensive line has graded out well in run blocking, but the matchups will be there for Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams, and Otito Ogbonnia to win at the point of attack and try to limit Derrick Henry – especially on early downs. Doing so will be the key to earning pass rush opportunities in longer down and distances to allow Donovan Ezeiruaku, Rashan Gary, Malachi Lawrence, and even Von Miller, to assert themselves into this game. Both starting guards and the Ravens starting center are new to their lineup. Rookie first-round draft pick Vega Ioane will be making his third start at right guard. Jovaughn Gwyn has been in the league since 2023, but played his very first snaps on offense as a starter in week one for this year’s Ravens. John Simpson is a veteran left guard, but one the Cowboys saw last year when he was with the Jets, and won that matchup handily. In fact, Simpson was the Jets’ lowest PFF graded player for the whole offense in that game. It’s still no easy task, but if the Cowboys defensive front can have their best game of the season, Christian Parker’s scheme can commit enough bodies to the coverage umbrella to limit downfield shots, keep eyes on Jackson when scrambling, and keep the Cowboys own offense within striking distance of winning this game. Those strikes will have to be delivered by Prescott through the air for the most part, as confidence in Dallas running the ball well consistently right now is low. A hallmark of a Jesse Minter defense is not being moved off the ball at the point of attack easily, but the Cowboys will need to force themselves to try and find some balance in their approach offensively. Early down runs that actually keep the offense on schedule and don’t feel like wasted plays would help Dallas control this game with their best players on the field, the defense resting on the sideline, and the Ravens most dynamic players also on the sideline without the ball in their hands. The Dallas Cowboys will lose to the Baltimore Ravens if… they can’t contain Derrick Henry outside the tackles. Through two games, the ageless Derrick Henry is second in the NFL in rushing yards and tied for first in touchdowns. His best runs have come outside the tackles, as we see on these two charts via Next Gen Stats: While it’s true that the Cowboys defense saw some encouraging things from rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham at the MIKE position and Dee Winters against the Commanders, this Ravens game could easily be a fall back to reality for a group that’s still unproven. Barham is still a rookie starter at a somewhat new position, wearing the green dot and trying to get a lot of new players lined up properly. There will be even more new players in the Cowboys defensive lineup against the Ravens as they deal with injuries, and the tackling from this group against such a big, physical back like Henry is a major concern. Rookie Caleb Downs has performed well in this area, but Dallas is using him close to the line of scrimmage in a lot of assignments. When Henry is able to break contain and get on the edge, the Cowboys will need an answer for who can get the angle on him, and more importantly bring him to the ground. Henry has also caught all four of the passing attempts thrown his way this season, proving he’s still a one-man gameplan wrecker on any given Sunday. Turning and handing the ball off could also prove to be the safest plan for both teams on offense, as the footing and condition of the field surface has been a concern all week leading up to kickoff. The Ravens come into this matchup with a huge advantage on paper when it comes to Henry’s production compared to Javonte Williams as the lead back for the Cowboys.

title: Cowboys roundtable discussion: BrandonAubrey, Jaishawn Barham, and Brazil
summary: Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo, Dyllan Rivers, Tom Ryle and Sean Martin.  Do you have better faith in Brandon Aubrey after punching all seven kicks for points against the Commanders, which included a […]
full_text: Photo by Mauro PIMENTEL / AFP via Getty Images Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo , Dyllan Rivers , Tom Ryle and Sean Martin . Do you have better faith in Brandon Aubrey after punching all seven kicks for points against the Commanders, which included a 60-yard field goal? Mike – Honestly, the faith in Brandon Aubrey was already high, but games like that only make it stronger. Going perfect on all seven scoring kicks, including a 60-yarder, is not normal, that’s a weapon. Aubrey gives Dallas something most teams do not have, the ability to turn stalled drives near midfield into points and change how the coaching staff thinks about field position. The bigger issue is not whether Cowboys fans should trust Aubrey, it is whether the offense becomes too comfortable settling for him. Jorge – I think he calmed some of the nerves, for sure. He needed, and the fans needed, to see that 60-yarder go through, and he nailed it. As long as he doesn’t have a Brett Maher-like meltdown, he should still be considered among the best kickers in the NFL and a huge asset for this team. Tom – All he can do to calm our doubts is to nail his kicks, and he did. I feel pretty good about him going forward. Sean – He’s butter. What else is there to say? The kicks sure looked good to me. Dyllan – I was only about 3.6% worried after last week. Now I’m back to a solid 0.0% in the worried about Aubrey department. Butter is simply the best there is. What grade do you give Jaishawn Barham for his first game wearing the green-dot, and where does he need improvement? Mike – I’d give Barham a B+ for his first game wearing the green dot. For a young linebacker taking on that much responsibility, he looked ready for the moment. The forced fumble was the headline, but the bigger takeaway was that the defense did not look utterly overwhelmed with him communicating calls and helping get players aligned. The improvement still needs to come but it was a quality start. Jorge – If we’re going with a letter grade, I’d have to say he was a B. Some of the communication issues were cleaned up, but the defense still had issues and gave up some plays, particularly in containment of Jayden Daniels, who ran wild at times. Still, Dallas is asking a ton out of the rookie, and the defense’s slight improvement is a good sign. Barham was a big part of that improvement, and one would think he’s only going to get better. Tom – B sounds about right. That was a huge load to put on the rookie’s shoulders, and he bore it well. And he caused one of the biggest plays of the game, and the best highlight for the defense so far this year. Sean – I’ll go with a B as well. We want to have higher expectations for this defense, and then they go and start an unproven rookie day two pick smack dab in the middle of the defense, and it makes those expectations difficult. Like Jorge said it wasn’t perfect, but the Dallas defense put tangible things to build off on on tape with some of their alignments, coverages, hustle to the ball, and of course a takeaway which was caused directly by Barham lowering the “Bar-hammer”. Dyllan – I’ll give Barhammer a B+ this week. The defense looked much tighter in communication with the rookie LB wearing the green dot. He also made some great plays throughout, including the forced fumble to put the offense in great field position. He somehow morphs through blocks and is always around the ball. This kid is going to be special. This week sees the Cowboys travelling to Brazil to face the Baltimore Ravens. Their last international game was in London back in 2014 with a 31-14 victory, but how confident are you feeling for this international clash? Mike – Cautiously confident is how I put it, and I’ve seen first hand how the Cowboys handle international pressure watching them in London way back when. The Cowboys have momentum after the Washington win, and an international stage should not scare a franchise that has handled this kind of spotlight before. The concern is the opponent. Baltimore brings the type of physical, awkward matchup that can expose any lack of discipline, especially with the travel, different routine, and field-condition questions in Brazil. Jorge – I am worried. It’s a 10-plus-hour flight, over 4,000 miles across three time zones, to a country in spring while we’re in fall, which could affect the natural circadian rhythm, and that’s a big deal. As someone who has traveled from Japan to the U.S. several times, that is not a trip to take lightly. On top of that, the Ravens are coming off a tough loss against the Saints and are going to be locked in for the bounce-back win, and oh, by the way, they own us historically in the head-to-head matchup six wins to one. My worry scale would be at a 9 out of 10 in this case. Tom – I’m not too worried about that rhythm, because the day will be almost exactly the same length. What does worry me is that Dallas has been so vulnerable to running quarterbacks. Now here comes Lamar Jackson. If they can’t find a way to slow him down on the ground, this one will be rough. Oh, and the pass defense hasn’t exactly sparkled so far. The early spread had the Cowboys as a three point underdog, and I think that is a bit kind to them. I have some hope if the offense can continue to ball out, but that may be a tall order against Baltimore. Sean – The pregame thoughts on this game feel too chalk, as if something completely unexpected is going to happen. The Ravens seem to have this type of early season head-scratching loss where they implode every single year, and the Cowboys have a win that still leaves an uneasy feeling. Logic would say keep going down the chalk line and the Ravens own the Cowboys yet again. My worry about that being a possibility in Brazil is still at a firm 7/10, but things are rarely, rarely this easy to predict in pro football, so let’s just see what Rio de Janeiro has in store. Dyllan – I’m extremely worried. Dallas has struggled against two mobile QBs through the first two weeks. Now they have the opportunity to face the best mobile quarterback in the NFL. On top of that, the ageless wonder Derrick Henry adds an intensity that not many other backs possess. Mix in the traveling and the beat up field; this is going to be a sloppy, brutal game for both sides. RAPID FIRE Who scores first for Dallas? Jorge – CeeDee Lamb stays hot. Tom – I’m going to stick with Javonte Williams. Sean – Hunter Luepke. You gotta get weird for an international game. Dyllan – George Pickens gets the first TD of the game and his first TD of the season. Jake Ferguson receptions- 4.5, over or under? Jorge – Under; Ferg is still too erratic for me to buy consecutive weeks of big impact like 5 receptions. Tom – Under. I’d guess George Pickens is going to get a lot of balls. Sean – I’ll go over. Dyllan – Under. Dallas just has so many weapons. Javonte Williams rushing yards- 59.5, over or under? Jorge – Under; Ravens currently own the 6th-best run defense in the NFL, and the Cowboys are struggling to get the ground game going. Tom – Under. Same reasons. Sean – Under this time. Dyllan – Under. Dallas has struggled to run the ball. I don’t see that changing now. Lamar Jackson rushing yards- 59.5, over or under? Jorge – Over; Jayden Daniels just ran for 69 yards in one half. Lamar is going to feast. Tom – Unfortunately, over. The defense is helpless against running QBs. Sean – Under because he still wants to throw the ball first. Dyllan – Over. Dallas has struggled vs mobile QBs and now they face the king of mobile QBs. Sacks recorded by Dallas- 1.5, over or under? Jorge – Under; Although the Cowboys’ pressure looked good at times, they didn’t register a single sack against Daniels or Mariota, and they have been poor tacklers in the first two games. Tom – Under, sadly. Sean – Yeah, under. Dyllan – Under. Although I…
author: Mike Poland

title: Cowboys news: Dallas secondary depth will be tested vs Ravens
summary: After a much needed bounce back win in week two, the Dallas Cowboys are set to take on the Baltimore Ravens in Rio for their week three matchup against the 1-1 Ravens. Both teams are heading into Rio a bit banged up, with some questionable field conditions on the horizon. While the Cowboys await to […]
full_text: Photo by Mauro PIMENTEL / AFP via Getty Images After a much needed bounce back win in week two, the Dallas Cowboys are set to take on the Baltimore Ravens in Rio for their week three matchup against the 1-1 Ravens. Both teams are heading into Rio a bit banged up, with some questionable field conditions on the horizon. While the Cowboys await to see if Ravens star WR Zay Flowers will play in this matchup, the Cowboys have already ruled out four players on the defensive side, who are all expected to play a big role for the Cowboys defense in 2026. Updates: Cowboys rule out four players for Brazil – DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys secondary has been under to microscope so far this season, but through two weeks that have played relatively well. Unfortunately they are heading into Rio a bit banged up at both safety and cornerback. Second-year cornerback Shavon Revel is expected to get the start at cornerback. DeMarvion Overshown headlines a list of four players that will not make the trip with the Cowboys to Brazil to take on the Baltimore Ravens. Overshown continues to rehab his injured hamstring and has been officially ruled out, as is Cobie Durant with an injured hamstring. Like Durant, PJ Locke suffered injury against the Washington Commanders, though to his foot, and will not make the trip to Rio. Malik Hooker is still recovering from a fractured forearm that will hold him out as well until, at minimum, Week 4 against the Houston Texans, though that remains to-be-determined. Cowboys will be all business in Brazil, to the disappointment of some international fans – Joesph Hoyt, The Dallas Morning News The Cowboys game in Rio has gained a lot of traction over the last few weeks. While field condition concerns have been in the forefront, the Cowboys seem to only be focused on the Ravens with kickoff just one day away. It isn’t cliché when Cowboys players say they’re treating this weekend’s 10-hour trip to Brazil as a business trip. The Cowboys will land in Rio de Janeiro on Friday morning. They’ll have a walkthrough practice later that day at the practice facility for Flamengo, a professional soccer team in town. The next day, they’ll do a literal walkthrough at Maracanã Stadium , which carries an added importance after concerns arose from one Flamengo player about the field’s conditions . Shortly after Sunday’s game ends the Cowboys will be on their charter back to Texas. Digging into the numbers to predict Cowboys vs Ravens – Dyllan Rivers, Blogging the Boys On paper, the Cowboys and Ravens game in Rio should be a tight one. Can the Cowboys slow down the Ravens running game? Can the Ravens slow down the Cowboys passing game? Let’s dive into the numbers to see what they tell us. Pressures increased between week one and week two. Dallas had just two pressures when rushing four against the Giants and nine when rushing four versus the Commanders. They couldn’t seal the deal and wound up as just one of four teams to not record a sack last week. But the fact that they are able to generate pressure without blitzing is a promising step in the right direction. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Dallas Cowboys rookie Caleb Downs drops a quote that shows exactly why he’s going to be a star defender in no time – Maurico Rodriguez, A to Z Dallas Caleb Downs has been a hot topic of conversation online over the last few weeks. One thing is for certain, Caleb Downs is a really, really, really good football player, and will be for a long time. “I was pretty much just the curl-flat player, I was in a high-low situation and was just reading the quarterback’s eyes,” Downs said. “Later on in my career, you’ll see that ball picked.” That’s exactly what you want to hear from Downs, and not just because of the cheesy reasons. Not only does that comment reflect a rookie hungry for more, but this is the attitude that makes Caleb Downs, Caleb Downs, you know? 4 emergency Cowboys trades to jumpstart the defense amid injuries – Wynston Wilcox, Fansided.com Maxx Crosby has dominated trade discussions for the Dallas Cowboys, but there’s other, more realistic names to consider. Here are four trades the Cowboys could make to help jump-start their defense in 2026. The Los Angeles Chargers’ season couldn’t be off to a worse start. That’s precisely why the Dallas Cowboys should trade for Khalil Mack as they could use some depth off the edge. This is an interesting move because they don’t need someone as good as Mack that should be an every-down player, but at the same time, they can’t pass up on the chance to get any depth.

title: 49ers star edge rusher Nick Bosa suffered a calf injury and could miss next week’s game vs. the Broncos
summary: According to ESPN’s lead league insider Adam Schefter, 49ers five-time Pro Bowl defensive end Nick Bosa suffered a calf injury during practice this week and is expected to miss a “few weeks,” and the team is determining whether Bosa will land on the injured reserve or not. This is relevant to the Broncos because they […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 09: Nick Bosa #97 of the San Francisco 49ers works out during a San Fransisco 49ers Practice Session at AAMI Park on September 09, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Morgan Hancock/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to ESPN’s lead league insider Adam Schefter, 49ers five-time Pro Bowl defensive end Nick Bosa suffered a calf injury during practice this week and is expected to miss a “few weeks,” and the team is determining whether Bosa will land on the injured reserve or not. This is relevant to the Broncos because they will head to Santa Clara next week to take on Kyle Shanahan’s 49ers, who could be down their star pass rusher for this key matchup. Five-time Pro-Bowl DE Nick Bosa pulled his calf during Thursday’s practice and now is expected to miss “a few weeks”, including Sunday’s game vs. the Cardinals, sources tell me and @RapSheet . The team is figuring out whether or not Bosa needs to be placed on injured reserve. pic.twitter.com/eQIb7JBKut — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 25, 2026 The Broncos have caught some injury breaks in recent weeks, with Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua both unlikely to play on Sunday Night. Now, their opponent next week, the 49ers, could be down their star pass rusher Nick Bosa while continuing to suffer injury blows throughout their roster. Now, things can change in a week, but it does sound unlikely that Bosa will be back and healthy in a week due to the wording of Schefter’s tweet. The Broncos’ offensive line is considered one of, if not the best units in the NFL. However, they struggled with the rest of the team in Week 1 but did bounce back and perform better in Week 2. They will face a tough Rams front 7 on Sunday Night before heading to Santa Clara to take on a banged-up 49ers roster, potentially being down their star pass rusher. For now, the Broncos have to take care of business on Sunday Night vs. the Rams and hopefully improve to 2-1 on the season with back-to-back impressive wins against two of the better teams in the NFL. If they can do that, they can turn their attention to the potentially Bosa-less 49ers with the hopes of improving to 3-1, or if all goes wrong on Sunday Night, getting back to .500 at 2-2. Since Sean Payton has taken over the Broncos, they have been the least injured team in the NFL, which is a big reason for their success. They need to continue to stay healthy while also taking advantage of teams not being at full strength. Do that, and the Broncos will be one of the best teams in the NFL once again this season.
author: Scotty Payne

title: Rams WR Puka Nacua is listed as doubtful for Sunday Night’s game vs. the Broncos
summary: It appears the Broncos could catch a major break on Sunday Night. According to Sarah Barshop, who covers the Los Angeles Rams for ESPN, star WR Puka Nacua did not practice for a third straight day on Friday and was later listed as doubtful for Sunday Night’s game vs. the Broncos by the Rams. Nacua […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 25: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams runs during an NFC Championship NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on January 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images It appears the Broncos could catch a major break on Sunday Night. According to Sarah Barshop, who covers the Los Angeles Rams for ESPN, star WR Puka Nacua did not practice for a third straight day on Friday and was later listed as doubtful for Sunday Night’s game vs. the Broncos by the Rams. Puka Nacua will not practice and will be listed as doubtful for the game against the Broncos. — Sarah Barshop (@sarahbarshop) September 25, 2026 Nacua is dealing with a hip/groin injury and was trending this way all week and now is listed as doubtful and seems unlikely to play on Sunday Night. This is a major break for the Broncos, who will avoid playing star edge rusher Myles Garrett and star wide receiver Puka Nacua. Both players are among, or in the case of Garrett, the best player in their position group, so the Broncos will need to capitalize on this opportunity against a Rams team that will not be 100%. With that said, this is still a talented Rams team that dominated the New York Giants on Monday Night without both players. Veteran wide receiver Davante Adams turned back the clock and had a vintage, dominant performance vs. the Giants, and the Rams still have the returning Aaron Donald and a talented Rams front 7 even without Garrett. Broncos cornerbacks Pat Surtain, Riley Moss, and Ja’Quan McMillian will be tested on Sunday Night. Even without Nacua, the Rams and reigning NFL MVP Matthew Stafford are expected to throw the ball. They also have a strong running game and love to utilize their tight ends in the passing game. Those two things have been an area of weakness in the past for the Broncos’ defense, and I expect the Rams and head coach Sean McVay to try to exploit that. While it looked murky at the start of the week, the Broncos will have veteran starter JK Dobbins and second-year back RJ Harvey back from injuries. Both were dealing with hamstring issues but are good to go for Sunday Night. However, talented breakout rookie Jonah Coleman has been ruled out due to a sprained ankle, which has, for the time being, slowed down that hype train. The Broncos will look to lean on their run game early on and hope quarterback Bo Nix and explosive wide receiver Jaylen Waddle can get them going and have a rare fast start to the game. This should be a fun game between two teams with Super Bowl hopes, and hopefully, the Broncos can continue their dominance at Mile High and improve to 2-1 on the season with a victory over the Rams.
author: Scotty Payne

title: Broncos vs. Rams: 3 Players to Watch in Week 3
summary: The Denver Broncos host the Los Angeles Rams for their Week 3 gridiron matchup in primetime on Sunday Night Football. In order for the Broncos to achieve their second victory of the season, these are three players need to stand out in a big way tomorrow evening. Zach Allen — Defensive Lineman It was a […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars is pursued by Zach Allen #99 of the Denver Broncos during the second quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos host the Los Angeles Rams for their Week 3 gridiron matchup in primetime on Sunday Night Football . In order for the Broncos to achieve their second victory of the season, these are three players need to stand out in a big way tomorrow evening. Zach Allen — Defensive Lineman It was a night and day difference for the Broncos’ defense when comparing their execution in Week 1 versus Week 2. One player who really stood out to me in their comeback win over the Jaguars was defensive lineman Zach Allen. Allen may have not been a monster on the traditional stat sheet, but he was consistently applying pressure on Trevor Lawrence all game long. He made their interior offensive line look bad (especially rookie left guard Emmanuel Pregnon) and was a key reason Lawrence had a poor performance through the air. The eighth-year pro has been a tremendous player for the franchise since coming over alongside Vance Joseph from the Arizona Cardinals in 2023. There’s no doubt he is one of Denver’s best players, and certainly one of the most underrated defensive linemen in the National Football League. In order to slow down Matthew Stafford and aerial attack of the Rams, Allen’s pass rushing prowess will have to be on display. Over the past few seasons, Los Angeles has done a good job protecting Stafford and giving him plenty of time to hit his array of weapons from the pocket. I’m optimistic Allen will rise to the occasion and cause issues on Sunday night. Riley Moss — Cornerback The secondary performed well last Sunday against the Jaguars. Outside of a few busted plays, their coverage was sound and their starting trio at cornerback did an incredible job limiting Trevor Lawrence’s impact through the air. I felt all of them had some great plays throughout the game. After a few bad plays in Week 1, cornerback Riley Moss came back with a vengeance. His second half interception was a crucial play in the game. It served as a big momentum shift that helped earn the Broncos their first win of the season. The Rams boast two great receivers in Davante Adams and Puka Nacua. Though it does seem unlikely that Nacua is going to play due to injury. Regardless, I do expect there to be situations where Moss has to go up against Adams—unless the Broncos opt for a defensive gameplan that permanently fixates Patrick Surtain II on him. Either way, I expect Moss to be targeted often. This offseason, Moss discussed the importance of getting stronger and being more physical at the catch point going up against big receivers. He’ll certainly have an opportunity to do that in primetime. The Broncos will need him to be at his best to keep the Rams’ passing attack from taking off at Mile High. Luke Wattenberg — Center The Broncos’ offensive line faces another big test this going up against defensive front seven of the Rams. They have a handful of quality players that have to be kept in check. Denver’s big men up front are going to have to do well to protect Bo Nix. Additionally, they will need block well to jumpstart their running game to have a shot at winning. Through two games, I think there is certainly improvement to be had from Denver’s offensive line unit. Routinely ranked as one of the NFL’s best heading into the season, they haven’t been firing on all cylinders thus far. One particular offensive lineman that I will be keeping a close eye on is center Luke Wattenberg. Wattenberg has struggled with some of his snaps this season. He has also been susceptible to giving up interior pressure and dealing with blitzes and stunts. There will be times Aaron Donald is likely isolated on him in one-on-one matchups. Despite coming out of retirement and not playing for several years, Donald had nearly a 28-percent pass rush win rate against the New York Giants. The fifth-year center is going to need to perform well on Sunday Night Football to keep the future Hall of Famer in check. Denver can’t afford to get beat up the middle if they want to let Nix step up into the pocket and rip it and establish their running attack.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Future Broncos: 2 Rising Prospects to Watch in Week 4 of NCAA Football Season
summary: Another weekend, another installment of Future Broncos. In the first three weeks, we have highlighted nine prospects from entirely different position groups. Moving forward, there will certainly be overlap at certain positions. In the comments section, a few people talked about more tight ends and linebackers. That’s why two rising prospects will be on the […]
full_text: Another weekend, another installment of Future Broncos . In the first three weeks, we have highlighted nine prospects from entirely different position groups. Moving forward, there will certainly be overlap at certain positions. In the comments section, a few people talked about more tight ends and linebackers. That’s why two rising prospects will be on the radar this week for discussion. Without further ado, here are my trio of prospects for Broncos Country to watch today in Week 4 of the college football season. Luke Reynolds — Tight End — Virginia Tech Oregon standout Jamari Johnson was the first tight end I mentioned as a potential first-round target for the Broncos next April. Truth be told, I wasn’t planning to do another tight end so early on in the season. However, after his dominant performance against Maryland last week and start to the ‘26 season, Virginia Tech standout Luke Reynolds is worth mentioning. Reynolds began his collegiate career at Penn State. As a freshman in 2024, he played in sixteen games and had just nine catches for 111 yards and one touchdown. That’s not impressive production, but it’s worth nothing he was backing up future first-round pick Tyler Warren. As a sophomore, he split time with two other players in a heavy rotation at the position. His production as a receiver went up a smidge and finished the year with 26 catches for 257 yards. He was also a key inline blocker for running backs Nicholas Singleton and Kaytron Allen to bolster Penn State’s rushing attack. A coaching change with the Nittany Lions coupled with many of their key offensive starters going to the 2026 NFL Draft were big reasons Reynolds transferred to Virginia Tech this year. The decision looks to be wise with respect to his draft stock which is now soaring. In three games with the Hokies thus far, he has 25 catches for 265 yards and 4 touchdowns. He is coming off a 12 catch, 107-yard, and one touchdown performance against the Terrapins. It took a few years, but everyone watching is beginning to see why he was the nation’s top potential recruit several years ago. He may not be a top-tier athlete but is savvy finding spots against zone coverage and has the toughness to break tackles and create yards after the catch. Prospects who can move the chains, be a threat in the redzone, and propel the run game with good blocking are in high demand across the league. If Reynolds keeps this level of play up, he should easily be a Top 50 selection next Spring as an early declarant. In my opinion, he is a terrific fit for Head Coach Sean Payton’s offense. Reynolds can do it all. You can catch the junior in action when the undefeated Hokies head on the road take on Boston College for an ACC matchup this morning. Ben Roberts — Linebacker — Texas Tech Last year, readers of Future Broncos were definitely high on linebacker Jacob Rodriguez. Watching him, you would have undoubtedly seen his teammate Ben Roberts making his fair share of plays too. One of the best off-ball linebacker prospects in the nation, Roberts is hoping to build upon a junior season where he posted 90 tackles and 4 interceptions. Entering his fourth year as a starter for the Red Raiders, Roberts is an imposing prospect at 6’3” and 245 pounds. That’s NFL ready size. If prospects who force turnovers are high on your list, the fifth-year senior is one of the best prospects this cycle. Over his collegiate career, he has half a dozen interceptions to his name and nearly an identical number of forced fumbles. Quite simply, #13 is a turnover magnet. For those wanting to see better coverage chops from Denver’s linebacking corps, Roberts really stands out. He was a multi-star athlete in high school and played defensive back. With his safety background, it shouldn’t be a s surprise he touts top-notch coverage skills as a linebacker. That being said, no prospect is perfect and there are a few things he needs to work on. This season, I’m hoping to see some improvement and consistency in the run game. He added weight and strength this offseason to do better at shedding blocks. He has over 300 career tackles, but very few of those have been behind the line of scrimmage. I believe he can do a much better job with diagnosis and his pursuit angles. In 2025, he had nine missed tackles—but his sub-8-percent missed tackle rate is slightly better than average for the position. For whatever reason, I’ve seen Roberts ranked as a Day 3 prospect on a lot of consensus boards. That seems pretty wild. I’d wager a four-year starter that has played at an incredibly high level with his traits and production will be a Top 64 selection in the ‘27 NFL Draft—even with the rough edges and flaws that need rounding out. If you’re still banging the “Broncos need to draft an inside linebacker!” drum, you can catch Roberts in action when the eleventh ranked Red Raiders host Sam Houston this morning. It’ll be a cakewalk game for them, and I expect Roberts to put on a dominant performance.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Davis Webb did exactly what he needed to do to get Broncos back on track
summary: The regular season is already flying by it seems. We’re already heading into Week 3 and the Denver Broncos will be in prime time again — this time on Sunday Night Football to host the Los Angeles Rams. For both teams, the start to the season began with disaster and segued into a strong performance. […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - SEPTEMBER 20: Offensive coordinator Davis Webb of the Denver Broncos reacts to a penalty called against his unit during the second quarter against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, September 20, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The regular season is already flying by it seems. We’re already heading into Week 3 and the Denver Broncos will be in prime time again — this time on Sunday Night Football to host the Los Angeles Rams. For both teams, the start to the season began with disaster and segued into a strong performance. In Denver, that first week was met with some serious meltdowns from fans over new offensive coordinator Davis Webb and him seemingly getting outplayed at every turn by Kansas City Chief defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo. In hindsight, going up against a multi-decade experienced defensive coordinator like Spags was probably not a great way to start ones career as a new offensive coordinator. Head Coach Sean Payton was asked this week when calling plays began to feel natural to him and he sure wasn’t sure how to answer that one which makes me think maybe a coach can never get too comfortable when they are the play caller. “There’s a learning curve, always, and then I think the most important thing is it’s not plays within the scheme, it’s players,” Payton said. “So you’re constantly moving relative to what you have. I can look at ‘06 New Orleans, I can look at ‘09, 2013, 2017 and you would be like, ‘Man, there’s some…’ But there were a lot of changes too relative to who and I think the same here or there’s some fundamental things that we want to do and yet you also move in the direction of what the skill set allows.” It seems like he just likes to remember the good seasons when he had the most fun calling plays. I suppose that would make it feel more natural when everything is going the right way. That answer did lead to another question about Davis Webb directly and whether or not he was evaluated unfairly after that first week. “Yes, I think every scenario is different,” Payton said. “I think just being yourself in the process during the week and getting to the things that we think are going to fit. I think all those things go into it, but I think in each case they’re all somewhat a little different.” And his response leads back to the whole going up against a guy like Spags in your first game as play caller. Not the ideal situation, but how Webb handled the black eye and followed it up with a stellar performance calling plays in the team’s win over the Jacksonville Jaguars is a huge check in the box for him. Of course, at the end of the day the players executed last week and did not the previous week. As fans we can point to that, but again it would be on the coaches to have the players prepared in the first place. I personally think Webb is going to be just fine and so will the Broncos. author: Tim Lynch

title: Sean Payton pleased with performance of Evan Engram and Nate Adkins thus far
summary: One area the Denver Broncos hope to improve upon this season is the impact their group of tight ends make on offense. Last year, the group failed to impress and didn’t make a lot of big plays through the air. Instead of pursuing a major addition in free agency, the Broncos opted to run it […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Evan Engram #1 of the Denver Broncos runs with the ball during the fourth quarter of the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images One area the Denver Broncos hope to improve upon this season is the impact their group of tight ends make on offense. Last year, the group failed to impress and didn’t make a lot of big plays through the air. Instead of pursuing a major addition in free agency, the Broncos opted to run it back with most of their players at the position. A big free agent signing during the 2025 offseason, Evan Engram wasn’t the ‘joker’ player the team thought he would be last season. Though in his first two games of his 2026 season with the squad, Engram has made the most of the opportunities that have gone his way. Yesterday after practice, Head Coach Sean Payton pointed out that he was impressed with how Evan Engram was doing early on this season in his second year with the team. “He’s doing well. He’s had a catch in each game, there’s some things he gives you in the passing game, and I think he’s blocking well, so I’m excited for him. I think he’s shown, especially in regard to protections and certain things, he gives you that threat. He’s doing well within the role,” stated Payton. Last season, Engram caught 50 passes for 461 yards and just 1 touchdown. Those were some of the lowest production totals in his NFL career. In two games, Engram has caught five of six targets for 60 yards and a touchdown with four of those receptions moving the chains for a first down. Payton also remarked that he was impressed with the work Engram had put in over the offseason and training camp to improve his blocking. In turn, that has led to more reps on the field and involvement in helping in the run game. Thus far, the ten-year veteran has been on the field for 57-percent of Denver’s offensive plays—a fifteen percent jump from 2025. In addition to Engram, Payton is pleased with what third-year tight end Nate Adkins has achieved. Third in Denver’s trio of tight ends behind Adam Trautman and the aforementioned Engram, Adkins has been a versatile player for Denver’s offense and is looking to rebound after missing almost half of last year due to injury. Thus far, he has been a key blocker to kickstart Denver’s rushing attack. Moreover, he recently flashed as a safety outlet for quarterback Bo Nix. Last week in their comeback victory over the Jaguars, Adkins had a quality performance. He hauled in three receptions on three targets for 32 yards and a touchdown. Since signing with the Broncos as an undrafted free agent in 2024, he has been an underrated player in the team’s offensive endeavors. Payton noted the aforementioned, but also his special teams’ abilities as something that has stood out to him early on making him a valuable member of the team. “He does a lot of things well. He can play in the kicking game; he blocks well. I don’t want to use the word Swiss Army Knife, but he’s one of those guys where once you describe the assignment, he’s really good blocking in space. You see some of that carry over into the kicking game.” Over the course of the season, the Broncos will need Engram and Adkins to continue to be quality contributors. With Jaylen Waddle in the fold, there will be less targets to go around for Denver’s tight end group, but if they can maximize the opportunities that come their way like they have thus far, the offense should be a lot more consistent than they were a season ago.

title: Broncos vs Rams 5 questions: What does Aaron Donald’s return mean for LA?
summary: Aaron Donald is back. Unfortunately, or fortunately for the Denver Broncos, Myles Garrett is on IR. But bringing back one of the best defensive linemen in NFL history to a defense is obviously huge. That’s one of the reasons the Los Angeles Rams were heavy favorites to win the Super Bowl heading into the season […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams warms up prior to the game against the New York Giants at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Aaron Donald is back. Unfortunately, or fortunately for the Denver Broncos, Myles Garrett is on IR. But bringing back one of the best defensive linemen in NFL history to a defense is obviously huge. That’s one of the reasons the Los Angeles Rams were heavy favorites to win the Super Bowl heading into the season and still are the favorites. Offensively, LA has the reigning MVP and an explosive offense. So what does the return of Donald mean? To get a feel for the Rams and how big it was to get their first win against the New York Giants, we go “behind enemy lines” with Evan Craig from Turf Show Times . MHR: How important was that win over the New York Giants on Monday night? What was different between the first two games Evan : The win was extremely important and exactly what the doctor ordered. Los Angeles looked all out of sorts in Week 1, and the 49ers took full advantage. New York really didn’t stand a chance, even if Jaxson Dart had never gotten injured. The Rams poured too many resources into improving this offseason, and they weren’t about to let the Giants ruin that by dropping them to 0-2. I will say, there are things to clean up, especially as LA was only up 11 at halftime. It should’ve been much worse, but back-to-back turnovers on a Matthew Stafford pick and a signature Kyren Williams fumble momentarily gave the G-Men hope. Still, it was a night-and-day difference. It helped that the Rams, as Sean McVay eloquently put it, didn’t have a “dumbass” travel plan ahead of the game. Much of their awful showing in Australia was due to the fact that they arrived a day before the game. Several new pieces needed to gel together, but it was mainly due to the travel plan MHR: What does the return of Aaron Donald mean for the Rams defense and the team? Evan : Aaron Donald’s return means a great deal to this team, and Monday night was a huge reminder of why. During the win over the Giants, AD didn’t put together much of a stat line, yet his presence was felt on every one of his 33 snaps. It was also as if he had never left, with his power and burst on full display. That was impressive to see in someone who was two years removed from the game. I guess that fitness regimen he was on during retirement certainly paid off. If he gets better as the season progresses, and it’s very likely he does, that should scare all opposing offensive coordinators. Now, imagine what will happen once Myles Garrett returns. Did anyone else get chills? At first, Donald’s return seemed like nothing more than a gimmick and an unnecessary distraction for a team aiming for another Super Bowl run. Gimmick might not be the correct word, as he seemed genuine about returning, even if a large percentage of the NFL world was doubting it. Clearly, Rams fans can see he’s committed to helping the team secure a ring. Maybe you can go home after all. MHR: How does LA get the win on Sunday night? What must the Rams do defensively and offensively? Evan : LA will get the win if they take a page out of the Chiefs’ Week 1 playbook. Kansas City rushed for 220 yards and ran the ball down the Broncos’ throats in the opener. Against the Giants, the Rams’ two-headed attack of Williams and Blake Corum combined for 164 rushing yards. They have a strong enough attack on the ground to keep Denver on its toes all game. Also, the Rams must have better pass distribution. Davante Adams and Terrance Ferguson combined for 19 targets when no other pass catcher had more than two targets. Spreading the ball out will help take the pressure off Adams, especially if Puka Nacua’s out. The Rams have a diverse array of playmakers to make this happen. Defensively, the Rams must make the Broncos one-dimensional. Denver doesn’t have the strongest running game, but if LA can take away that run game and put a ton of pressure on Bo Nix, they can secure the win. Nix is a very capable quarterback, yet assuming the Rams follow KC’s playbook, they can limit his effectiveness by taking away his new favorite target in Jaylen Waddle and security blankets Courtland Sutton and Troy Franklin. MHR: What do you make of the current spread? And what is your best bet for the game? Evan : I think 2.5 points is a fair spread, but I don’t like LA as the favorite. Denver is a really tough place to play, and the Broncos deserve more credit as a team, even if they haven’t had the smoothest start to begin the season. Yes, I believe the Rams are a better team on paper when they’re at full strength, yet they’re without Garrett and possibly Puka for this one. That, to me, feels like the sportsbooks are disrespecting Denver, at least this week, which wouldn’t be the first time for them. My best bet is Matthew Stafford under 200 passing yards. The Broncos have a far superior secondary than the Giants, meaning they won’t allow Davante Adams to run wild on them if, again, Nacua is out again this week. MHR: How does this game unfold, and what is your prediction? Evan : This is a tough game to predict, since the Rams are typically slow starters to begin the season. Last season was their best start in years, and it was only with a 3-2 record. The Broncos were in the same boat in 2025 because they began the year 1-2 before winning 13 of their next 14 games to finish the season and clinch the top seed. That said, I wouldn’t be surprised if the Rams drop this one, which would certainly spell trouble among the fan base right before they travel to Philly. I also expect this to be a low-scoring game due to the strength of both defenses. The first one to 20 should win this one, and I expect it to be Denver. Broncos 21, Rams 17

title: Scouting the Enemy: Los Angeles Rams
summary: The Denver Broncos host the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football. Both teams are coming off impressive Week 2 wins after faltering in their season openers. Here is a deeper look at the Broncos’ Week 3 opponent. 2025 Los Angeles Rams Season Review The Rams finished their 2025 regular season with a 12-5 record […]
full_text: Inglewood, CA - November 02: Head coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams reqxcts with quarterback Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams after a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints in the first half of a NFL football game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood on Sunday, November 2, 2025. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The Denver Broncos host the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football. Both teams are coming off impressive Week 2 wins after faltering in their season openers. Here is a deeper look at the Broncos’ Week 3 opponent. 2025 Los Angeles Rams Season Review The Rams finished their 2025 regular season with a 12-5 record earning second place in the NFC West. They would go on to lose the NFC Championship game to the Seattle Seahawks 31-27. 2026 Los Angeles Rams Offseason Additions and Departures After failing to make the Super Bowl, General Manager Les Snead made a series of high-profile trades and moves this offseason. The big focus was on improving their defense. They made a gargantuan trade with the Cleveland Browns to acquire Myles Garrett. However, he suffered a knee injury in Week 1 and won’t be available for their matchup versus the Broncos on Sunday Night Football . They also made a trade with the Kansas City Chiefs for star cornerback Trent McDuffie to improve their secondary. Versatile defensive back Jaylen Watson was also added into the mix on a three-year deal. And the big surprise? Defensive lineman Aaron Donald came out of retirement to help the team’s pursuit of another Lombardi Trophy. Instead of getting a player to help them win now in the 2026 NFL Draft , the Rams picked Alabama quarterback Ty Simpson in the first round. With Matthew Stafford getting up there in age, it’s understandable, but a lot of their fan base was certainly hoping for a player that could have provided a year one impact for the team. In the second round, they took Ohio State tight end Max Klare—another curious decision since they brought back Tyler Higbee and had drafted Terrance Ferguson in the second round in the 2025 NFL Draft. Offensive X-Factor: Quarterback Matthew Stafford A handful of players could have earned this designation for the Rams. However, choosing last year’s MVP makes the most sense. That’s longtime quarterback Matthew Stafford who is in his eighteenth season in the NFL. Stafford’s productivity and longevity will certainly result in him eventually being enshrined in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Last season, Stafford threw for 4,707 yards and 46 touchdowns with just 8 interceptions. It was arguably one of the best seasons by a signal caller in NFL history. The Rams touted the best offense in the NFL in 2025. His primary target last season was Puka Nacua, who reeled in 129 of 166 targets for 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns. However, his availability for Sunday’s primetime matchup is uncertain and it seems unlikely he will be able to play. Even so, Davante Adams gives them a top-notch wide receiver. Adams was the Rams’ second leading receiver with 60 receptions on 114 targets for 789 yards and 14 touchdowns last year. He is coming off a huge game versus the New York Giants where he had nearly 200 receiving yards and two touchdowns. The longtime veteran could be a huge problem for Denver. There’s no doubt the Rams have a prolific passing attack with Stafford at the helm. He’s also been a hard quarterback to sack over the years. Dialing up the heat on Stafford and limiting Adams’ impact will be crucial for Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph. They can’t let their passing attack go wild on Sunday Night Football . Defensive X-Factor: Cornerback Trent McDuffie Myles Garrett certainly would have earned my designation here, but he won’t be playing. That’s good news for the Broncos. Aaron Donald earned some consideration, but I ultimately wound up going with two-time All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie. The Rams gave up a lot of draft capital to acquire McDuffie and gave him one of the biggest contracts at the position in NFL history. In his first two games for the Rams, so far so good for the fifth-year cornerback. McDuffie has been targeted six times and allowed four receptions for just 23 yards. Against the Giants, he was able to pick off Jameis Winston after starting quarterback Jaxson Dart left the game due to injury. Bo Nix already has a few bad decisions and turnovers this season. Denver can’t afford to have him get picked off by McDuffie in primetime. It’ll be interesting to see who McDuffie ends up trailing the most in coverage. Conventional wisdom says Courtland Sutton, but with the way the Broncos are trying to involve Jaylen Waddle in their aerial attack, it wouldn’t be surprising to see McDuffie matched up against Waddle on occasion. How the Broncos can secure a victory over the Rams ICYMI: I offered a blueprint for a Broncos’ victory yesterday. This is going to be a very tough game for Denver to win, but I do like the fact Denver will have homefield advantage. Some people will discount that, but the stadium was absolutely rocking due to fan noise against the Jaguars. The Broncos need to have a strong rushing attack and have time consuming drives. This also means better execution on third down. The Rams have an offense that can strike quick and score a lot of points. This isn’t a game where I want to see Nix have to throw forty times and try and outduel Stafford. I’d also like to see them do much better with starting field position. They did not do well in this regard against the Jaguars and were routinely inside their own fifteen-yard line to begin several drives. Hopefully Marvin Mims Jr. is able to return from injury and offer some impact as a returner on special teams. And as I say most weeks—no more penalties. This is absolutely crippling the offense’s ability to be efficient. Somehow, someway, I think the Broncos will squeak out a victory in primetime. Hart’s Prediction: Broncos 24, Rams 23.

title: New York Jets vs. Detroit Lions Week 3 preview: 6 key stats
summary: It’ll have been a long ten days for the Detroit Lions fan base between games against AFC East foes, and they’ll gladly welcome the challenge of taking on old friend Aaron Glenn. His New York Jets nearly started 2-0 before coughing up a fourth-quarter lead to the Green Bay Packers last week. Glenn’s Jets—who haven’t […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 18: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions throws the ball during the first half against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on December 18, 2022 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’ll have been a long ten days for the Detroit Lions fan base between games against AFC East foes, and they’ll gladly welcome the challenge of taking on old friend Aaron Glenn. His New York Jets nearly started 2-0 before coughing up a fourth-quarter lead to the Green Bay Packers last week. Glenn’s Jets—who haven’t made the playoffs since Dan Campbell was in his first year of coaching in 2010—appear ready to put up more of a fight than some expected throughout the offseason. It’ll be a good challenge for the Lions to continue improving and should be anything but a penciled-in win. Below are my six-pack of key stats and matchups for the Lions’ return home looking to make improvements from their mini-bye. Note: Unless otherwise indicated, all statistics are sourced from NFL Pro, FTN Fantasy, Pro Football Reference, SumerSports, or Pro Football Focus. Precious Cargo After finishing in the bottom half of the league with 23 giveaways last year, the Jets—and especially their signal caller Geno Smith—have suddenly stopped making the costly mistakes that give opponents the football. Smith finished second in the NFL in giveaways and threw a league-high 17 interceptions in only 15 miserable starts last season. Through two weeks, that has completely flipped. Only two offenses in the NFL have yet to turn the ball over: the New York Jets and Buffalo Bills. Creating those takeaways is more challenging for the Detroit Lions defense without turnover machine Kerby Joseph. Still, they started the season by forcing three turnovers against the Saints in Week 1, tying their most in a game under defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard. The Lions have now forced three turnovers in four different games under Sheppard, but obviously weren’t able to take the ball away from Josh Allen and the Bills offense last week. Since Sheppard took over as defensive coordinator at the start of last season, the Lions are 9-3 when forcing at least one turnover and a perfect 6-0 when forcing two or more . When they haven’t been able to force a turnover and play complementary football, they’re just 1-6. Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell have displayed a prowess for punching the pill out, but the question remains: Who else on this Lions roster can prove to be a playmaker and take the football away? This defense may not be able to consistently stop the Jets offense—or other offenses this season—and simply force them off the field. That makes generating turnovers imperative, starting against one of only two offenses that has yet to give the ball away. Jettsetting Smith Keeping the Jets grounded will be a challenge. Turnovers are one thing, but the Lions also need to find areas where they can clip Geno Smith’s wings. In three games against the Lions as Seattle’s starting quarterback, Smith averaged nearly 350 passing yards per game alongside a 60.3% passing success rate, 8.2 yards per attempt, and a 107.2 passer rating—all figures that would have ranked top three among quarterbacks last season. One area where the Detroit Lions might struggle to contain Smith is if they remain dead-set on throwing the kitchen sink at him instead of being more selective. The Lions’ blitz rate has jumped from 31.7% (8th) last year to 42.2% (5th) this season, and that aggressiveness could cost them against Smith. While the Packers were able to generate a little heat on Smith late in the game, for the most part, the Jets offense has succeeded when defenses bring extra rushers. Against the blitz this season, Smith is 14-for-18 passing for 177 yards, with a 77.8% completion percentage (4th), 9.8 yards per attempt (3rd), +0.18 EPA/dropback (8th), a 61.1% passing success rate (5th), and a 16.7% explosive pass rate (3rd). The last thing the Lions defense should do is take defenders out of coverage and help turn the Jets into a top-10 passing attack. Their best bet may be to try to win with four up front and allocate more ammunition to the back end. Red-Eye Zone The Detroit Lions defense has had its well-broadcasted struggles this season, and the red zone has been no different. They have allowed touchdowns on nine of ten red-zone possessions, with their 90% red-zone touchdown rate ranking fourth-highest in the NFL. The Jets offense has scored a touchdown on four of six red-zone possessions so far this season, but when you double-click into the numbers, they’ve been even better when the field shrinks and the defense essentially gains a 12th defender with the back of the end zone. In the red zone, the Jets offense has successfully moved the ball with +0.37 EPA/play (5th) and a 60.0% success rate (4th), finding success in the margins by bulldozing its way to a top-three yards-before-contact mark in the run game while also ranking top 10 in yards after catch. Holding Smith, Breece Hall, and Garrett Wilson to three points—or even forcing a turnover—on just one trip inside the 20 would be huge. So far, about the only thing that has consistently stopped the Jets’ operation in the red zone has been itself, with three penalties, the second-most in the NFL. Prior to last year, the Lions defense had developed a bend-but-don’t-break identity, winning situational football in the red zone and on third down under defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn. Week 3 provides an opportunity for Kelvin Sheppard’s unit to start taking a step back in that direction. Protecting the Pilot For the third straight week, the Lions defense will face a formidable, well-built offensive line. The banner players are the bookend recent first-round offensive tackles, Olu Fashanu and Armand Membou, but the Jets also added one starter this offseason who caught my attention: left guard Dylan Parham, a player I highlighted as a potential bargain-bin option for the Detroit Lions in free agency and my favorite available guard in terms of value. The former high school tight end and triple jumper moved all across the offensive line at Memphis and with the Las Vegas Raiders, but is now able to concentrate on left guard. Through the first two weeks of the season, he is off to a career-year start. Parham is PFF’s highest-rated guard with a 92.8 PFF offensive grade through two weeks. Parham has always been a strong run blocker and appears to be putting it all together next to Fashanu, while also excelling as a pass protector. He has allowed only six hurries across 78 pass-blocking repetitions without surrendering a sack or quarterback hit, while also avoiding any penalties. Parham playing at this high of a level will challenge Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams, and Skyler Gill-Howard to outperform him and win on the interior for the Lions defense. Shutting down the Jets’ inside run game and generating pressure on Smith up the middle will be two areas of focus, and Detroit’s defensive tackles will have their hands full trying to disrupt the protection around the pilot. Early Departure The Jets defense, now with Aaron Glenn calling plays and bolstered by the reunion with stalwart linebacker Demario Davis and the addition of second-overall pick David Bailey, has surprisingly been much improved through its first two games—even while extending its streak without an interception to 19 straight games. The Jets defense ranks second in yards per play allowed (4.0), tied for fourth in EPA/play (-0.25), ninth in success rate (39.4%), and third in defensive DVOA (-29.7%). They’ve done it while, interestingly, playing nickel defense at a top-five rate on nearly 78% of their snaps, using the second-lightest average box in the league, and playing the third-fewest snaps with eight or more defenders in the box. Even with that lighter personnel usage—a stark contrast from Glenn’s tenure with the Lions—they’ve beaten the pulp out of the…

full_text: Does Madden 27 have any true predictive power when it comes to real NFL games? Based on my experience, the answer is almost certainly no. Madden is crazy, random, and illogical so many times that we run our Madden sims that no one should be taking these seriously. But for the first two weeks of the season, Madden hasn’t been too far off from the actual results for the Detroit Lions’ 2026 season. Here’s how our Madden sims have played out thus far: Week 1 vs. Saints Actual score: 31-30 Lions (OT) Madden score: 27-17 Lions (click link to watch the simulation Week 2 at Bills: Actual Score: 41-31 Bills Madden score: 31-23 Bills So what does Madden 27 think of this week’s matchup between the Detroit Lions and New York Jets? You’ll have to watch live to find out. Saturday morning at 10 a.m. ET, I’ll fire up a game of Madden 27 and let the computer face the computer for a full simulation. title: Discussion: Who will be the Detroit Lions’ MVP vs. the Jets?
summary: The Detroit Lions will be the first to tell you that good, fundamentally sound football requires the effort and skill of 11 players working in harmony. That was painfully obvious last Thursday night, when just about every play had one or two players not doing their assignment, and it made the entire team look disjointed […]
full_text: Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta (87) makes a catch against Minnesota Vikings during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, November 2, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions will be the first to tell you that good, fundamentally sound football requires the effort and skill of 11 players working in harmony. That was painfully obvious last Thursday night, when just about every play had one or two players not doing their assignment, and it made the entire team look disjointed against the Bills. Obviously, in order to turn things around this week against the New York Jets, the Lions need to get everyone on the same page. But even if they do, it will still require heroic efforts from individuals to move Detroit to 2-1 through three weeks. So today’s Question of the Day is: Who will be the Lions’ MVP against the Jets? My answer: I think this could be a big Sam LaPorta game. This week Scottie Montgomery basically said that teams were surprisingly not double-teaming Amon-Ra St. Brown, and they were totally fine just feeding the All-Pro receiver until someone tried to stop them. “When Saint continues to play at the level that he plays at, we will start to see something that we haven’t seen quite as much this year—maybe because of the training camp that Jameson (Williams) had—we haven’t seen as much double (teams) on Saint, which is allowing him to get some one-on-one situations,” Montgomery said. But what he said next is where I’m going with this. Montgomery knows Jets coach Aaron Glenn knows how St. Brown can take over a game, and he’s betting he won’t let him. “I know that that’s the last thing that he wants to see, Saint running around,” Montgomery said. Whether the Jets will be able to contain St. Brown is a matter of opinion, but I do believe that will be their focus this week—especially considering how leaky the Jets’ middle of the defense is. Now, that may open up opportunities for Williams deep this week, but personally, I think LaPorta will benefit most. If the Jets’ best linebackers and safeties are providing bracket coverage for St. Brown, that should leave LaPorta to operate over the rest of the field. On top of that, I still believe LaPorta’s impact in the run game is underappreciated. The offensive line may need some extra help with a pretty strong Jets offensive line, and LaPorta could be the key to help Jahmyr Gibbs break a big run or two that could shift the game. title: Dan Campbell presser takeaways: Lions’ zone coverage increase, update on OL health
summary: Most of the stories for the week have been written by Friday when it comes to the NFL. Fans are just ready for the games after a week of endless chatter. But every week in the Detroit Lions calendar ends with a Dan Campbell press conference on Friday, and, generally speaking, it can be a […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - SEPTEMBER 13: Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell talks during his post-game press conference following a regular season NFL football game between the New Orleans Saints and the Detroit Lions on September 13, 2026 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Most of the stories for the week have been written by Friday when it comes to the NFL. Fans are just ready for the games after a week of endless chatter. But every week in the Detroit Lions calendar ends with a Dan Campbell press conference on Friday, and, generally speaking, it can be a fairly news heavy. So moving forward, I plan on posting the main takeaways from Campbell’s pressers on Friday as one last news dump for the week. Offensive line health update The Lions currently have four offensive linemen on the injury report: LG Christian Mahogany (hip) LG Ben Bartch (foot) RG Tate Ratledge (elbow) RT Blake Miller (knee) Campbell provided updates on three of the above. For Mahogany and Miller, who missed Thursday’s game against the Bills, it appears both should be good to go for Sunday against the Jets, barring any setback on Friday. “I think both of those guys are going to be okay, barring no setbacks today,” Campbell said. Bartch, on the other hand, doesn’t sound like he’ll be available with a foot injury. I asked Campbell if there’s any concern for a long-term injury since he’s been dealing with a foot injury all offseason. Campbell essentially shut that down. “I don’t think long-term, but it doesn’t look good for this week,” Campbell said. There was no update given on Ratledge, who has been limited in practice this week with an elbow injury. Ratledge was at practice on Friday. Why more zone coverage? A staple under both Aaron Glenn and Kelvin Sheppard has been an overreliance on man coverage. The hope is to hold up receivers long enough for pressure to get there. However, Detroit’s coverage strategy has shifted quite a bit so far this year. Through two weeks the Lions have played around 76 percent zone coverage compared to just 60 percent last year. Campbell was asked if this was a response to the personnel they had or a sign of their desire to create more turnovers. “I think it was a little bit of both. We just felt like this would suit us a little bit better up to this point and then be disruptive and get takeaways, which worked well Week 1,” Campbell said. “We had two ops last week against Buffalo we weren’t able to get, but they’re there.” Detroit has largely been using zone coverages to pair with an aggressive and disruptive front. The hope is to speed up the clock of opposing quarterbacks to make a brash decision, while disguising zone coverages on the back end to bait them into a mistake. In theory, that works, but Campbell admits they need to both do a better job getting to the quarterback and covering it cleanly on the back end. “It’s challenging and that’s why a lot of the things we’ve done in zone for the most part have been to reduce that stress level back there. But, that also requires the front getting there. And if you don’t get there, we already kind of talked about that, but there is a trust there,” Campbell said. Safety help Campbell didn’t sound optimistic about Thomas Harper’s availability this week (“I don’t know if he’s going to make it to the game”), which means the Lions will likely be down four of their top five safeties (Brian Branch, Kerby Joseph, Avonte Maddox, Harper). That has left them perilously thin at the position. To no surprise, the Lions have been playing Christian Izien at the position all week in practice, getting him the full-speed reps he needs to be ready on Sunday. “Izzy’s been working a lot back there and had a full week. And he’s gotten a ton of work and this week a ton of reps, full-speed reps,” Campbell said. “This is what you’re going to do, this is the calls and just dousing him with full speed reps and he’s done a good job this week.” He later added: “Izzy’s going to be a huge part for us.” He’ll pair with veteran Chuck Clark, but who will be Detroit’s backups? Campbell interestingly noted that rookie nickel cornerback Keith Abney could be part of that plan, along with practice squad safety Jalen Mills, who was with the team last year and was signed at the beginning of this week. That is a tough ask for Abney, but Campbell praised the rookie’s mental acumen of the game. “For a rookie, he’s a pretty dang smart, conscientious, aware football player that’s got a ton of room to really take off,” Campbell said. “So, that’s a good sign. But yeah, it can be. He’s young. He’s another one. He just needs reps and reps. But, if we need it, that’ll be a guy who may have to go in for us.” Competitive love for Aaron Glenn It’s been a bit of a love fest between Aaron Glenn and Dan Campbell this week, with both head coaches sharing admiration for each other through the media. Campbell told an amusing story about the two, comparing their competitive spirits as teammates to how the feeling will be on Sunday from opposite sidelines. “AG was like he is now, one of the greatest teammates, people you could ever be around. You could talk to him about anything: family, friends, situation, football. We’d all be together and man, we’re laughing, locker room, you go out getting ready for practice and all of a sudden it goes on. “You put your hands on him now and it goes from zero to a hundred like this. It is on. There’s no, ‘let’s work our way into this.’ It’s ‘get your hands off of me.’ And so that’s what this is a little bit like, man. We are dear close friends, but we’re competing. He wants to win, we want to win. And until that game’s over, that’s the way the game is played because we’re competitors and he is certainly a competitor. So, that’s what it’s going to be.”
