title: Jaguars vs. Patriots Injury Report: Who’s In & Out?
summary: The New England Patriots are heading into Sunday’s road matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars with one of the more significant injury lists in the early portion of the 2026 season, as the accumulation of damage from back-to-back weeks is beginning to take a toll. Jacksonville, by contrast, returns home as they have been all season. […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - SEPTEMBER 13: Davon Hamilton #52 of the Jacksonville Jaguars runs out on the field before the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Cleveland Browns on September 13, 2026 at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Fl. (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots are heading into Sunday’s road matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars with one of the more significant injury lists in the early portion of the 2026 season, as the accumulation of damage from back-to-back weeks is beginning to take a toll. Jacksonville, by contrast, returns home as they have been all season. Here is a full breakdown of everything you need to know from Friday’s injury report heading into Sunday. New England Patriots Injuries WR AJ Brown – Injured Reserve (Ankle) The Patriots’ most significant offseason acquisition is already on the shelf, as Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 1 against the Seattle Seahawks and was placed on Injured Reserve shortly after. That development was made considerably worse by the timing of the Kayshon Boutte trade. New England sent Boutte to the Houston Texans just six days before the roster cutdown deadline in exchange for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round pick. Brown’s injury immediately exposed that transaction as a risk. Brown and Boutte’s absence places the receiving burden squarely on Romeo Doubs, who signed a four-year, $68 million deal with New England this offseason. In addition to Doubs, the Patriots’ primary receiving room options are veteran receiver Mack Hollins and DeMario Douglas. RG Mike Onwenu – Injured Reserve (Ankle) Onwenu was placed on Injured Reserve on Tuesday, September 22nd, after suffering a reported broken right ankle against the Steelers. Greg Van Roten stepped in immediately after Onwenu went down but struggled in that assignment against Pittsburgh. The veteran lineman was signed by New England roughly a month ago as additional depth. Considering what Arik Armstead has shown himself to be capable of against starting caliber guards, this should provide a potential opening for a big day against a guard making his first meaningful NFL start in years. Vrabel gives injury updates ahead of Patriots-JAX. 🎥 via @Patriots pic.twitter.com/IONzFlbhiU — Wire Report NFL (@WireReportNFL) September 25, 2026 OLB Dre’Mont Jones – (Shoulder) – Out One of New England’s most significant defensive additions this offseason, Jones brought seven sacks to Foxborough and was expected to be the centerpiece of a retooled pass rush. However, Jones left the Steelers game in the second quarter with a shoulder injury, sustained after a strip-sack. With the veteran backer now ruled out Sunday, his absence creates a significant gap in New England’s edge rush depth. OLB Quintayvious Hutchins – (Knee) – Out Jones’s primary backup at linebacker also did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday, before being ruled out with a knee injury on Friday. Both a starting and backup pass rusher being simultaneously unavailable could be a significant compounding problem for the Patriots defense that held Pittsburgh to three points in Week 2, but will now face a considerably more dynamic opponent. TE Eli Raridon – (Thigh)- Questionable The Patriots’ rookie tight end, a third-round pick who scored the team’s only touchdown in the Week 1 loss to Seattle and caught a 30-yard pass before exiting in Week 2 against the Steelers, is now a legitimate game-time question after being a surprise did not participate (DNP) on Thursday or Friday following limited work Wednesday. This injury has the potential to drastically alter New England’s offensive game plan, as the Patriots ran two or more tight end formations on approximately 29% of their 2025 offensive snaps, and have increased that usage to 34% in 2026. S Craig Woodson – (Shoulder)- Questionable Woodson did not finish the Steelers game, exiting with a shoulder injury and he has not practiced since. The Boston Globe reported he was spotted wearing an arm sling in the locker room after the Week 2 victory. However, he has since shed the sling, and practiced as a limited participant Friday. His potential absence would likely force recent trade acquisition Jaylen Reed into meaningful action. Jacksonville fans will likely recognize that name, as Reed was the safety New England received in the Boutte trade with Houston and was a backup for the AFC South Texans. Jacksonville Jaguars Injuries Friday Injury Report pic.twitter.com/EaNXPr0lBj — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) September 25, 2026 Jacksonville returns to Everbank Stadium in reasonably strong health, with the primary injury considerations this week being OL Patrick Mekari and DE B.J. Green II, both on Injured Reserve for the next few weeks. DT Albert Regis – (Elbow) – Doubtful Only one additional Jaguar is expected to be unavailable heading into the weekend, rookie defensive lineman Albert Regis. Regis was added to the injury report with an elbow injury on Friday and is listed as doubtful to play Sunday. Regis’ absence does impact the Jacksonville defensive line depth, especially when facing a heavy-run, physical line such as the New England Patriots. Regis played 12 snaps against the Cleveland Browns in week one, all on defense. In Week two, he played just seven total snaps, with six coming on defense. On the positive side, great news following Davon Hamilton’s late exit from Sunday’s matchup, as the veteran defensive lineman looks to be good to play after suffering a fourth quarter back injury. And while the official Friday injury report did reflect Hamilton and running back LeQuint Allen with limited Friday sessions, neither has a game day injury designation. The Bigger Picture Over the first two weeks in New England, a compounding injury problem has developed across three distinct phases of their roster: wide receiver, offensive line, and pass rush that Jacksonville is now positioned to exploit. The loss of Onwenu and the insertion of Van Roten at right guard create a matchup that directly benefits Arik Armstead Sunday. Jones and Hutchins both being unavailable remove New England’s most impactful edge rusher and a backup from the equation simultaneously, potentially allowing Trevor Lawrence significantly more time in the pocket than he had in either of his first two games. Similarly, the loss of AJ Brown and his backup Boutte provides an opening for this Jacksonville secondary to potentially have one of its better games of 2026. However, nothing is ever guaranteed. As the 2025 Seahawks matchup showed us, even with two defensive backs and a linebacker out, an NFL defense, in the right matchup, can still perform in a dominant fashion. The Jaguars will still need to show up and play their game for a win on Sunday, no matter who lines up.

title: Chiefs-Dolphins: 5 questions with The Phinsider ahead of Week 3
summary: On Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs face the Miami Dolphins in the early window of Week 3 games. We welcome Kevin Nogle of The Phinsider — our sister SBNation site covering the Dolphins— for Five Questions with the Enemy. Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device and join the Phinsider community through Sunday’s […]
full_text: (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs face the Miami Dolphins in the early window of Week 3 games. We welcome Kevin Nogl e of The Phinsider — our sister SBNation site covering the Dolphins— for Five Questions with the Enemy . Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Join fellow Chiefs fans to react to every explosive play and game-changing moment in real time. Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device and join the Phinsider community through Sunday’s game to get perspectives from both sides of the Week 3 matchup! 1. Miami has opened the season 0-2 after losing consecutive games by double digits and being outscored 62-26. How much of this start should be viewed as the expected growing pains of a young team beginning a rebuild under Jeff Hafley, and how much should concern Dolphins fans? 1. Miami has opened the season 0-2 after losing consecutive games by double digits and being outscored 62-26. How much of this start should be viewed as the expected growing pains of a young team beginning a rebuild under Jeff Hafley, and how much should concern Dolphins fans? It should absolutely be the former. The Dolphins are the youngest team in the league this year, and they are relying on a lot of youth to get them through the season. Miami is, by far, the team leading the way in rookie snap counts this season: Rookie Snap Count % through Week 2 1. MIA 27.6% 2. CLE 16.4% 3. NYG 15.1% … 30. ARI 2.3% 31. DEN 1.1% 32. LAR 0.7% pic.twitter.com/dA2rPZ8FZV — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) September 22, 2026 This year isn’t about wins and losses; it’s about building the foundation for future seasons. They are not losing on purpose; there is no “tank” in progress, but they are probably going to have the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft because this is a complete rebuild of the franchise – from the front office through the coaching staff to the players. The Dolphins even changed presidents this offseason. That said, people are already complaining about the hire of Hafley. They are somehow surprised that the Dolphins are struggling early in this season. I have already seen some saying Miami needs to fire Hafley and move on. I have no idea how you can say that after two games, especially when none of this should surprise anyone. The Dolphins are going to struggle this year, but as long as they are looking better by the end of the season, this will be a success. 2. Through two games, Malik Willis has completed 29 of 50 passes for 417 yards, one touchdown and one interception while being sacked nine times. How would you evaluate his performance beyond the numbers, and how much of Miami’s offensive difficulty falls on Willis compared with the protection and personnel around him? I think a few things are at play with Willis. First, in Week 1, offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik moved away from giving the ball to running back De’Von Achane and turned to Willis to try to throw Miami back into the game. That should never happen – Miami’s offense has to flow through Achane. Second, Willis seems to be trying to prove he can be a pocket passer. He is waiting for someone to get open rather than getting away from pressure. A couple of the sacks also come from him running out of bounds as he looks for a receiver, rather than throwing the ball away and living for the next play. I do not know if the game is going faster than he expected – yes, this is his fifth season in the league; he has only eight starts; he is still inexperienced and is trying to grow just like the rest of the roster. Third, the offensive line has struggled. Right tackle Austin Jackson, who I have described as a solid tackle when he is not injured, is not living up to being an average tackle right now. He doesn’t seem injured, but he is not playing well. It did not help that the Dolphins left him on an island against Nick Bosa for much of the game last week, expecting him to contain Bosa in one-on-one assignments. Right guard Jonah Savaiinaea is settling back into his natural position after being moved to left guard as a rookie last season, and he is playing better, but he is still young. Left guard Kadyn Proctor is a rookie who is making rookie mistakes; after Week 1, he was highlighted for several successful pancake blocks against the Las Vegas Raiders , but it was pointed out that he was not blocking the right player on some of those. I think Willis will be fine as he grows into his role. Is he the franchise quarterback that the Dolphins need? Maybe, maybe not. I know the coaches are hoping he is, so they can use their first-round pick on another position (likely an edge rusher), but he has to show a lot more over the remaining 15 games. 3. San Francisco scored touchdowns on its first five possessions, while Brock Purdy completed 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and finished with a 149.1 passer rating. For a team led by a defensive-minded head coach, what has been the biggest problem defensively—scheme, communication, lack of pressure or simply an inexperienced roster? Youth is clearly the biggest issue, and it has led to communication problems throughout the secondary. We have seen several times when two defensive backs cover one player, leaving another receiver wide open. Handoffs are not happening as well as they should – as is probably expected with communication among younger players. Lack of pressure has been a HUGE issue this year. Miami is not getting to the opposing quarterback. Last week, the edge rushers at least flushed Purdy out of the pocket or got in his face before he threw the ball a couple of times, but they are nowhere near successful in the pass rush right now. It has been a huge source of frustration. 4. Chop Robinson missed Week 2 while in the concussion protocol, and Miami struggled to generate pressure without him. How important is his potential return against Patrick Mahomes, and does this defensive front have enough pass-rushing depth to disrupt Kansas City if Robinson is unavailable or limited? I would love to say Robinson is going to have an impact, but he wasn’t much of a factor last year, and he hasn’t done anything to prove he is a top-level pass rusher this summer or in Week 1. I am terrified of what Mahomes will do to a young secondary because he will likely have plenty of time to read, wait, read again, and then throw. Maybe the third week of using Hafley’s defensive system will open something up, but right now, it does not feel like the Dolphins have the talent to get home routinely. 5. De’Von Achane remains Miami’s most dangerous offensive weapon, but the Dolphins have produced only two touchdowns through two games. What is Miami’s best path to pulling off the upset against Kansas City, and how do you expect Sunday’s game to play out? Finish. In the first half against the 49ers, Miami proved they could move the ball. Yes, Achane is the focus of the defense, but even with everyone in the stadium knowing he was going to get the ball, they kept moving forward. He averaged 3.7 yards per attempt on the ground – not record-setting, but that is a first down every three rushes. That will work. Of course, the Dolphins also crush themselves with penalties right now, a product of fielding such a young roster. They do not have the talent to overcome self-inflicted penalties. As a whole, Miami averaged 5.1 yards per offensive play and were able to control the ball for just over half the game (30:13). In the first half, they drove to the 49ers’ 33-, 10-, and five-yard lines, but came away with just two field goals (missing a 51-yard attempt on the first drive). The Dolphins have to figure out how to finish drives. Even the touchdown drive was really a 77-yard touchdown pass.

title: Chiefs-Dolphins: 5 things to watch in the Week 3 matchup
summary: This week, the Kansas City Chiefs will take on the Miami Dolphins in a Week 3 showdown in Miami. The game is set to kick off at 12:00 p.m. Arrowhead Time and will be broadcast locally on CBS (KCTV-5). The Chiefs enter the game 2-0 after a thrilling overtime victory over the Indianapolis Colts on […]
full_text: (Photo by Mark Brown/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week, the Kansas City Chiefs will take on the Miami Dolphins in a Week 3 showdown in Miami. The game is set to kick off at 12:00 p.m. Arrowhead Time and will be broadcast locally on CBS ( KCTV-5 ). The Chiefs enter the game 2-0 after a thrilling overtime victory over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday night. Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes put up his best performance in over a year, finishing with over 380 passing yards and three touchdowns. Travis Kelce reached the century mark for the first time in nearly two years and showed the league he is still a top tight end. Running back Kenneth Walker continued his hot start and, through two games, has 369 all-purpose yards. The Dolphins have had a disastrous start to the season and find themselves in a 0-2 hole after blowout losses to the Las Vegas Raiders and San Francisco 49ers . The Dolphins are ranked 27th in offensive yards per game and have scored only two offensive touchdowns this season. Here are five things to watch in another AFC battle. 1. Containing De’Von Achane He’s been quiet to start the 2026 season, but that could change quickly. Dolphins running back De’Von Achane has been one of the most explosive players in the NFL since being drafted in 2023, and the Chiefs will need to know where he lines up on every play. 📈 De'Von Achane has had 100 or more scrimmage yards in every home opener so far in his career: ➖ 2023 vs. Denver Broncos – 22 touches, 233 scrimmage yards, 4 TDs ➖ 2024 vs. Jacksonville Jaguars – 17 touches, 100 scrimmage yards, 1 TD ➖ 2025 vs. New England Patriots – 19… pic.twitter.com/aLXOR7etOn — FinsXtra (@FinsXtra) September 24, 2026 In his only career matchup against the Chiefs, Achane was held in check, rushing for only nine yards and catching three passes for 31 yards in a frigid Wild Card victory over the Dolphins in the playoffs in January of 2024. Although he has been off to a slow start this season, Achane finished last season with 1,838 all-purpose yards and 12 touchdowns. The Raiders and 49ers both kept him under 100 yards, and with the Chiefs defense coming off a game they would rather forget — giving up over 130 all-purpose yards to Colts back Jonathan Taylor — they should be motivated to keep the Dolphins’ primary source of offense from creating game-breaking plays. I would look for the Chiefs to bring quicker secondary players in the box — in Dime and Nickel personnel — to help contain Achane against the run, and have a variety of looks to slow down his receiving. 2. Extended look for young skill players Watching the Chiefs stars lead the charge has brought energy to the team early on, but in a game that heavily favors them, the team should look to spread the ball around on offense and let younger players get involved in the game plan. Tight end Travis Kelce has turned back the clock and leads the team through two games with 172 yards, but this week, the Chiefs should allow him more time to rest and spread the passing game around. Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy could see an uptick, but the emphasis should be on players like wide receivers Jalen Royals, Cyrus Allen and tight end Jake Briningstool this week, especially with a chance to get them live snaps. Kenneth Walker has also started the season at a historic pace, but to keep him fresh, the team would be wise to let rookie Emmett Johnson take more snaps this week. ELECTRIC: #Chiefs rookie running back Emmett Johnson recreated the LEGENDARY Dante Hall play. Kansas City may have something special in the rookie. This is remarkable: pic.twitter.com/JuOz9q3ITH — MLFootball (@MLFootball) September 22, 2026 Johnson has flashed, showing tackle-breaking and an elusive running style, but he has seen no more than ten touches in a game. This week would be the perfect opportunity for the Chiefs to turn up the dial on his volume. 3. Rushing the passer Last week against the Colts, the Chiefs’ pass rush had little impact, and the unit struggled to pressure quarterback Daniel Jones. This week should be a chance for them to change their fortunes and rebuild momentum by getting after quarterbacks. Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis has been sacked nine times , the most in the NFL so far this season. With the offensive line issues and a lack of downfield passing attack, the Chiefs should look to take advantage. Defensive tackle Chris Jones and defensive end George Karlaftis are both looking for their first sacks, and this could be a good week for them to break out. Woods still has to find a way to win quicker off the snap on pass downs, but he shows off some good power ot shake free from Nelson after he recognizes that it will be a pass. pic.twitter.com/ahDHfeGt6t — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) September 23, 2026 This could also be a good opportunity for rookie Peter Woods to get his first career sack, and edge rusher R Mason Thomas to continue his impressive start to the season. 4. Old friends The Dolphins have several players on their roster with former ties to Kansas City, and many who are listed on their two-deep depth chart. The most notable name is No. 40 Willie Gay Jr., who is listed as the Dolphins’ starting strong-side linebacker. Gay played in Kansas City for four seasons, winning two Super Bowls as a starter, and was a fan favorite. Listed as the Dolphins’ starting free safety is Zayne Anderson, who spent time with the team in 2020 and 2021. While a practice squad member and special teams player in Kansas City, Anderson has played in over half of the Dolphins’ defensive snaps this season. #FFIDP Here's an example of a Vegas' inside run. Jeanty shifts to the interior when the hole is created. Forces linebackers to react. Zayne Anderson breaks off his block to get in on the tackle. Coming from deep. Surprised Rodriguez didn't get credit for an assist here. pic.twitter.com/ZTExpgb19L — Mike Woellert (@Mike_Woellert) September 20, 2026 Defensive lineman Malik Herring will be expected to play in a reserve role, and Chu Godrick is listed as the Dolphins’ third-string tackle after being released by the Chiefs at the end of training camp. 5. Explosive plays for Mahomes? After struggling in Week 1, Mahomes found wide receiver Tyquan Thornton deep twice for big plays. After two consecutive seasons of conservative football, the deep shots were a welcome sight and should have everyone clamoring for more. The Dolphins have allowed five passing plays of over 20 yards so far this season, and Mahomes has completed five passes over 20 yards. After a dormant week one, Mahomes and Thornton picked up where they left off last season. Worthy's route holds the defense in place as Thornton blows by the safety. Mahomes has time in the pocket and lets it fly. Beautiful throw. Just short of the end zone. pic.twitter.com/LmCtXtzRx7 — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) September 22, 2026 According to NFL Next Gen Stats , this pass was the sixth-most improbable pass of the 2026 season, with a 21.1% chance of being a completion. With Mahomes dialed in and connecting on big plays, the Chiefs should look to attack early and often.
author: Caleb James

title: Will the Chiefs’ offense see the best of Xavier Worthy soon?
summary: I loved the pick. Unabashedly loved it. “He’s fast, he’s productive, and he’s going to add the element this offense has been missing.” That was my initial impression when the Kansas City Chiefs drafted wide receiver Xavier Worthy in the first round. That was not necessarily the consensus. Some national analysts panned the selection because […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images I loved the pick. Unabashedly loved it. “He’s fast, he’s productive, and he’s going to add the element this offense has been missing.” That was my initial impression when the Kansas City Chiefs drafted wide receiver Xavier Worthy in the first round. That was not necessarily the consensus. Some national analysts panned the selection because he was more of the same for the Chiefs’ receiver room, with too many small, gadget-type receivers. I rejected the notion. This would be different. Andy Reid selected him in the first round for a reason. He clearly had a plan. That appeared to be the case, at least in year one. After a slow start — 20 receptions in his first 9 games — Worthy was thrust into action in the second half of his rookie year. He became the team’s leading receiver in the second half of the season after Rashee Rice went down to injury. Worthy racked up nearly 400 yards in his final seven regular-season games. That seemed to offer a glimpse of what was to come. Xavier Worthy is not your typical Combine track star. He’s a real deal receiver with outlier speed. https://t.co/iHaM7FwmEp — Brandon Kiley (@BKSportsTalk) August 17, 2024 But then he ran into tight end Travis Kelce on a crossing route in the first game of the 2025 season, and everything changed. His shoulder became an issue. He missed a couple of games. An ankle injury also held him back. He finished the 2025 campaign with barely 500 receiving yards and only one touchdown. It was a frustrating season, marred by injury. The Chiefs spent the offseason telling anyone who would listen that this year would be different. Worthy would be healthy, and we would see a return to the player we watched in the second half of the 2024 campaign. I was optimistic. This would be the year he proved the doubters wrong, once and for all. I’m still waiting for that to happen. Worthy doesn’t look like the confident player he was in the second half of his rookie year. He’s shying away from contact. He’s not strong at the catch point. He’s not beating defenders to the corner. I’m struggling to understand how to use a player who doesn’t win deep, doesn’t play with the physicality needed to win across the middle, and can’t break tackles to win after the catch. What’s the proper usage for such a wide receiver? That seems to be the question the Chiefs are asking, too. I hope the Chiefs find that answer sooner rather than later. This offense looks like a legitimate contender. Running back Kenneth Walker has added an explosive element the Chiefs have been lacking for years. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes looks as confident as he has in his supporting cast since 2022. Kelce is rejuvenated. Wideout Tyquan Thornton is a legitimate deep threat. Receiver Rashee Rice is working his way back to prime form. If Worthy can return to his second-half 2024 form, this group is cooking with gas. Can he get back to that form, though? That remains to be seen. The history of first-round wide receivers who have produced like Worthy through two-plus seasons is less than ideal. 60 wide receivers were selected in the first round between 2011 & 2025. Worthy ranks 32nd among them in receptions, 38th in receiving yards and 33rd in receiving touchdowns through his first 33 games. By volume, none of those statistics are particularly alarming. The efficiency is where the trends are far more worrisome. Worthy is targeted at roughly the average rate among the 60 wide receivers selected in the first round over the past 15 years, but he’s produced fewer yards per target than nearly any other receiver on the list. His 6.6 yards per target is through his first 33 career regular season games ranks 51st among that group. The only other first-round wide receivers over that stretch to average fewer than 7 yards per reception through 33 career regular season games are Kevin White, Garrett Wilson, Josh Doctson, A.J. Jenkins, Nelson Agholor, John Ross, Kadarius Toney, Jalen Reagor, Xavier Leggette, Breshad Perriman, Cordarreelle Patterson, Tavon Austin, N’Keal Harry, Laquon Treadwell, Corey Coleman and Jonathan Baldwin. Uh oh. That’s not a group you want to be included in. It’s a who’s who of wide receiver busts over the past decade-plus. It’s especially worrisome that Worthy is producing like this with a future Hall of Fame coach and quarterback. Most receivers who overcame poor early-career efficiency (Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Malik Nabers, and Garrett Wilson) were dealing with a poorly designed offensive scheme, a below-average quarterback situation, or both. That excuse or explanation doesn’t apply to Worthy. The only reason I’m holding out hope my priors are correct on Worthy is the injuries. Maybe the first couple of weeks are a blip on the radar. Maybe he’ll have a second half similar to his rookie year. Maybe he’s still tentative after playing through so many ailments last season, and it’ll just take time to get himself right. Maybe. Hopefully. The Chiefs offense doesn’t need Worthy to step up the way it once did. But it sure would be nice if he could. I’m still holding out hope, but patience is running thin.

title: Chiefs pass rush must improve after quiet Colts game
summary: A pair of seemingly contradictory defensive performances for the Kansas City Chiefs have left fans pondering how much trust to put in the unit. Kansas City opened the season with a dominant 31-10 beatdown of the Denver Broncos, sacking quarterback Bo Nix four times and holding the reigning AFC West champions to just 176 total […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A pair of seemingly contradictory defensive performances for the Kansas City Chiefs have left fans pondering how much trust to put in the unit. Kansas City opened the season with a dominant 31-10 beatdown of the Denver Broncos , sacking quarterback Bo Nix four times and holding the reigning AFC West champions to just 176 total yards. A week later, however, the Chiefs sweated 70 full minutes for a 33-30 overtime victory over the Indianapolis Colts . The Colts gained 329 yards against Kansas City. Despite multiple close calls, quarterback Daniel Jones played five quarters without being sacked. Speaking before Thursday’s practice, defensive line coach Joe Cullen credited the Indianapolis offensive line for thwarting the Chiefs’ pass rush. “They’re a physical offensive line,” observed Cullen. “They’ve always had a good offensive line. And one of the things we stressed is we got to get them in those down and distances like we had a third-and-16. [Defensive end George Karlaftis] made a great play on the screen… We had a third-and-11, and George jumped the gun, went offside. So now you’re down to third-and-6, and the ball gets out a little quicker. But they’ve always had a decent offensive line. And I think we saved the best rush for the last one when George put him on his back, but they’re a good offensive line.” On Thursday, defensive tackle Chris Jones reiterated the importance of wins and losses over all other stats while acknowledging the need for improvement. He does see an overtime victory as an indication of the Kansas City defense’s perseverance. “I think the most important thing that matters is wins and losses,” said Jones. “We were able to pull through, but we were also able to learn a lot about this team — the resiliency of the team and the core strength of the team. But there are still areas for improvement.” One area for improvement will be preventing quick passes — as Jones was able to seemingly get off for completions any time the Chiefs’ pass rush threatened him. Cullen knows it is a problem, but it will take the whole defense to prevent a repeat performance by opposing quarterbacks. “We’ve had some consistent pressure,” remarked the coach, “and it’s not always going to be a sack, but we’ve put pressure on the quarterback in a lot of different ways. But the coverage in the back end and the rush go hand in hand. Those are the things that when they’re tied in together, you’ve got to get home. [When] the quarterback’s patting that ball for over three seconds, you’ve got to get home. “Ball gets out quick —you may have to change your rush and get your hand up to knock a slant down. The slant’s getting out in 2.2 seconds. When you make the quarterback clutch it, you got to get home, and when he doesn’t, and he’s getting it out quick, we got to get our hands up and helping the slant game.” The Chiefs’ defense will next be tested on Sunday in South Florida against the Miami Dolphins . Cullen expects a well-prepared squad from new head coach Jeff Hafley. The Chiefs also have respect for possibly the league’s fastest running back, De’Von Achane, and quarterback Malik Willis — who took Kansas City to overtime in 2022 while with the Tennessee Titans . “We’re excited,” Cullen declared. “A great opportunity going on the road for the first time down to Miami, and Coach Hafley’s building that program, and they’ve got some really skilled athletes on offense. [Achane] — No. 28 —is as good a back as there is. He’s had 5.7 [yards] to carry last year. We played Malik Willis when he was at Tennessee in the game here. So great athletes, and we’ll have our hands full, but we’re excited and looking forward to the challenge.”

title: Chargers-Bills Game Preview: 3 things to watch for in road trip to Buffalo
summary: The Chargers need to turn things around NOW. Not next week. Not next month. Now. But they couldn’t have asked for a more difficult opponent to pull that off against than the Bills who are led by current MVP-frontrunner Josh Allen. The defense is not likely to look all that great as the Bills are […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Justin Herbert #10 and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel of the Los Angeles Chargers celebrate a touchdown against the Arizona Cardinals during the first quarter of the game at SoFi Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers need to turn things around NOW. Not next week. Not next month. Now. But they couldn’t have asked for a more difficult opponent to pull that off against than the Bills who are led by current MVP-frontrunner Josh Allen. The defense is not likely to look all that great as the Bills are scoring 38.5 points per game, but it’s the offense who has a shot against a Buffalo defense that is allowing 31 points and 368 yards to their opponents on average thus far. I know many will not have hope, but the NFL can be wacky and wild in the weirdest of times, so a Chargers win here would almost be par for the course. “Any given Sunday,” right? That said, here are three things that I’ll be watching for when these two teams take the field on Sunday. 1.) Will increased QB meetings help the Chargers offense? This week, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel told reporters that he is “much closer to Justin Herbert now than he was two weeks ago.” That’s because, with the rough start, the Chargers play-caller is now leaving nothing to chance as he’s increased the amount of times Herbert and him are meeting throughout the week to make sure at least those two are on the same page. McDaniel went on to say he’s much more connected with what his players are most comfortable with running offensively, meaning he’s seemingly cutting back on some of the playbook to make sure his unit is not getting overwhelmed with the amount on their plates while trying to get this new scheme to click. I take some positives and negatives away from this. The positives being that McDaniel is willing to change and adapt if things are not working like they should. I also think it’s good to hear him meeting with Herbert more and that relationship could never be “too close.” On the negative side, it’s not good that he’s been pushed to do such things, or feels like he wasn’t doing enough before. Why weren’t you already meeting with Herbert on an obsessive basis? They’re human and have lives, but at least through training camp and into the regular season, this should have been at the forefront of his priorities. Secondly, it’s not ideal that there seems to have been an unnoticed divide between what his team was actually comfortable with offensively and what the team has been trying to do out on the field the past two Sundays. It’s been fairly obvious that Herbert does not look like he’s in control of the offense the way we’re used to seeing in years past. Past the initial reads, it does not look like he is ever capable of improvising, and that honestly stretches to his pass-catchers. The plays look “dead in the water” quick and then there’s never a Plan B when it goes sideways. At this rate, the team just needs to look like they know what they’re doing. They don’t even need to exactly “dominate,” just show that they’re capable of running an offense with all its nuances and adjustments. If the other team is simply that much better and they shut it down, fine! That’s the way it goes sometimes. But right now, it’s the Chargers defending themselves before the other team even gets a chance. Here’s to hoping the extra time together between McDaniel and Herbert shows some fast results. 2.)How will the Chargers handle the latest injury along the offensive line? New starting left guard Kayode Awosika unfortunately did not make it through two games with the Chargers before an injury struck him. While he was not placed on injured reserve this week, the team expects him to miss at least this week with a fibula injury. Jim Harbaugh said he’d miss “some time” and my bet is at least two games. Who is there to play left guard in the meantime? The backup to start the season there was Trey Pipkins but he missed Week 2 with a knee injury and he has yet to practice in Week 3. When Awosika went out last week, it was veteran Trevor Penning who filled in. Earlier in that game, Penning rotated in with Cole Strange and, funny enough, he played a role in Omariom Hampton gashing the Raiders en route to his second touchdown on the ground. It’s worth mentioning: When Penning was in for Strange, the rushing attack looked like the unit we expect it to be every week. When Strange was in and Penning was in the game on the other side, things weren’t churning the same. Everyone and their mother knew the Strange signing was going to be a bad move. As a depth piece? Sure, why not. As the immediate starter with no competition? No way. But here we are. As things stand, it’ll be Penning at left guard and Strange at right guard against the Bills. Here’s to hoping stud Bills defensive tackle Ed Oliver doesn’t return this week. 3.) Is Chris O’Leary right to keep Marlowe Wax off the field? This week, defensive coordinator Chris O’Leary fielded questions about keeping second-year linebacker Marlowe Wax off the field on defense through the first two games. Wax was stellar in the preseason and with veteran Denzel Perryman remaining on IR for two more weeks, the expectation was that Wax could see some real snaps next to Daiyan Henley. However, it’s been just Troy Dye and Del’Shawn Phillips with Henley thus far, the latter of which has been the designated starter with Henley. Phillips and Dye have actually played well through two games. Per Pro Football Focus, each are on pace to have their highest-graded seasons ever. On the other hand, Henley is off to a rough start and is currently on pace for his worst-graded season. He’s been graded harshly in coverage through games, posting a 45.5 mark. Henley is the unquestioned leader in the middle. He’s not going to lose snaps to anyone, but something has to give if the Chargers cannot defend the middle of the field better. I’m not saying Wax is the answer, but something feels like it needs shaking up. That or Henley, like the rest of the team, needs to shake off this rough start to find their stride again and get back to the standard they’ve made for themselves in the Jim Harbaugh era. Chargers DC Chris O’Leary on Marlowe Wax not playing on defense: “He is playing and performing at a level we would trust him out there…We really like what Troy, Del’Shawn, and Daiyan are doing for us. So right now there’s no need to shuffle it.” “It’s more him staying ready for… — Alex Insdorf (@alexinsdorf99) September 24, 2026

title: Is Sean Payton overrated?
summary: The Denver Broncos gave up a first-round and a third-round pick for Jaylen Waddle in the offseason to spark one of the most functionally-limited passing offenses in the NFL in 2025, but the early returns have Sean Payton’s offense stuck in third gear with a slow start in 2026. Although Payton relinquished play calling duties […]
full_text: The Denver Broncos gave up a first-round and a third-round pick for Jaylen Waddle in the offseason to spark one of the most functionally-limited passing offenses in the NFL in 2025, but the early returns have Sean Payton’s offense stuck in third gear with a slow start in 2026. Although Payton relinquished play calling duties to Davis Webb this season and has pushed some of the responsibility onto a first-year offensive coordinator, he can’t avoid the lingering question that has followed him from New Orleans to Denver: Is Sean Payton the most overrated coach in the NFL? The Broncos gave up a first-round pick for Payton in 2023, believing that his offensive “genius” could at least make Russell Wilson a serviceable quarterback for a fraction of his $230 million contract. Instead, Payton and Wilson beefed and the quarterback was benched before the end of the season to avoid an injury guarantee kicking in. Denver’s offense ranked 19th in points and 26th in yards. The next year, Payton orchestrated a team decision to draft Bo Nix 12th overall despite some concerns that the veteran college quarterback wouldn’t have the arm talent for the NFL. Nix has allayed the skepticism somewhat by being an adequate game manager on a team that has arguably the best defense in the NFL since 2024, but his 4.5 air yards per completion as a rookie ranked 32nd. That number only went to 4.7 AY/C in 2025, which ranked 30th. The reason this matters is that it could prove that Nix has not proven his critics wrong. He’s proven them right. Bo Nix had an Average Depth of Target of 3.86 yards in week 1. For reference: the average American watches TV from about 3.67 yards away. pic.twitter.com/YBwtJ5Ci39 — Novig (@Novig) September 16, 2026 Bo Nix, to date, is one of the least threatening downfield passers in the NFL who still holds a starting job. This doesn’t make him bad in and of itself, but it is a tad concerning when that quarterback is young, if not in the prime of his career. Nix’s attempted air yards sits with the likes of Geno Smith, Kirk Cousins, and Aaron Rodgers. That’s not the company he wants to keep in 2026 . This was the quarterback who Payton was comfortable resting his offensive reputation on because Drew Brees is also not known for his arm strength. Brees was one of the most devastating “game managers” in NFL history, if not one of one. However, there is no comparing the Broncos offense to the Saints offense of the 2010s, which again brings us back to the notion that Sean Payton is a future Hall of Fame-level coach who led the charge for one of the most potent passing offenses in NFL history for a decade. Now it’s starting to look like that had a lot more to do with Brees than Payton. Most wins when team allowed 30+ points: ▪️Drew Brees (20) Most losses when team scored 30+ points: ▪️Drew Brees (16) — NFL Researcher (@NFL_Researcher) May 1, 2026 Payton goes 12-4 with Brees in 2020. Then 9-8 without Brees in 2021 and promptly enters semi-retirement in 2022. He takes over a dumpster fire in Denver in 2023 and immediately helps the team finish nearly .500 (8-9) that first year, before improving to 10-7 in 2024, and 14-3 in 2025. So one could then argue that Payton couldn’t possibly be overrated because the Broncos reached the AFC Championship game and “only lost” because Nix was injured in the divisional round and unable to start. However, let’s not forget that Jarrett Stidham was supposed to be “Payton’s guy” handpicked to be ready to go as a functional quarterback at a moment’s notice, but proceeded to go 17-of-31 for only 133 yards in the biggest moment of Denver’s season. Consider what the Broncos have invested into offense since Payton’s arrival: 2nd round pick on WR Marvin Mims 1st round pick on QB Nix 4th round pick on WR Troy Franklin 5th round pick on RB Audric Estime 7th round pick on WR Devaughn Vele 2nd round pick on RB RJ Harvey 3rd round pick on WR Pat Bryant 4th round pick on RB Jonah Coleman A first-round quarterback with two day two receivers and a day two running back but Harvey, Bryant, Mims, and Franklin are of little regard. They probably won’t last long. Payton was not able to build a good rushing offense, even with a highly-respected offensive line. So the Broncos had to trade a first and a third and pay Waddle instead as a pairing for Courtland Sutton, one of the only guys who Payton inherited. The Broncos acquired J.K. Dobbins and Dobbins is merely OK, not special. To add insult to bad drafting, the Broncos traded Vele to the Saints and now Vele has 133 yards through two games. Waddle has 140 yards. If the reason that Denver is good is defense, and Vance Joseph controls the entire defense, then I’ll ask again: Is Sean Payton overrated? Rams chance to find out The Rams take on the Broncos this week and while Sean McVay’s reputation has only gotten better since the 2018 NFC Championship game, Payton’s bank account seems to be the only thing growing since then. Payton has done NOTHING revolutionary on offense in the last 15 years, whereas McVay seems to stay on the cutting edge of offensive identity every single season. As a reminder, Payton’s Saints went 25-23 in his first three seasons, and then New Orleans won the Super Bowl in 2009 while ranking first in points and passing touchdowns. Respect. But over the next four years, with prime Drew Brees, the Saints posted double-digit wins three times (Payton was suspended for all of 2012 and they went 7-9) and failed to get past the second round of the playoffs. They went Jeff Fisher’s 7-9 in each of the next three seasons after that. Then wasted Brees again every year from 2017 to 2020, never winning more than a single game in a postseason. Sean Payton went 3-0 in the 2009 playoffs. Sean Payton is 6-9 in the postseason over the last 16 years. His best offensive seasons were Drew Brees. His best Broncos seasons were Vance Joseph. So what exactly does Sean Payton do ? I guess we’ll find out on Sunday.

title: Puka Nacua doubtful for Week 3, but expected back soon
summary: Puka Nacua missed the L.A. Rams’ Week 2 win over the New York Giants and is expected to be held out again on Sunday against the Denver Broncos, but Sean McVay believes that the star receiver will return in Week 4. Nacua is going to be listed as doubtful for the Broncos game, an injury […]
full_text: Puka Nacua missed the L.A. Rams’ Week 2 win over the New York Giants and is expected to be held out again on Sunday against the Denver Broncos, but Sean McVay believes that the star receiver will return in Week 4. Nacua is going to be listed as doubtful for the Broncos game, an injury designation that typically results in a 94-99% chance of being ruled out. However, McVay sees a path towards Nacua returning from a hip injury in Week 4 against the Philadelphia Eagles. Sean McVay believes that, barring a setback, Puka Nacua could return next week vs. the Eagles. https://t.co/sMbD1gKpFv — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 25, 2026 McVay shared other injury updates on Friday. also including Kamren Kinchens, who is nursing a hamstring strain that also kept him from playing against the Giants. Kinchens will be listed as doubtful. There was no mention of a timeline for Kinchens’ return. In positive news, Jordan Whittington came off the injury list and is the logical choice to take over as a starting receiver alongside Davante Adams, a job he did admirably for two games in 2024 when the Rams were down both Cooper Kupp and Nacua in games against Chicago and Green Bay. Whittington caught 13 of 18 targets over those two games for 151 yards. It should be noted that Tutu Atwell also rose to the occasion in those two games, taking on a far heavier load. Atwell could be one to watch as well. This game could also serve as a coming-out party for Terrance Ferguson, the Rams’ highly touted second-year TE. With Colby Parkinson ‘questionable’, Ferguson could be asked to take over as TE1. McVay mentioned Parkinson was “trending in the right direction” , but it remains to be seen if he will take the field come game time. Ferguson was targeted nine times against New York, catching six passes for 54 yards. Against the strong Denver secondary anchored by Patrick Surtain, the Rams need strong performances from whoever Matthew Stafford throws to, with or without Nacua.

An overwhelming percentage of fans (90%) are confident that the Rams are heading in the right direction. This comes after more than two-thirds of the fanbase were not confident in the team’s direction a week ago after LA’s season-opening loss to the 49ers in Australia. What a difference a week makes, that’s for sure. This certainly paints an overly optimistic picture of the Rams, with a tough matchup looming against the Broncos on Sunday night. Now, while it’s promising to see the fanbase confident in the team, is it more of a short-term feeling or a sign of things to come? Some fans are unsure, as they would rather wait to measure their confidence levels after the game in Denver this weekend. The Australia game wasn’t a great measure of the team’s success because they were set up to fail from the start. That “travel experiment” cost them early ground in the NFC West and the conference. Plus, the Rams beating up on a Giants team that was without its starting quarterback for most of the game wasn’t overly impressive. The New York win ultimately proved that LA beat who they needed to, which isn’t always awe-inspiring. Another fan echoed the sentiment and added that the next three games feature not only the Broncos, but the Eagles and Bills. Los Angeles has plenty of work to do to win over more of the fanbase. These next few weeks against Super Bowl contenders will be the ultimate test for the Rams, one they must pass to increase the confidence level among fans even further. They will likely meet more resistance to that plan in Week 3 against the Denver Broncos. With Puka Nacua set to miss his […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams dominated when pushing the ball down the field in their Week 2 win. Specifically, Matthew Stafford and Davante Adams dominated the New York Giants when pushing the ball. They will likely meet more resistance to that plan in Week 3 against the Denver Broncos. With Puka Nacua set to miss his second game in a row, Adams will be the featured piece in the pass catcher corps again this week. He was tremendous in that role against the Giants, posting eight receptions for 195 yards and two touchdowns, his best game since joining the Rams last year. He was especially good when working downfield. Next Gen Stats defines a “downfield target” as a pass of 10+ air yards. Stafford targeted Adams eight times on downfield throws, and Adams hauled in seven for 191 yards and both of his scores. He wasn’t just dicing up the Giants’ secondary, he was hitting home run after home run against them. It would be fantastic for L.A. if the 33-year-old receiver could do that again, but, unfortunately for him, he’s got a tougher matchup this week than New York cornerbacks Greg Newsome II and Colton Hood. Kevin Harlan is a national treasure 😅 Davante Adams' first TD had Harlan & @kurt13warner fired up 🔥 pic.twitter.com/iWcN0hPy2H — Westwood One Sports (@westwood1sports) September 22, 2026 Instead, he will likely see a lot of Denver cornerback Patrick Surtain II. That means he’ll battle arguably the best cornerback in the NFL on Sunday night. Only three cornerbacks have won AP Defensive Player of the Year in the last three decades: Surtain (2024), Stephon Gilmore (2019) and Hall of Famer Charles Woodson (2009). It goes without saying that he’s a special player. This season, he’s only allowed three receptions for 20 yards over two games, a blowout loss to the Kansas City Chiefs and a close win over the Jacksonville Jaguars. More pertinently, according to Next Gen Stats, Surtain hasn’t allowed a downfield reception in his last 213 coverage snaps. Since the start of 2025, he’s only allowed three of them. It is extremely hard to create explosives through the air against him. Of course, that doesn’t mean he’s unbeatable. Adams, in fact, has been as good as anyone in the league when matched up on Surtain, though they haven’t dueled since 2023. The Rams’ receiver has run 70 routes against Surtain in four games, 40 of which have come with man coverage. Adams has been targeted 22 times in those matchups with 13 receptions for 172 yards and two touchdowns. Those are the best numbers for any receiver against Surtain in the cornerback’s career. Not for nothing, the quarterbacks throwing to Adams in those four games were Derek Carr, Jimmy Garoppolo and Aidan O’Connell. Davante Adams vs. Patrick Surtain II. Round 5 Adams vs. Patrick Surtain Last 4 Matchups: 2022 Week 4: 5 receptions, 54 yards, 0 TD 2022 Week 11: 4 receptions, 85 yards, 2 TD 2023 Week 1: 2 receptions, 16 yards, 0 TD 2023 Week 18: 3 receptions, 26 yards, 0 TD pic.twitter.com/wLgCcoP0kw — LAFB Network (@LAFBNetwork) September 24, 2026 That brings us back to Sunday’s matchup. There’s good reason to believe Adams can still produce against the NFL’s best corner, but the opportunities to take the top off the defense with vertical concepts will be more limited. You can probably deduce the most likely way the Rams’ best active receiver will have to win this time around. Stafford is obviously one of the league’s best at pushing the ball and using all portions of the field, while Adams’s technical ability as a route runner is especially deadly in the intermediate and deep levels of the defense. But that doesn’t mean those two can’t play a more underneath, conservative game this week. If someone with that kind of separation ability is getting the better of such a dominant corner, you’ll take those wins any way you can get them. It should be noted that the Rams don’t want to give up entirely on taking shots down the field. There should be opportunities for others whenever Surtain is occupied, and this could be another chance for tight end Terrence Ferguson to show off his field-stretching ability. It’s also generally a smart gamble to attack Denver No. 2 cornerback, Riley Moss, who’s a good player in his own right but also led the NFL in penalty yardage committed last season. The Rams don’t have to concede everything to the Bronco defense this week and settle for a dink-and-dunk passing attack. But the same downfield opportunities likely won’t be available for Adams, so they’ll need to find a different approach to picking apart the Denver secondary.

title: Rams should consider Matt LaFleur reunion if Packers move on
summary: Former Los Angeles Rams offensive coordinator Matt LaFleur had a rough night following his Packers’ 35-14 loss to the winless Falcons Thursday. If the Packers move on from LaFleur — which could realistically happen any week now — the Rams should consider bringing him back in some capacity. The case for bringing LaFleur back is […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - SEPTEMBER 24: Head coach Matt LaFleur of the Green Bay Packers looks to throw the red flag against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter of the game at Lambeau Field on September 24, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Former Los Angeles Rams offensive coordinator Matt LaFleur had a rough night following his Packers’ 35-14 loss to the winless Falcons Thursday. If the Packers move on from LaFleur — which could realistically happen any week now — the Rams should consider bringing him back in some capacity. The case for bringing LaFleur back is simple, as he was part of Sean McVay ’s first coaching staff in Los Angeles. LaFleur and McVay go back a long way, dating back to their time together in Washington from 2010-13. Green Bay’s current coach spent only one year as the Rams’ OC before joining the Titans in the same capacity in 2018, a year before getting the Packers job. Now, before anyone freaks out about LaFleur bringing his coaching stink to LA, it wouldn’t be like he’s calling the plays. He could serve as a consultant to the Rams on offense or defense, similar to what he did for longtime friend Robert Saleh after the Jets gave him the boot in 2024. LaFleur brought in Saleh that October to assist the Packers on offense ahead of their matchup against the Jaguars. It was a smart move on LaFleur’s behalf to get a new perspective for his team. Very McVay-like innovation, I might add. Also, in this business, you have to treat your friends right, and you have to believe McVay would welcome his buddy with open arms. It’s not like it would be a long-term move either. Regardless of his recent struggles with the Packers, LaFleur will be a highly coveted head coaching candidate if GB moves on. McVay could bring in LaFleur to help him get his head straight before receiving more coaching opportunities. And remember, LaFleur is 5-0 against McVay during his Packers tenure. So, if you can’t beat ‘em, it’s better to let them join you. Matt LaFleur’s days numbered in Green Bay The Packers have lost seven of their last eight games, and that doesn’t bode well for LaFleur’s chances of sticking around in Wisconsin. Thursday’s 21-point loss — in their home opener, no less — was a microcosm of Green Bay’s struggles under LaFleur, dating back to last season. GB blew double-digit leads to the Bears twice, including a 21-3 halftime lead at Chicago in the Wild Card Round. Then, the Packers led 22-10 against backup Carson Wentz and the Vikings in Week 1 before giving up 29 unanswered points to lose by 17. They needed a comeback win over the Jets in overtime to prevent an 0-3 start. The Packers have lost two of their first three games this season by 17+ points. They had not lost multiple games by 17+ points in an entire season since 2017. pic.twitter.com/hETKsMKG2C — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 25, 2026 LaFleur signed a multiyear extension in January, which is looking like a bust with each passing week. There seems to be a reason why those contract details weren’t released to the public. Green Bay essentially rewarded mediocrity by committing to him after watching his team choke away a playoff game to a bitter rival. He has also won just three playoff games in his career with reasonably strong quarterback play from Aaron Rodgers and Jordan Love. If not for the inclusion of the seven seed, the Packers would’ve missed the playoffs in four straight seasons. No doubt an underserved extension. This isn’t even the gauntlet of their schedule, as GB will face the Bears and Cowboys in back-to-back weeks after facing the Buccaneers in Week 4. Losing to the Vikings and Falcons doesn’t spell confidence in LaFleur, considering he’s given cheeseheads more constipation than dairy lately. Moving on from LaFleur certainly seems to be the most logical answer in Green Bay. Whenever that day comes, assuming it happens around midseason, McVay and the Rams should give LaFleur a temporary home while the veteran coach figures out his next move.

title: 5Qs, 5As with Mile High Report: Rams urged to test Broncos’ iffy run defense
summary: The Los Angeles Rams look to continue building momentum as they hit the road again, this time against the Denver Broncos on Sunday night. According to FanDuel Sportsbook, the Rams are a 2.5-point favorite in the Mile High City against the reigning AFC runner-up. Including the playoffs, the Broncos have gone 26-13 under veteran head […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Bhayshul Tuten #33 of the Jacksonville Jaguars runs the ball during the third quarter of a game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams look to continue building momentum as they hit the road again, this time against the Denver Broncos on Sunday night. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Rams are a 2.5-point favorite in the Mile High City against the reigning AFC runner-up. Including the playoffs, the Broncos have gone 26-13 under veteran head coach Sean Payton. Denver, like LA, is a Super Bowl hopeful. Ahead of this weekend’s primetime showdown, I spoke with Ian St. Clair of Mile High Report to get more intel on the Broncos. Q – The Broncos have struggled mightily on offense in the first two games. Denver scored 10 points against the Chiefs in Week 1 and started slowly versus the Jaguars before scoring 17 unanswered points to secure the win. What is your initial impression of offensive coordinator Davis Webb, and what areas must the unit improve on moving forward? A – Through the first six quarters, Bo Nix and the offense did struggle. However, it finally clicked in the second half. “Finally,” like it’s been half of the season. But what the Broncos offense showed against a good team and defense is an appetizer of what the unit can become. If Denver converts the two first-half trips to the red zone into touchdowns, the discussion changes. That’s where the focus should be – on finishing drives. That also takes care of the other issue – starting faster offensively. Dating back to last season, the Broncos offense doesn’t get going until the second half. That must change, and finishing drives is the first step. Denver also must stick with the running game. We saw it in the second half against the Jaguars, but consistently and effectively running the ball sets up the rest of the offense. As for Webb, he got into a rhythm in the second half and called a great game. Take that to Sunday night, build off it, and find ways to improve the offense even more. Webb is a bright young mind and he had some struggles to start. Some of it was execution, but just like life, he’ll need to take the failures and successes together. He has another big test this Sunday. Q – Speaking of offense, new wide receiver Jaylen Waddle had a great game against Jacksonville, catching eight passes for 138 yards. How are you enjoying the Waddle-Bo Nix connection two games in? A – What will make me enjoy it even more is if that type of playmaking becomes consistent, thus making the offense harder to defend. It’ll force defenses to shift coverages to ensure Waddle is the focal point. That then opens the ability to utilize Courtland Sutton, Marvin Mims (when healthy), Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Evan Engram. After Sunday, I’m enjoying the Nix-Waddle connection quite a bit, but I want to see how Denver expands it. Q – The Broncos have had one of the NFL’s best defenses in the last two seasons under defensive coordinator Vance Joseph. If you’re Sean McVay, what types of plays should you be calling to keep Joseph’s unit on its toes on Sunday night? A – Test the Denver rush defense. Even dating back to the playoffs last year, the Broncos struggled to stop the run. The biggest issue against Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs is that Denver couldn’t tackle. The tackling was much better for the Broncos against Jacksonville, but run Kyren Williams and Blake Corum on Sunday night. That allows McVay to use the heavy offensive sets that he typically likes to run, especially the plays with three tight ends. Then he can have Matthew Stafford use those tight ends in the passing game. That’s the other thing Denver struggles with – covering tight ends. Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad, in a word, are not very good. So force the two linebackers into coverage and the Rams will likely have success. Q – Denver advanced to the AFC Championship last season and likely would’ve advanced to the Super Bowl had Nix stayed healthy. The team has certainly come a long way from the Nathaniel Hackett and Russell Wilson days, so what are your realistic expectations for the Broncos this season? A – Payton, Nix and this Denver team should compete for the Super Bowl again. To be honest, this could be the Super Bowl matchup. It is just Week 3, but these two teams could meet again on Valentine’s Day in LA. And both teams have that expectation. There’s no doubt the opener on Monday Night Football in KC was startling, but similar to the Rams, the Broncos struggle in September. The team we saw in Denver in the second half against a good Jaguars team is the team that will make it a contender. Q – What is one question that you have for Rams fans? A – How do fans feel about the “Super Team” moniker and all that comes with it?

title: Las Vegas Raiders-New Orleans Saints FEED topic: Can Raiders’ secondary contain Chris Olave?
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders have passed their first two tests of the 2026 season. However, in the NFL, the exams only get tougher as each week passes, and that’s the case with the Raiders’ Week 3 matchup on the road against the New Orleans Saints. The Saints are an up-and-coming team in the league, finishing […]
full_text: (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders have passed their first two tests of the 2026 season. However, in the NFL, the exams only get tougher as each week passes, and that’s the case with the Raiders’ Week 3 matchup on the road against the New Orleans Saints. The Saints are an up-and-coming team in the league, finishing last season strong and beginning the current campaign 1-1, with a one-point overtime loss to the Detroit Lions serving as the blemish on their record. A big reason for New Orleans’ rise is its relatively new quarterback and wide receiver connection: Tyler Shough and Chris Olave. Dating back to last season, Shough has been the Saints’ starting quarterback for 11 games, and Olave has 76 receptions for 962 yards and six touchdowns during that timeframe. Over the past two weeks, they’ve been one of, if not the best, duos at taking deep shots to put heavy stress on opposing secondaries (more details in this week’s key matchups column ). The other aspect of Olave’s game that makes him a tough cover is that he splits his time fairly evenly between being a left or right outside receiver and in the slot. So every defensive back who steps on the field for the Raiders will have to be on high alert. Las Vegas’ secondary has been fairly stingy so far, as the team ranks 11th in the NFL with just 368 passing yards allowed in two games. However, the unit hasn’t seen a passing attack as strong as New Orleans’ yet, and there are a few question marks in the defensive backfield. Rookie free safety Treydan Stukes is in concussion protocol, while Week 1 starting corner Darien Porter missed the Chargers game with a foot injury and was limited during the team’s first practice of the week . Granted, rookie corner Hezekiah Masses might start anyway, seeing as he’s coming off an AFC Defensive Player of the Week performance with two interceptions. But Sunday would be just Masses’ second career start. Meanwhile, veterans Eric Stokes and Taron Johnson haven’t been particularly sticky in coverage to begin the campaign. So, for this week’s game day discussion on The FEED , we’ll be focusing on the Raiders’ secondary to see if they can keep Olave in check, since that should be defensive coordinator Rob Leonard’s biggest key of the game. The game kicks off at 1:25 p.m. PST and will air on CBS (check your local listings). I look forward to talkin’ some ball with y’all!

title: Raiders Week 3: The Saints Las Vegas must account for in road matchup
summary: Naysay all people want, but the fact that the Las Vegas Raiders are 2-0 to start the 2026 campaign under rookie head coach Klint Kubiak is impressive. This variant of the Silver & Black looks different than prior incarnations with Kubiak and Co.. I’ve said this to our Matt Holder: A professional football team. I […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Naysay all people want, but the fact that the Las Vegas Raiders are 2-0 to start the 2026 campaign under rookie head coach Klint Kubiak is impressive. This variant of the Silver & Black looks different than prior incarnations with Kubiak and Co.. I’ve said this to our Matt Holder: A professional football team. I know, that sounds asinine as Las Vegas is indeed one of the 32 teams in the NFL and “professional” is the status quo of the league. But for far too long, the Raiders were cellar dwellers as a moribund franchise. But teams play the opponents in front of them and Las Vegas stacked two victories so far. And there’s a very good test on the Raiders’ plate with the Week 3 road trip to face the New Orleans Saints. Like the Silver & Black, the Black & Gold engaged in a franchise course correction hiring a hotshot offensive-minded head coach Kellen Moore in February of 2025 to helm the team. Similarly to Kubiak, Moore is young (he’s 38 while Kubiak is 39) and brings a wealth of play-calling experience to the table. Both young leaders are instilling new cultures in their respective places and despite being 1-1 in the standings, the Saints easily could be unbeaten just like the Raiders. New Orleans boasts talent in all three phases — offense, defense, and special teams (including a very familiar face to Las Vegas) — and present quite the challenge for the visiting Raiders. Moore Is Required Elite edge rusher Maxx Crosby is keen to say and post on social media “More is required.” That’s definitely an apt mentality heading into this matchup with the Saints. Moore’s offense is seventh overall in the league averaging 383.5 yards and 27.0 points per game. The aerial attack led by quarterback Tyler Shough is second overall with 305.5 passing yards per game. And the second-year quarterback is the league leader with 662 passing yards heading into Week 3 action. Shough’s leading target — wide receiver Chris Olave — is off to an explosive start with 18 receptions for 268 yards and a touchdown. His 13 catches for first downs leads the NFL and he comes into this matchup with the Raiders off an eight-catch, 86-yard, and one-touchdown outing against the Baltimore Ravens in the Saints’ Week 2 24-17 win. Fellow wideout Devaughn Vele and tight end Juwan Johnson round out the top three pass catchers for Shough with 12 receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown and seven catches for 120 yards and a score, respectively. Tyler Shough zips it in to Chris Olave for SIX 🎯 NOvsBAL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oDswfhPi71 — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 Crosby and the secondary have played well for Las Vegas in the first two matchups of the season and the battle with Moore’s offense will rigorously test the Raiders’ ability this Sunday. The pass rush and coverage need to b e on point to combat the productive passing game as Moore loves to attack all over the field to truly stress the opposition. And even though New Orleans has the 28th ranked ground game — 78 yards per game average thus far — running backs Travis Etienne and Alvin Kamara are capable ball carriers and pass catchers. Young & The Restless Kubiak made it clear after the Raiders’ Week 2 26-14 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers: Quarterback Kirk Cousins was hit way too much for his liking. And there’s a high likelihood the Saints matchup can be a repeat of what displeased Cousins. Brandon Staley’s defense did a tremendous job containing and limiting the Ravens offense last week (233 passing yards and 65 rushing yards yielded) and the attacking style New Orleans deploys can be quite the predicament for a pure pocket passer like Cousins if the Raiders offensive line isn’t on point. Keeping Cousins upright against edge rushers Chase Young (team leading 1.5 sacks alongside three quarterback hits) and Carl Granderson (one sack), and linebacker Pete Werner (team leading 18 tackles with 1 sack) is a sound challenge for Kubiak and offensive line coach Rick Dennison. Veteran linebacker Kaden Elliss paces the Saints with five quarterback hits and has 15 total tackles. Once again, CHASE YOUNG. 📺 #NOvsBAL on CBS pic.twitter.com/fr0tmfN4oX — New Orleans Saints (@Saints) September 20, 2026 The Saints secondary features young talent with a veteran safety Julian Blackmon (who sealed the win against Baltimore with an interception) creating a similar front end/back end capability the Rob Leonard’s Raiders defense has shown on the young season. Head-to-Head Sunday’s contest marks the 17th between the Raiders and Saints and the Silver & Black leads the overall series 8-7-1. All games are regular season matchups as the two squads haven’t met in postseason play. Las Vegas won the last meeting between the two teams in New Orleans 25-10 back in December of 2024. Before that, the Saints won handily 24-0 back in 2022. The Raiders were victorious in the pair of meetings before that in 2016 and 2020, however. Quotes of Note “It’s been a huge part to the first part of the season, these victories, these team victories. Like I said, they have the attention of the other side of the ball. We just got to keep working to get better, and every week is a whole new game.” —Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak on how significant the team’s pass rush is despite not having to blitz much “I just think it’s important that we come back in every day, every week, regardless of the outcome win, loss, tie – the same person, same locker room. I think you just have to have your process, your way of getting ready for Sunday. That’s got to be consistent. You got to trust that routine, that rhythm, and not allow an outcome from a day before to suddenly change that. I think if you do that, you’re grasping at the win.” —Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins on if he’s noticed a difference in the locker room from the start of the season to a 2-0 record
