title: Raiders’ secondary must be ready for Tyler Shough, Chris Olave in Las Vegas Raiders-New Orleans Saints Week 3 matchup
summary: In what was viewed as a rebuilding year during the offseason, the Las Vegas Raiders find themselves at 2-0 heading into their last game of September. Meanwhile, the New Orleans Saints (1-1) are one point (and a controversial overturned strip sack) away from also being undefeated leading into the Raiders-Saints Week 3 contest. That puts […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images In what was viewed as a rebuilding year during the offseason, the Las Vegas Raiders find themselves at 2-0 heading into their last game of September. Meanwhile, the New Orleans Saints (1-1) are one point (and a controversial overturned strip sack) away from also being undefeated leading into the Raiders-Saints Week 3 contest . That puts two teams who are looking to end the month as potential playoff contenders against each other, where winning the three key matchups below could go a long way toward accomplishing that goal. Raiders DBs vs. Shough-Olave It’s early, but the Saints are making a compelling argument to have one of the NFL’s best young quarterback and wide receiver duos between Tyler Shough (turns 27 on Monday) and Chris Olave (26). Shough currently leads the league in passing yards with 662 through two games, while Olave is second in receiving yards with 268 . A big reason for that is those two have a strong connection down the field. According to Pro Football Focus , the second-year QB has completed six of eight (75%) pass attempts of 20 or more yards past the line of scrimmage, which is tied for the second-most completions and tied for best completion percentage on such throws. Additionally, he ranks third with 197 yards and owns a near-perfect PFF grade (99.9) on deep passes. Olave has been Shough’s go-to receiver, especially when pushing the ball downfield. He’s caught three of five targets (with one drop) and is third among wide receivers with 110 receiving yards on targets of 20-plus yards, trailing leader Davante Adams by just four yards, per PFF . The drop brings down Olave’s grade a bit, but he’s still tied for 12th at the position with a 94.2 mark. So, Las Vegas’ safeties will have to be on high alert. Rookie Treydan Stukes has taken the team’s most snaps at free safety ( 67 ) and looked sharp in the season opener, coming down with an interception off a deep shot from Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis. However, Stukes exited last week’s contest against the Los Angeles Chargers early with a concussion and hasn’t cleared the NFL’s protocol at the time of writing. [Editor’s note: Stukes was ruled out for the Saints game on Friday, after this was written.] That could mean Jeremy Chinn, the Raiders’ strong safety, rotates to the backend of the defense more often. Chinn has the second-most snaps at free safety (65) and is solid in that role but typically does his best work in the box. Meanwhile, Isaiah Pola-Mao is the backup center fielder and was a starter last year, but lost his job to Stukes in training camp. Pola-Mao filled in for the rookie last week and, most notably, had a coverage bust that yielded a 53-yard catch. But beyond the deep ball, a big part of what makes Olave a difficult cover is that he commands the entire secondary’s attention because he lines up all over the place. Of his 134 snaps in 2026, 48 have come as a left outside receiver, 44 on the right side and 42 in the slot, per PFF , a near 33.3% split across the board. So, cornerbacks Eric Stokes, Taron Johnson, Hezekiah Masses and/or Darien Porter all have to be at their best. Stokes was one of the few pleasant surprises from last year’s 3-14 team, ranking first among cornerbacks with 19.8 coverage snaps per reception during the regular season, per PFF . However, he’s struggled during the first two games of 2026, allowing five catches on nine targets (55.6%) for 63 yards and a 45.4 PFF coverage grade . Also, he hasn’t forced any incompletions this year, with three coming via errant throws and another receiver tipping the ball in the passing lane to account for the other. Johnson has been solid in slot coverage, giving up just two completions on three targets when playing nickel. However, he is susceptible to giving up a big play, with the two catches going for 42 yards, and the incompletion was a drop that would have been another 20-yard or more gain. The veteran defensive back has also been rotating into a free safety spot post-snap under new defensive coordinator Rob Leonard to factor into the deep ball equation as well. Finally, Masses is coming off his first start, where he won AFC Defensive Player of the Week by hauling in two interceptions. He was filling in for the injured Porter — whose Week 3 status is up in the air at the time of writing — and has been targeted seven times for two completions, 16 yards, one PBU (in addition to the two picks) and a 0.0 passer rating, per PFF . That will likely keep the rookie in the starting lineup even if Porter is healthy. But it still wouldn’t be surprising to see the second-year pro get at least some run, since he gave up just one catch and 12 yards despite getting thrown at five times by the Dolphins. Long story short, everyone in Las Vegas’ secondary must show up to keep Shough and Olave in check. Miller vs. Young Defensively, New Orleans doesn’t have many stars and has been a below-average unit through two weeks, ranking tied for 18th in points (48) and 23rd in yards (681) allowed. However, edge rusher Chase Young headlines the Saints’ defense and has had a hot start to the 2026 campaign. Among edge-rushers who have at least 18 pass-rush snaps, Young is tied for seventh with nine pressures (1.5 sacks), has the third-best win rate (26.0%) and is fifth in PFF pass-rush grade (85.8). Also, he’d have a strip-sack on his 2026 stat line if it weren’t for the controversial call referenced above. After injuries slowed down the beginning of his NFL tenure, the 2020 Defensive Rookie of the Year revived his career with the Saints, coming off a 10-sack performance in 12 games a year ago. Seeing as Young lines up almost exclusively as a right outside linebacker, he’s a big problem for opposing left tackles. Meanwhile, Kolton Miller has been the blindside protector for several Raiders quarterbacks over the last eight, going on nine seasons. He’s made a name for himself in pass protection over the years, and the first two games of 2026 have been no different. Per PFF , Miller has surrendered just two pressures on 63 opportunities to rank tied for second among offensive tackles with an 84.3 pass pro grade. That sets up for arguably the most important one-on-one battle in the trenches of the game. Jeanty vs. Elliss While Kaden Elliss doesn’t have any Pro Bowls or All-Pros on his resume, he’s one of the most underrated linebackers in the NFL. Elliss is a Swiss Army knife who can contribute on all three phases of the defense, which is why the Saints gave him a three-year, $33 million contract to return to New Orleans in the offseason. The eight-year veteran has shown off his versatile skill set to begin this season. In coverage, he’s only surrendered 19 yards when targeted, ranking tied for 16th among qualifying linebackers, and is yielding a completion once every 20 coverage snaps (tied for ninth), per PFF . As a run defender, his five ‘ defensive stops ’ are one less than the nine-way tie for first at the position, and his 1.7 average depth of tackle is tied for 16th (minimum 14 run defense snaps). But what makes Elliss somewhat unique for an off-ball backer is his pass-rush ability. The former seventh-round pick finished last season with the second-most pressures ( 30 ) at the position, and he currently ranks second in the metric with six on 19 opportunities in 2026. That’s where having a father, Luther Elliss, who is a former two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle and 1995 first-round pick, helps. In other words, Elliss and Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty should see plenty of head-to-head matchups on Sunday. Jeanty has had two very different performances this season. In Week 1, the offensive line paved plenty of rushing lanes for him to pick up 102 rushing yards (4.4 ypc), with 79 of them coming after contact, per PFF . However, Las Vegas’ offensive line had much more trouble with Los Angeles’ front seven, limiting the running back to 48 rushing yards (2.3 ypc), while…

title: Raiders are optimistic Brock Bowers will play Sunday at Saints
summary: Las Vegas Raiders superstar tight end Brock Bowers didn’t practice Friday, still the team is hopeful he will make his season debut Sunday at the New Orleans Saints. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Friday keeping Bowers out of practice Friday was part of the team’s plan and he said he is optimistic Bowers will play […]
full_text: (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders superstar tight end Brock Bowers didn’t practice Friday, still the team is hopeful he will make his season debut Sunday at the New Orleans Saints. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Friday keeping Bowers out of practice Friday was part of the team’s plan and he said he is optimistic Bowers will play Sunday. He was limited in practice both Wednesday and Thursday. Bowers missed the first two games of the season, both Raiders’ victories, after having knee surgery 17 days ago. Bowers was limited in practice Friday and worked out prior to the Chargers’ game Sunday, but was inactivated Raiders’ coach Klint Kubiak said after the game Bowers was “very close” to being ready to play. Kubiak noted there will not be a similar pre-game workout for Bowers in New Orleans. Michael Mayer would make his third straight start if Bowers can’t play Sunday. Starting defensive end Kwity Paye returned to practice Friday after being out Thursday with an illness. Still, Kubiak said he is questionable to play Sunday. Rookie starting safety Treydan Stukes has been in the concussion protocol all week and he will be out Sunday. Isaiah Pola-Mao, who Stukes beat out in training camp, is in line to start. Cornerback Darien Porter has been practicing fully and will play Sunday. However, it wouldn’t be a surprise if he plays behind Zeke Masses. The rookie fifth-round pick was named the Week 2 AFC Defensive player of the week after he had two interception in a win over the Chargers in his first NFL start. Number three quarterback Aidan O’Connell is listed as questionable Sunday, but he is not traveling with the team to New Orleans. . He announced his father has died and he has been away from the team since Sept. 17

full_text: (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders have begun the Klint Kubiak era 2-0. He is fifth coach in the franchise’s 25 non-interim head coaching tenures to win his first two games. Let’s look at the others: Al Davis, 1963: The eventual Raiders’ Hall of Fame owner went 23-1603 as the team’s head coach from 1963-65. The Raiders went 10-4, but did not make the playoffs. Davis was the AFL Coach of the Year that season. John Madden, 1969: The Hall of Fame coach went 103-32-7 spanning 1969-78 and the Raiders won a Super Bowl during that time. The Raiders went 12-1-1 in Madden’s first season and lost in the AFL championship game. Mike White, 1995: White went 15-17 spanning 1995-96 in Oakland. The Raiders went 8-8 in 1995. Bill Callahan, 2002: Callahan went 15-17 in two seasons with the Raiders. He inherited the best team of any of these coaches and the Raiders went to the Super Bowl in his first season. Now, let’s see what Kubiak can do in his Silver and Black career. It’s certainly off to a strong start.

title: Miami Dolphins review: 5 Things I Think I Think About Week 2
summary: Week 1 made me think, “OK, we lost, but maybe we’ll be better than people think.” Week 2 ground that idea into dust and already has me regretting my six-win prediction. Here’s my perhaps less-than-sanguine take on our team after Week 2. Not all of the Dolphins’ problems are due to youth. Do you remember […]
full_text: Week 1 made me think, “OK, we lost, but maybe we’ll be better than people think.” Week 2 ground that idea into dust and already has me regretting my six-win prediction. Here’s my perhaps less-than-sanguine take on our team after Week 2. Not all of the Dolphins’ problems are due to youth. Do you remember the Takes No Talent wall from 2019? When Brian Flores coached the team, players (and coaches!) would have to run to the TNT wall following a mistake or lapse in execution. It was intended to emphasize effort, discipline and accountability. I might not be the biggest Flores fan, but it takes no talent to: Secure the snap before punting . Make routine kicks. Avoid procedural penalties. Line up correctly. Execute assignments. Catch a punt. This roster’s path to victory is already narrow due to its youth and dead cap allotment. They can’t be missing field goals, muffing punts, gifting opponents short fields and coming away empty on red-zone drives. The Dolphins aren’t good enough to beat themselves and their opponent on the same Sunday. The lack of a pass rush might be the biggest problem on the roster. When you strip a team down to the studs and start building from scratch, you can’t be surprised that none of your position rooms is giving you even league-average play. But the Dolphins’ pass rush has been exceptionally bad through the first two games. How bad? The Dolphins are the only team to not record a sack through two games this season. They also have the second-worst defensive passing rating allowed. Brock Purdy completed 91% of his passes on Sunday – 91%! Sunday’s pressure statistics were just as bad. Fifty-seven pass rushes by tackles Zeek Biggers, Zach Sieler, Jordan Phillips and Keith Cooper generated just one quarterback pressure. On the edge, Josh Uche managed three pressures, but Malik Herring, Clelin Ferrell, Robert Beal, and Max Llewellyn failed to generate a single pressure on 25 combined pass-rushing snaps. Part of their struggles could be attributed to draft strategy – remember the Dolphins passed on Reuben Bain to draft OL Kadyn Proctor. But something tells me even Bain wouldn’t be enough to fix this motley group. My opinion of Austin Jackson is changing … for the better. Don’t get me wrong – my opinion of AJ’s game wasn’t especially high. And Sunday’s game was epically bad: 9 pressures allowed. 2 sacks allowed. 14% pressure rate allowed, which is the highest pressure percentage among qualifying offensive tackles. False starts and holding penalties. For one, that’s going to happen when you’re facing Maxx Crosby and Nick Bosa. Both are All-Pro-caliber pass rushers. More to the point, Austin Jackson is on a one-year contract and is highly unlikely to be on the team next year. I’m not judging him by sacks or pressures allowed as much as I’m asking, “Can he hold down the fort at right tackle while Kadyn Proctor learns to play left guard?” In a rebuilding year, that’s all I want from AJ: Keep Malik Willis upright while Proctor develops into, hopefully, an All-Pro of his own. (And just stop with the calls to start Caedan Wallace. Wallace is a 26-year-old who has appeared in 10 games for his career. Wallace protecting Willis from Crosby or Bosa would have gotten Willis killed.) Maybe Proctor’s future is at right tackle, but let’s get him comfortable at guard before having that conversation. Jeff Hafley’s job is safe for 2026. Losing to the bad teams and getting blown out by the good teams is not a recipe for long-term job security, even for first-time coaches conducting a rebuild. Still, as we discussed earlier, this isn’t a year to be judged by wins and losses. Hafley is building a culture on a team where one-third of his roster comprises first- or second-year players. I believe he could go 0-17 and still be given another year to see this rebuild through. What could make me change my mind? This: View this post on Instagram Undisciplined play, mental errors, a broken locker room – those things might cause me to question if Jeff Hafley is the right person for the job. But if we continue to see players playing hard and first- and second-year players grow into their positions, I think he stays. Rooting for the Dolphins will feel different this year. I’m the last person to tell anyone how to fan, especially if you support the Dolphins. If you are 25 years old or younger, then you were not even alive the last time the team won a playoff game. The fact that people are willing to root for this team at all is astounding, if you stop to think about it. We all knew the plan this offseason: Invest in youth and eat a record amount of dead cap. Still, hope springs eternal, especially in the final days before Labor Day. “Maybe if Malik is the second coming of Lamar Jackson, and if Players X and Y take a leap, who knows?” But after watching a couple of games, I think we have a better idea of what we’re in for. This isn’t one of those seasons where you think “Maybe we’ll steal a game from the Bills.” It’s more a season of “Maybe we’ll steal a game from the Jets,” and man, that’s hard to swallow. And yet, despite all of it, I’m as excited about the long-term future of this team as I’ve been in years. After years of treading water, firing the GM but keeping the coach and then firing the coach but keeping the GM, we finally get to watch a team build from the ground up. A young, tough team that is fun to root for. We have a player who is 6’5”, 315 pounds, whose last name is literally “Biggers.” Are you kidding me? How can you not root for Zeek Biggers? So fine, we’re underdogs against the Chiefs, like we’ll likely be throughout the season. But as these players grow, you can finally see a path toward the kind of sustained success this franchise hasn’t had in decades. You can sign me up for that right now.
author: Jim Reed

full_text: LAS VEGAS, NV - SEPTEMBER 13: Miami Dolphins linebacker Chop Robinson (44) walks off of the field after a NFL regular season game between the Las Vegas Raiders and Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium, Sunday September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, NV. (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Miami Dolphins third-year pass rusher Chop Robinson missed last Sunday’s loss to the San Francisco 49ers due to a concussion he suffered during practice leading up to the game. According to Robinson, it was his fifth documented concussion — third as a member of the Dolphins. On Thursday, speaking with the South Florida media, Robinson said that as a result of his latest brain injury, he will begin wearing a padded Guardian Cap moving forward in an effort to prevent further concussions. “ Just for me personally, I’m starting with a Guardian Cap, so I’m being smart about it, ” said Robinson. “ I want a future and [to] have kids and have a family and everything. So, I’ll just put the Guardian Cap [on]. There’s no harm in wearing it, so I might as well put it on. ” When speaking on the incident that caused his concussion during practice, Robinson said that it was “ just a football hit ,” but declined to further elaborate. According to an independent study , Guardian Caps can reduce incidences of concussions by 54-62%. We will continue to keep you updated on all things Miami Dolphins as the team prepares to battle the Kansas City Chiefs at Hard Rock Stadium this Sunday.

title: Three Reasons With The Earl: Miami Dolphins Hope, Concern Week 3
summary: The 2026 season looks rough for the Miami Dolphins. They were outclassed against an NFC contender and now turn around to face Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. There is not going to be much hope to be found this season. But dagnabbit, I will squeeze what little hope I can out of this team. Just […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins looks on before a game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 season looks rough for the Miami Dolphins. They were outclassed against an NFC contender and now turn around to face Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. There is not going to be much hope to be found this season. But dagnabbit, I will squeeze what little hope I can out of this team. Just for you’uns (pronounced ‘yuns’). Like I said last week, I’m going to focus on areas that may not be major talking points elsewhere e.g. Patrick Mahomes. 3 REASONS FOR HOPE SOMEONE CALL OSHA… BUT NOT FOR ME ! The Dolphins get their first home game of the season and that hot Miami sun will likely be a factor. The projected weather report says mid 80s for the game, and that sun and heat will still be a factor, as it always is. Home cooking is always a positive factor in the NFL. Sure, the Dolphins fans may not be as enthusiastic about the team this year and may not pack the stadium, but home games are still beneficial to the host regardless. Last week, Miami controlled the time of possession by a slight margin overall, but considerably more in the 1st half. They held a 19:17 to 10:43 lead in TOP. They also had scoring opportunities they just didn’t capitalize on. If they can lean on the run game and control the clock in the Miami weather, the Chiefs defense will start to wear down. And in the NFL, all it takes is an opportunity or two for a big play to turn a game around. THE CHIEFS HIT THE ROAD The Chiefs are coming off a two primetime contests at home, including an overtime SNF contest against the Colts. Arrowhead is a notoriously dominant home field advantage, but now they must travel to the east coast to play a 1PM EST game. The Chiefs are a good team and should be favored – as they are – but road games in the NFL, even against bad teams, are still tough to win. Coach Hafley has started to get tougher on this team and he mentioned that despite the youth and talent deficiencies, they are playing harder, tougher, and with good intensity and teams are noticing that. A young, hungry team wanting to impress their coach and get him his first W of the season at home might make for a punch in the mouth the Chiefs aren’t expecting. Add that in with the weather factor, this could be a tougher out than imagined for the favored team. AN OPPORTUNITY FOR REDEMPTION Last week I mentioned that the 49ers did not generate much pressure against the Rams. Though the Rams have a better OL than the Dolphins, I still thought Miami had an opportunity to keep Willis cleaner than they did against the Raiders. Well, they kinda did and kinda didn’t. Willis was pressured often, mostly due to issue with one particular offensive lineman. But 2 of the sacks Willis had were him running out of bounds behind the line of scrimmage. He should have thrown the ball away if we are being honest. We can also say he’s becoming a runner at that point. But it goes on the stat sheet as a sack. The 49ers only got Willis on the ground twice and that’s with a premier pass rusher in Nick Bosa. The 49ers also don’t blitz at a high rate, so when they did, they caught the Dolphins in a bind. The Chiefs do not have a premier edge rusher. They have 3 sacks on the season, with 2 coming from the edge group. George Karlaftis III is the most productive of the group with 30.5 career sacks. Felix Anudike-Uzomah has 4 career sacks with 3 of them prior to 2026. Ashton Gillotte is a second-year player with 1.5 career sacks and R. Mason Thomas is a rookie with 1 sack on the season. The Dolphins have faced the likes of Maxx Crosby and Bosa and now get a less prominent group. That doesn’t mean they are bad and won’t generate pressure, but they haven’t proven to be the weapons the Dolphins have seen so far. They do have Chris Jones as an interior rusher, but that’s not an issue for the OTs. The Chiefs also blitz at a higher rate. They are 5th in the league at 39.4% (Miami faces Brian Flores and the Vikings next week who lead the league in blitz rate at a whopping 81.8%). The Raiders and the Niners blitz in the 22% range. Why is this fact a positive? Because the Dolphins can expect and plan for it. They can build in protections and outlets to get the ball out of Willis’ hands quicker to take advantage of the blitzes. The Chiefs have faced two QBs this season who have decent scrambling ability. But neither have the rushing ability that Willis possesses. A poorly timed blitz could get Willis out on the edge and into the secondary before they know it. It will be up to Slowik and Willis to account for this and use it wisely. BONUS REASON: Watch this reel: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DdmCOhxkVLE/?stkn=MTlwaXcxcXpidW5tOQ== REASONS FOR CONCERN THE CHIEFS HAVE A RUNNING GAME If I asked you where you think Miami falls defensively in terms of yards allowed, where do think it would be? Dead last right? Ackchyually, they are middle of the pack. They are 19th in yards allowed overall and 18th in both passing and rushing yards allowed. Given how both Vegas and San Fran tap-danced their way up and down the field, I would have thought the Dolphins would be league worst. But you know who is league worst? The Indianapolis Colts, the team the Chiefs just beat on SNF. Part of that is pass defense, but both Chiefs’ opponents this season are bottom 4 in rushing yards allowed and yards per attempt allowed. That’s because they faced off against the league’s leading rusher and reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker. Walker has 290 rushing yards on 47 carries in 2 games. The Chiefs are leaning on him and he’s producing. The Dolphins quietly had a solid day against the rushing attack of the 49ers. They gave up 3 rushing TDs, but both main RBs for SF had 48 yards on 17 carries. It was QB Brock Purdy leading the way with 3 scrambles for 30 yards. This game will look more like week 1 where the Raiders leaned on Ashton Jeanty, who went 23 for 102. In a game where heat and TOP will be a factor, the Chiefs will likewise try to take advantage of it with their new weapon. The Dolphins are near the top of the league in missed tackles with only 9. The Broncos and Colts are the bottom two at 27 and 22 respectively. Some of that may be on the defenders. But Walker is tied for 2nd in the league in broken tackles with 6 and is 1st in yards after contact with 199. He is 2nd in YAC/att at 4.2. Much of the talk will be about Mahomes, but Walker is the imminent threat. NO CALEB DOUGLAS = NO BUENO The emergence of Caleb Douglas has been the best story from an offseason and young season that offers little in the way of positives for the Dolphins. The 49ers have a solid pass defense, and they limited Douglas to 2 catches for 19 yards, with the second catch not coming until midway into the 4Q. He’s a rookie and we expect some ups and downs. The problem is after that catch, Douglas went down with an injury, which appeared to be an ankle injury. He limped off and was walking on the sideline, so perhaps it’s not too severe. But he has not practiced yet this week. If he misses the game or is limited, the Dolphins will have little to lean on in the way of the passing game. Malik Washington has had some moments where he got open, but the Chiefs play Cover-1(man) 25.8% of the time, their highest usage of typical coverages. The Dolphins don’t have guys that can beat man coverage on a consistent basis. Douglas is their best chance. Not only that, but the Chiefs have the 4th best passing defense in terms of yards allowed and in yards per attempt allowed. They are 9th in passer rating allowed. They are tied with several teams for 3rd place with only 2 passing TDs allowed. If they stuff the Dolphins run game, the offense may not get off the ground without Douglas. The silver lining is that both TDs the Chiefs’ pass defense…

title: Vikings Emerge as Early Favorites to Win the NFC North
summary: In what seems like a long time ago already, but still only two weeks ago, the Minnesota Vikings were projected to finish at the bottom of the NFC North and had the longest odds to win the division at +550 or so just prior to the start of the season. But after a 2-0 start […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - SEPTEMBER 13: Minnesota Vikings cornerback Zemaiah Vaughn (5) and Minnesota Vikings linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel (43) sack Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) causing him to fumble during the fourth quarter of a NFL game between the Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers on September 13, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis MN. (Photo by Nick Wosika/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images In what seems like a long time ago already, but still only two weeks ago, the Minnesota Vikings were projected to finish at the bottom of the NFC North and had the longest odds to win the division at +550 or so just prior to the start of the season. But after a 2-0 start with wins over two division opponents in the Packers and Bears, the Vikings have become the betting favorites to win the division, with odds shortening to +150. Meanwhile, the odds for the Packers have lengthened from around +200 just prior to the season start to +760 today. The odds for the Bears have also lengthened some to +385. The odds for the Lions have stayed roughly the same at +170, just behind the Vikings now. It’s easy to jump to conclusions based on early results, but it’s a long season and most teams in the division still have 15 games to play and anything can happen. Having said that, there are some developments that could influence division results. Let’s take a look by team. Green Bay Packers The Packers are now 1-2 after losing their home opener to the Atlanta Falcons 35-14 and getting booed off the field by the Packers faithful. It was the first home opener the Packers have lost in 14 seasons and it was an ugly one. The main issue for the Packers is their offensive line is historically bad at this point. They have the worst pass blocking win rate after three games since they started recording the stat. They also have the fewest rushing yards after three games in franchise history going back to 1933. They have the worst overall team PFF grade and a bunch of other not-so-flattering stats. But fixing the offensive line at this point- and they just lost their only good offensive lineman in Zach Beto-Bewele (formerly Tom) for the season- is a nearly impossible task. All five starting offensive linemen are bad at this point and replacing them with better performers in-season is basically impossible. The only hope is they improve as the season wears on. The fear is that if they continue at this level there is no way starting quarterback Jordan Love will manage to escape injury, making things that much worse. The Packers have gotten good starts from wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, and Lukas Van Ness appears to have taken his game to the next level, which will make a formidable edge-rushing tandem with Micah Parsons when he returns in a month or so, but by that time it may be too little, too late. Chicago Bears The Bears started the season strong, racking up 59 points against a weak Carolina defense, but fell back to earth against the Vikings, scoring just 3 points in the Chicago rain. Caleb Williams also suffered a grade 1 hamstring injury which will likely keep him out of the next couple games for the Bears. Backup Tyson Bagent also suffered a concussion in the Vikings game, which will keep him out of their matchup against the Eagles on Monday night. The Bears have the toughest schedule in the division by a significant margin and a suspect defense so if the Bears drop a game or two early on (and most expected them to beat the Vikings at home), it may be difficult for the Bears to make up for that later in the season. Detroit Lions The Lions need overtime to beat the Saints week one, then lost convincingly to the Bills in week two. Overall, it is a weak start for the Lions largely due to their defense, which ranks 31st in both points and yards allowed after two weeks. The Lions have a few injured players in their defensive secondary, most notably Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph, who are currently on the PUP list. Branch will likely return after two more games, but Joseph’s return is more doubtful. Beyond that, there is some concern about Kelvin Sheppard as defensive coordinator and the talent of the secondary with so many injuries and even the healthy starters at cornerback. The Lions’ offensive line looked shaky to start the season but has held up reasonably well so far. They are dealing with some injuries but overall it hasn’t been terrible. It’s not as good as 2024 either, however. Overall, the Lions don’t seem to be as dominant out of the gate as some people expected, and they have a test on Sunday against the Jets, who nearly beat the Packers last week after beating the Titans to start the season. The Jets have the toughest defense the Lions have faced so far this season. But the Lions also have by far the easiest schedule in the division and that should help keep them in contention for the division crown over the course of the season. But the question of just how good the Lions really are remains unanswered thus far. Minnesota Vikings The Vikings are off to the early lead in the division race, with a one-game lead plus a tie-breaker advantage over the Packers and Bears in head-to-head matchups, with a chance to widen that lead by the end of Monday night. The Vikings play a desperate Tampa Bay team at 0-2, given that only one team has ever made the playoffs after going 0-3 to start the season (The Texans did it twice). The Bucs fell behind 24-10 to the Bengals to start the season but rallied to make it a one-score loss at 33-27 but then lost to the Browns at home 23-20. The Bucs have lost the turnover battle in both games so far but have been good in the ground game and stopping the run. But I suspect this Buccaneers team is looking for an identity as they’ve struggled out of the gate and don’t really have much top-tier talent across their roster. The Vikings are a 1.5-point road favorite. But the Vikings also have questions, particularly on offense. The defense has carried the team so far, with Carson Wentz stepping in for the injured Kyler Murray. But the Wentz-led offense ranks last in total yards, last in passing yards, second-to-last in passing yards per attempt, and 25th in rushing yards per attempt. Winning the turnover battle and being effective on both sides of the ball in the redzone have been the keys to success so far. The expectation is that Kyler Murray will put up at least average numbers in the passing game and add some to the running game on occasion, but he had a poor start in his 11 plays against the Packers, throwing an interception before suffering a concussion on a scramble run. If Murray is able to put up at least career-average numbers for him, that combined with a dominant defense should keep the Vikings in the top spot in the division based on how things have unfolded so far, but whether Murray can be a catalyst for the offense, and whether Brian Flores’ heavy-blitz approach will continue to be so successful remains to be seen. Bottom Line The way the first couple weeks have unfolded in the NFC North reveals perhaps a weaker division than originally thought and one the Vikings are in good position to win at this point. All that has been a surprise to most pundits. In my own forecast I had the Vikings and Lions fighting it out for the division title, with the Packers and Bears further back. Will see what happens down the road, but so far the NFC North may be the most surprising division in the league. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

summary: The Minnesota Vikings and Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their final injury reports, along with injury designations, in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup in Tampa. Here they are. full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Will Reichard #16 of the Minnesota Vikings is congratulated by Brett Thorson #19 after kicking a field goal against the Chicago Bears during the fourth quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings and Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their final injury reports, along with injury designations, in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup in Tampa. Here they are. Minnesota Vikings Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Jordan Mason* RB Thumb DNP DNP DNP IR-OUT Jake Golday LB Ankle DNP LP FP — Aaron Jones* RB Knee DNP LP FP — Brett Thorson* P Hamstring DNP DNP DNP OUT DeeJay Dallas RB Toe LP LP FP — Ty Ingram-Dawkins* DL Oblique LP FP FP — Brian O’Neill* RT Knee LP FP FP — Jalen Redmond DT Elbow LP LP FP — Nick Samac C Knee LP DNP DNP OUT Christian Darrisaw LT NIR-Rest — — DNP — Harrison Smith S NIR-Rest — — LP — Tampa Bay Buccaneers Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Rueban Bain Jr.* OLB Groin DNP DNP DNP OUT Baker Mayfield* QB Illness FP FP FP — Jalen McMillan WR Knee FP FP FP — Anthony Nelson LB Shin DNP LP FP — Jacob Parrish CB Back FP FP FP — Josiah Trotter* LB Shoulder DNP DNP LP DOUBTFUL A’Shawn Robinson* DL NIR-Rest — LP FP — Injury Report Terms and Glossary FP = Full participant in practice. LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and play on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically, only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and play on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day, and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Vikings, the only two players with injury designations are Brett Thorson and Nick Samac and both of them will be inactive on Sunday. Johnny Hekker, who lost the punting/holding competition to Thorson in training camp last month, was signed to the practice squad earlier this week and will be elevated to the active roster to take on the punting/holding duties. It sounds like Thorson could potentially miss at least an additional game as he works through his hamstring injury. Hekker will likely continue to be elevated to the active roster as rules allow while Thorson recovers. For the Bucs, two starters on defense have injury designations – edge rusher Rueban Bain Jr. and linebacker Josiah Trotter. Bain will not play on Sunday and Trotter is unlikely to be active as well, given his doubtful designation. Bain had not been particularly effective in his first two games, so perhaps not a big loss there, but Trotter had played well over the first two weeks so that will be a bigger loss if he is indeed inactive on Sunday as expected. title: Week 3 Preview: A Desperate and Dangerous Opponent
summary: The Minnesota Vikings are on the road again in Week 3, traveling to Tampa Bay to face a desperate and dangerous Buccaneers team. They are desperate because, at potentially 0-3, they face only about a 3% chance to recover and make the playoffs. And it’s only that high because the Houston Texans managed it last […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 10: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings runs the ball against Carlton Davis III #24 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the second quarter of a game at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 10, 2023 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Adam Bettcher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings are on the road again in Week 3, traveling to Tampa Bay to face a desperate and dangerous Buccaneers team. They are desperate because, at potentially 0-3, they face only about a 3% chance to recover and make the playoffs. And it’s only that high because the Houston Texans managed it last year, which was oddly their second time achieving the rare feat (2018). Dangerous because they are arguably the NFL’s most consistently inconsistent team. It would not surprise me if they went on the road and beat the Kansas City Chiefs or lost a game at home to, well, the Cleveland Browns. The range of outcomes on any given Sunday is enormous. SETTING THE STAGE The Buccaneers have been the big fish in the small pond that is the NFC South, winning the division three of the last four years under head coach Todd Bowles. However, their best record over that span was 10-7. They actually won the division with an 8-9 record in 2022. The Vikings and Buccaneers have met only once in the Kevin O’Connell era, a 20-17 home loss in Week 1 of 2023. That was a frustrating game. The Vikings started slowly, but Kirk Cousins finished with 344 yards and 2 TDs. In the end, three turnovers proved too much to overcome. It was indeed a harbinger of an up-and-down, but ultimately disappointing season for the Vikings. The game also marked Brian Flores’ first as the Vikings’ defensive coordinator. It wasn’t without drama, as Baker Mayfield later claimed he had figured out the Vikings’ defensive signals coming in from the sidelines. I suppose it’s plausible, given it was Flores’ first game and the players were in a new and incredibly complex defensive scheme. Needless to say, Mayfield won’t benefit from anything like that again on Sunday. VIKINGS ON OFFENSE The big news, of course, is the return of Kyler Murray. Hopefully, we can finally see what this offense can do. He should get an opportunity, as Tampa Bay’s defense has been far better against the run (4th) than the pass (21st). They’re also coming off a game in which they let Deshaun Watson have maybe his best outing since being traded to the Cleveland Browns (238 yards, 2 TDs, 121.9 QB rating). Over the first two games, they’ve allowed a whopping QB passer rating of 105.4. Bowles also serves as the Buccaneers’ defensive coordinator, and his fondness for the blitz is no secret. After seeing the first few series in Week 1, it’s unlikely he will question that philosophy. I’d be shocked if he didn’t test Murray and the Vikings’ offensive line early and often with varied pressures. Getting home has been an issue for their defense, with just three sacks in two games. That is not good given their high blitz rate. I’d expect KOC to be ready for this and to run effective screens and quick-hitting counters. Murray’s mobility will also help. The challenge for the Vikings offense will be to maintain its commitment to the run against a tremendous Buccaneers front that’s allowing only 75 yards per game and 3.0 yards per carry. Bowles wants to get you into those 3rd-and-long, predictable passing situations so he can bring the house. If things aren’t going well for Aaron Jones early, KOC may seek to manufacture plays through read-option/Murray keepers or other creative ways to stay ahead of the sticks. There should be opportunities for Murray to make hay if the offensive protection holds up. If things go as planned, this could be the debut of what could be a scary offense. Then again, we are the Vikings. Things going as planned hasn’t exactly been our thing over the years. Let’s be optimistic, shall we? VIKINGS ON DEFENSE Brian Flores has the Vikings defense rolling into Week 3, allowing 12.5 points per game and ranking in the top five in DVOA. Under Flores, the Vikings have ranked #1 in blitz frequency every year of his tenure here, but this year is on another level altogether . While he previously topped out at 49.4% in 2023, he’s at an absolutely ridiculous 75% clip so far in 2026. "I tell our guys all the time, 'If we're going to go down, we're going to go down a certain way. We're going to go down blitzing people.'" – Brian Flores pic.twitter.com/ou5PmInSHh — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) September 22, 2026 I’m fist-pumping the air as Frank Sinatra sings “My Way” in my head. This philosophy will face a Buccaneers offense under new coordinator Zac Robinson that has been mediocre over the first two weeks: 16th in points, 19th in net yards, 23rd in net pass yards, and 12th in rush yards. They already have a horrible -4 turnover margin, and Baker Mayfield has taken seven sacks in two games. In the end, Baker is going to be Baker; he’s capable of looking like the league’s MVP one game, then making a series of head-scratching mistakes the next. And while Mike Evans is gone, the cupboard isn’t bare when it comes to offensive weapons. Chris Godwin and Emeka Egbuka form an explosive and dangerous wide receiver combination. Cade Otton is solid at tight end. Running back Bucky Irving has a tremendous 5.4 yards per attempt so far this season. Given the state of desperation and since this is as much of a “must-win” game as you can have in Week 3, I expect Zac Robinson to roll the dice. It’s going to be tough for the Buccaneers to win this game without a handful of explosive plays, and Baker Mayfield is not the type of guy you need to ask twice to channel his inner Nick Mullens. What makes the Flores defense so innovative and difficult to play is that he plays like Buddy Ryan upfront but like Vic Fangio in the back end. ESPN’s Kevin Seifert wrote a great article on it back in 2023, and it explained how Pittsburgh Panthers head coach Pat Narduzzi helped influence Flores to create something new and unique at the NFL level. Given these defensive intricacies, if Robinson and Mayfield do the Rex Grossman routine on Sunday, it could very well blow up in their faces. We shall see. PREDICTION I believe Todd Bowles wants to put this game on (yet) unproven Kyler Murray. He’s going to take away Aaron Jones and force Murray to show he’s comfortable with KOC’s new system. Given that it’s Week 3 of the regular season and Murray has played only 11 snaps, it’s a sensible strategy. I’ve been on record saying Murray will have a strong season overall, but it may take time for him to truly hit his stride. The key here is to avoid turnovers. I have a hard time seeing the Buccaneers win this one without winning the turnover battle and getting some short fields. We couldn’t do that in the 2023 meeting, but we do so this time around. Murray is solid, and the defense continues to play at an exceptional level. Minnesota Vikings: 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 14

title: 3-Point Stance: How Drake Maye can bounce back from his rough start
summary: Two games into the 2026 season, Drake Maye has not looked like himself. So far, the New England Patriots quarterback has thrown four interceptions to just one touchdown. Maye committed three of those turnovers in the fourth quarter alone against the Seattle Seahawks, effectively losing New England the season opener. While the 2025 MVP runner-up’s […]
full_text: Two games into the 2026 season, Drake Maye has not looked like himself. So far, the New England Patriots quarterback has thrown four interceptions to just one touchdown. Maye committed three of those turnovers in the fourth quarter alone against the Seattle Seahawks, effectively losing New England the season opener. While the 2025 MVP runner-up’s third season hasn’t been catastrophic by any means and doesn’t warrant long-term concern, he consistently appears to be flustered in the pocket and not confident in what he’s seeing past his offensive line. And considering the Patriots soon match up against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Buffalo Bills and the Chicago Bears before star wide receiver A.J. Brown can return, timely adjustments need to be made. Although we can’t know exactly how Maye is processing the field, we have the resources to make estimates about why the signal-caller has struggled and how he can respond. Embracing the short game It’s important to note that NFL defenses are always adjusting. Therefore, Maye will have to adapt while also reestablishing the traits that made him an MVP candidate just one season ago. Across the Patriots’ first two contests, the Seahawks and Pittsburgh Steelers defenses lined up with two-high safeties just over 50% of the time when facing Maye. Oftentimes, their play designs call for split-safety coverage, with their defense playing in cover two, four, or the dreaded cover six. Progressing past the chains by taking the routine underneath plays forces those safeties to eventually adapt and play closer to the line of scrimmage. Excelling in the short passing game involves remaining “disciplined,” a word offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels used last week to describe how New England can adjust to how opposing teams will approach defending Maye. The 24-year-old was efficient in that approach against Seattle, leading the reigning Super Bowl champions 7-0 at halftime, until he “lost patience.” McDaniels added that there’s a “fine line” between taking care of the ball and taking what the defense allows while staying aggressive and making downfield plays. He called that attribute one of Maye’s greatest. Reestablishing his poise in the pocket Maye’s presence in the pocket is an area where the third-year quarterback has struggled to start the season, lacking the poise and composure that allowed him to methodically maneuver around pressure and throw with strong velocity and accuracy while staying in the pocket. Yet this season, Maye often bails from the pocket when he doesn’t need to. He appears to be playing too quickly, second-guessing himself and making abrupt decisions, potentially indicating that opposing defenses are speeding him up mentally as he diagnoses what’s happening in front of him. Pro Football Focus assigned Maye a 26.8 passing grade under pressure. A potential reason why he looks stiff in the pocket may be an effort to prevent fumbles, which he struggled with in the 2025 postseason, losing possession four times. Still, as McDaniels alluded to, there’s a middle ground. Recapturing those attributes begins with Maye playing more decisively without letting defenses accelerate his mental processing. That means operating the short passing game quickly and with confidence in his decision-making. “Being decisive and believing in what you see,” head coach Mike Vrabel said on Wednesday about his quarterback. “Again, what we ask all our players to do is prepare to try to play fast and aggressively and make great decisions. “Ultimately, it’s [Maye’s] responsibility to distribute the football as quickly and decisively as possible in the places that it’s supposed to go, continuing not to force things and try to just create a next play on every single play.” Preventing the underthrows If defenses are disrupting Maye’s timing, it could also be contributing to his uncharacteristic underthrows. Operating in the pocket while questioning decisions in the moment can alter his throwing mechanics and timing, causing passes to fall short. Two of Maye’s takeaways resulted from passes coming up short, with the final one against the Seahawks being an ill-advised decision to force a pass rather than settle for a tying field-goal attempt. That trend could make Sunday’s matchup especially challenging as Jacksonville’s defense excels at producing turnovers. Last season, the Jaguars ranked No. 2 in the NFL with 22 total interceptions, which was just one takeaway shy of the Bears in first. Throughout their two games thus far, they already have two. Until Maye makes the necessary adjustment, the Patriots could be playing from behind on Sunday. “One of the best things about getting new chances every week is having to let the other ones go,” Maye said on Wednesday. “That’s one of the best things about this sport and playing this position. You have to let plays go, and you want to be attacking the next play, learning from the ones in the past and getting after the next one. “So, I definitely think [it’s] hard to play this position when you’re thinking about a lot of different things. It’s going to be natural to think about motions, fronts, defenses, what our guys are doing, route concepts and what they’re doing versus the play we have [set] up. So, just thinking and trying to be instinctive. That’s one of the best things I learned in college is to be instinctive and try to play as fast as you can back there.”

(Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots will head into the fall without Quintayvious Hutchins on the field. The organization officially placed the rookie outside linebacker on injured reserve Friday afternoon. No corresponding 53-man roster move was announced as the Jacksonville Jaguars await the arrival of the 2025 AFC champions. That leaves a spot open on the way to EverBank Stadium. Hutchins, 23, had been ruled out along with veteran outside linebacker Dre’Mont Jones after missing three consecutive practices due to a knee injury. The former Boston College team captain was among several players to not finish last weekend’s 20-3 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers and will now miss a minimum of four games. Taken in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL draft at No. 247 overall, Hutchins marked the last selection for the war room. The 6-foot-3, 245-pound rookie out of Chestnut Hill outlasted the 53-man roster deadline following training camp. In two games from there, he had a hand in three tackles across 16 snaps on defense and 12 snaps on special teams. He stands as the 10th player currently on injured reserve in Foxborough. The Patriots recently promoted edge rusher Jose Ramirez from the practice squad to the active roster amid the attrition. The depth chart also includes sophomore starter Elijah Ponder and rookie second-rounder Gabe Jacas, who have combined for two sacks, one interception, one fumble recovery and one touchdown return this September. New England’s final injury report saw tight end tight end Eli Raridon and safety Craig Woodson listed as questionable for the road trip to Jacksonville. Sunday’s kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET.

title: Patriots rookie Namdi Obiazor emerging as a special teams standout
summary: The New England Patriots’ first two games of the season have started the same way: rookie Namdi Obiazor making a tackle on the opening kickoff. Obiazor hasn’t stopped there. After becoming the first Patriots player since at least 2000 to record three special teams tackles in his very first NFL game, Obiazor recorded two more […]
full_text: The New England Patriots’ first two games of the season have started the same way: rookie Namdi Obiazor making a tackle on the opening kickoff. Obiazor hasn’t stopped there. After becoming the first Patriots player since at least 2000 to record three special teams tackles in his very first NFL game, Obiazor recorded two more in Week 2 against the Steelers. Through two weeks, his five special teams tackles are tied for second in the NFL. “Taking advantage of his opportunities, man. And he’s playing to our identity,” special teams coordinator Jeremy Springer said Thursday. “He’s full tilt to the tackle. He’s finishing on the guy with the ball. He’s making great decisions. He’s being detailed his technique and fundamentals. He’s being disruptive at the ball. So all the things I think Coach Vrabel talks about from a team culture, he’s doing that right now. “Just want to continue to progress him, keep him confident, and that’s his role right now, and I hope he continues to take advantage of that and do what he’s doing.” Despite taking on a limited special teams role over his final few seasons at TCU, New England’s special teams coaches identified the athletic Obiazor as a potential fit ahead of the 2026 NFL Draft. The Patriots went on to select Obiazor in the sixth round with the 212th overall pick, where he then assumed a top special teams role for the majority of training camp to earn a spot on the 53-man roster. “He’s just being a pro. I mean, he’s taken every rep — like we just had a walk through [Thursday morning] and he’s very locked in and focused on the things he needs to do to win the game,” Springer said. “He’s watching the film. He’s paying attention to the scouting report and, yeah, he’s doing everything a pro should do in a job that he has right now. That’s his role. That’s what he’s doing. “He’s taking full ownership of that and I think he’s doing a great job with that. He’s just got to continue to progress through the season.” The Patriots saw major turnover on their special teams units this season. Seven of the 12 players to log more than 100 special teams snaps last season did not start the year on the Week 1 roster, including ace Brenden Schooler, who began the year on the reserve/non-football injury list. That opened the door for younger players like Obiazor to take on larger roles across multiple units, and the sixth-round pick has quickly established himself as one of the Patriots’ most productive special teams players — a transition that has stood out to the coaching staff. “I think he has really improved,” head coach Mike Vrabel said. “I would say just for young players, sometimes NFL special teams is a little different, right? The punt is different; our kickoff is different. But the guys you’re going against, too, they’re special teams, that’s what they do, and they’ve got the tricks of the trade we talked about. But I think he’s really learned quickly and improved each and every week from training camp, and it’s been really good to see him translate that not only on his coverage units but also in protection. “Talking about the kickoff return, he’s done a really nice job with that. So, excited for him to have some success and keep going, pile up the tackles.”
author: Brian Hines

title: Patriots vs. Jaguars weather forecast for NFL Week 3
summary: The New England Patriots have not played in 80-plus degrees since a game in Miami last September. That streak will come to an end on Sunday: their Week 3 road game against the Jacksonville Jaguars is projected to kick off at around 83°F. According to NFL Weather, temperatures will climb to 85°F during the game […]
full_text: The New England Patriots have not played in 80-plus degrees since a game in Miami last September. That streak will come to an end on Sunday: their Week 3 road game against the Jacksonville Jaguars is projected to kick off at around 83°F. According to NFL Weather , temperatures will climb to 85°F during the game while there is a slight chance of rain showers in the second half. Humidity, however, is not expected to exceed 30%. There will be wind gusts of up to 11 mph with the real-feel temperature hovering around 82-83°F all day. For the Patriots, this marks a change compared to their first two games of the season. Both their season-opening loss in Seattle and their win over the Steelers in Foxborough last Sunday were played in comparatively moderate temperatures of 74°F and 63°F at kickoff, respectively. Despite the increased heat, the forecast is still relatively favorable from a New England perspective. Jacksonville’s first opponent this season, after all, had to play in 90-degree weather with humidity in the 60s; the visiting Browns lost that game 34-10. The Patriots leaving Florida with a different result in hand starts with preparing for the heat both mentally and physically. “Have to be hydrated. Get an IV,” defensive tackle Milton Williams said on Thursday. “I’m going to put a hoodie on now for practice. … I try to make myself get accustomed to the heat a little bit more, but I feel like if you’re hydrated, you should be all right.” Kickoff between the Patriots and Jaguars is scheduled for Sunday, Sept. 27 at 1 p.m. ET.

title: Patriots mailbag: What problems will the Jaguars present Drake Maye?
summary: After a Week 2 victory that came with the injury bug, the New England Patriots are set to head down to Jacksonville for a Week 3 matchup with the Jaguars. So, let’s get into this week’s #PostPulpit Mailbag. What defensive schemes do the Jags run? How are the coverage corners? Will we see some man? […]
full_text: After a Week 2 victory that came with the injury bug, the New England Patriots are set to head down to Jacksonville for a Week 3 matchup with the Jaguars. So, let’s get into this week’s #PostPulpit Mailbag. What defensive schemes do the Jags run? How are the coverage corners? Will we see some man? How good are they in 2 deep zone? Have they effectively run cover 6? What’s their blitz rate? How effective are they at just rushing 4? What did the Broncos do to turn that game around and put up 17 unanswered? How are the Jags vs stopping the run? – Maye The Force Be With You Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile has quite the coaching background, having come up under defensive coaches Vic Fangio, Brian Flores, Jeff Hafley and other respected defensive minds. “He’s got his own style. I’ll say that,” offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels said. “I know where he’s come from and who he’s been subjected to and I’m sure he’s learned an immense amount from those people. But he’s got his own personality. You can see it on the film. There’s games where they do some different things and challenge you schematically.” Similar to Fangio, Campanile leans heavily on zone coverages, running them more than 75% of the time. And speaking of the infamous Cover 6, the Jaguars have used it at the second-highest rate (19.6%) in the NFL since 2025 — only behind Fangio himself — with strong results. Campanile’s background under Flores then shows up in his exotic blitz packages, where Jacksonville sends extra rushers at the ninth-highest rate in the NFL (36.7%). As for their personnel, Jacksonville has a unique rotation in its secondary, with four cornerbacks — Montaric Brown, Jarring Jones, Travis Hunter and Jourdan Lewis — each playing between 53% and 77% of the defensive snaps. Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker bookend the defensive front — a good, but not great unit like the Patriots have played the first two weeks. The scheme and aggressiveness have led to plenty of turnovers, with Jacksonville forcing three in two games after ranking second in the NFL last season with 31. But that aggression can also be exploited, as the Jaguars have been one of the NFL’s worst deep-pass defenses through two games. Denver also found success getting Bo Nix on the move, something the Patriots could look to replicate with Drake Maye. I have a feeling the injury to Onwenu could prove to be a disaster for the Offensive Line. I thought Van Roten was scary awful when Onwenu went down. Will they give someone else a shot next week. Like Walter Rouse, they even had Lomu play some Guard in camp. Will Lomu, Rouse, or someone else get a chance at Guard? – Elderly Lothario It certainly wasn’t perfect in relief on Sunday for Van Roten, who admitted he was a bit rusty, but we’ll give him some grace getting thrown into the fire just weeks after signing with the team. The veteran played solid football at right guard for the Giants last season and I’d expect him to continue to get the opportunity to hold that spot in Onwenu’s absence. His experience playing next to Morgan Moses should also help. As for Lomu, I would prioritize continuing to get him ready at tackle. It could be an option down the line, something Mike Vrabel did not rule out , as well as a few other options. “So, we will get [Van Roten] working there with Morgan [Moses]. I think Walter [Rouse] will get some opportunities to go there and practice,” Vrabel said. “Walter Rouse is a player we got from Minnesota who has been working really hard, and we will see how he does. Ben Brown is back and working. So, we’ll get a bunch of guys in there the next couple days and try to make a decision.” The Pats offensive line has been a headline for years. Almost always a concern. Is it the same for the other NFL teams but we don’t hear about it or is there more stability on other teams? – funnyattimes Outside of a few teams around the league who have found consistency up front, this is life in the NFL up front. There simply aren’t enough good offensive lineman, specifically tackles, in football today and the lack of padded practices over the offseason make it harder to develop the position. With Woodson and Pettus injured what are the chances we try to sign John Saunders Jr. off of the Jets Practice Squad? – naplesme Pettus landed on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. As for Woodson, he was spotted in the locker room this week without a sling — which he wore post game — and avoided injured reserve. Still, he did not practice Wednesday and Thursday and seems set to miss this Sunday. As for Saunders, I would have kept him around on the practice squad in the first place after an impressive summer. The fact they did not and signed other safeties in the process would indicate to me they will role with Mike Brown off of the practice squad. Any chance of adding to our tight end depth via a trade or is it too soon for that path? – jpd985 Eli Raridon’s (thigh) status is worth watching this week after he was downgraded from a limited participant on Wednesday to a did not participate on Thursday. If he can’t go, Cameron Latu and Tanner Arkin remain on the 53-man roster. With Raridon’s injury not a long-term issue, that group appears to be fine to move forward with. They did also add tight end Tanner Conner to the practice squad this week. I know it’s hard to say, but realistically how guys on IR with designation do we really think 1) will come back, 2) be able to contribute and 3) before the season is too late? – Patriot in Chicago Among the nine players on injured reserve, Julian Hill, Jeremiah Webb, and Myles Montgomery will miss the entire season being placed on IR during the offseason. As for the rest of the group, I’d expect them all back at some point except for Mike Onwenu (outside of a potential return during a deep playoff). That means A.J. Brown, Marcus Bryant, Khalil Jacobs, Dell Pettus, and Bryce Baringer will return at some point. Obviously Brown is the big one, but I’d expect the majority, or all, of that group to contribute as depth pieces and on special teams. How concerned are you about the Pat’s dwindling salary cap? Seems to be around $6 Million left, and that doesn’t leave much room for October trade deadline maneuvers to backfill or upgrade down the stretch. – WannaBe Pats GM No concern. As always the salary cap can easily be tinkered with and any midseason addition should not come with a large price tag. A lot of doom and gloom going around due to the series of injuries. What positive regression do we have to look forward to this year? And where is the team improving/has room to improve? – LandenPatz1 I do not believe the Drake Maye we’ve seen through two games is the version of the quarterback we’ll see the rest of the season. He’s too good of a player to continue making the early season mistakes and should settle in with new players around him. From there, the Patriots defense has certainly been a positive through two weeks. While it has come in matchups vs. Drew Lock and 42-year old Aaron Rodgers, I’d say the encouraging sign is that they’ve seemed to find their blueprint of a man blitz defense. With Christian Gonzalez and the group of corners they have, keep it coming. That’s all for this week’s #PostPulpit mailbag. If you have questions you’d liked to be answered next week, submit them online in our weekly submission post on the Feed. Make sure to follow @iambrianhines and @PatsPulpit as well.

title: Defensive head-to-head preview: Saints vs Raiders
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are entering the Superdome with a 2-0 record under new head coach Klint Kubiak. And while Kubiak is known for being one of the better offensive play-callers in the NFL, it’s actually been the defense for Vegas that has been leading the charge through the first two weeks. The Raiders come […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - SEPTEMBER 13: New Orleans Saints safety Jonas Sanker (7) and New Orleans Saints defensive end Chase Young (99) wait for the play during a regular season NFL football game between the New Orleans Saints and the Detroit Lions on September 13, 2026 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are entering the Superdome with a 2-0 record under new head coach Klint Kubiak. And while Kubiak is known for being one of the better offensive play-callers in the NFL, it’s actually been the defense for Vegas that has been leading the charge through the first two weeks. The Raiders come into Week 3 leading the NFL with 8 sacks and a 50% pressure rate, all while only blitzing 7.4% of the time. The Raiders are showing that they are going to get pressure with four, and when they do, they are going to get home and finish the job with a sack. The Raiders have been able to do this because they have transitioned from a 4-3 defense under former DC Patrick Graham to a 3-4 defense under new DC Rob Leonard. The simulated pressure looks force QBs to hold the ball longer after the snap because the pre-snap protection could have identified the incorrect pass protection. The Raiders are not only getting sacks without heavy blitz packages, but they are also forcing turnovers. The Raiders have 3 interceptions through two games, which has them tied for second across the league, and they are also +2 in turnover margin. They have also been able to hold teams to 23.5 points per game. But while their passing defense has been really solid, the run defense is middle of the pack. The Raiders are giving up just over 100 rushing yards per game, which has them ranked 16th in the league. This game has an obvious key to victory for the New Orleans Saints: Can they hold up on the offensive line, especially with Kelvin Banks Jr. not playing for a while? If they can manage the protection and establish a rushing attack, it will help expose the defense and give Tyler Shough the ability to make plays off play action. The Saints cannot allow the defense to pin its ears back and just attack the offense however it wants to. Also, keep in mind the level of competition that the Raiders have faced over the past two weeks. They matched up against the Chargers and Dolphins, who may very well be two of the worst teams in the league. As for the Saints, the defense has been better than what the numbers are showing. The Saints’ defensive performance against the Lions may have been an outlier to begin the season. Last year under DC Brandon Staley, the Saints were a top-10 defense in the NFL, and in Week 1 they gave up a lot of yards on the ground. But in Week 2, against one of the most prolific rushing combinations in the league, they held the Ravens to 108 rushing yards and 312 yards of total offense. The Saints defense is showing so far that its ability to defend the pass is starting to take another step forward, while the run defense still needs a little more consistency. The question becomes: Which run defense shows up? Ashton Jeanty has not had a great start to the season. So far, he has 150 yards on 44 carries and 0 TDs through two games. He’s averaging 3.4 yards per carry, while the Saints are allowing 5.0 yards per carry through two weeks. It is very important for the Saints to stop Jeanty early and keep the Raiders offense off schedule. Cousins, being the veteran QB he is, needs to stay ahead of the chains to keep the offense moving. He is not a dynamic QB, but if the offense is steady enough and he is in the game late, he can make the throws necessary to threaten the Saints and potentially win this game on the road. Forcing the Raiders into second-and-long and third-and-long situations will be very important. If you look at this Raiders offense, it almost resembles a lesser-quality version of the Detroit Lions. Cousins is similar to Goff in that both like to get rid of the ball quickly and are statues in the pocket. Both offenses feature a dynamic running back with the ability to break a game open in Jeanty and Gibbs. They also have an all-around TE who must be identified on every play—a good blocker and elite pass catcher—with Bowers for the Raiders and LaPorta for the Lions. The comparisons are there, but the difference is that the Lions have better talent at some of the core positions, and the Saints nearly stole that game on the road. Being at home and having the defense get a chance to play with this crowd behind it should be a huge advantage, especially on third downs. This is one area where the defense has been very good so far this season. The Saints have held their first two opponents to 9-of-22 on third downs, a 40.9% conversion rate. Keep the running game in check, force them into third-and-long situations, and let the pass rush go to work with the decibels in the Dome touching 115-120. If the Saints can do that, this should be a great opportunity for the defense to have a strong outing. Which defense do you think has the advantage in this game? Were you surprised that the Raiders are leading the league in several defensive categories through the first two weeks?

summary: Through the first two games, the Saints are showing signs of improvement in pass defense, but stopping the run is still a bit of an issue, as they are allowing an astounding 5.0 yards per carry. That’s an area that will need to be addressed in the offseason by adding additional personnel. It is only […]
full_text: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - SEPTEMBER 5: Ty Benefield #2 of the LSU Tigers celebrates after a play against the Clemson Tigers at Tiger Stadium on September 5, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Ella Hall/University Images via Getty Images} Through the first two games, the Saints are showing signs of improvement in pass defense, but stopping the run is still a bit of an issue, as they are allowing an astounding 5.0 yards per carry. That’s an area that will need to be addressed in the offseason by adding additional personnel. It is only Week 3, so a lot of things can change. Here are some players to watch in college football with a great slate of games on Saturday. Justin Scott, a defensive lineman from Miami, is a 6’4”, 303-pound interior lineman who, for his size, is unbelievably quick. He has a really great first step and was an anchor for the Miami defense that helped lead the Hurricanes to the 2025 national championship. So far this season, Scott has 5 total tackles and a PFF grade of 70. Miami will face Central Michigan at 5:30 p.m. on The CW. Another defensive lineman to watch this week will be Will Echoles from Ole Miss. Coming off an absolutely dominant performance against LSU last week, it will be fun to watch how he follows it up against a gritty, run-heavy Florida team. Echoles is currently ranked as a top-15 player on the big board and is widely considered to be the first interior defensive lineman who could be drafted. Ole Miss finds itself as the underdog as the Rebels/Landsharks/Black Bears travel to Gainesville for a 2:30 p.m. kickoff on ABC. Another big performance from Echoles will be needed to help keep their undefeated season intact. Finally, A’mauri Washington is a name to watch. He is currently trending up big boards and is the No. 21-ranked player. Washington is another interior defensive lineman who plays for the University of Oregon. Washington does not have the flashy stats, but the athleticism is off the charts. This is a 6’3”, 303-pound lineman who can run 21 miles per hour, squat 755 pounds and bench press 475 pounds. Washington has the physical ability, but he is still a prospect who will need to showcase continued development as the season progresses. Oregon is on the road in a major Big Ten matchup against USC. If the Ducks lose this game, their playoff hopes could be over. This game is set for a 6:30 p.m. kickoff on NBC. Who are some players you are excited to watch this weekend, and through two games, what areas would you like to see the Saints improve throughout the season? Share your thoughts in the comments.
