title: Key matchups: Saints vs. Raiders
summary: The New Orleans Saints are heading into a big game, hosting the Las Vegas Raiders in their Week 3 home opener. While the Saints are coming off a big win over the Baltimore Ravens, this isn’t the same old Raiders. Las Vegas is undefeated and playing hard under new head coach Klint Kubiak. With a […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints looks to pass against the Baltimore Ravens during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints are heading into a big game, hosting the Las Vegas Raiders in their Week 3 home opener. While the Saints are coming off a big win over the Baltimore Ravens, this isn’t the same old Raiders. Las Vegas is undefeated and playing hard under new head coach Klint Kubiak. With a 3 p.m. kickoff, there will be more eyes on the Saints than there has been this season. If New Orleans wants to get to 2-1, they’ll have to win these matchups. QB Tyler Shough vs. Raiders’ secondary NFL passing leader Tyler Shough has been nothing short of impressive after his slow start against the Detroit Lions in Week 1. Shough is averaging 331 passing yards per game and 2 touchdowns passing touchdowns. The second-year quarterback is in for a possible strong game against the Raiders, who have a young and inexperienced secondary. For the Raiders, they have five players in their secondary with one year or less of experience, with plenty seeing significant playing time. Despite this, Las Vegas has kept opponents in a blanket and currently holds the 11th-best passing defense, allowing an average of 184 yards per game. The Raiders have also allowed just one passing touchdown over the first two weeks. Shough will certainly be looking to get the ball to his favorite wideout, Chris Olave, and he’s likely in for a big day. But with the inexperience in the Raiders’ defense, expect the Saints to try and take advantage, hooking up on deep balls. Saints pass protection vs. DE Maxx Crosby The headline of the game will be the Saints’ offensive line against superstar pass rusher Maxx Crosby. With second-year star tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. going down with injury, Crosby is eyeing a big game. Asim Richards, who took over for Banks against the Baltimore Ravens, will resume his responsibilities. Richards’s transition was seamless after he took over in the win. Despite his strong showing, with a game plan around him, the Raiders will look to exploit Richards. Keeping Shough upright is the Saints’ most important task, and it starts with the offensive line. Expect running back CJ Donaldson to make plenty of appearances in pass protection, and Crosby to be double-teamed. Saints RBs vs. Raiders run defense It’s no secret the Saints’ run game has been one of the worst in the league through the first two weeks. Through two games, New Orleans is averaging just 78 rushing yards per game, with Shough being the second-leading rusher. Las Vegas’ run defense is middle of the pack through two weeks, allowing an average of 100.5 yards per game, but is coming off a poor performance, allowing the Los Angeles Chargers to rush for 127 yards on 4 yards a carry. The road to establishing itself may have just gotten harder, however, with Travis Etienne announced to be dealing with a hamstring injury. Who Dat Nation vs. the Raiders Offense Well, well, well, look how far we’ve come. The Superdome used to be one of the hardest stadiums to play in the NFL, but it lost some of that spark in the team’s losing seasons. Now, with the season opener being in Week 3 after a big win, expect the Superdome crowd to make a difference. The fans finally have something to believe in, and they are ecstatic to see it in person. New Orleanians believe Shough and Kellen Moore are the start of the turnaround for the Saints, and they are playing exciting football. If the Black and Gold take an early lead, life will get extremely hard for the Raiders’ offense.

title: Interview with the Enemy: Las Vegas Raiders
summary: This Sunday, the New Orleans Saints return to Caesars Superdome for their home opener against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 3 of the 2026 regular season. To break it down, Matt Holder of Silver And Black Pride joins us to preview this weekend’s matchup. NJ: With Klint Kubiak’s first two games as a head coach in the […]
full_text: This Sunday, the New Orleans Saints return to Caesars Superdome for their home opener against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 3 of the 2026 regular season. To break it down, Matt Holder of Silver And Black Pride joins us to preview this weekend’s matchup. NJ: With Klint Kubiak’s first two games as a head coach in the books, both resulting in wins, what are the vibes like around this current Raiders team? Does it feel like they are finally starting to put the pieces together? MH: It’s Vegas, so I’ll put it this way: The vibes are as high as starting a bachelor party by hitting the jackpot on a slot machine! There aren’t many people, myself included, who had the Raiders starting 2-0 this season. I think everyone expected them to beat the Dolphins because Miami is the only organization to hit the reset button harder than Las Vegas did in the offseason. But two weeks ago, the Chargers had Top 10 Super Bowl odds, and the Raiders entered that game as a touchdown underdog, only to win by 12 points. Back-to-back wins and both by two possessions is undoubtedly a great start to the Kubiak era. Of course, the Dolphins are what they are, and the Chargers are a disorganized mess right now. However, the Raiders were literally the worst team in the league last year. So, at the very least, the team is headed in the right direction by separating themselves from the bottom of the NFL. They’re showing signs of a well-coached team , which Raider Nation hasn’t seen in a long time. This is supposed to be a rebuilding year, and there are plenty of indications that the club is ahead of schedule through two weeks. NJ: Who are some notable names who will be sidelined for the Raiders on Sunday against the Saints? Does Brock Bowers look ready to go? MH: Bowers is the big one, and he’s missed the first two games of the season. However, ESPN’s/NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport recently reported that “there’s a good chance” the tight end is back in the lineup this week against the Saints. Bowers was a game-time decision in Los Angeles and was spotted on the field running routes without pads on before ultimately sitting out for one more game. So, all signs point toward the two-time Pro Bowler making his 2026 debut on Sunday. Defensively, rookie safety Treydan Stukes, who had a solid NFL debut with an interception in Week 1, is in concussion protocol after exiting the Chargers game about halfway through. If Stukes can’t play in New Orleans, that’d be a big hit to Las Vegas’ defense because he’s the best free safety it has. Starting cornerback Darien Porter suffered a foot injury in the fourth quarter against the Dolphins and missed last week’s contest. However, rookie Hezekiah Masses stepped in last Sunday and had two picks, including one to end the game and seal the win for Las Vegas. So, even if Porter is healthy, Masses might get the nod after a strong outing. Those two were competing for a starting spot in training camp. Other than that, the Raiders are pretty healthy right now. Running back Ashton Jeanty had a scare with a sprained ankle at the end of camp, but Jeanty was fine by the season opener, leading the team with 147 yards and two touchdowns in that contest. He had a bad game last week, but that had nothing to do with his ankle. The Raiders’ offensive line had a tough time in the running game against the Chargers’ defensive tackles, and Jeanty had three drops as a receiver. NJ: What are some areas that New Orleans could potentially exploit based on what you saw from Las Vegas through the first two week’s? MH: It’s funny, when the Chargers’ site asked me this question last week, I said load the box and make Kirk Cousins beat them. That’s essentially what L.A. did, taking advantage of Vegas’ shaky guards (Spencer Burford and Jackson Powers-Johnson), but Cousins beat them. LOL! He struggled to push the ball down the field in Week 1, but it was a different story last Sunday, connecting on a few deep shots to wide receiver Tre Tucker, who had one of the best games of his career with five catches for 119 yards and a touchdown. Still, I think that’s the best plan of attack for stopping the Raiders’ offense because the 38-year-old’s arm isn’t what it used to be. If I’m Brandon Staley, I’m making Cousins prove it again. Defensively, Las Vegas’ defense is playing out of its mind right now. It’s a small sample size, but analytics guru Ben Baldwin recently posted a graphic where the unit is leading the NFL in Defensive EPA per play. Granted, that’s against two struggling offenses. But new defensive coordinator Rob Leonard has a scheme that’s similar to Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald’s (Leonard was an assistant under Macdonald with the Ravens in 2022), and it’s helping mask some of the Raiders’ talent deficiencies on that side of the ball. But the defense is weak at defensive tackle and pretty young at cornerback, with either Masses (rookie) or Porter (second-year player with just 11 career starts) starting this week. So Chris Olave could get favorable matchups, and the Saints could run the ball up the middle. The only problem is Leonard loves to rotate coverage and play a lot of pattern-matching concepts, forcing quarterbacks to hold onto the ball a little longer as they diagnose the defense. Also, he’s big on mixing up the looks in the trenches and doing a lot of stunts to keep offensive linemen on their heels. In other words, it won’t be as simple as lining up and targeting a specific defender. NJ: Who is one Raiders player you think Saints fans should keep an eye on Sunday—someone who may not receive much national attention but could have a strong performance? MH: I’ll go with Tucker offensively. Everyone knows about former first-round picks Bowers and Jeanty, but Tucker could be a big X-factor with so much attention paid to the tight end and running back. As mentioned previously, the fourth-year pro is coming off an excellent outing and has really developed into a quality receiver during his tenure in Vegas. Especially since the Saints don’t have a lot of proven talent at cornerback, I think Tucker could be a big part of Kubiak’s game plan. On defense, I don’t know if Nakobe Dean is a great fit as someone who people don’t recognize. But Dean isn’t exactly a household name and is playing very well right now. He’s helped hide the defensive tackles against the run, coming up with a handful of big stops in key moments, including a forced fumble in the fourth quarter that allowed the Raiders to take a two-possession lead. Also, the free-agent signing is one of the best off-ball blitzers in the league, notching four pressures (1.5 sacks) on six pass-rushers, per Pro Football Focus. NJ: According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Saints (-164) are currently 3.0-point favorites over the Raiders (+138) in Sunday’s matchup; what is your final score prediction and how do you see the game playing out?? MH: I usually try to stay objective with the score predictions, but the Raiders starting 2-0 is bringing the homer out in me! I think the Saints will undoubtedly be their toughest test yet, especially since it’s their first true road game. Yes, Las Vegas played in Los Angeles last week. But SoFi is always filled with black jerseys when the Silver and Black roll into town, given the organization’s L.A. roots. So, I think Kubiak is able to scheme up some runs for Jeanty and play-action passes to Bowrers and Tucker, while Leonard keeps Tyler Shough guessing enough for the pass-rush to hit home. Raiders 24-21! Thank you again to Matt Holder for joining us to preview this week’s matchup! You can check out the rest of his work here .
author: Nic Jennings

title: Week 3 Film Preview: Highlights from the All 22
summary: Raiders 26 – Chargers 14 The Raiders thus far have played two of the worst teams in the NFL over the first two weeks in the Chargers and the Dolphins. While I think the Chargers are likely a better team than the Raiders overall, this past week they made too many mistakes to come away […]
full_text: Raiders 26 – Chargers 14 The Raiders thus far have played two of the worst teams in the NFL over the first two weeks in the Chargers and the Dolphins. While I think the Chargers are likely a better team than the Raiders overall, this past week they made too many mistakes to come away with the divisional win and sent the Jim Harbaugh’s home winless heading into the toughest stretch of schedule in football (yikes LAC). I mention the Raiders schedule to explain the reason they are 2-0 and point to another statistic of theirs that is misleading, a league leading 8 total team sacks. Maxx Crosby and his buddies will need to be grounded if the Saints hope to win, but I firmly believe the Saints are the best OLine and team the Silver and Black have faced yet. Pressure the Passer Timing and Anticipation is crucial to Kirk Cousins's game. The Saints must affect Cousins comfortability with constant pressure to throw him off this weekend and force turnovers. Small errors by the Raiders offense can lead to big results for the defense. pic.twitter.com/MlTuZVoFz3 — Andrew Lotz (@andrewlot3) September 24, 2026 Brandon Staley schemed up some brilliant and effective ways to pressure Lamar Jackson last week and I expect him to do the same this week to attack the limited mobility of Kirk Cousins. The 38 year old with a repaired Achilles tendon will not be able to escape a serious pass rush and will become uncomfortable if Chase Young and the other Saints pass rushers can get home on Sunday. The video above is a good example of how easily mistakes can be made by Cousins if there are any issues in the timing of routes as zone defenders lurk. While the example shows the Raiders keeping a clean pocket and a mistake by the receiver, the Raiders have yet to face a defensive line with the talent that the Saints possess at that position group. The Saints must pit Cousins’s high level of football awareness against him to force him into sacks and turnovers. When a quarterback is using his brain to make up for the lack of arm talent that currently plagues the aging Cousins, added pressure can speed the clock up in his head just enough to throw passes before necessary and lead to crucial errors. To do this, if I were the Saints, I would consistently attack right tackle D.J. Glaze (below) by giving him a full rotation of Chase, Cam and Carl (did I just discover the killer C’s??) with stunts a nickel blitzes sprinkled in. There's an obvious weak link on the Raiders offensive line that the Saints need to exploit this weekend. pic.twitter.com/5thqO9Roxt — Andrew Lotz (@andrewlot3) September 24, 2026 Win the Rushing Battle The Chargers have the cutest running plays (not a complement) in the NFL pic.twitter.com/iNpkaP7Auq — Andrew Lotz (@andrewlot3) September 24, 2026 The Chargers have what I would define as the “Cutest rushing attack in the NFL” with all their cool Mike McDaniel trademark gadget plays that some (me) would call highly unnecessary and were still able to rush for 127 yards. Jim Harbaugh’s squad were able to be successful on the ground by out scheming the Raiders in the run game for most of last Sunday’s matchup. Below you can see that in the box (what is pictured), the Chargers have 7 blockers for 7 defenders (commonly referred to as the offensive having numbers or a hat on a hat) which means that if the Bolts can execute their blocking scheme in the play below, they will be able to run until someone outside the box can make the tackle. This is a problem for the Raiders that I expect the Saints to try to exploit and have their best rushing output of the season in doing so. In their nickel package shown below, the Chargers chose to go away from the triangle which includes the Raiders best run defender and their worst as they use Crosby to hide Taron Johnson (their nickel corner) and run a man blocking scheme I call double insert or double ISO. While this was successful, this would never work running at Maxx Crosby (he immediately beat Joe Alt on this play). When the Saints are able to outnumber the Raiders similar to this look, I expect their zone heavy rushing attack to give the Raiders fits as the Saints have a much better OLine than the Chargers and (although they haven’t produced many yards yet this season) better backs in Eitienne and Kamara which theoretically will have plenty of space to cut into the running lanes. Mistake Free Football The Kellen Moore version of the Saints have yet to play a game without any pre-snap penalties or turnovers to my recollection. The Saints need to take their opportunity Sunday to fine tune their discipline and overcome this final hurdle of becoming a seriously good team. Now that Tyler Shough seems to have settled in completely, I do not foresee the Raiders zone blitz scheme to be an issue for him if he can continue to identify blitzers properly (we saw this vs the Ravens) as the Chargers had countless wide open receivers on Sunday thanks to blown coverages by the Silver and Black. LAC was not able to take advantage of these as Justin Herbert was running for his life most of the game and his receiving corps (if you know you know) did him no favors by dropping multiple could be explosive plays and even (David Njoku) bobbling a pass straight into a defender’s hands after being wide open 20 yards down field. Thankfully, the Saints receiving corps has been one of the better units in the NFL so far this year and unless there is a cataclysmic event in the Dome on Sunday, I have faith that will not happen if Olave, Juwan, Vele, and the rest of the bunch are left open the way some Chargers were. Bonus: Were you aware that Tyler Shough is possibly the funniest quarterback in the NFL. How could you not like this guy? The turns have certainty tabled for the Black and Gold since the Derek Carr days. “This is why Tyler Shough is the best” -Big Cat pic.twitter.com/dOc5rgR3Jb — Barstool Sports (@barstoolsports) September 22, 2026 Keys to Victory Pressure Kirk Cousins to throw off timing Win the rushing yards battle Emphasize discipline and play mistake free

title: Saints vs. Raiders predictions: Bring the noise
summary: After opening the season with back-to-back road games, the New Orleans Saints finally return to Caesars Superdome on Sunday, looking to build on their first win of the season. New Orleans enters Week 3 with a 1-1 record following a 24-17 victory over the Baltimore Ravens. Meanwhile, the Las Vegas Raiders arrive in New Orleans […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - DECEMBER 29: Ameer Abdullah #8 of the Las Vegas Raiders tackled by Pete Werner #20 and Willie Gay #6 of the New Orleans Saints during the first quarter at Caesars Superdome on December 29, 2024 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Sean Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images After opening the season with back-to-back road games, the New Orleans Saints finally return to Caesars Superdome on Sunday, looking to build on their first win of the season. New Orleans enters Week 3 with a 1-1 record following a 24-17 victory over the Baltimore Ravens. Meanwhile, the Las Vegas Raiders arrive in New Orleans undefeated at 2-0 under first-year head coach and former Saints offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak. Sunday’s matchup presents an opportunity for the Saints to build some early-season momentum, but it won’t come easy against a Raiders team that has gotten off to a strong start. Through the first two weeks, Tyler Shough has given Saints fans plenty of reasons to be optimistic. After throwing for 410 yards and three touchdowns in the season-opening overtime loss to Detroit, Shough followed up with another solid performance against Baltimore, completing 27 of 34 passes and scoring the go-ahead touchdown on the ground. His connection with wide receiver Chris Olave has already proven to be one of New Orleans’ biggest offensive weapons, and the Saints will need that chemistry again Sunday. However, protecting Shough could be a major concern. With left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. out indefinitely with an ankle injury, New Orleans must find a way to contain Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby, who is capable of disrupting an offense on his own. One of the biggest storylines surrounding Sunday’s matchup is the return of Klint Kubiak, who served as the Saints’ offensive coordinator in 2024. Kubiak has led Las Vegas to a 2-0 start, with veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins leading an offense that has shown it can make big plays. Cousins threw three touchdown passes in the Raiders’ 26-14 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2, while wide receiver Tre Tucker racked up 119 receiving yards. New Orleans showed improvement defensively against Baltimore, particularly in the second half. The Saints will need another strong performance, especially when it comes to pressuring Cousins and preventing explosive plays. The biggest difference this week is that New Orleans will have a very loud and proud home crowd behind them. Prediction: Saints 34 – Raiders 27 You can expect this one to be another entertaining matchup, with both offenses finding ways to put points on the board. But finally playing in the dome for the first time this season will give the Saints an extra spark, and I think they will make enough plays in the fourth quarter to hand the Raiders their first loss of the season. title: By the Numbers: Saints vs. Raiders
summary: Both the New Orleans Saints and Las Vegas Raiders are coming off road victories ahead of their week three matchup in the Big Easy. Las Vegas defeated the Los Angeles Chargers 26-14 for their second win in as many weeks, while New Orleans upset the Baltimore Ravens 24-17, picking up their first win and improving […]
full_text: Both the New Orleans Saints and Las Vegas Raiders are coming off road victories ahead of their week three matchup in the Big Easy. Las Vegas defeated the Los Angeles Chargers 26-14 for their second win in as many weeks, while New Orleans upset the Baltimore Ravens 24-17, picking up their first win and improving to 1-1. Let’s check out the breakdown of numbers for this week’s contest. 8 : Las Vegas is tied for 1st in the NFL with eight sacks as a team through two games. The Raiders already have five players with at least one sack, so you never know who will wind up getting after the QB. This could be bad news for a Saints team with a struggling offensive line that has already given up eight sacks this year and will now be without starting LT Kelvin Banks Jr. for an extended period after landing on IR with a high ankle sprain. 35 : Las Vegas’ fifth-round selection CB Hezekiah Masses, who rocks jersey number 35, has looked every bit the part of an NFL talent through the Raiders’ first two games. The rookie from California (Cal) is already making his mark in the defensive backfield with two interceptions (tied 1st in the league) and three passes defensed (tied 7th in the league). 55.6 : Kirk Cousins has faced the New Orleans Saints nine times in his career and has a near even split of 5-4 in those games, or a .556 record. Most recently, Cousins swept the division series in 2025 against New Orleans as a member of the Atlanta Falcons, but the veteran QB will now return to the Superdome at the helm of Klint Kubiak’s offense with the Raiders. 60 : New Orleans is celebrating its 60th season as an NFL franchise this year, and Sunday will mark the home opener inside the Caesars Superdome for the celebratory year. 136.5 : After facing two of the top running backs in the NFL in Jahmyr Gibbs and Derrick Henry, the Saints have given up an average of 136.5 yards on the ground per game. Things will not get much easier for New Orleans as they will now hope to slow down agile RB Ashton Jeanty whose managed 210 all-purpose yards thus far. 662 : The Saints have found themselves a QB of the future (and current) in Louisville product Tyler Shough. The second-year QB currently has a league-leading 662 passing yards and will now attempt to throw the first TD pass against the Raiders’ defense this season. 2021 : The Raiders have not begun a season with a 3-0 record since 2021. Las Vegas, then led by QB Derek Carr, had two overtime victories in the first three weeks of the regular season. This is also the last time that the team made the postseason. 2023 : Meanwhile, New Orleans has not gotten out of September with a winning record since 2023, when they beat the Tennessee Titans and Carolina Panthers to open the season. Sunday’s game will have a huge effect on the trajectory of the rest of both squads’ seasons.

summary: The nor’easter expected to slam into the East Coast this weekend could have a major impact on Sunday’s New York Giants vs. Tennessee Titans game in East Rutherford, N.J. The National Weather Service is forecasting an inch or more of rain in the East Rutherford area on Saturday, followed by another half- to three-quarters of […]
full_text: WEEHAWKEN, NJ - SEPTEMBER 25: The sun sets on the skyline of midtown Manhattan, the Empire State Building and Hudson Yards as a rainbow forms ahead of an approaching nor'easter storm in New York City on September 25, 2026, as seen from Weehawken, New Jersey. (Photo by Gary Hershorn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The nor’easter expected to slam into the East Coast this weekend could have a major impact on Sunday’s New York Giants vs. Tennessee Titans game in East Rutherford, N.J. The National Weather Service is forecasting an inch or more of rain in the East Rutherford area on Saturday, followed by another half- to three-quarters of an inch of rain on Sunday. Temperatures are expected to be in the mid-60s, with steady winds around 20 MPH and gusts of up to 38 MPH. Sunday will mark Jameis Winston’s first start at quarterback for the Giants this season after the season-ending injury to Jaxson Dart. The wet, blustery conditions could make it a difficult day to throw, catch, kick, and hang on to the football. In John Harbaugh’s first season as head coach, the Giants have built a power running game that they will likely need to rely heavily upon Sunday afternoon. Conditions could also make travel to and from the game treacherous. If you are planning to attend, leave yourself extra time.

title: New York Giants mailbag: It’s all quarterback all the time
summary: Ed Helinski asks: What’s the Giants Plan C if Jameis Winston isn’t the answer for whatever reason? Ed says: Ed, how many times actually have a realistic Plan C at quarterback? The reality is that if you are down to your third quarterback, things are not going to go well. There are 32 NFL teams. […]
full_text: Ed Helinski asks: What’s the Giants Plan C if Jameis Winston isn’t the answer for whatever reason? Ed says: Ed, how many times actually have a realistic Plan C at quarterback? The reality is that if you are down to your third quarterback, things are not going to go well. There are 32 NFL teams. Even if every quarterback is healthy, there aren’t 32 good starting quarterbacks in the league. By extension, there aren’t 32 good backup quarterbacks. The truth is nobody ever wants to see their third quarterback play — that guy is a baseball cap-wearing third quarterback or practice squad guy for a reason. That said, I’m sure the Giants will look around at practice squads, a street free agent like Jimmy Garoppolo, and trade options. Considering how many quarterbacks have gotten hurt in the first two weeks of the season, though, how many teams are going to be willing to trade away someone they consider to be a capable backup? At this point, that’s GM malpractice. The Giants just gave Jameis Winston a two-year, $13 milliion extension. They didn’t do that to replace him as soon as they need a backup quarterback. Todd Graf asks: Do the OC and DC come down to the locker room at halftime or do they work the 2nd half game plan from the booth? Thought about this with Jameis taking over for Jaxson and his 1st half struggles…. And also because there isn’t much time at halftime. Ed says: Todd, let me clarify that to my knowledge defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson works from the sideline. To answer your question, all of the coaches who work from upstairs make a beeline for the locker room at halftime. At MetLife Stadium, that means taking the elevator from the sixth floor down to the ground floor and then hustling down the tunnel to the room for a brief interaction with John Harbaugh, players, and other coaches, then back upstairs before the second half starts. Ted Schwartz asks: All of the cards appeared to be aligning for what would be an exciting season where I finally could watch all of the games while being surrounded by fellow fans! Alas, the football gods have struck down that excitement. Watching the devastating injury to Dart and the massive blow it struck to this team for the season, leaves me wondering about accountability within the team. I know football is a dangerous sport and any player can get injured through no fault of their own or their teammates. But this injury appears to me to be squarely on the shoulders of the Left and Right tackle who both got beat badly on the same play and left their quarterback exposed to the vicious punishment his body received. Does this affect the team chemistry with some players feeling if even one of them did their job properly their quarterback would not be injured and the team would not be in this position. Dart stayed in the pocket, did not put himself unnecessarily in harms way and trusted and relied on his teammates, who failed him. Does the team discuss this as a whole, are the players spoken to individually, is there any penalty for them within the team environment or is it just chalked up as an unfortunate football injury. Have either of them spoken out about their role in this injury? Of course they didn’t mean for it to happen and Im sure they were trying their hardest not to let it happen. But they let their quarterback down, let their team down, and let their fans down. Ed says: Ted, trying to assign blame to other players for a guy getting injured is not constructive, and not something teams or players do. I did not get an opportunity to speak to Andrew Thomas or Jermaine Eluemunor when I was there on Wednesday. Both guys are among the best in the league at their jobs, and are highly-respected inside that locker room. Players get beat sometimes. The guys on the other side are also professionals. It happens. This “they let their quarterback down” stuff is way over the top. Spoken to individually? Penalty within the team? I am sure the team has looked at the film and understands why the play happened, but these guys aren’t children. I think you are looking for some type of team divide or finger-pointing that simply doesn’t exist. I think the video below from Chris Simms is instructive. I agree with him that this play was in “disarray” before the ball was snapped. That doesn’t mean I am blaming Dart, either. Dart’s not the first quarterback to get sandwiched by multiple defenders, and he won’t be the last. The play where Dart got hurt was in disarray before the snap. pic.twitter.com/b4WKB6p0wS — Chris Simms (@CSimmsQB) September 22, 2026 Bob Donnelly asks: How does the loss of Jaxson Dart impact your projection for Giant’s 2026 win/loss record? Ed says: Bob, as Big Blue View readers probably (should?) know I predicted 9-8, calling that the “most optimistic” prediction I could make for 2026. I would think 9-8 without Dart would be a fantastic season. I think right now it would be hard to complain about seven wins. The next three weeks — winnable games against the Titans, Cardinals, Commanders — will tell us more about what to expect. Patrick Morris asks: The injury to Jaxson Dart is awful. His play when he has been available has been inspiring. But, the season without him is not as hopeful, and the odds of the Giants having a high draft pick have gone up. If the Giants end the season with a poor record, but an opportunity to draft one of the top 3 QBs in the upcoming draft class…do they take it? Ed says: I don’t know what they would do. But, I think the answer would be no. My answer would definitely be no . John Urbielewicz asks: The inside linebacker play against the Rams was horrible. One could make an argument that Micah McFadden is our best inside linebacker at this time. I think Arvell Reese is going to be a great player in this league, but right now with Brian Burns missing time, I would move Arvell to the end rusher and play McFadden. Your thoughts? Ed says: John, no. Arvell Reese is an inside linebacker. That is what the Giants drafted him to be. That is where he has practiced since the spring. That is where he is best. The Giants align him outside occasionally to change the look of the defense and try to create desirable matchups. Maybe that happens a little more frequently with Burns out, but moving Reese to the edge and starting McFadden is an overreation. Chris Chianese asks: Ed, in your “Ride with Winston” article it left me thinking … finally there is someone showing some common sense and reality with the Dart injury and where we are with the QB for the Gs this season. First and foremost, Harbaugh and Schoen didn’t sign Winston to an extension to move on from him if Dart got injured. I suppose a person could take issue with Winston being the backup considering he is such a different QB than Dart. So, in other words, the Gs offense will need to be revamped to accommodate Winston’s abilities. So my question is, which QBs out there that are free agents or on a practice squad, most emulate what Dart’s abilities to sign as a backup to Winston? Milton? Hooker? Or, for continuity in the 2026 season, does signing Jimmy Garoppolo make more sense as a backup to Winston since Jimmy G is more like Winston? Ed says : Chris, I honestly don’t think emulating Dart has anything to do with it. I think the point is to find the player the Giants believe can do the best job helping them win games if he has to play. If that is a quarterback who offers the chance to use the quarterback run game, fine. If it is more of a pocket passer, fine. John Harbaugh has succeeded with Joe Flacco, a pocket passer, at quarterback. He also succeeded with a running quarterback — Lamar Jackson. Matt Nagy, Greg Roman, Brian Callahan have worked with both types. Submit a question Have a Giants-related question? E-mail it to bigblueview@gmail.com and it might be featured in our weekly mailbag.

title: NY Giants news: Andrew Thomas to play, Jaxson Dart surgery, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need as the Giants get ready to take on the Tennessee Titans tomorrow at 1 p.m. Giants’ season hinges on John Harbaugh after Jaxson Dart injury | The Athletic We’re going to learn a lot about the New York Giants over the next few […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need as the Giants get ready to take on the Tennessee Titans tomorrow at 1 p.m. Giants’ season hinges on John Harbaugh after Jaxson Dart injury | The Athletic We’re going to learn a lot about the New York Giants over the next few weeks. The team was delivered a gut punch with the news that second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart is out for the season with a knee injury. But coach John Harbaugh didn’t get a $100 million contract just to captain the franchise through smooth seas. This type of adversity is when Harbaugh’s talents as a culture-building coach should emerge. Harbaugh isn’t a miracle worker. The Ravens went 6-12 in the 18 games they started a backup during the seven seasons since Lamar Jackson became their starter. The Giants don’t need a miracle, but they need Harbaugh’s leadership to prevent Dart’s injury from sending the season off the rails. Practicing what they preach John Harbaugh says the Giants had their best practice of the year yesterday and followed it up with a "very good" practice today pic.twitter.com/Cro3uKyVm2 — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) September 25, 2026 Harbs Weekly: Turning the page to Tennessee | Giants.com Q: Like you said, the NFL is high-level drama. With everything that has transpired this week, are you just eager to get to Sunday and turn the page? Harbaugh: The guys are excited about the game. It’s an opportunity to get to 2-1, 1-0 for the week is the mantra. Circumstances are always what they are. So yeah, it’s a tough circumstance with the quarterback. It’s unique. We’re not the only team that’s ever faced that, not even the only team that’s facing it this week in the National Football League, and we won’t be the last team to face it. It’s not something that’s unknown to mankind. It’s an adversity that’s going to hopefully serve to make us a better football team and that’s really the goal – to become the best football team we can be. But within that, play our best football game this week and we have a team that’s really determined and really locked in to do that. Jaxson (Dart) is supporting that. He’s been in meetings all week supporting the guys and supporting Jameis (Winston). So yeah, we’re excited to play the game. NFL Week 3 picks, predictions, schedule, odds, fantasy tips | ESPN.com The Giants’ offense will look different against the Titans. They’ll have to cater it to QB Jameis Winston’s skill set, which doesn’t include the same running ability as Jaxson Dart (knee). The Giants already have the plays in their playbook. Guard Jon Runyan said they have more than 300 plays already. Now, OC Matt Nagy & Co. will lean on what works better for Winston. That likely means using Winston’s arm and ability to throw downfield to complement the running game. Why are Giants barely putting Odell Beckham Jr. on the field?| New York Daily News Beckham and Jaxson Dart never appeared to develop any obvious chemistry during training camp, but Jameis Winston and Beckham had a rapport. They’re both veterans. Winston often plants his back foot and fires, and Beckham is a precise, timing-based route runner. And Beckham logged more snaps with the backups than the starters, giving him more time on task with Winston. And yet when Winston took over for Dart in Monday’s first quarter, and as the Giants’ offense floundered while falling behind big, Beckham was nailed to the bench. It just seems Beckham should be worked in as an option, particularly with Winston now under center. How Giants offense changes now with Jameis Winston at quarterback | The Record Cam Skattebo doesn’t see why anything has to change offensively for the New York Giants. With respect and love to Jaxson Dart, whom he called “my best friend” on the day the 23-year-old was placed on injured reserve with knee surgery pending, and Jameis Winston’s ascension to a starting role, Skattebo has a solution to replacing the juice missing without Dart. Giants trade candidate aims to spark ‘terrible’ defense: ‘It’s been hard’ | NJ.com The Giants need their defense to lift them in Sunday’s home game against the Titans — which still seems winnable, even without quarterback Jaxson Dart. But if coordinator Dennard Wilson’s group plays as poorly as it did Monday night in Los Angeles, the Giants are doomed — and coach John Harbaugh’s once-promising first season might begin to spiral out of control. On Sunday, they Giants will turn to a fascinating potential trade piece, outside linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux, since elite edge rusher Brian Burns will be sidelined by an ankle sprain he sustained in that 28-6 loss to the Rams. Special teams have been a bright spot The Giants have the best kickoff coverage unit through two weeks Average Drive Start Position After a Kickoff👇 pic.twitter.com/LjwOe03Wzg — Gridiron Stats and Info (@GridironInfo_) September 25, 2026 Giants’ young specialists giving Chris Horton something to build on | USAToday.com Dominic Zvada supplied every Giants point in Monday night’s 28-6 loss to the Rams, hitting from 24 yards late in the first half and from 52 in the third quarter. “From the day we got him here, always believed in him, and just needed to get him out there to get him those opportunities,” Horton told reporters on Wednesday. “And we know who he is, he knows who he is. And so, it was very encouraging to get him out there in a game setting and let him kick that 52-yard field goal.” Jordan Stout is the other half of that battery. Horton said the punter’s ability to flip the field has been outstanding, including 70-plus-yard boots and one that approached 80. That only works if the rest of the unit lets it work. “You can’t allow him to do the things that he does if you don’t allow your punt coverage, also those other guys to work,” Horton said. “Situationally, we’re just allowing him to be who he is, and it just starts with everybody understanding what kind of punter we have. We protect the punt, and then we need all-out effort. title: NY Giants-Tennessee Titans injuries: Andrew Thomas will play; Brian Burns uncertain
summary: New York Giants left tackle Andrew Thomas, dealing with a groin injury suffered late in Monday night’s 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, is determined to play Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. Thomas simply said “Yep” when asked on Friday if he would be in the lineup on Sunday. Thomas was injured on the […]
full_text: New York Giants left tackle Andrew Thomas , dealing with a groin injury suffered late in Monday night’s 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, is determined to play Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. Thomas simply said “Yep” when asked on Friday if he would be in the lineup on Sunday. Thomas was injured on the team’s final drive, but said he intended to go back in the game had the Giants gotten the ball back. “I was planning to go back out there,’ Thomas said. ”Obviously, didn’t have that opportunity, but the mindset was to wrap it up and go.“ Thomas missed practice on Thursday, saying that the training staff “held me out.” He was back on the practice field Friday. “I was sore right after the game, but I’m feeling good today,” Thomas said. “I think all of us are always trying to play. Obviously, you’ve got to put your body first. I mean, that’s the most important. But I think all those guys you named are trying to step up for Jameis [Winston]. Obviously, I hate what happened to [Jaxson] Dart. Anytime anyone gets hurt, especially a quarterback. But we’re trying to rally around Jameis and do the best we can for him.” Thomas was listed as a limited participant in Friday’s practice, but is not carrying an injury designation. So, he will play. Three Giants are questionable: Brian Burns — The edge defender and defensive captain did not practice all week due to an ankle injury. Media on hand Friday saw Burns work some on the side with trainers. It seems unlikely he will play. Deonte Banks — The cornerback missed Monday’s game against the Rams with a calf injury. he has been listed as a limited practice participant all week. Tyler Nubin — The starting safety has a calf injury. Like Banks, he was listed as limited all week. For the Titans, former Giant cornerback Cor’Dale Flott is questionable with a quad injury. He did not play in Week 2 against the Philadelphia Eagles. Running back Tyjae Spears is also questionable with an ankle injury.

title: Cam Skattebo on losing QB Jaxson Dart: ‘He’s my best friend’
summary: Perhaps no New York Giants player felt the blow of losing Jaxson Dart quite so acutely as running back Cam Skattebo. Dart and Skattebo were drafted together in 2025 and immediately seemed to be soulmates. Both players are aggressive and exceedingly competitive, with a type of energy that seems to feed, and feed off of, […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo | Getty Images Perhaps no New York Giants player felt the blow of losing Jaxson Dart quite so acutely as running back Cam Skattebo. Dart and Skattebo were drafted together in 2025 and immediately seemed to be soulmates. Both players are aggressive and exceedingly competitive, with a type of energy that seems to feed, and feed off of, the other. The two have energized the fanbase and pretty quickly became two of the NFL’s brightest young stars a year ago. Skattebo had a media availability after Thursday’s practice and the topic of conversation was, unsurprisingly, the loss of Dart for the season. The general theme of Skattebo’s remarks were characteristic of the brash young back: Injuries suck. “Yeah, it sucked,” Skattebo said on Thursday. “I talked to him on the sidelines a little bit, and he’s my best friend. So, it’s a little emotional for me. It sucked to lose him, but we got to move on. The team has still got a full season left. We’ve got 15 games minimum left, and it’s something we have to battle through and continue to work together as a team.” This isn’t the first time the duo has been broken up. Dart had to see Skattebo suffer a gruesome ankle injury last year, then carry on without him. This time the roles are reversed and Skattebo saw Dart get hurt and now needs to finish the year without his best friend. Making matters worse, all the excitement for seeing Dart, Skattebo, and Malik Nabers healthy and developing together has been put on hold for yet another season. “The good thing is it’s only year two and three,” Skattebo said when it was noted that the trio have only played 43 snaps together. “I got hurt last year. I didn’t get to play with the guys, and then he [Dart] gets hurt this year,” he added. “It sucks. It does suck. But the bright side is we have a long future ahead of us, and with Malik being in year three, I’m in year two, Jaxson in year two, I mean, we have a lot of football ahead of us, and it really does suck to be on that side of the fence. But, I mean, at the end of the day, we’ve got to continue to work. Last year I got hurt, and they continued to work without me. So, we’ve got to continue to work. And Jaxson’s going to be here every day working his butt off to make sure that Jameis is in a good spot, the guys are in a good spot, and he’s doing everything, whatever he can to help. So, we’re ready to go.” According to Skattebo, Dart is in high spirits, is in a good headspace, and is ready to attack the recovery process. “He’s doing great,” he said. “Obviously, when you get hurt it sucks, and you don’t know what to think,” Skattebo added. “And like Coach Harbs kind of says, it feels like the world’s over when you get hurt. But there’s another day to live on. He knows he has more football left in his life. And it does suck, especially now but as he gets through this rehab process and he starts feeling better, he’ll have a better light on things. And he’s strong-minded. He’s been through this a couple times already. So, he knows how to deal with it.” Both Dart and Skattebo know that the injury is over, and now they simply have to move on and move forward. But that means different things to each player. For Dart, it means surgery and rehab, as well as getting into the building and continuing to hone the mental side of his game. For Skattebo, and the rest of the players, it means picking themselves up and getting ready for the next fifteen games. “You just lost your starting quarterback, a guy that was playing really well, a guy that was doing a lot of good things for us, and it does take a toll on you,” he said. “But at the end of the day, like I said, we have to continue to go. He knows we have to do that. He’s going to have our back doing that. And it’s just like losing anything significant in your life. We lost a big part of this team, and we have to fill it and continue to roll. So, I’m excited to see what we got.” One guy they have is backup quarterback, and former first overall pick, Jameis Winston. The Giants signed Winston to a 2-year, $13 million contract extension just three weeks ago. The Giants’ brass obviously believes in him as a backup and as a leader in the locker room. So to does Skattebo, and the rest of the team seems to love the charismatic former 1st overall pick as well. “We have Jameis’ back,” Skattebo said. “He’s going to go out there and perform and dominate the game. And I’m fully behind that, and I really do think that. And I think these guys came out here today to work really hard, and they bought in.” “I’m excited for Jameis,” he added. “He can do everything. He looked great today in practice. I appreciate it for his leadership, the way the guys came in and out of the huddle on and off the field. That was kind of an emphasis today in practice, and he took control of that, and he made sure that the guys were locked in. And today went smooth, and everything looked really good.”
author: Chris Pflum

title: NY Giants QB Jaxson Dart having surgery Friday, per report
summary: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is undergoing surgery Friday on his injured knee, according to the New York Post. That is an early surgery that will allow Dart to begin attacking the rehab sooner rather than later. Dart suffered damage to the PCL, MCL and meniscus on his left knee on Monday night when […]
full_text: When is the next time we will see Jaxson Dart run onto a football field? | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is undergoing surgery Friday on his injured knee, according to the New York Post . That is an early surgery that will allow Dart to begin attacking the rehab sooner rather than later. Dart suffered damage to the PCL, MCL and meniscus on his left knee on Monday night when he was high-lowed by Los Angeles Rams’ defenders Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart. Giants coach John Harbaugh would not rule out a return to action for Dart in the playoffs, should the Giants make it that far. “Regular season at least, I’d say,” Harbaugh said on Wednesday. “Yeah. I said it, regular season. Other than that, how do you know? There’s no way to know, it just depends on the recovery. You can’t pinpoint it exactly.” Four months might be the most optimistic timeline. According to Dr. Kyle Flik, a sports medicine orthopedic surgeon specializing in knee and shoulder injuries for Ortho NY, the timeline depends on the severity of the injuries beyond the meniscus. “I would say if the PCL is getting reconstructed then I think that [four months] would be a silly time frame and not make a lot of sense,” Flik said. “If it’s only the MCL and the meniscus, that would be a possibility.” Flik said that PCL reconstruction, MCL repair, and meniscus repair would be the “worst-case scenario.” A return for Week 1 of the 2027 season should not be an issue without ACL damage.
author: Ed Valentine

title: Matt Nagy in charge of ‘lane change’ for NY Giants’ offense
summary: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh calls the team’s necessary offensive stylistic change, with Jameis Winston replacing Jaxson Dart at quarterback, a “lane change.” The man primarily responsible for implementing that lane change is offensive coordinator Matt Nagy. He knows what the Giants are getting into with Winston, a 12-year veteran quarterback whose play […]
full_text: Jameis Winston | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh calls the team’s necessary offensive stylistic change, with Jameis Winston replacing Jaxson Dart at quarterback, a “lane change.” The man primarily responsible for implementing that lane change is offensive coordinator Matt Nagy . He knows what the Giants are getting into with Winston, a 12-year veteran quarterback whose play can swing wildly from positive to negative. In Big Blue View parlance, Winston might be considered a walking “Kwillie.” “We know who he is,” Nagy said. “We talked all training camp about protecting the football. There is a lot of that feast or famine with him. We’ve joked over time about the 30 touchdowns and 30 picks, but now here it is.” That is a reference to Winston’s confounding 2019 season with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. That year, Winston threw for an incredible 5,109 yards with 33 touchdowns. He also threw 30 interceptions. That made Winston the only quarterback in NFL history to go 30-30 in touchdown passes and interceptions. “Respecting that football and ball security is paramount, this type of team that we have. So, he knows that,” Nagy said of Winston. “And again, he’s as true of a pro as you’ll be around, preparation-wise and how he handles this. So, you just play his game, be who he is, and then we’ve got to help him as a staff, too.” “We know who he is.” — Matt Nagy on Jameis Winston ‘Ultimate trust’ in Winston The Giants know they can’t survive with the 11 of 27 for 111 yards and an interception performance Winston had Monday in relief of Dart becoming a regular thing. Nagy believes they can help Winston with a game plan tailored to the things that suit his skill set. “Probably the biggest thing is – one of the things with this offense when we first got started is we wanted to be able to be prepared to have multiple styles of offense,” Nagy said. “And so, if something like this does happen, it doesn’t put you in a hole where you just — it changes everything. Obviously, Jaxson (Dart) is a dual-threat quarterback. That’s one of his strengths. It’s what he does well. And so, when you lose that part of it and what he does well, that’s part of the playbook. That’s stating the obvious. “But at the same point in time, we look at it with Jameis that here’s a guy that’s played a lot of football games in his career. We have ultimate trust in him. And so, unlike the game when it happens on play seven, where you have most of your game designed around Jaxson, now we get a chance to design around Jameis’ strengths and what he does.” ‘Reps are huge’ Nagy was asked about the difficulty — for both coach and backup quarterback — of navigating a situation where the starter is injured so early in a game. “The first part is that there’s a part of the playbook that we do lose any way you look at it,” Nagy said. “And I’m sure this is for most teams, when you have the strength of your quarterback, a lot of that is directed towards what they do well. So, if there’s areas of his game that, when you lose him, you lose that part of the playbook. But it’s not a massive number to where you can’t run an offense. I want to be clear with that. “The other part of this, too, is your reps are so valuable throughout the week, and I think I said it last week to you all, but the walkthrough reps are huge. And we have our volume of plays is – there’s a lot of plays that we run throughout the week, and Jameis has to do it mentally. And so, Jaxson himself is trying to get timing down with some of these skill receivers, running backs, wideouts, tight ends, etc. Now you’re thrown into the mix seven plays in and running these plays that you didn’t run all week. You did mentally, but you didn’t timing-wise. There’s a lot involved there.” Nagy said the Giants did try to adapt some things on the fly. The issue there, though, becomes not running things the way they were practiced. “I’ll give you an example. If there’s a motion and a shift in a play, we either eliminated it or we used one motion, not two. That’s just an example,” Nagy said. “If there’s something on the play where we could make it easier for him [Winston] to play faster and have less decisions, we wanted to do that. So, you try to adapt in the game. But now, again, we get to have a full week of prep, and he gets to get out here and get throws on time, which helps.” As Nagy acknowledged, the quarterback run is not something that can be a regular part of the plan with Winston. There will also be some differences in the types of throws Winston prefers to what Dart is best at. “There might be a couple concepts where you’re able to do some different things to his strengths,” Nagy said. “For us as coaches, I think it’s very important that you know that Jameis knows what we do offensively. Thank God he’s been here for all the OTAs and training camp. So, calling a play, understanding why a play is in, where to go, his eyes going to where our eyes go, is good. “But then he also has his strengths on certain routes that he throws, and maybe he does it slightly better than Jaxson, maybe he doesn’t. But we need to make sure that we’re putting that stuff in to where Jameis feels comfortable, and that’s what I think we’re doing.” Will the Giants’ “lane change” land them in the slow lane or the fast lane? We will see what that looks like on Sunday vs. the Tennessee Titans.
author: Ed Valentine

title: Giants vs. Titans: How will New York handle Brian Daboll’s offense?
summary: The New York Giants are regrouping for a Week 3 matchup against the 0-2 Tennessee Titans. New York lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart for the season, a brutal gut-punch. The Giants are 2.5-point favorites, with the Over/Under at 39.5 points. The Giants welcome back former head coach Brian Daboll. It is the Titans’ first road […]
full_text: Brian Daboll | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants are regrouping for a Week 3 matchup against the 0-2 Tennessee Titans. New York lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart for the season, a brutal gut-punch. The Giants are 2.5-point favorites, with the Over/Under at 39.5 points. The Giants welcome back former head coach Brian Daboll. It is the Titans’ first road game of the 2026 season. Tennessee is rebuilding in Robert Saleh’s first season as head coach, but does have its quarterback of the foreseeable future and a few young offensive weapons. Let’s look at how the Giants’ defense matches up with Tennessee’s offense. Brian Daboll’s offense Daboll took Carmen Bricillo, Shea Tierney, and Cade Knox to Nashville to coach under Saleh. Daboll inherited quarterback Cam Ward, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. Ward looked much more comfortable in the Titans’ 24-20 last-second loss against the Philadelphia Eagles. Daboll’s squad mustered only 10 points in their Week 1 loss to the Jets. The Titans have used 11 personnel at a 71% rate through two games — as expected after signing Wan’Dale Robinson to a four-year, $70-million contract. Ward has operated under center at a 37% rate; under Daboll last season, Dart was under center only 20% of the time. The Titans’ offense has yet to eclipse 300 yards in a game this season. They’re 10 of 25 on third down ( 40% conversion rate ), and they have three touchdowns through two games; Ward has two touchdowns on the ground, and he threw a touchdown pass to Elic Ayomanor in Week 1. Ayomanor dropped a touchdown in Week 2, but the throw was off-target. Ward is 32 of 53 ( 61.5% ) through the air for 323 yards ( 6.2 YPA ) with just one touchdown and no interceptions. Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears split rushing work, but rookie Nicholas Singleton dressed after being a healthy scratch in Week 1. Pollard has rushed 21 times for 99 yards ( 4.7 YPC ) with six missed tackles forced and a 3.05 yards-after-contact number, while catching two passes for zero yards. Spears sprung a long catch in Week 2 and has secured four passes for 41 yards through two games. He averaged 5.3 yards per carry with just ten rushes for 53 yards, and an impressive 3.90 yards after contact. Tennessee’s receiving corps consists of three young receivers: Ayomanor, Chimere Dike, and first-round pick Carnell Tate. Robinson operates the slot, and Calvin Ridley is still a Titan. Ridley has played 62% of the snaps this season. Tennessee used more 12 personnel against the Eagles, leading to more Daniel Bellinger, who is the second tight end behind Gunnar Helm. Ayomanor leads the Titans in receiving yards; he’s caught three of six targets for 80 yards and one receiving touchdown. Tate has seen 11 targets and secured seven for 65 yards. Robinson has caught six of seven for 47 yards, and Helm has secured all six of his targets for 41 yards. The Titans’ offensive line has former Giants’ center Austin Schlottmann anchoring the unit; Pro Football Focus has graded him well in pass protection, but poorly in run blocking, which is consistent across the Titans’ front, who dealt with two solid defensive fronts with the Eagles and Jets. Dan Moore Jr. and JC Latham will have their hands full with the dangerous Giants’ pass rush on the edges, while Peter Skoronski and Fernando Carmona — the latter has surrendered four pressures on the season already — will be starting at guard for Bricillo. The Giants can win the matchup of the trenches. Giants’ game plan Dart wasn’t the only significant loss in Week 2. Brian Burns had his ankle rolled up on with six minutes left in the 28-6 game. The Giants will be without their star edge defender, which will force Dennard Wilson to change how he uses his personnel. Kayvon Thibodeaux is in for an increased role without Burns. He’s played 59 snaps so far this season to Burns’ 91 and Abdul Carter’s 108. Chauncey Golston may receive more snaps on the edge, as well as Arvell Reese in certain packages. Tae Banks remains questionable for the game; if he can not dress, Colton Hood will receive the spot opposite Greg Newsome II. The Giants should dress Jason Pinnock in this game as insurance behind Tyler Nubin, who was attacked by McVay’s offense in Week 2. The Giants faced a Rams team that used 13 personnel on over half of their snaps — that won’t be the case against Brian Daboll’s offense. Giants’ nickel cornerback, Dru Phillips, played on just 48% of snaps against the Rams, after playing on in 83% against Dallas. Expect to see less base personnel and more nickel packages against a Titans team that has run 11 personnel at a 71% rate. Daboll has used 12 personnel at an 18% rate. The 17% blitz rate from Week 2 is going to increase in Week 3. Cam Ward has been blitzed at a 31% rate overall and a 38% rate on third down. I expect to see more five-man rushes from the Giants. Wilson should dictate via aggression against the young quarterback. There is an option to expand Reese’s role as a blitzer, too. Reese has 11 pass rush snaps this season; possible use of him on the edge in certain situations versus 11 personnel could be something for the Giants to explore. New York could use a lot of Cover-3, middle-of-the-field-closed with both strong/weak-side buzz rotation against 3×1 sets. Final thoughts I expect the Giants, although injured, will handle business against the Titans. I believe we’ve seen the worst of Jameis Winston, and he’ll help stabilize the offense, which will likely be in 12 and 22 personnel often. I also expect Wilson to have more freedom and comfort to get creative against Ward and Daboll’s offense. I have the Giants winning, 20-13.
author: Nick Falato

title: Giants vs. Titans: Can the Giants’ offense rebound on a short week?
summary: It was a long flight home to the Meadowlands for the New York Giants after their Monday nightmare against the Los Angeles Rams. That flight turned into a long and trying Tuesday as the Giants learned that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart was lost for the remainder of the season. In doing so, the keys to […]
full_text: New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston throws a pass. | Getty Images It was a long flight home to the Meadowlands for the New York Giants after their Monday nightmare against the Los Angeles Rams. That flight turned into a long and trying Tuesday as the Giants learned that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart was lost for the remainder of the season. In doing so, the keys to the Giants’ offense were passed to backup quarterback Jameis Winston . Winston’s first test will come against the Tennessee Titans and a collection of former faces. This game had been circled for a while, largely because of all the storylines surrounding it. Brian Daboll , cornerback Cor’Dale Flott , wide receiver Wan’Dale Robinson , center Austin Schlottman , and tight end Daniel Bellinger are all familiar familiar with Winston, as well as many of their offensive linemen, tight ends, and running backs. Robert Saleh will be calling the Titans’ defense, but he has plenty of resources from whom he can seek insight. The Titans were expected to be a relatively easy win after the Giants steamrolled the Dallas Cowboys. Now, the Giants are only slim favorites at home. How will the offense respond in Winston’s first test? Jameis Winston at QB The Giants had to adapt to a new reality early on in their loss to the Rams, when Dart was lost for the game to a knee injury. It didn’t go well and Winston appeared rattled when he came on the field for the Giants against the Rams. While his job as the veteran backup is to be a steady presence in troubled times, he did not appear comfortable at all on Monday night. Winston appeared to distrust his protection, not see the defense well, nor throw the ball well. For as bad as Winston looked after coming onto the field following Dart’s injury, there is the silver lining that the Titans can’t be sure just what the Giants’ offense will look like with a pure pocket passer under center. They can be sure that Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely will still be centerpieces, but they can’t know just what form the offense will take. Winston is a different type of quarterback from Dart. The two share charisma and competitiveness, as well as a baseball background and impressive arm talent, however they’re very different athletes. That’s going to change how the Giants structure and call their offense. The quarterback run game that kept defenses honest is gone, as is the threat of a scramble once things break down. However, Winston is also a much more experienced quarterback who has seen just about every type of defense the NFL has to offer, and is willing to attack them all. That can get him into trouble, but it can also be an asset if the Giants embrace it. It’s worth remembering that the Winston-led Giants never trailed in regulation against the Lions and he was solid against the Green Bay Packers, and that was with a more flawed coaching staff and a worse offensive roster. Winston has the arm strength to push the ball down the field and the Giants have enough pieces to take advantage of mistakes in coverage when they happen — assuming Winston can control his characteristic aggression long enough for them to manifest. The possibility of explosive passing plays could also loosen things up for the run game, which we know John Harbaugh wants to rely upon. The Giants have very limited time in which to shift gears from Dart to Winston, but the fact that the Titans can’t know exactly what the Giants will do is an advantage they should seize. How will the Titans defend Jameis? The Giants aren’t the only ones who have to shift gears after the injury to Dart. The Titans now have a very different quarterback to defend, with different challenges. Conventional wisdom suggests that the Titans will focus on Harbaugh and Greg Roman’s desire to be a run-first team. It would follow that they would focus on stacking the box and force Winston to beat them through the air. However, Saleh is (yet another) member of the Fangio tree. He prefers to rotate between Cover 4 and Cover 3 looks, and San Francisco ran among the highest rates of those coverages in the NFL. Saleh’s defense was also among the League leaders in nickel usage. The Titans obviously don’t have the same defensive personnel as the 49er’s, nor do they have anything like San Francisco’s offense. However, Saleh’s overall philosophy has been pretty consistent over the years. The Fangio style of defense is designed to both prevent explosive plays and confuse quarterbacks with late rotations. The Titans won’t have to worry about the Giants’ quarterback run game with Winston under center, nor will they have to pay particular attention to spying a mobile quarterback. The Giants should be alert to the possibility that rather than try to go against their defensive philosophy to sell out to defend the run, they’ll instead try to force Jameis Winston to be patient and frustrate him. Winston has a bad history of throwing the ball to the team wearing the wrong color jerseys, and safety Amani Hooker intercepted Jalen Hurts twice last week (nearly returning one for a touchdown). The Giants could look to be a more explosive passing offense with Winston, moving away from the surgical attack they used with Dart to emphasize Winston’s arm strength and aggressiveness. Playing coverage would keep a lid on the Giants’ offense and potentially take away Winston’s biggest asset, while also providing the defense with opportunities to take the ball away. Inside, the Titans would be counting on defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to both pressure Winston into making a mistake as well as disrupting runs behind the line of scrimmage. Their linebackers played relatively well against the Philadelphia Eagles last week, and could frustrate the Giants’ underneath passing game. Attacking Saleh’s defense How the Giants attack the Titans’ defense will likely be decided over the first drive or two and there will likely be a “feeling out” period for both of these teams. The Giants are shifting gears in an offense that’s still new. There’s little tape on the Giants’ offense and basically none on the Giants’ offense with Winston. On the flip side, the Titans are only playing their third game in a new defense. While Saleh’s general scheme and philosophy, there’s still only limited tape on how it’s being applied to the Titans’ roster. The easy answer is that the Giants should counter-punch however the Titans opt to defend them. If the Titans try to lock down the run, the Giants should take the dare to beat them through the air. Conversely, if the Titans play coverage, the Giants should play to their running strengths and use an intermediate passing attack to supplement the run and attack the voids underneath the deep coverage zones. That may be frustrating for Winston, but keeping the offense moving would (hopefully) mitigate that until opportunities for explosive plays open up. The Giants’ offense wants to be based on running the ball, however they do have an unconventionally built roster. The Giants are heavy on running backs and tight ends, but light on receivers. If the Giants play a more conventional passing offense, they’ll be able to use their personnel to disguise their intentions. Isaiah Likely and Theo Johnson are both athletic tight ends who can stress the seams of Saleh’s Cover 3 shells, while all of the Giants’ running backs are able to catch the ball. Likewise, Nabers, Darnell Mooney , and Likely are all able to pick up yards after catch on screens or quick passes to the flats. The Giants’ lives were made significantly more difficult on offense after the injury to Dart. That, however, doesn’t mean that it’s time to pack it in. They still have weapons and pieces that can allow them to continue to win. The job of Harbaugh, his coaching staff, and Winston is now to steady the ship and rally the team with a win at home.
author: Chris Pflum

title: Previewing the Jets’ opposition: Detroit Lions
summary: The New York Jets and Detroit Lions are both 1-1 heading into Sunday’s matchup, but both are in search of a bounceback game after the Jets lost in overtime and the Lions gave up 41 points in last Thursday night’s loss to the Bills. Let’s break down the Lions’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Amon-Ra St. Brown #14 of the Detroit Lions celebrates with Jared Goff #16 after scoring a touchdown against the Buffalo Bills during the third quarter of the game at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets and Detroit Lions are both 1-1 heading into Sunday’s matchup, but both are in search of a bounceback game after the Jets lost in overtime and the Lions gave up 41 points in last Thursday night’s loss to the Bills. Let’s break down the Lions’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks Jared Goff has had three seasons in a row with over 4,500 passing yards and he’s off to a good statistical start so far in 2026. He leads the league with six touchdown passes and doesn’t have an interception. He has been sacked five times and fumbled three times, though. Goff has also been durable. This will be his 72nd consecutive start, dating all the way back to the end of the 2021 season. The Lions moved fast to address their backup situation when Teddy Bridgewater retired in the offseason. His replacement, Josh Dobbs, is an extremely smart quarterback who has started 15 NFL games. Offensive Line The Lions had a trio of starting offensive linemen who were limited in practice this week: Left guard Christian Mahogany, right guard Tate Ratledge and right tackle Blake Miller. However, all three returned to practice on Friday and are expected to start. Mahogany’s return is just in time because Ben Bartch, who started the first two games in his place, is out of this weekend’s game due to injury. He had been struggling in pass protection, so this should be an upgrade, although Mahogany gave up a team-high six sacks in 2025. The first round rookie Miller will make his return after Larry Borom filled in for him last week. He gave up two sacks and had three penalties, so this again looks like it will be an upgrade. Left tackle Penei Sewell is their best lineman, having been to the past four pro bowls. He gave up just two sacks last year. The other starter is Juice Scruggs who is the center, although Cade Mays would probably be starting if he wasn’t on injured reserve. He lines up alongside Ratledge, who led the team in offensive penalties last year. The other backup is guard Miles Frazier, who was a fifth round pick last year. They will also need to elevate another one with Bartch ruled out. Running Backs The two-headed monster is no more, as David Montgomery is now in Houston, but this has freed up Jahmyr Gibbs to try and establish himself as the league’s best running back. He’s off to a decent start with 299 yards from scrimmage in the first two games. With new addition Isiah Pacheco on injured reserve, the number two is the converted safety Sione Vaki, although he has only 10 carries in three seasons. Jacob Saylors is the number three, but mostly on the team for his special teams abilities. Pass catchers Pro bowler Amon-Ra St. Brown is off to an excellent start this year. He leads the NFL with 19 catches and four touchdown receptions. He’s by no means the Lions’ only weapon, though, as Jameson Williams is also coming off back-to-back thousand-yard seasons. Then you have tight end Sam LaPorta, who had 17 touchdowns in his first two seasons before missing eight games last year. Detroit’s other starting receiver, Isaac TeSlaa, only caught 16 passes last year but six of them were touchdowns and he’s established himself as a big play threat and capable of highlight reel grabs. Tay Martin and Tom Kennedy are also both on the team at wide receiver but neither has played an offensive snap so far this season. Depth at tight end comes from ex-Jet Tyler Conklin, Jackson Meeks and Brock Wright. Wright, who also plays fullback, caught a crucial touchdown pass when the 2022 Jets blew a late lead to the Lions in the last meeting between these teams. Defensive Line Former number two overall pick Aidan Hutchinson is the star of the Lions defensive line. He had 14.5 sacks last year and already has three in the first two games of this season. DJ Wonnum is the other starting edge with second round pick Derrick Moore on the bench along with another rookie, the undrafted Eric O’Neill. Ahmed Hassanein was inactive last Thursday. Tyler Lacy is also listed as an edge but he’s 300 pounds and also plays inside. In addition, the Lions also have former first round pick Payton Turner, but he’s on injured reserve. The starters on the interior are Alim McNeill and Tyleik Williams. McNeill’s importance is evident by the fact that he’s easily Detroit’s highest paid defensive player. Sixth round rookie Skyler Gill-Howard provides depth off the bench along with Levi Onwuzurike. Mekhi Wingo is also on the roster but was inactive against the Bills. Linebackers The linebacker unit is anchored by all-pro Jack Campbell, who had 176 tackles last season. Derrick Barnes is the other starter and he’s had an effective start to the season with 13 tackles, two pass breakups, two sacks and an interception in the first two games. Depth comes from Trevor Nowaske, Malcolm Rodriguez and the experienced Devin White. Fourth round pick Jimmy Rolder has been inactive so far, though. Defensive Backs The Lions have serious issues in their secondary, which is the main reason they have given up the second highest yardage total and points total in the first two games. Safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph, each of whom were pro bowlers in 2024, began the year on the PUP list, so the Jets have known for some time Detroit would be undermanned in the secondary for this game. However, Avonte Maddox, who was filling in, suffered a season-ending foot injury in the Bills game and, as if that wasn’t bad enough, his replacement Thomas Harper is also out of Sunday’s game due to an ankle issue. Options that remain include ex-Jets Chuck Clark and Jalen Mills. Clark started the first two games but Mills was only just added to the practice squad a few days ago. Offseason addition Christian Izien may need to step up, while undrafted rookie Bishop Fitzgerald is also an option. The Lions are theoretically at full strength in terms of the cornerback position but their starting trio – DJ Reed, Rock Ya-Sin and slot corner Roger McCreary all lack size which could be an issue against some of the multiple tight end looks the Jets run. Fifth round rookie Keith Abney II, Khalil Dorsey and Ennis Rakestraw Jr. provide depth at corner. Special Teams Kicker Jake Bates has made all 10 of his kicks so far this season, but he missed nine in 2025. He has a big leg but was just 4-for-9 from beyond 50 last season. Punter Jack Fox, a pro bowler in 2020 and 2024, is off to a solid start after his numbers dropped off a bit in 2025. Longtime return specialist (and former Jet) Kalif Raymond is now with the Bears, so the Lions have Kennedy and Saylors returning kicks. Kennedy has handled punts so far, with the kickoff duties shared. Nobody has broken a long one yet this year. Martin and Dorsey are the team’s primary punt gunners and Martin leads the team with four special teams tackles so far this season. Nowaske, Vaki and Saylors were productive in kick coverage last year.
