title: One 49ers rookie will need to step up in big way after injuries
summary: Once again, the San Francisco 49ers continue to be hit by the injury bug, and it’s coming in heaps on the defensive line. Star defensive end Nick Bosa suffered a calf injury in practice during warmups, with head coach Kyle Shanahan expecting him to miss a few weeks, although the 49ers are not expected to […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Gracen Halton #93 of the San Francisco 49ers tackles De'von Achane #28 of the Miami Dolphins in the fourth quarter of a game at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Once again, the San Francisco 49ers continue to be hit by the injury bug, and it’s coming in heaps on the defensive line. Star defensive end Nick Bosa suffered a calf injury in practice during warmups, with head coach Kyle Shanahan expecting him to miss a few weeks, although the 49ers are not expected to place him on Injured Reserve with their number of injuries. While he’s expected to return this season, that marks the sixth defensive lineman that has gotten injured over the past few weeks, with Bosa joining C.J. West as a multi-week injury on the defensive line. Currently, the 49ers are without Bosa, West, Mykel Williams, Alfred Collins, Sam Okuayinonu, James Thompson Jr., and Romello Height, who is out for Sunday with a broken hand. The 49ers were hoping for better results from their defensive line after their 2025 unit ranked last in the NFL in sacks. Now, they’ll be working without a good portion of their rotation, with a ton of new bodies in the building. Osa Odighizuwa will have to lead this defensive line now. While he hasn’t gotten a sack, Odighizuwa has done quite well through two weeks as a pass-rusher. His eight pressures lead the team and he has a very-respectable 15.8 percent pass rush win rate, according to PFF. But it’s the surrounding pieces that will have to step up. At the top of that list? Rookie fourth-round defensive tackle Gracen Halton. Halton, considered one of the “value” picks by the 49ers in the 2026 NFL Draft, was expected to be a rotational piece on the interior for San Francisco with Alfred Collins, C.J. West, and Odighizuwa all in the mix. However, his role has changed dramatically with the injuries. Halton played 32 snaps against the Miami Dolphins in Week 2, which was second amongst defensive tackles behind Odighizuwa. It was the same story in Week 1 when he played 31 snaps against the Los Angeles Rams. That number could even start to go up this week without West, who had played 23 and 26 snaps in the first two weeks, and Bosa. What has Raheem Morris seen from his rookie so far? “He played well,” Morris said of Halton’s performance against the Dolphins. “He had some good plays, had some rookie plays. You know, there’s always going to be some ups, always going to be some downs, but really excited to see. I think he got a tackle for loss that I can remember, had a nice celebration on. Did some really good things, gave us great energy, great juice inside there. Plays bigger than his actual stature. Did a lot of really cool things. Really excited about where he’s going to go and what he can do for the Niners.” Halton had two pressures in Week 2, and is now tied for third on the team with three in two weeks. What has surprised the coaching staff so far? “I think I said this before, but his movement was not the surprise,” Morris said. “He had great movement and things like that in Oklahoma. His natural ability to move around and kind of stunt and do some things like that. We thought we would get like this guy that can really help out in the pass rush. We knew that right away. “But, when he got here, really shocked us with his ability to use his hands and played well in the run game and be able to be stout and do some real cool things there. I forget when we kind of got that revelation. I think it was sometime in camp, we put the pads on for sure, but his ability to go out there and play the run for us is really good as well. We’re excited about that with him going forward.” During the pre-draft process, Morris had a strong comp for Halton: Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Kobie Turner, as he believes the rookie can be versatile. “He certainly can [be versatile and play multiple spots],” Morris said of Halton. “You like Osa to be at that three technique. You like him if we’re playing with the four-down front for him to be at that nose tackle. But, he can do both. He can multitask. I think I compared him to Kobie Turner in the draft when I was talking to you guys last. I’m not sure, but he’s kind of got some of those type of qualities where he can play nose, play three technique, do a couple of different things. Really smart, really sharp young man. Really excited about him.” The 49ers will need their rookie to really start stepping up in the coming weeks, as they’re shorthanded up front on the defensive line. Next up is the Arizona Cardinals, but after that comes the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks. Some pretty tough and important matchups are on the way.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: Kyle Shanahan shares how Nick Bosa got hurt; calls 49ers injuries ‘unusual’
summary: Mike Evans practiced Friday for the San Francisco 49ers. That’s a good sign for his availability in Week 3 against the Arizona Cardinals. However, rookie pass rusher Romello Height missed Friday’s session. Height had hand surgery earlier in the week after breaking it, and his status for Sunday was always in question. He was ruled […]
full_text: (Photo by Morgan Hancock/Getty Images) | Getty Images Mike Evans practiced Friday for the San Francisco 49ers. That’s a good sign for his availability in Week 3 against the Arizona Cardinals. However, rookie pass rusher Romello Height missed Friday’s session. Height had hand surgery earlier in the week after breaking it, and his status for Sunday was always in question. He was ruled out for Sunday. The only other players who weren’t on hand were players you’d expect to miss: Nick Bosa (calf), James Thompson Jr. (ankle), and Demarcus Robinson (ankle). Here’s the final injury report: DE Nick Bosa (calf) WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) DT James Thompson Jr. (ankle) DE Romello Height (hand) QUESTIONABLE WR Mike Evans (hip) One reporter asked whether it feels like Groundhog Day with all of the injuries. Kyle Shanahan said, “Losing Bosa was rough yesterday. Losing 6 out of the 10 d-linemen in the last two weeks that made our team is a little unusual. Don’t think I’ve been a part of that. That has been different.” Enough players to start and two depth pieces in two games at one position. Unusual, indeed. Kyle Shanahan explained that Bosa’s injury occurred when he was warming up doing high knees before the official team stretch: “He does his warm-up deal, right before walkthrough. He does his own warm-up on the side. Just got his calf doing it.” Shanahan said the injury happened right before practice. Shanahan didn’t put a firm timeline on Bosa’s return, but said, “guessing around a few weeks.” The original question was whether Bosa would miss “months.” The injury isn’t expected to impact Bosa long-term. As for the injured reserve, “it’s a discussion. He’s right there at that point, along with a couple of other guys that are in the same boat. Because of the number we have on it, we won’t be able to do all of them. So we’ve gotta decide. We’re just trying to guess which ones go longer, which ones have the chances of being sooner. It’s just a guess. They’re all close in the same boat, so gotta decide that tomorrow at 1.” If Bosa doesn’t land on the injured reserve, that’s relatively good news. It’s a sign that Bosa’s injury may not keep him out for four games. Shanahan sounded confident that Bosa will play again this season, saying, “I know he was bummed out, but he’ll be back.”

title: 6 takeaways from the 49ers coordinators: Jordan Watkins is ‘going to get some ops’
summary: Both San Francisco 49ers coordinators, Raheem Morris and Klay Kubiak, speak every Thursday. We’ll start having takeaways from their media sessions to see if they give any hints about what’s to come for the upcoming game. For the second week in a row, the 49ers offense and defense exceeded expectations. Morris is doing it without […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Both San Francisco 49ers coordinators, Raheem Morris and Klay Kubiak, speak every Thursday. We’ll start having takeaways from their media sessions to see if they give any hints about what’s to come for the upcoming game. For the second week in a row, the 49ers offense and defense exceeded expectations. Morris is doing it without some key contributors along the defensive line. For the next few weeks, Morris will be without his best player . Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris “Next man up, mentality.” The 49ers lost Nick Bosa, CJ West, and James Thompson Jr. two weeks after losing Sam Okuayinonu and Alfred Collins. That’s more than half the defensive linemen who made the roster heading into Week 1. Morris said what every coach would say in this situation, “We’ve got to step up. Next-man-up mentality. It’s unfortunate what happened to C.J. because he took a step forward this game, just like everybody else did when it comes to that matter. But, really excited about the next guy to go out there and get the opportunity to do it.” Naquan Jones and one of the practice squad trio of Sebastian Valdez, Kevin Givens, or McKinnley Jackson are the candidates for “next man-up.” Osa Odighizuwa (70 snaps) and Gracen Halton (58) out-snapped West (47) and Thompson (39) through two games, but that’s a lot of volume to replace, especially for a defense that’s started each game in 5-man fronts. Through the first two weeks of the season, the 49ers have used 5-man fronts on 37% of their snaps — 4% above league average — compared to four-down fronts 58% of the time. When injuries eat into your depth the way they have early on, it Nick Bosa’s been ‘dominant’ without a sack Before Bosa’s injury, Morris was asked how teams are game-planning for Bosa, and what he’s seen from Bosa so far. Morris said, “He’s been really the most dominant player without a sack. I mean, I have to say he’s been awesome. You know, when he’s rushing the passer, the first play of the game, the first play of the season, was absolutely outstanding. You know, this week checking around Willis and he just forgot how to sack people. But other than that, man, I’ve joked with him this weekend, but other than that, he’s been awesome. We’ll see moving forward all the stuff that happens with him, but he’s been playing great.” Sumer Sports charts “impact” plays. On a per-snap basis, only Texans’ pass rusher Will Anderson Jr. and Blls’ edge rusher Greg Rousseau have more impact plays than Bosa. His pressures and wins have directly led to sacks for his teammates. No offensive coordinator in their right mind will ignore Bosa when he’s on the field. It opens up opportunities for players like Keion White to rush inside, where he’s been flying under the radar. The trickle effect of not having Bosa on the field is role players like White being asked to do things you normally wouldn’t ask of them. It’s easy to take for granted how dominant Bosa is, but he didn’t miss a beat coming off injury. Ogbo Okoronkwo is 11th in pressure percentage. To me, that’s a Bosa stat. An actual Bosa stat and where they’ll miss him the most is Bosa’s run defense. Only Anderson Jr. has more run stops than Bosa at their position. “One of the plays I didn’t like this week was kind of on me” Speaking of the run defense, Morris gave a long-winded answer: “It’s continued to get better every time. You know, the first week we give up probably four or five runs that you want back. It might’ve even been a little more in the Rams game. This game, it got cut down to about three. And there’s always different things. You always have some things where you have, one we had a bad alignment. One I thought was a holding. One of the plays that I didn’t like this week was kind of on me. It was third down and long. They caught us in a conversion down. They popped the run. Some of those situations happen, whether it was the 17-yarder, the nine-yarder, the eight-yarder. You know, those things happen, but I did like how fast we played in the runs that we played really well. That’s starting to breed understanding. I think [LB] Fred [Warner] alluded to it earlier, but sometimes I say things in the game, it’s the first time you actually hear it in the game. You’ve got to go out there and execute it when you’re playing tackle football. It’s not always going to be perfect, but I do like the natural development the guys have taken. We went from probably, and I’m guessing, we probably went from about eight runs in that first game that you didn’t like to maybe cut it down to three or four in this game that you just didn’t like. There was always some things you can clean up, but I really like where the guys are going and how the understanding is starting to come together.” In Week 1, the Rams had success with the second defensive line unit came on the field. In Week 2, it was much of the same. Outside of some early second quarter runs in both games, the run defense has been fine. But that was before the 49ers needed to rely on players who weren’t on the roster as recent as two weeks ago. The Gracen Halton revelation A couple of players Morris may lean into more are Gracen Halton and Osa Odighizuwa. Morris liked what he saw from the rookie against the Dolphins: “He played well. He had some good plays, had some rookie plays. You know, there’s always going to be some ups, always going to be some downs, but really excited to see. I think he got a tackle for loss that I can remember, had a nice celebration on. Did some really good things, gave us great energy, great juice inside there. Plays bigger than his actual stature. Did a lot of really cool things. Really excited about where he’s going to go and what he can do for the Niners.” Halton has been a pleasant surprise against the run. Morris was asked whether he was surprised by Halton’s run defense: “I think I said this before, but his movement was not the surprise. He had great movement and things like that in Oklahoma. His natural ability to move around and kind of stunt and do some things like that. We thought we would get like this guy that can really help out in the pass rush. We knew that right away. But, when he got here, really shocked us with his ability to use his hands and played well in the run game and be able to be stout and do some real cool things there. I forget when we kind of got that revelation. I think it was sometime in camp, we put the pads on for sure, but his ability to go out there and play the run for us is really good as well. We’re excited about that with him going forward.” Morris compared Halton to Rams’ defensive tackle Kobie Turner, and finished by saying, “Really smart, really sharp young man. Really excited about him.” Offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak Brandin Cooks’ ‘reputation kind of precedes itself’ Cooks played with the Rams back in 2018 and 2019. Kubiak said because Cooks has been in essentially every scheme, he’ll naturally have familiarity with things like the 49ers route tree and some formations, but playbooks evolve, so maybe his Rams tenure helped “just a little bit.” Kubiak sounded like he’s been impressed with Cooks’ work ethic: “Yeah, good to have him here. He’s a pro. He’s been doing it a long time. He’s a worker. Everything. His reputation kind of precedes itself. He’s a heck of a worker. Everywhere he’s been, people just talk about how hard he practices, obviously how hard he plays. He’s a vet. He’s picking up our offense quick. It’s good to have him out there and get him involved and just get him incorporated into our offense. So, he’s been a pleasure to have.” Cooks grew up a 49ers fan and was born and raised in Stockon, California. Getting an opportunity with the 49ers, even if it isn’t this week, has to be a dream come true. “Jordan’s going to get his opportunities” It might be too much to ask to expect anything from Cooks after he’s been in the building for a few days. We’ll see how the 49ers elect to replace Demarcus…

full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers will look to start 3-0 when they take on the Arizona Cardinals in Week 3, giving them their second NFC West matchup in three weeks. San Francisco has been on a roll to start the season, securing blowout wins over the Los Angeles Rams (27-7) and the Miami Dolphins (35-13) behind their offensive engine. They haven’t really been threatened in either game, dominating the second halves to get an early jump in the division race. With how good the NFC West is, every division win counts, placing an extra emphasis on this game. The Cardinals are coming off a 31-7 loss to the Drew Lock-led Seattle Seahawks after they upset the Los Angeles Chargers 26-14 in Week 1. It’s a game the 49ers are expected to win by more than a touchdown . Those odds have remained consistent throughout the week on FanDuel Sportsbook . Faithful, take 49ers game day wherever you go! Stay connected to the action and share every reaction with fellow 49ers fans on the SB Nation app. Join the live game-day chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Will the 49ers take care of business? Here are three predictions for Sunday’s game against the Cardinals. 49ers run game finally gets going We’ve seen San Francisco’s passing attack get off to a hot start behind Brock Purdy, but the run game didn’t materialize in Week 2, when Christian McCaffrey had just 23 yards on 10 carries. Kaelon Black continues to get in the mix. He had seven carries for 25 yards in Week 2 after 14 carries for 65 yards against the Rams. After a down week running the ball, this is a great opportunity for the 49ers to get going in the run game. Their offensive line holds a clear advantage over the Cardinals’ defensive line. While Arizona has pieces like Walter Nolen and Josh Sweat, the Cardinals have been below average defending the run this season, and now face a top-10 offensive line with the 49ers. Sure, Arizona could sell out against the run, but the 49ers’ passing attack has been making opponents pay. I think Arizona will look to limit explosives here, and the run game will finally get an opportunity to flourish. It will be a heavy blitz day for Raheem Morris Without Nick Bosa , the 49ers are going to have to generate pressure on Jacoby Brissett. Now, this is a unique spot for San Francisco’s defense. Brissett has proven to be a quality passer, but the Cardinals don’t run play-action much with his mobility, and he doesn’t look to scramble. Now, with Brissett’s propensity to get the ball out, I’m not sure how many sacks the 49ers will get on Sunday. But I do think Raheem Morris will throw out a lot of different blitz packages to get to the quarterback, creating better late-down situations for the 49ers defense. Arizona has not done well on third downs this year, ranking 22nd in conversion rate at 34.6 percent. I’m looking for Morris to tee off on Brissett, especially if the 49ers get up early. 49ers drop 27+ for a third straight week The Niners have been humming as an offense through two weeks, and I don’t see that changing in Week 3. The offensive environment is all in place. They’ve got the advantage in the trenches, have a quarterback who’s playing his best football, and a quality set of skill-position players to throw the ball to. San Francisco has shown it can create explosives and sustain long drives. After Seattle dropped 31 on them last week, I see the 49ers getting to at least the 27 points they’ve reached in their past two games. That could lead to a third straight double-digit win.

title: 49ers star Nick Bosa is expected to miss ‘a few weeks’ after pulling his calf
summary: Another 49ers season, another potentially season-ending injury for Nick Bosa. Or at least that is the scenario according to NBC Sports Bay Area’s Jennifer Lee Chan. Bosa popped up on the injury report on Thursday with a calf problem. Speaking on her YouTube channel, Chan reported that there’s concern that Bosa has suffered a “serious […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Another 49ers season, another potentially season-ending injury for Nick Bosa. Or at least that is the scenario according to NBC Sports Bay Area’s Jennifer Lee Chan. Bosa popped up on the injury report on Thursday with a calf problem. Speaking on her YouTube channel, Chan reported that there’s concern that Bosa has suffered a “serious calf injury” and, if he’s not out for the season, he’ll be out for multiple weeks Here’s the full quote from Lee Chan: “Nick Bosa was supposed to talk to us on media day, that was Wednesday. He did not talk to us on Wednesday, then he did not talk to us today, on Thursday. We waited around for him. Knee and calf. It’s not good. I just..it doesn’t feel good. My spidey sense is saying that this is a serious injury for Bosa. If he’s not out for the season, he’s out for multiple weeks.” The 2022 Defensive Player of the Year missed most of last season due to a torn ACL he suffered in the Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals, whom the 49ers will face in their third game of the season this Sunday. Lee Chan began to backpedal in this tweet: I said “COULD HAVE” have due to his practice status changing and other factors. I also said I COULD be wrong. Let’s not pick and choose words. https://t.co/sd5QWJ3BHJ — Jennifer Lee Chan -all platforms: @jenniferleechan (@jenniferleechan) September 25, 2026 But Adam Schefter confirmed what she said, tweeting that Bosa will miss a few weeks after pulling his calf in practice on Thursday. Ian Rapoport said Bosa could land on injured reserve. San Francisco’s pass rush was non-existent without him in 2025, and any kind of prolonged absence would be a hammer blow to a defensive line that already has very thin depth. After consistently pressuring Matthew Stafford in the season-opening win over the Los Angeles Rams, the 49ers registered four sacks of Malik Willis in their blowout victory against the Miami Dolphins in Week 2. Bosa’s ability to collapse the pocket was a huge part of the latter performance and, if he is out, it will be substantial pressure on a young group to excel without him. Head coach Kyle Shanahan is due to hold his final press conference ahead of the Cardinals at 1:35 PT, about an hour after the 49ers practice. Bosa’s status will be the main talking point as San Francisco gears up for a difficult division game. Here is the lengthy list of defensive linemen to suffer an injury, just in the past two weeks: Nick Bosa (calf) Alfred Collins (torn patellar tendon) Sam Okuayinonu (broken foot) James Thompson Jr. (high-ankle sprain) Romello Height (broken hand) CJ West (bone chip in knee) Schefter said the 49ers are leaning toward not placing Bosa on the injured reserve because the team is running out of injured reserve spaces. Week 3 just began. That’s how banged up this team is.

title: Outlining a plan to address the Washington Commanders secondary
summary: Things have not gone according to plan for the Washington Commanders and their secondary through the first two weeks of the season. The idea of frequent and disguised pressures shouldering the bulk of the burden for the defensive backs is not sustainable if teams can slow the pressure and exploit coverage lapses, and there have […]
full_text: Things have not gone according to plan for the Washington Commanders and their secondary through the first two weeks of the season. The idea of frequent and disguised pressures shouldering the bulk of the burden for the defensive backs is not sustainable if teams can slow the pressure and exploit coverage lapses, and there have been plenty to exploit. As many fans will tell you, the ship has sailed on any significant personnel additions at this point in the season, but in this article I will outline how defensive coordinator Daronte Jones could try to fix the issues in the secondary with the players he currently has on the roster. The most difficult part of the plan is it requires the coaching staff to make personnel changes instead of dispensing platitudes and focusing on communication and leveling up . It also needs to happen quickly, before the team is 0-4 to start the season. Listening to Daronte Jones’ last press conference , I don’t know if they feel the same urgency to make the necessary changes. Daronte Jones on when it's time to think lineup changes: "You've got to first dive into why is it happening, and then if it's become 'Hey, this guy's just not doing what we're asking him to do, then you may have to make a personnel change in that regards" pic.twitter.com/GoGcp2n4xv — Martenzie Johnson (@10zJohnson) September 24, 2026 Still, here is what I think Jones should do if he decides to switch things up, using Hogs Haven writer MattInBrisVegas’s wonderful Stats and Snaps series as our guide. Bench Mike Sainristil After the first two games, Mike Sainristil currently has a 153.7 allowed passer rating, is ranked 94th out of 94 CBs by PFF , and is coming off a atrocious performance last week where Pro Football Reference assigned him 3.07 Y/Cov Snp . Hogs Haven’s Mark Tyler has some interesting ideas on what to do with Mikey, but with the goal of improving the secondary immediately, I am going with the bench option. It might be wise for Jones to assign Sainristil nothing but slot reps in practice and see if he can work his way back into the lineup, but for now he needs to sit. Out Nick Cross Initially, I had a different version of this plan put together, one that included Cross as a key piece of the puzzle, but with the news he was hospitalized after the Cowboys game and ruled out completely on Wednesday, I think Commanders fans should not plan on him being part of the solution for a couple of weeks. So what’s the plan? If we look at Matt’s tables from this week’s article, we can identify what positions Jones will need to fill this week versus Seattle after removing two starters. Mike Sainristil played the majority of his snaps at LCB, but there are also some slot and box snaps that need to be accounted for as well. Nick Cross moved around the secondary but was the team’s primary slot defender. So we need to look at three different roles: LCB , Slot/Box , and FS . LCB Jones has already been trending towards the first move by giving Rasul Douglas more snaps last week. The veteran cornerback hasn’t been perfect, but PFR has him with a more palatable 97.4 allowed passer rating. Matt’s data from the Cowboys game tells us that Douglas had a bad day in coverage, allowing 5 targets and 4 receptions for 52 yds in 18 coverage snaps (2.89 Y/Cov Snp), but I would think a good chunk of the allowed yards came from this play where he read the route wrong. CeeDee Lamb and the Cowboys had Rasul Douglas (29) fooled on this one. Turpin's clear route makes it look like it's designed to free Lamb on the in-breaking route. 88 sells it beautifully. Great tendency breaker. pic.twitter.com/F0UzsYGDSm — Mauricio Rodríguez (@MauNFL) September 21, 2026 While this certainly is not what you want to see, the remainder of his reps were better and Douglas would be a step up for what we have seen from Sainristil on the boundary. The thought would be to have Rasul work almost completely on the outside, as he has done for most of his career and find another option at the slot position. Slot/Box Last season, when corner Jeff Odukah went out with a concussion, the Vikings elevated Fabian Moreau from the practice squad to the active roster. The 32-year-old veteran did surprisingly well playing limited snaps there, posting very respectable containment numbers (0.51 Y/Cov Snap) and a 54.6 allowed passer rating on 152 coverage snaps. Across 152 coverage snaps, Moreau allowed 8 receptions on 16 targets for a total of 53 yards, a long reception of 11 yards, no TDs, and only committed 1 penalty per PFF — BREVY BRIGHTLIGHTS (@brevmanbane) May 20, 2026 Moreau was brought in as a break glass in case of emergency option as the veteran who knows Jones’ system after two seasons with the Vikings. Unfortunately, I think we have reached that point. Limiting Fabian’s snaps would be important, but the 6’0”, 204-pound Moreau could provide some solid ones as a big nickel. Jeremy Reaves was initially one of my players to bench, as his 158.7 allowed pass rating is one of the worst in the league, but with Nick Cross sidelined, there is a void in the total snap count for the secondary. The fix is to play Reaves in the box with little to no snaps at the free safety position. Jeremy is still a very physical player and can trigger downhill in run support and the short-to-intermediate parts of the field. I don’t love this solution, but it could work until Cross returns from injury. Free Safety Here is where the plan gets a little thin. The team never accounted for the free safety role in their roster planning during the offseason with Martin or Harris potentially filling the role but ultimately ended up demoting Martin, releasing Harris, and going with Jeremy Reaves in their place. With Reaves relegated to the box, the team needs to find another player at free safety. Tyler Owens has been a career special teamer so far, but still might be the best option to replace Reaves and Cross in the deep part of the field. He has the size, speed, and athleticism, but in his one chance last season he looked lost in his assignments. #Commanders S Tyler Owens Most snaps in career (25) Most coverage snaps in career (15) 3 sacks 1 STOP 2 targets 2 receptions long 18yds #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/HTGx7IrYle — Deuce_Redzone (@redzoneinthelab) October 29, 2025 The thing to note here is that Owens played heavily up by the line of scrimmage and in the slot, instead of in a free safety role. In fact, according to Matt’s write-up for last season’s matchup versus the Chiefs he played none at the position. In a role that keeps the play in front of him, limits his reads, and allows him to utilize his range, Owens could potentially perform significantly better. Quan Martin hasn’t been quite as bad as Sainristil through two games, with a 118.7 allowed passer rating per Pro Football Reference . The catch is he has played about half the total number of snaps as Mikey. PFF has him ranked 83rd out of 84 safeties. He was also initially on my bench list as well but also gets a pass with Cross out as the team will likely need him here for two high safety looks, if they decide not to play Reaves there. Coaching & Communication The Washington Commanders decided to retain defensive backs/safeties coach Tom Donatell during the offseason while promoting William Gay from assistant coach to defensive backs/cornerbacks coach. The two decisions were surprising given the secondary’s performance last year and Donatell’s previous track record with the San Diego Chargers. Daronte Jones’ previous ties to defensive coordinator Ed Donatell may have added a layer of familiarity after LSU safeties coach Jake Olsen changed his mind about accepting an offer to join Washington’s coaching staff. Whatever the reason, the two coaches do not seem to be successful installing coverage and communication techniques and Jones will have to take valuable time away from developing his defensive game plan to correct it. title: Commanders fans split on Jayden Daniels return – poll results
summary: Most weeks of the year, and every week of the season for several years now, Hogs Haven runs Reacts surveys, and I write an article breaking down the results. Because I’m writing about what Hogs Haven readers have said in a collective sense, I rely heavily on the comments section to inform what I write. […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 20: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders warms up before a game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Most weeks of the year, and every week of the season for several years now, Hogs Haven runs Reacts surveys, and I write an article breaking down the results . Because I’m writing about what Hogs Haven readers have said in a collective sense, I rely heavily on the comments section to inform what I write . The collective opinion expressed in the survey may not always match my own, but I try to offer an honest peek into the reasons behind the numbers as best I can make sense of them . This week, I want to take a slightly different approach to analyzing the survey results, as you’ll see in the article below. This week, we asked two questions , which is our norm during the regular season. Question 1: Fan confidence The first question asked, as it does every week of the season (at least until early December), whether you are confident in the team’s direction . From our first survey to our second—before and after the opener in Philadelphia—confidence actually climbed from 70% to 83%. That early surge seemed based entirely on the “quality” of the loss: Washington went on the road against an elite Eagles team, pushed them to the brink in a 24-22 nail-biter, and looked competitive throughout. The general feeling was that the outcome turned on a handful of fixable execution errors. This week, however, confidence collapsed to just 20%. A 37-20 loss in Dallas will do that to a fan base. The defense looked disjointed, the secondary surrendered big plays through the air, and the interior offensive line struggled in short-yardage spots. To make matters worse, franchise quarterback Jayden Daniels suffered another dislocation to his left elbow on the final play of the first half. Ron's teams went 7-9, 7-10, & 8-8-1 in his first three years here. His QBs were Smith, Haskins (RIP), Heinicke, Wentz, & Kyle Allen. He didn't have Jayden Daniels and his teams those first years never went through a 2-12 stretch. You take 5 from AP/DQ, they've been outdone by RR. — Oz (@OBtoojiveforyou) September 23, 2026 Sitting at 0-2 overall and 0-2 in the NFC East with the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks arriving in Landover for the home opener, fans are not, to put it mildly, feeling optimistic. Question 2: Jayden Daniels’ 2026 outlook The second question in our survey asked whether you believe Jayden Daniels’ 2026 season came to an end with his injury in Dallas. Visit our partners at FanDuel In a roughly 60:40 split, the majority of survey respondents — who voted in the poll before any update or decision was announced by the team — believed that Jayden would return to the field at some point this season. Again, voting took place early in the week before we had much official word from the team. On Friday, GM Adam Peters gave an update on his weekly radio appearance, and later in the day, head coach Dan Quinn provided confirmation on Daniels’ status. It turns out that the 59% of fans who expected Jayden to return this season were right, at least, according to both AP and DQ, though the exact timing of his return remains up in the air aside from the fact that he is not being placed on IR at the moment. The significance of not being put on injured reserve As you are probably aware, players who are on IR must miss at least 4 games. For Daniels, a stint on IR would have meant Weeks 3 to 6, followed by a bye in Week 7, with a return allowed no earlier than Week 8 at home against the Eagles. The fact that he is not being put on IR signals that the team expects him to return to play earlier, meaning in Week 4, 5 or 6, against the Colts in London, Giants in Landover, or the 49ers in San Francisco. Yes, London remains on the table. Just have to wait/see. https://t.co/yWNXYRay4V — John Keim (@john_keim) September 25, 2026 The Noah Brown lesson Of course, we all remember WR Noah Brown, who, last season, was injured in the Week 2 game vs the Packers. He was not immediately placed on IR, indicating that the team expected him to return by the Week 6 game in mid-October. Instead, when that mid-October date arrived, Brown was not activated, instead being put on IR on October 15th and staying there until early December. So, while it is clear that Adam Peters, Dan Quinn and Jayden himself all expect or hope for his return to play sometime in October, the example of Noah Brown from last season reminds us that return from injury is an uncertain process. In any event, one thing is clear — the team, like the majority of our survey respondents — expect Jayden to be back as captain and quarterback in the coming weeks. Commanders fans: Make your pick in the SB Nation app! Take Reacts surveys, create Commanders polls, and see how your answers compare with fellow Hogs Haven fans. Then discuss the results with the Burgundy and Gold community. Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . An experiment: Mapping 740+ comments with AI As I noted at the top, I try to integrate the thoughts of survey respondents into these weekly articles. This week, I faced both a challenge and an interesting opportunity. The survey article generated over 210 comments on Tuesday and Wednesday. Meanwhile, Monday’s All aTwitter post had drawn more than 530 comments following the Dallas game and covering much of the same territory. Across just 72 hours, this community posted roughly three-quarters of a million words dissecting the state of the franchise in the context of Daniels’ (re)injury. Rather than cherry-picking 4 or 5 comments and calling it a day, I decided to try something different. Having read so much about how Artificial Intelligence is revolutionizing work flows around the world, I figured I could ‘opt in’ and make the revolution work for me. I fed all 530+ comments from Monday’s All aTwitter and all 210+ comments from the Reacts thread into Gemini, asking it to summarize the arguments and track how community sentiment evolved as the week progressed. I know there is plenty of justifiable skepticism across the internet about AI content replacing human writers. Rest assured, I am not handing over my keyboard, but as an analytical tool for mapping community psychology, it seemed like the perfect opportunity to integrate some of the latest technology into my decidedly low-tech writing. What follows in the italicized block below is the AI-generated synthesis of your comments across both threads: The community breakdown (generated via Comment Text Analysis) 1. Immediate aftermath: The Monday vent (All aTwitter) Following the Dallas game, comments reflected acute shock, in-game tactical frustration, and heated debate over Daniels: The Daniels status debate: Discussion split between a minority urging Daniels to get fitted with a brace and return immediately to protect his developmental momentum (LionRoars1987 citing Kurt Warner) and a strong majority rejecting that path, citing re-injury risk and pain. Debate also sparked over whether awkwardly planting an arm is a recurring durability issue or an unavoidable fluke. In-game frustrations: Sharp criticism focused on end-of-half clock management—specifically Daniels trying to make a play rather than taking an easy field goal—leaving the team down 7 rather than 4. Commenters tallied missed opportunities and called out interior offensive line failures in short-yardage spots under center. Front office & staff: Sweeping criticism emerged regarding GM Adam Peters’ three-year roster build, pointing to depth issues along the offensive line and in the secondary. Commenters vented about Dan Quinn’s game management, with a few floating early speculation about offensive coordinator David Blough. 2. The NFL schedules did the Commanders no favors this year with last season’s Super Bowl champions, the […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Antonio Williams #14 of the Washington Commanders catches a pass during the fourth quarter the Philadelphia Eagles against at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s Week 3 and the Washington Commanders are finally playing their first regular season game in front of their fans at Northwest Stadium. They are 0-2 losing back-to-back road division games to the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys. The NFL schedules did the Commanders no favors this year with last season’s Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks, coming to town for a critical Week 3 game. They opened up as big favorites, and that numbers has gone up since Monday. The two teams are on opposite ends of the QB injury spectrum. The Seahawks lost starter Sam Darnold in the first game with an injury that looked worse than it turned out to be. It originally looked like a bad hip injury that could require surgery, but Darnold has been practicing this week with a glute injury and is expected to start on Sunday. The Commanders also could be getting lucky with shorter than initially expected recovery time for Jayden Daniels’ dislocated elbow. He suffered the injury at the end of the half last week vs the Cowboys, and dealt with the same issue last season. General manager Adam Peters and head coach Dan Quinn said that surgery was not an option at this time, and he’s not going to injured reserve which means he could be back in a week or two. It’s the Marcus Mariota show until Daniels returns, and that has affected a lot of the odds and prop bets for Sunday afternoon’s game. The Commanders are big underdogs (+7), but the over/under is low (40.5). This means oddmakers are expecting a low-scoring game with the Seahawks putting the majority of the points on the board. Washington’s offense under first-time offensive coordinator David Blough has been putting up big numbers, but will get a fresh arm and set of legs in Mariota. Terry McLaurin has been catching more flak from fans than balls during games, and that trend needs to change quickly if Washington wants to keep their season alive while they wait for JD5 to return. McLaurin has 4 receptions for 64 yards and no touchdowns over the first two weeks which isn’t good enough production for a receiver that should be getting 10+ targets per game per his new OC. Will that change with Mariota under center, or will he turn to new targets like Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams? I’m going with the rook. Bill Croskey-Merritt is Washington’s RB1, but Rachaad White looked improved in his second game with the team. Bill has 28 rushes for 106 yards and 1 TD, while White has 14 carries for 64 yards. White adds value in the passing game with 8 receptions for 45 yards. The run game has been stronger than the pass game in the new offense, and will get a big test against the #8 run defense. title: Dan Quinn: Jayden Daniels week-to-week; Marcus Mariota named captain
summary: Dan Quinn spoke to reporters after Friday’s practice and confirmed several things that general manager Adam Peters said earlier today in an interview with the Junkies on 106.7-FM The Fan in Washington. Jayden Daniels isn’t getting surgery and he won’t be placed on injured reserve. He’s considered week-to-week, and the team is happy with the […]
full_text: Dan Quinn spoke to reporters after Friday’s practice and confirmed several things that general manager Adam Peters said earlier today in an interview with the Junkies on 106.7-FM The Fan in Washington . Jayden Daniels isn’t getting surgery and he won’t be placed on injured reserve. He’s considered week-to-week, and the team is happy with the positive signs they’ve seen. Quinn wouldn’t commit to the prospect of any future surgery, and said the team’s record wouldn’t play into that decision. He also said no decision has been made about Daniels traveling with the team for their Week 4 game in London. The Commanders had 14 players on their injury report on Wednesday who were either limited or not participating. Daniels and Nick Cross have already been ruled out, and Quinn said three other players were unlikely to be ready for Sunday’s home opener against the Seattle Seahawks. Frankie Luvu (groin) and Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) will be missing their second games, and Sam Cosmi (concussion) misses his first of the season. title: Commanders GM Adam Peters provides Jayden Daniels injury update
summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has traveled around the country seeing specialists for how to best treat a left elbow dislocation that occurred at the end of the first half of a Week 2 loss at Dallas.   Daniels got back late on Thursday and the team was still sitting down to decide on the best […]
full_text: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has traveled around the country seeing specialists for how to best treat a left elbow dislocation that occurred at the end of the first half of a Week 2 loss at Dallas . Daniels got back late on Thursday and the team was still sitting down to decide on the best course of action moving forward. General manager Adam Peters didn’t have definitive answers about Daniels’ rehab process, but he did say that surgery is not on the table and that the team isn’t currently discussing injured reserve for Daniels. That should be considered a positive for the Commanders, creating a prospect that Daniels might not miss much time. “He just got back late last night and the guys are meeting with him this morning,” Peters said Friday morning during his weekly appearance with the The Junkies on 106.7-FM The Fan in Washington . “We met with doctors all over the country and were really thorough. And we got a lot of good opinions. And now it’s a matter of thinking about what’s the best course of action. “As of right now surgery is not on the table and we haven’t discussed (injured reserve). It’s just a matter of how we’re going to get him back on the field. That’s still to be determined.” Peters said the Commanders will lean on medical personnel to makes final decisions about the best course of action. Not placing him on IR would suggest some confidence he can return faster than the four weeks he’d be out with that designation. Washington’s GM hedged that first answer a little bit later in the interview, making sure his previous comments were related this moment. “At this time,” Peters said. “I don’t want to make any proclamations, but those aren’t things we’ve discussed and landed on yet. He just got back. We haven’t even sat down and talked about what we’re doing moving forward.” The Commanders will try to get Daniels back in play quickly, and he’ll wear a brace on his left elbow. He has been ruled out of Sunday’s game versus Seattle but nothing beyond that. As Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer points out, they’ll have to make a decision on whether to bring him to London — they play Indianapolis there in Week 4 — by Tuesday. Commanders QB Jayden Daniels traveled to New York and Los Angeles this week, and met with multiple specialists in both places, leading to his and the team's decision to go forward with the plan to forgo surgery, and bring Daniels back in the coming weeks. title: Washington Commanders vs Seattle Seahawks Week 3: Five Questions with Field Gulls
summary: It’s week 3 of the NFL season, and the 0-2 Washington Commanders will be facing a 2-0 Seattle Seahawks team at home in Northwest Stadium in Landover, MD this Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET. Despite losing starting QB Sam Darnold to a glute injury on the first drive of the first game, the Seahawks have […]
full_text: In a home game at Northwest Stadium on Nov. 2, quarterback Jayden Daniels scores the only Commanders touchdown in the 38-14 week nine loss against the Seattle Seahawks. | Marcus Relacion/The Washington Informer It’s week 3 of the NFL season, and the 0-2 Washington Commanders will be facing a 2-0 Seattle Seahawks team at home in Northwest Stadium in Landover, MD this Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET. Despite losing starting QB Sam Darnold to a glute injury on the first drive of the first game, the Seahawks have managed to beat the Patriots 13-10 in week 1 and beat the Cardinals 31-7 in week 2. It is unclear if Darnold will return to play in week 3, but he has practiced this week. On offense, the Seahawks are coached by OC Brian Fleury, former TEs coach and run-game coordinator of the 49ers from 2022 to 2025. A TEs coach has good insight into both the blocking and pass-catching aspects of offense due to TEs being heavily involved in both duties. The fact that Fleury was also the run-game coordinator for the 49ers means he should be well suited to understanding and coaching all aspects of the Shanahan offense (note that Cowboys OC Klayton Adams was formerly a TEs coach for the Colts and OL coach for the Cardinals who designed their prolific run game before moving to Dallas). So far, the Seahawks offense has stayed true to its Shanahan roots , with heavy use of under center, play action passing, and an outside-zone run game. Perhaps to simplify the passing game for a backup QB, the Seahawks have been targeting WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba with an absurd 44% share of targets (last year he led the NFL with a 35.8% target share). It makes sense to simplify things for your backup QB by scheming him to just throw it to his best player. On defense, the Seahawks are still coached by head coach Mike Macdonald, former DC of the Ravens, and DC Aden Durde, former defensive line coach of the Cowboys. Perhaps unsurprising given that their DC is a former DL coach, the Seahawks defense is anchored around the excellent play of their defensive line. Last year, the Seahawks were able to achieve the 6th-best QB pressure rate despite the 7th-lowest blitz rate, meaning they were able to get pressure rushing four most of the time, and leave more players back in coverage to stop passing plays and explosive plays. The result is a defense that allows the NFL’s fewest passing yards and 9th-fewest rushing yards through two games this year. I asked John Gilbert of Field Gulls five questions to better understand the state of the Seahawks and what to look for in this game. 1) The Seahawks defense has held their opponents to 10 or fewer points in the last two games. How much of this is personnel, how much is scheme, and what is special about Mike Macdonald’s scheme and playcalling? Holding both 2026 opponents they have faced to 10 or fewer points really seems to be a continuation of how the Seattle defense finished the 2025 season, which was by holding five of the last nine teams played to 10 or fewer points. Of the games in which the other team has managed to put more than ten points on the board against this defense since Thanksgiving, they were quarterbacked by Philip Rivers (16), Matthew Stafford (37 & 27) and Drake Maye (13), and any team with a quarterback that isn’t in the tier of those named has struggled against the defense. As for what makes Macdonald’s defense so successful, it’s not one thing in particular. The players are good, but Macdonald makes them better by putting them in a position to succeed by understanding the tendencies of the opponent, while simultaneously giving his players the freedom to operate as needed for success. For example, former undrafted free agent linebacker Drake Thomas changed the defensive front Macdonald had called on a key second and one near midfield early in the game against the Cardinals. Similarly, on the fourth down that effectively clinched the NFC Championship for the Seahawks, DeMarcus Lawrence recognized what the Rams were trying to do and broke off his assignment to prevent Stafford having an easy completion to Kyren Williams for either a first down or score. It’s a rare combination of a scheme that confuses opponents, with players who perform at a high level within the system and have the skills and football IQ to operate with a higher level of freedom, and the experience necessary in the system to play fast without having to think to analyze how to react. 2) On the other side of the ball, how has the Seahawks offense looked? Is it different under new OC Brian Fleury and what changes with Drew Lock vs Sam Darnold at QB? The season opener did not start off well for anyone hoping for the offense would be as explosive as it was last season, as the team was shutout by the Patriots until after halftime. Certainly a part of that is likely due to the fact that Sam Darnold’s injury meant Drew Lock taking over, as well as some rust overall as the starters had not played during the preseason. The fact that the backup is in at quarterback means the jury is largely still out as far as a lot of the questions that surrounded the offense heading into the season. With that said, through the first two games one of the consistent threads that has continued through from 2025 has been the continued usage of two and three tight end packages. Specifically, during the 2025 season the Seahawks used 12- or 13-personnel on a little more than a third of their offensive snaps, while so far in 2026 the usage has been even higher. A big piece of that, of course, is likely that they were up big and running the ball a lot against the Cardinals in the second half of Week 2, so it remains to be seen how much they’ll rely on their tight end heavy packages in more competitive contests. In addition, Fleury has tweaked how the Seattle offense uses motion through the first two games, and that has made things more difficult for opponents to figure out what’s coming. One clear change made by Seahawks OC Brian Fleury is removing a tell from last season. Seattle motioned on 32% of runs and 85% of passes in the Super Bowl. A clear sign a pass was coming. Seattle has motioned on 60.0% of runs and 55.6% of passes this season. No clear pattern. pic.twitter.com/knMhlNhnwz — Brian Nemhauser (@hawkblogger) September 21, 2026 3) What is your overall opinion of Seahawks GM John Schneider and has it evolved since the hiring of Mike Macdonald? Did you ever think he should have been sent packing along with Pete Carroll for a completely fresh start? After coming out of the gates on an absolute scorcher and drafting multiple Hall of Fame caliber players to start his career as a general manager, things went off the rails for several years. From 2017 through 2021 the results of the team’s drafting was not on par with what is necessary for sustained success in the NFL, and that certainly contributed to Carroll’s demise. A big piece of the issues from 2018 on appear to have been reworking the draft board and an over reliance on looking for “maturity” in the wake of the Malik McDowell debacle of 2017. Beginning in 2018 the Seahawks draft classes were consistently among the oldest in the NFL, while many of their biggest hits to come out of those drafts were players like DK Metcalf who were among the younger members of their respective draft class. Where the wheels truly came off, though, was when the Seahawks made a conscious decision to effectively punt on the 2021 draft as a result of the anticipated uncertainty of the COVID season. Seattle made only three selections in the 2021 draft after trading a first and a third for Jamal Adams, a fifth for Gabe Jackson and a seventh for Carlos Dunlap. Of course, the draft is about uncertainty, and the Loser’s Curse is a concept developed decades ago regarding the uncertainty of the draft. That all said, since 2022 Schneider has been back on a heater, and the quality of the roster shows. Even after the departure in free agency of Kenneth Walker, Coby Bryant, Boye…

title: NFL Week 3 betting guide: Analysis and top plays for Sunday's games
summary: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 3 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
full_text:
Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: finding betting value.

 Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game-winners from tape study and his understanding of the league.

 From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, favorite defensive props and the top game to bet in Week 3.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 Jump to: 
 Bowen's Game of the Week  | Solak's plays  | Walder's props 

 

 

 Bowen's Game of the Week 

 Kansas City Chiefs at Miami Dolphins (-10.5, 46.5) 
1 p.m. ET on CBS, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens, Fla.

 

 I tend to stay away from double-digit spreads in this league (especially for road favorites). That can be bad business given the talent level and coaching we get on Sundays. But looking at the matchup and scheme advantages with Kansas City, I'm in on Andy Reid's team. I'll give you my quick notes for both clubs, along with some player props.

 

 When the Chiefs have the ball: The offseason addition of Kenneth Walker III has given the Chiefs a true difference-maker with dual-threat traits in the backfield. Walker has rushed for at least 117 yards -- with at least 23 carries -- in both games this season, and in a Week 2 win over the Indianapolis Colts he caught six of 10 targets for 61 yards. We can expect Walker to get his touches on the ground against a Miami defense giving up 112.5 rushing yards per game (18th in the NFL), which allows Reid's unit to control offensive tempo.

 In the pass game, I see clear matchup advantages for the Chiefs. The Dolphins are giving up an average of 8.6 YPA (30th in the NFL), and they play man coverage at a rate of 58.9% (fourth most). Look for Reid to set up his receivers for catch-and-run throws from Patrick Mahomes , with Rashee Rice and Travis Kelce working multiple levels of the field against a Miami secondary that lacks high-end talent.

 When Miami has the ball: The Dolphins have struggled to build offensive rhythm and lack an identity, having failed to score more than 13 points in each of their first two games. Running back De'Von Achane has rushed for a total of 110 yards this season, and we aren't seeing his elite pass-catching ability (he has only 49 yards receiving). Quarterback Malik Willis has shown flashes, but his accuracy has been inconsistent (completing 58% of his passes), and he has thrown only one touchdown pass.

 Now, Miami does have some young talent in the pass game with Malik Washington , Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell , but Douglas has been ruled out for this matchup after missing practice all week with an ankle injury. The Dolphins lack a proven No. 1 who can win critical game situations at a high rate and they average only 183.5 passing yards per game. Now they'll face a multiple Chiefs defense -- one that leans on late movement and schemed pressure. This Kansas City defense is giving up 90 yards rushing per game and only 5.5 YPA. Miami will need to find a way to create positive game flow while producing some explosive plays to stay in this one.

 

 Now, let's get to some prop bets ...

 Rashee Rice receiving yards OVER 47.5 (-114) 

 Rice, who caught four of six targets for 83 yards in the Week 2 win over the Colts, could have early opportunities against the Dolphins' single-high man coverages. Rice can turn an underneath throw into an explosive gain.

 Travis Kelce receptions OVER 4.5 receptions (-114) 

 Kelce's play speed looked different last week against the Colts, both in the route stem and after the catch. Kelce caught nine of 11 targets in that game, using his high-end coverage awareness to find open grass. He should be a priority target again for Mahomes on Sunday.

 Tyquan Thornton anytime TD (+475) 

 I'm thinking of a shot-play throw here to Thornton on Sunday. Thornton caught all four of his targets for 86 yards last week against the Colts, so look for Reid to set up him on a deep-ball concept in Miami.

 

 

 
 Solak's plays 
 

 Baltimore Ravens -3.5 (-105) vs. Dallas Cowboys 

 Injuries are important to watch heading into this game. Not one of WR Zay Flowers , OT Ronnie Stanley or OLB Trey Hendrickson practiced Wednesday for the Ravens. Still, head coach Jesse Minter said after practice that he feels "like we will have a good shot with a lot of guys this week."

 

 Assuming the Ravens are relatively close to full strength, I like their matchup against Dallas quite a bit. The Cowboys' back seven has struggled tremendously through two weeks of the Christian Parker era on defense; it's a challenging defensive scheme, and they are generally lacking for team speed. Their light edge rushers can be targeted in the run game. Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has excelled at two things so far: attacking the edge in the running game, and generating YAC opportunities for Flowers. Baltimore might steamroll the Cowboys.

 I'm a little worried about the travel and field in Brazil, which can introduce some chaos. The Cowboys' offense can also score in bunches. But the Ravens are a better pressure team, thanks to the play of Hendrickson and Minter's willingness to send pressures on key downs. I like them to get enough stops in what should be a high-scoring affair.

 I'd take this up to -4 (-110), but only if we get positive injury news throughout the week.

 Zay Flowers 90+ receiving yards (+154) 

 I have all of the Flowers overs and alts for similar reasons listed above. Flowers was red hot in Week 1, with five catches for 150 yards and a score on six targets in just the first half against Indianapolis. Now he gets a Cowboys secondary that might be without starting CB Cobie Durant and S P.J. Locke , both of whom defensive coordinator Brian Schottenheimer said are likely to sit out multiple weeks, and fellow safety Malik Hooker , who fractured his forearm in Week 1, sat out Week 2 and did not practice Wednesday. The Cowboys' secondary is already bleeding talent.

 This also is a bust-riddled group that has already dealt with communication changes (rookie third-round LB Jaishawn Barham wore the green dot in Week 2) because of linebacker injuries. With Flowers' speed and positional versatility, the Ravens should be able to funnel him easy targets in space at will.

 Of course, Flowers might not go this week; he's dealing with a hamstring injury, and the field in Brazil is reportedly imperfect. But if he does go, I want to have his numbers from early in the week before they get steamed.

 Houston Texans -1.5 (-118) at Indianapolis Colts 

 Two 0-2 division rivals seemingly with their seasons already on the line -- intense stuff for Week 3. I admired the Colts' pluck in their game against the Chiefs, but the Texans' defense is made of far stiffer stuff. Houston has won the last five games between the teams, though QB  Daniel Jones was hurt for the most recent matchup.

 

 The Colts have relied heavily on big-play receiver Alec Pierce to generate explosive plays against DeMeco Ryans' aggressive defense. Last season against the Texans across two games, Pierce had eight catches, 210 yards and three touchdowns. Pierce hurt his heel against the Chiefs and is on injured reserve, which puts all the more pressure on Josh Downs , Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell at receiver. It's hard to imagine the Colts finding the same big plays that the Buffalo Bills and Cincinnati Bengals have against this Texans secondary.

 It looks like star receiver Nico Collins will miss…

title: NFL Week 3 picks, predictions, schedule, odds, fantasy tips
summary: Jalen Hurts against Chicago? Aaron Glenn back in Detroit? Dak vs. Lamar? There are 15 more games in Week 3, and we have picks, predictions, key stats and more.
full_text:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season is here. Can Justin Herbert and the Chargers finally get back on track? How will Kyler Murray  and (potentially) Sam Darnold fare in their return games? What can we expect in Jets coach Aaron Glenn's return to Ford Field? And will we see a bunch of points in a showdown between the Ravens and Cowboys?

 We're here to get you ready for the action. First, our NFL Nation reporters take you inside the locker room with the best thing they heard this week, and ESPN Research provides a key stat to know. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder makes a bold prediction for each matchup, NFL analyst Ben Solak gives one reason to tune in to each game (and rates the watchability of the matchup), fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel, and betting analyst Pam Maldonado hits betting insights for each contest. We also have the  Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and Maldonado, Moody and Walder each give us final score picks for every game.

 Let's get into the full Week 3 slate, which culminates with a "Monday Night Football" matchup between the Eagles and Bears on ESPN . (Game times are Sunday unless otherwise noted, and all odds are via DraftKings.)

 
 Jump to a matchup: 
 NE-JAX | LAC-BUF | SEA-WSH 
 HOU-IND | NYJ-DET | CIN-PIT 
 KC-MIA | TEN-NYG | CAR-CLE 
 ARI-SF | MIN-TB | BAL-DAL 
 LV-NO | LAR-DEN | PHI-CHI 

 Thursday: ATL 35, GB 14 

 
 

 What ESPN Analytics says ... 
 

 

 
 

 Patriots (1-1) at Jaguars (1-1) 
 1 p.m. ET | CBS | JAX -3 (45.5 O/U) 

 What we're hearing on the Patriots: Coach Mike Vrabel, who faced Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence twice a season during his final three years as Titans coach, said he has noticed a change in the QB. "He is just much more decisive and comfortable. I think you could always count on some turnovers, maybe three or four years ago. I don't think that is necessarily the case now," he said.  -- Mike Reiss 

 What we're hearing on the Jaguars: One of the biggest problems the Jaguars will face Sunday is Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez . Coach Liam Coen called him a "hell of a player" and lauded his physicality, aggressiveness and ball skills. "He's a problem," Coen said. "He gives everybody some fits. You've got to fight through contact with him. We're going to have to help the guys when we can with formations, motions and things like that, but we have to go win one-on-one battles, and at the catch point, we've got to be as strong as ever." -- Mike DiRocco 

 

 Stat to know: Jaguars WR Parker Washington has five straight games with 80-plus receiving yards, which is tied for the longest streak in franchise history. -- ESPN Research 

 Bold prediction:  Maye will record an 80-plus QBR. Yes, I know he has struggled. But I'm just not going to move that far off my prior -- that Maye was arguably the best QB in football last season -- after two games, especially playing in the same offensive scheme as before. This ship will right itself. -- Walder 

 Viewers rating (out of 10): 8.4. This is an important game between two 1-1 AFC contenders. The Jaguars just came off a game in which interior pressure ruined them; now they get to block DTs  Milton Williams and Christian Barmore . The Patriots are riddled with injuries --  Dre'Mont Jones , A.J. Brown , Mike Onwenu , Craig Woodson and more. -- Solak 

 Injuries: Patriots | Jaguars 

 Fantasy nugget: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson returned in Week 2 against Pittsburgh and led the backfield in snaps, routes run and carries, finishing with 13.6 fantasy points. He has five rushing touchdowns of at least 30 yards since the start of 2025, the most in the league.  Rhamondre Stevenson  will still have a role in the Patriots' backfield, but Henderson belongs in lineups. See Week 3 rankings . -- Moody 

 Betting insight: The Jaguars are 8-1 against the spread (ATS) at home under Coen, including 5-0 ATS as home favorites. Maye (who has taken six sacks and thrown four interceptions this season) faces a Jacksonville defense that has held opponents to 5-for-19 on third down. If New England keeps ending drives early, Lawrence should get enough chances to cover three points. Read more . -- Maldonado 

 Maldonado's pick: Jaguars 24, Patriots 20 
 Moody's pick: Jaguars 27, Patriots 20 
 Walder's pick: Patriots 30, Jaguars 27 
 FPI prediction: JAX, 57.5% (by an average of 2 points)

 

 Matchup must-reads: Why Patriots must be better at managing the clock before halftime ... Jaguars hope to get Hunter more involved in offense vs. Patriots 

 
 

 Chargers (0-2) at Bills (2-0) 
 1 p.m. ET | Fox | BUF -7 (50.5 O/U) 

 What we're hearing on the Chargers: The Chargers' usual platitude-laden QB, Justin Herbert , broke character this week after Los Angeles fell to 0-2. He cut off a reporter's second question about vocal leadership with a fierce response. "I'm going to stop you right there and say that it's very present," he said. "I don't think anyone is panicked or worried because that's not going to be the sentiment. It's moving on to the next play and understanding that we're close; we've made mistakes -- how do we fix it?" -- Kris Rhim 

 What we're hearing on the Bills: WR DJ Moore ( shoulder ) returned to practice in a limited capacity this week, and he and coach Joe Brady spoke optimistically about his chances of being available Sunday. Moore's contributions to the Bills' explosiveness are obvious. In Week 2, Buffalo averaged 8.9 yards per play before his injury and only 4.7 yards after he went out. But Brady cautions against correlating offensive aggressiveness directly to Moore's downfield talents: "The average depth of target is never important to me. It's about Josh [Allen ], if the opportunity is there, being able to take advantage of it. And when we have those, cashing in on them, right? A long incompletion doesn't do much either." -- Nick Suss 

 Stat to know: The Bills are the third team in NFL history to start 2-0 despite allowing 30 points in both games, joining the 2000 Rams and 1991 Bills. No team has ever started 3-0 and allowed 30 or more points in all three games. -- ESPN Research 

 Bold prediction: Herbert will record multiple interceptions. I'd have been pretty surprised two weeks ago if you told me Herbert would lead my model's Week 3 forecast for players more likely to throw two or more interceptions, but that's exactly the case. Because of how poorly the Chargers have played and the fact that they are solid underdogs to Buffalo (and therefore will likely have to pass frequently), Herbert has a 24% chance to throw at least two picks, according to the model. -- Walder 

 Viewers rating (out of 10): 5.4. Watching the Chargers has been extremely depressing so far. They had the potential to be such a cool team -- instead, there have been execution errors and penalties abound. I will turn their games back on only if they figure things out sometime later in the season. -- Solak 

 

 Injuries: Chargers | Bills 

 Fantasy nugget: The Bills continue to lean heavily on 12 personnel (one RB, two TEs, two WRs) and 13 personnel (one RB, three TEs, one WR), which has kept TE Dalton Kincaid on the field for more snaps and routes. He has three career games with at least 18 fantasy points, with two of them coming this season. This matchup also carries one of the highest totals on the slate. Kincaid belongs in lineups. See Week 3 rankings . -- Moody 

 Betting insight: The Chargers have the worst average cover margin in the NFL through two weeks (minus-19.5 PPG). Their offense has struggled to extend drives: Herbert has taken six sacks, and Los Angeles is 7-for-22 on third down. The L.A. defense -- which is allowing 263 passing yards per game -- now faces Allen. This provides a clear route to another double-digit Chargers loss. Read more . -- Maldonado 

 Maldonado's pick: Bills 31, Chargers 23 
 Moody's pick: Bills 31, Chargers 23 
 Walder's pick: Bills 28, Chargers 16 
 FPI prediction: BUF, 78.2% (by an average of 8.2 points)

 

 Matchup…

title: Mike LaFleur's coaching roots fast track to NFL
summary: The Shanahan-LaFleur dynamic spreads to Arizona, where new head coach Mike LaFleur has taken the reins in the desert.
full_text:
TEMPE, Arizona -- Mike LaFleur's career is about to come full circle on Sunday.

 Twelve years ago, as a 27-year-old, LaFleur's first NFL season was spent on the banks of Lake Erie as an offensive intern for the Cleveland Browns under the direction of a young, up-and-coming offensive coordinator named Kyle Shanahan.

 Until then, LaFleur had spent his coaching career at small colleges such Division III Elmhurst, Division II Saint Joseph's College and Division I FCS Davidson, watching his older brother, Matt, make the jump to the NFL in 2008 and engrain himself with a group of young, nascent coaches who would go on to become friends and a coaching "crew," as one of them described it, that currently holds six of the league's 32 head-coaching jobs.

 In Week 1, that "crew," which includes Rams head coach Sean McVay, Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh, Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley, Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur and Shanahan, the San Francisco 49ers head coach, watched as Mike LaFleur walked the sideline as a head coach for the first time, getting a win in his debut. And Sunday, they'll all have an eye on his first game as a head coach against his NFL sherpa, Shanahan, when the Cardinals visit the 49ers (4:05 p.m. ET, Fox). Mike LaFleur was Shanahan's pass game coordinator and wide receivers coach from 2017 to 2020.

 The sentimentality of the moment Sunday has lost its shine after LaFleur faced Shanahan six times during three seasons as the Rams' offensive coordinator, but this one will, eventually, mean something.

 "When you're in the moment, you're in the moment, you're not thinking about that stuff," LaFleur said. "I'm excited to see him before the game, obviously, say what's up, but then it's on and that's how they're going to feel and that's how we feel.

 "And I'm sure when all is said and done next February and we get to see each other in the offseason, we'll talk about it. But I mean, this is the Niners versus the Cardinals."

 In LaFleur, who followed Shanahan from Cleveland to the Atlanta Falcons and then to the 49ers -- seven straight seasons in all -- Shanahan saw someone who was "as good as any of those other guys" that Shanahan had on his staff.

 That's saying something coming from Shanahan.

 Seven of his former assistants, starting from his time as the Houston Texans' offensive coordinator in 2008 to his time as the 49ers head coach, have gone on to become NFL head coaches. And it's quite a group: McVay, Matt LaFleur, Saleh, Hafley, former Dolphins head coach and current Los Angeles Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans and now, Mike LaFleur.

 "I've had a couple of these guys and Mike's right there with all those dudes in terms of he's very smart, he knows the game," Shanahan said. "There's lots of coaches who can do some good stuff, but you always know guys in your building who see it a little bit better than most people, and Mike's one of those guys."

 

 

 MIKE'S THE BABY of the group of Shanahan disciples at 39 years old, and after he got hired, the love showered on him felt like big brothers bragging about their little sibling.

 "I think he's one of the real good guys in this league," Hafley said. "He's going to treat people the right way."

 "Mikey's going to be a successful head coach because of his ability to communicate with his players, communicate with everyone in the building," Saleh said. "He's got a clear vision, and he can articulate it the right way."

 They're spread out across divisions and conferences but still keep tabs on each other. Hackett and Matt LaFleur FaceTime regularly. Mike and Matt talk often. And they see each other throughout the season. 

 "It's a cool, close-knit circle in the National Football League where if you're fortunate enough to be here long enough, you can work with some really talented people," McDaniel said.

 And after LaFleur's Week 1 over the Chargers, the texts flooded in.

 "I was really happy for Mike," McVay said. "He's obviously one of my closest friends and I love Mike. He's meant a lot to me and my family, his family has. I thought it was an awesome day for the Cardinals. I thought they looked really good in all three phases. I got a chance to watch that whole game.

 "It's unique because they're in the division, but it overrides because it's like family. Being able to see mom and dad and how nervous they were in the stands. ... Mom was excited to see it, even when they were in four-minute mode and had control when they showed them on the TV, and seeing Lauren and the kids. It was cool. They looked awesome."

 Hackett couldn't help but smile thinking about everyone attached to each other becoming a head coach at some point in their careers, him included in 2022 with the Denver Broncos for a season.

 "It's awesome," Hackett said. "I mean, all of us. I'm so happy for anybody that gets that opportunity. I mean, the reality of it is you never know what's going to happen."

 Yet, his friends recognize why LaFleur has a shot to be a success. "I think the biggest thing for Mike," said Ryans, who was on the 49ers' staff with LaFleur from 2017 to 2020, "is him being able to learn under Kyle for however many years he was there."

 

 

 ON THE DAY LaFleur was introduced as the Cardinals' head coach, Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn, who hired LaFleur in Atlanta in 2015, sent him a quick text. He followed up with a call later that night to tell LaFleur how "pumped I am for him" and that he'd be there for LaFleur to bounce ideas off or if something comes across his desk that he didn't know how to handle or wasn't prepared for as a first-time head coach.

 Then, about six weeks later, at the NFL's annual meetings in Phoenix, Quinn got to tell LaFleur in person how proud he was of his latest protégé becoming a head coach. In 2015, when Quinn was hired as the Atlanta Falcons' head coach, he built a staff that included LaFleur as an offensive assistant, his brother as quarterbacks coach, Shanahan as offensive coordinator and McDaniel as another offensive assistant.

 All four have gone on to be head coaches. "I would say I hope during the time that we were together, there's something that was significant in their development to be where they're at and be authentic in that way," Quinn told ESPN. "And I'm hopeful that I showed that and demonstrated that in some way to them and that they're able to hit into that same space.

 "But, man, I'm incredibly proud of them."

 Commanders reporter John Keim, Dolphins reporter Marcel Louis-Jaques, 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner, Titans reporter Turron Davenport, Rams reporter Sarah Barshop and Chargers reporter Kris Rhim contributed to this report.
