title: NFL Week 3 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines
summary: Touchdowns for Kenneth Walker III and Xavier Worthy? The Broncos pulling an upset of the Rams? Fantasy value for C.J. Stroud? And a big day from Geno Smith?
full_text:
Week 3 of the  2026 NFL season is underway after the Falcons beat the Packers on Thursday night . But what will happen in the remaining 15 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

 First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody gives three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

 Could the Broncos upset the Rams? Will the Chiefs' Kenneth Walker III and Xavier Worthy score against the Dolphins? Is Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud a fantasy sleeper against the Colts? And could the most entertaining game of the week be ... Raiders-Saints? Let's make 15 big predictions for all of Sunday and Monday's action.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Upset picks | Projected stat lines 
 Fantasy sleepers, surprises 
 TD scorers | Other predictions 

 
 

 Maldonado predicts two upsets 
 

 Denver Broncos +2.5 (+114) vs. Los Angeles Rams 

 Denver has the defensive formula to win this. With wide receiver  Puka Nacua likely sidelined ( groin ), Broncos cornerback  Pat Surtain II  can focus on Davante Adams . Meanwhile, Denver's pass rush can attack a vulnerable Rams offensive line. That pressure could keep Matthew Stafford from finding the rhythm he showed against the Giants .

 On the other side of the ball, Broncos quarterback  Bo Nix can use quick throws to find wide receiver  Jaylen Waddle and avoid long third downs.

 
 

 

 Dallas Cowboys +3.5 (+135) vs. Baltimore Ravens 

 The Cowboys' path is to make Baltimore play from behind in Rio de Janeiro. That shouldn't be hard since the sharpness of QB  Dak Prescott and Dallas' passing game gives the team a real chance to score early, putting more pressure on Lamar Jackson and a Ravens offensive line that struggled against New Orleans. The Cowboys' biggest concern is holding up against the Ravens' rushing attack.

 

 

 Walder predicts three stat lines 
 

 Abdul Carter , Edge, New York Giants : 2.0 sacks, 6 pressures, 27% pass rush win rate

 Carter's rookie season was noteworthy because, despite just 4.0 sacks, he finished top-10 in pass rush win rate at edge. That was a strong sign about the player he could become, and that signal has persisted in Year 2.

 Carter ranks 11th in pass rush win rate at edge and is tied for the fifth-most pass rush wins among all players. In Week 3 , Carter gets the chance to run after second-year quarterback  Cam Ward , whose 8.8% sack rate since the start of last season ranks third worst among qualifying quarterbacks.

 
 

 Xavier Worthy , WR, Kansas City Chiefs : 5 targets, 3 receptions, 64 yards, 1 touchdown

 Worthy's production has been lackluster to start the season, but that could easily turn around  against the Dolphins . For starters, Worthy is a candidate for some positive regression. He has converted only 11% of all air yards into completed air yards, which is an incredibly low rate. And while Worthy isn't strictly a run-straight-downfield receiver, he does run go routes or deep fades at an above-average rate.

 The Dolphins have played more single-high coverage than every team but the Browns. That should give Patrick Mahomes a chance to connect with Worthy on at least one outside vertical route.

 
 

 

 Jihaad Campbell , LB, Philadelphia Eagles : 13 tackles, 2 tackles for loss

 Campbell is close to an every-play role in Philadelphia's defense, and his numbers against the run have been strong. He's in the 94th percentile in run stop win rate and third best in NFL Next Gen Stats' defensive stop rate (a similarly-named but different statistic).

 With Bears quarterback  Caleb Williams  out of this game ( hamstring ), Chicago could be even more run-heavy than usual. And that ought to present a ton of tackling opportunities for Campbell.

 

 

 Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers 
 

 Dontayvion Wicks , WR, Philadelphia Eagles (rostered in 37.5% of ESPN leagues) 

 Wicks has emerged as Philadelphia's No. 2 receiver with at least four targets and 12 fantasy points in back-to-back games. He caught 5 of 6 targets for 74 yards in Tennessee  last week, and he could see even more opportunities against Chicago since TE  Dallas Goedert is out with an MCL sprain . The Bears have allowed the ninth-most passing yards per game this season.

 
 

 C.J. Stroud , QB, Houston Texans (33.8%) 

 Stroud has scored at least 16 fantasy points in each of the first two weeks of the season, as he's surrounded by  Nico Collins , Dalton Schultz and David Montgomery . This week -- even without Collins (hamstring) -- Stroud has a favorable matchup against a Colts defense that has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks. Managers dealing with injuries to Jaxson Dart or Jayden Daniels shouldn't overlook Stroud as a streamer.

 
 

 Adonai Mitchell , WR, New York Jets (28.4%) 

 Mitchell's role took a big step forward in Week 2, when he drew a team-high 12 targets while playing 82% of the snaps. He has clearly become a major part of the passing game behind Garrett Wilson and has the speed to create big plays. The Lions are tied with the Texans for the most fantasy points allowed per game to wide receivers, and their depleted secondary makes Mitchell an intriguing sleeper.

 

 
 

 Bowen predicts three touchdown scorers 
 

 Cam Skattebo , RB, New York Giants 

 Skattebo has seen at least 16 touches a game this season, so we know the volume will be there versus Tennessee on Sunday. Plus, he had two carries inside the 5-yard line in the Giants' Week 1 win over the Cowboys, scoring on a 3-yard run. The Titans' defense has allowed three rushing scores this season.

 
 

 Kenneth Walker III , RB, Kansas City Chiefs 

 Walker scored twice in the Chiefs' Week 1 win over the Broncos (one rushing, one receiving), plus he's averaging 23.5 carries and 4.5 receptions per game. Those are big numbers for someone who was part of a committee approach in Seattle. Let's take Walker to score Sunday versus a Dolphins defense that has already surrendered eight touchdowns.

 
 

 Jalen Coker , WR, Carolina Panthers 

 Coker has quickly emerged in Carolina's offense, catching 16 of 18 targets for 204 yards so far -- including two touchdowns in Week 1 against the Bears. The Panthers also like to get Coker the ball in scoring position. He already has targets on red zone throws from quarterback Bryce Young , and I expect more on Sunday in Cleveland .

 

 

 Solak makes four more predictions 
 

 Ravens WR Zay Flowers  will go for another 150 yards 

 The Ravens get the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro  this week . While I can't speak for the field conditions at Maracanã Stadium, I can speak to a Cowboys secondary woefully lacking in speed and man coverage ability. Flowers is the clear focal point of the Ravens' passing attack, and he should get plenty of free access targets Sunday. He got 150 yards in the first half of Week 1 before injuring his hamstring , which caused him to miss Week 2. Can Flowers knock on the door of 200 in Week 3?

 
 

 

 Jets QB Geno Smith  will throw three TD passes 

 He has only one through two games, as the Jets have largely been a run-heavy team and happy to play for field goals. Against the Lions' defense in a dome? I think we'll see a vintage Geno game. Plus, the Jets will likely spread the field out a little more given the absence of TE Mason Taylor  (thumb) and the weak spots at the Lions CBs.

 
 

 Raiders-Saints will be the game of the week 

 There are a couple of good contenders in Patriots-Jaguars and Rams-Broncos . But I want to see the Saints put together a complete game on offense, and they face a stiff Raiders defense that has impressed with speed and pressure from their front seven. Quarterback  Kirk Cousins has made it work without tight end  Brock Bowers so far, but the Saints should present the toughest defense…

title: NFL Week 3 uniforms: Colts to wear 'Anvil Strike,' Bills debut 'Nickel City'
summary: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 3, led by the new NFL Rivalries look from the Indianapolis Colts.
full_text:
Tuesday marked the first day of fall. The blue skies across the country will turn to gray with the colder months approaching. But to spot a more immediate gray shade, look no further than NFL uniforms in Week 3 -- namely, the Indianapolis Colts and Buffalo Bills . 

 

 Indianapolis will debut its Rivalries uniform against the Houston Texans . Nicknamed "Anvil Strike," they are inspired by the steel of an anvil and the jersey's "dark anthracite" color is one that "embodies the grit and intensity of Colts football." The all-gray threads are complete with a metallic blue helmet. For the first time in team history, the Colts' horseshoe is included on one of their uniforms -- a silver version appears on the sleeve. Other uniform elements are classic blue numbers and "For The Shoe" on the inside collar. The Colts are the first team to debut the latest batch of Rivalries uniforms this season. 

 Buffalo is similarly wearing all-gray when it faces the Los Angeles Chargers at home. The "Nickel City" uniforms are a tribute to the "strength, grit and authenticity" of Western New York. The all-gray design is directly inspired by the Buffalo Nickel , a coin minted from 1913 to 1938. A metallic royal blue "charge" helmet tops the look. The helmet's design is meant to bring a charging buffalo to life with the horn, eye and charge streak displayed in red. 

 The Denver Broncos will wear their midnight navy alternate look on "Sunday Night Football" against the Los Angeles Rams . Denver first introduced the look ahead of the 2024 season and is 2-0 in the all-navy combination . Last year, the Broncos paired their summit white helmet with the threads, but they'll go with a navy-colored lid this time around.

 In the throwback space, the Jacksonville Jaguars are rocking their classic prowler design . First unveiled in 2024, the teal uniforms include a prowling jaguar on the sleeves and a black helmet with the franchises' original primary logo on it. The numbers boast a custom font in white with a black and gold trim. A similar three-color accent runs down the white pants in a teal stripe with gold and black trim.

title: Predicting the next five Super Bowl champions
summary: Ben Solak had some fun and did the impossible -- picked Super Bowl winners for the 2026 to 2030 seasons. And there are some surprises ...
full_text:
ESPN will televise the Super Bowl for the first time in February 2027. We will count down to the big game with Super Bowl-centric stories every month. 

 Super Bowl winners are, by definition, improbable. It's not just the 1-out-of-32 math. It is mostly due to the fact that the NFL plays a best-of-one playoff series -- no best-of-five or best-of-seven series to save a good team that has a bad game or unlucky break. It's also the fact that injury attrition eliminates multiple playoff teams before the ball is ever snapped. It is so, so hard to win a Super Bowl.

 It's even harder to predict who will win a Super Bowl -- let alone the next five. (Why does nobody ever write about how much tougher my job is than an NFL head coach's?) We're two weeks into the 2026 season , and I have no idea who will win the Super Bowl in February. But I gave my best mid-September bet. Then, I went to next year (which is still kind of reasonable). And then I predicted the year after that (which was totally wacky). And then I did two more just because.

 To build this list, I tried not to be too scientific. A rigorous look at elite quarterbacks, elite coaches and a pedigree of winning would have given us ... the Chiefs, Rams and Seahawks in every Super Bowl down the way. I was reminded of Seth Walder's lovely FPI preseason simulation piece, in which he selects just one simulation from the set of thousands run during the preseason to determine team strength. It's a reminder that predicting an exact outcome -- not the likeliest outcome, but one exact outcome -- should carry with it some challenges to credulity. So ( spoiler alert ), if Ravens fans and Bills fans are upset that they are not included below, just know this: Browns fans and Dolphins fans also have the right to be upset.

 

 Remember to take these predictions as seriously as possible. Aggregate them with the headline "ESPN NFL analyst predicts [insert team] to win a Super Bowl within five seasons!" A lot of people will click. And more importantly, absolutely nobody will angrily DM me on social media.

 Jump to a season: 
 2026  |  2027  | 2028  | 2029  | 2030 

 

 

 2026 season: Seattle Seahawks 
 It's a little weird to pick a Super Bowl champion for the current season when we have only a two-game sample. It would be easier with no games (here are my preseason vibes) or something like eight games (OK, these guys are definitely good).

 I usually don't pick repeats -- it's so hard to get back to the dance after a long season the year before -- but it's difficult to argue any team has been better than Seattle through this short season. Quarterback  Sam Darnold  ( hip ) went down in the first quarter against the Patriots in Week 1 , and Mike Macdonald's group is still 2-0.

 

 What stands out about Macdonald's Seahawks -- and what makes them feel so repeatable -- is how the defense hasn't missed a beat despite offseason departures. We usually feel the brain drain (and long-season exhaustion) of a Super Bowl champion early in the ensuing season -- that is not so in Seattle. The entire defensive coaching staff remained and has easily accounted for the departures of safety  Coby Bryant , cornerback  Riq Woolen and edge rusher  Boye Mafe .

 The work of new offensive coordinator Brian Fleury with backup quarterback Drew Lock  has been impressive; Lock was ripping throws over the middle with timing and accuracy. Getting good play out of a QB2 is not the same skill set as getting good play out of a QB1, but all of the signs I've seen from Seattle thus far are that Fleury can keep up Klint Kubiak's momentum. The improvements in the running game -- even before Zach Charbonnet returns from injured reserve -- are noticeable, too.

 If the Seahawks repeat ... are they a dynasty? Probably not. Dynasties are made over a decade of dominance, not consecutive championships. Darnold would become the ninth quarterback to win consecutive Super Bowls, and with only one year left on his deal, he would likely demand -- and get -- a market-rate contract at the level of Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen . What are the Seahawks going to do,  not give it him?

 

 What I think happens: Seattle loses the NFC West title to the Rams by tiebreaker rules ... only to beat the Rams in an NFC Championship rematch as the fifth seed. That game ends 22-21 on a successful Seahawks two-point conversion at the end of regulation (no fumble hijinks this time).   Seattle goes on to face the Texans (yes, the currently 0-2 Texans) in one of the lowest-scoring Super Bowls of the 2000s -- not quite the 13-3 Patriots-Rams score from 2019 but close. The Seahawks win 16-10 at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles. Cornerback  Devon Witherspoon wins MVP (as he should have last season) with a stuffed stat sheet: seven tackles, three TFLs, one sack and one interception.

 
 

 2027 season: Cincinnati Bengals 
 It's actually quite rare to see a quarterback make a Super Bowl and then make his next one six years later. John Elway is perhaps the best example, though he made three close together (1986, 1987, 1989) and then another two after a long hiatus (1997,1998). Elway and Joe Burrow would be the only two to do it with the same franchise. Craig Morton did it back in the 1970s with two teams -- as a Cowboy in 1970 and a Bronco in 1977 -- and Kurt Warner did it with the Rams in 2002 and the Cardinals in 2009.

 But I think Burrow can do it by sticking with the Bengals, who have endured injury-ruined years and defensive decay ever since reaching the Super Bowl in 2021 . Their huge 2026 offseason bet on Dexter Lawrence II (and other defensive improvements aside) serves as proof of their desperation to get back before the current regime of coach Zac Taylor, de facto GM Duke Tobin and Burrow undergoes a major shake-up.

 

 The Bengals have a great shot at representing the AFC in 2026 because of their stars at premium positions: quarterback (Burrow), wide receiver ( Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins ), cornerback ( DJ Turner II ) and offensive tackle ( Amarius Mims ). Their lack of a true star edge rusher is mitigated by the presence of Lawrence, who through two games has been exactly the force multiplier they hoped on the interior.

 I am, however, concerned about the youth on the team in a 2026 playoff run. A lot of those key defensive players haven't taken serious playoff snaps. Demetrius Knight Jr. , Barrett Carter ,  Dax Hill , Turner -- even Lawrence himself has only two games of postseason action. For as clutch as Burrow is, and how dangerous that offense is, it's easy to forget that the defense powered the Bengals' AFC playoff run in 2021 -- holding Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs to three points in the second half of the AFC Championship Game, intercepting Ryan Tannehill with 20 seconds left in the divisional round and holding on fourth-and-goal against the Raiders in the wild-card round.

 

 What I think happens: The Bengals will use a deep 2026 playoff run that falls just short to propel themselves over the hump in 2027. In free agency, the team retains both Turner and Hill (somehow, don't ask me) to keep the secondary in a strong spot. Cincinnati also swings a bold trade for offensive tackle  Laremy Tunsil as the Commanders rebuild, banking that he has one last great year in him -- and he does. The Super Bowl victory comes a year later than they hoped, but the Bengals get revenge on the Rams -- in what ends up as Matthew Stafford 's final season -- with a 31-30 last-second win at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta.

 
 

 2028 season: Tampa Bay Buccaneers 
 Projecting 2026 and 2027 at least has some sort of tether in our current reality, but 2028 is where things slide quickly into dreamland. Consider projecting the Seahawks to win the Super Bowl two years ago. Pete Carroll was still the head coach,  Geno Smith was the quarterback, and  Jaxon Smith-Njigba was the No. 3 receiver. The NFL can change so fast over a two-year window.

 So who do I pick? The Browns? The Dolphins?…

title: The unshakable bond between Aaron Glenn and Dan Campbell
summary: Aaron Glenn and Dan Campbell grew up playing and then coaching in the NFL. When Campbell made Glenn his DC, their bond was sealed.
full_text:
The 2005 Dallas Cowboys were an incubator for future NFL head coaches, with six assistants from Bill Parcells' staff and two players from his roster ascending to the highest level of the football coaching profession.

 The future coaches included an intense, long-in-the-tooth cornerback who played bigger than his 5-foot-9 frame and a hulking tight end who was biting kneecaps long before he spoke it into the NFL lexicon.

 "He was the guy that Bill Parcells used to use to piss somebody off, and there were a number of fights in practice because of him," Aaron Glenn, the corner, said of Dan Campbell, the tight end.

 Campbell and Glenn formed a strong bond that season together. They went from teammates in Dallas to assistant coaches with the New Orleans Saints to head coach-defensive coordinator with the Detroit Lions , enduring tough times and moments of sheer joy.

 Their relationship was built on a promise by Campbell, who vowed to Glenn that he'd be his defensive coordinator if he ever became a head coach. Campbell did so in 2021 when he took over in Detroit, where the two developed an even closer bond, and doubled down in their first year together, standing by his guy in the 2022 season when it would have been easy to fire him after a rough start.

 "One of the greatest days of my life was him getting the [ New York Jets ] job, and one of the worst days of my life was him getting that job because you know you're losing a little piece of you," Campbell said Friday. "That's what he meant to me and to us. So, that's hard."

 On Sunday, they will face each other for the first time as head coaches (both sitting at 1-1), with Glenn bringing the Jets to Ford Field -- his home from 2021 to 2024. And nearly 500 miles away, at his house in Saratoga Springs, New York, the legendary Parcells will watch with pride.

 "I always told them all that [coaching] is not for well-adjusted people, so I don't know why they would pick that profession," Parcells said with a hint of sarcasm, alluding to Campbell, Glenn and his many protégés. "But they're football guys. They love it. That's their game."

 

 

 No change for the better 

 Campbell knew changes needed to be made in 2022 when the Lions were off to a 1-6 start.

 Coming off a 32-27 loss to the Miami Dolphins , Detroit scored on all five of its first-half possessions and entered halftime with a comfortable 10-point lead. But Glenn's defense squandered it, leading to a fifth consecutive loss.

 To that point, Glenn's unit was allowing a league-high 32.1 points per game, causing him to face heavy criticism, including calls for the first-time defensive coordinator to be fired.

 But Campbell maintained faith in Glenn. And the defense gradually improved, which was instrumental in Detroit winning eight of its final 10 games where it allowed just 20.2 points per game throughout that stretch and narrowly missed the playoffs.

 "[It] helps when you have somebody that you have a tremendous amount of trust for," Campbell said Friday. "You've been through a lot with them as a player and as a coach, you know what they're made of, and he's really -- he looks different than me. I'm taller, I'm whatever. He's quicker. All these different things, man, but we're really the same. I mean we're so much the same. And he's the defensive version, I'm the offensive version. And so, he was my right-hand man."

 Detroit would make some major changes, including firing defensive backs coach Aubrey Pleasant, but Glenn remained. Campbell credits Glenn for being a huge part of rebuilding the Lions' organization to what it is today after spending hours together planning and strategizing on ways they could improve. Glenn helped set the foundation for the Lions' current streak of four consecutive winning seasons (a first in over 50 years), including a franchise-best 15 wins in 2024.

 "Our players know exactly what's coming in here [on Sunday] because the defensive coordinator was here for five years," Campbell said. "... This is going to be a knockout, 60-minute brawl."

 

 

 This looks familiar 

 It's déjà vu in Detroit two weeks into the 2026 season. After a 1-1 start during which Detroit's defense allowed 71 points and gave up 915 total yards, Campbell recalled those tough early moments with Glenn.

 This time, Campbell is hearing some of those same concerns aimed at current defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard, whom Campbell continues to vouch for -- just like he did for Glenn in 2022.

 "I never second-guessed [Glenn]. And even during that period when we were going through it, we came into that year '22 with 'All right, this is what'll be best for our front. We're going to become more attack style and shoot gaps.' And even though that's something we didn't believe in necessarily ... we felt it was the right thing with what we had at the time and it proved to not be," Campbell recalled. "And all right, man, we get through basically the bye week, we start to shift and get back to what we do a little bit of.

 "I think that's important, to be able to identify, 'All right, let's make this correction. Let's try this. Let's tighten this up. Let's go back to this.' That's a sign of a good coach. And [Sheppard has] got that too, but that's why AG just, he checked all those boxes, and you've got to look through all the other stuff and really look at the substance behind it."

 Former No. 2 pick Aidan Hutchinson was a rookie on the 2022 team in Detroit that got off to a slow start. He still remembers how the defense was able to turn things around.

 "AG is such a leader of men for sure," Hutchinson said Wednesday, "and I think we all always trusted him to figure that out and I think the same as with Shepp ... he's cut from the same cloth.

 "Different coaching styles a little bit, but I think, yeah, that's the intention right now is all hands on deck."

 

 

 'That friendship will always last' 

 As assistants on Sean Payton's staff with the New Orleans Saints from 2016 to 2020, Campbell and Glenn spent hours talking defense. Looking back, Glenn suspects that maybe those long talks were informal job interviews.

 Glenn said it was an honor to serve as defensive coordinator, adding, "I was the first guy he hired and it took -- I don't know -- maybe a week before we hired anybody else, and we just sat in my office, and we talked football, and how we were going to change this program around. Those things will always stick with me because the things that we talked about, we actually did, and Detroit actually ended up being exactly where they are now."

 Since taking over the Jets last year, Glenn has made references to Campbell, and how his former boss gave him occasional head coaching responsibilities -- i.e. creating the Lions' practice scripts and allowing him to address the entire team, not just the defense. Glenn believes those learning moments helped prepare him for his current position.

 "That friendship," Glenn said, "will always last."

 Naturally, Glenn's goal is to create a Detroit-like turnaround, which took considerable patience by Lions ownership. Under Campbell, the Lions started 4-19-1 before that midseason flip in 2022.

 In New York, Glenn's record is 4-15, triggering intense criticism. The slow start hasn't dented his confidence. After all, he lived it in Detroit, where his defensive schemes combined with Campbell's leadership and motivational fury to change the perception of the franchise.

 "They just fed off each other," said Jets wide receiver Tim Patrick , who played for the Lions in 2024. "Dan was the vocal part about it, but AG's energy carried the same thing Dan was speaking and they were just one."

 The best example of the synergy, Patrick said, was their pep talks before a Week 14 (Thursday night) game against the Green Bay Packers . In a now-celebrated speech, a fiery Campbell vowed to be aggressive with his playcalling and challenged the offense to compensate for an injury-riddled defense. Chiming in, Glenn…

title: 'Growing pains': What's going on with the Chargers' offense?
summary: Is the Chargers' offense too complicated for the team? What's going wrong with McDaniels' scheme in L.A.
full_text:
LOS ANGELES -- Quarterback  Justin Herbert furiously slammed his hands on the SoFi Stadium turf. He yelled as he stood up. Yelled as he began walking. Turned around and yelled some more. In the background, wide receiver  Tre' Harris  lay with his head buried in the turf.

 Just a moment before, the Chargers failed to convert on third down in the third quarter of their Week 2 loss to the Raiders, with the play failing basically before it even started. Harris came in motion as the play clock wound down on third-and-inches with Herbert in the shotgun, but as center Jake Slaughter snapped the ball, it hit Harris in the leg.

 Herbert jumped on the ball, and what followed was as intense of an outburst as he has had during a game in his seven-year career.

 

 The moment was a microcosm for the Chargers' 2026 season through two weeks: an offense seemingly too complicated for this team and a quarterback who appears as frustrated as he ever has been in a season that's trending toward being another year where success remains a hypothetical. The offense will look to bounce back this Sunday against the Buffalo Bills ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ).

 "Growing pains," coach Jim Harbaugh said. "Yeah, we got some growing pains."

 "We're not standing on business in the least," offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said.

 McDaniel was the proverbial crown jewel of the Chargers' offseason.

 After two seasons of middling offensive play, Harbaugh fired  Greg Roman, the only offensive coordinator he had worked with in two stints in the NFL, following the Chargers'  16-3 wild-card round loss to the  New England Patriots .

 Fired in January  after four seasons as the coach of the  Miami Dolphins , McDaniel was still widely considered the top candidate available after the season. He's one of the most respected offensive minds in the NFL and chose to join the Chargers for the chance to work with Herbert and learn from Harbaugh.

 

 General manager Joe Hortiz spent the offseason retooling the team's offense to suit McDaniel's vision, which needed a different type of player for his wide zone scheme.

 McDaniel put up "wanted" posters for players he deemed essential, running back Keaton Mitchell and fullback Alec Ingold among them; Hortiz signed both. He added right guard Cole Strange , who worked with McDaniel when he coached the Dolphins, and drafted speedy wide receiver Brenen Thompson , partly at McDaniel's request.

 Players and coaches were equally excited about the offense's potential in the offseason. McDaniel promised "career highs across the board" for all the wide receivers.

 Instead, the Chargers had six fumbles versus the Raiders. Offensive tackle  Joe Alt  had three false starts. And Herbert didn't complete a pass of 20 air yards.

 "I think I can just plain and simply say that it's below our expectations," McDaniel said. "I know it's below a lot of people's expectations as well."

 Amid the struggles, McDaniel said that Herbert has blamed himself, which McDaniel doesn't believe is fair. He said the two of them have begun meeting more frequently and grown closer than they've ever been over the past two weeks.

 "It can be a lonely world as a starting quarterback," he said "... It can be lonely as a playcaller or an offensive coordinator. And the only way to approach it is that you're not alone."

 In the locker room after the loss to the Raiders, there was a mix of confusion and frustration. One team source told ESPN that the offense's poor execution doesn't make any sense because of how they practiced all summer. "We're making OTA mistakes," he said.

 

 Herbert's outburst on the third down was a reflection of the poor execution. If the play had continued without the fumble, an open running lane was forming on the left side of the line of scrimmage for  Omarion Hampton  to run through with Harris as a lead blocker. Mistakes caused the play to fail.

 And yet that poses a different question: Why was the playcall so complex in the first place? It was third-and-inches. The quarterback is 6-foot-6; the running back is a 220-pound, former first-round pick. It would seem that a sneak or under-center run would have done the trick.

 The complexity -- or the overcomplication even -- of this offense appears to be stumping the Chargers two weeks in. But Herbert rejected that theory.

 "I think every NFL offense is a complicated one," he said. "But I think it's just on us to be studying our stuff, making sure that we're ready to go."

 McDaniel said he has considered simplifying things as he gets to learn the players but is wary of overcorrecting.

 "Of course I consider [it]. I consider pretty much everything," he said. " What's important for my position is that if I'm saying not to overreact either way, good or bad.

 "What I know how to do is evolve. And so I think it's kind of lazy to just say, 'OK, there's the result. Not good. Let's do the opposite.' That's not why I'm here. That being said, you don't just point a finger and say, 'Well, it worked before.' So I think all of that is being taken under consideration."

 Nevertheless, the Chargers' offense has never looked this disjointed in the Harbaugh era.

 When comparing L.A.'s opening two games in the past two seasons under Roman with McDaniel's first two games, Roman's offense had far better numbers across the board, most notably a 75.82 offensive efficiency for Weeks 1 and 2 in 2025 (10th highest in the NFL) versus McDaniel's 17.97 offensive efficiency in 2026 (29th).

 Roman's scheme was simpler than McDaniel's, an approach Roman was criticized for. McDaniel uses pre-snap motion (74.1%) far more than Roman did last season (59.2%).

 Still, it has been an uncharacteristically bad start from a McDaniel offense, too.

 The Chargers' five turnovers are the most by a McDaniel offense through its first two games. Los Angeles' seven fumbles are its most through the first two games since at least 2000 and the most by a McDaniel offense.

 "We know we got to get better at a lot of different things and got to get better quick," Harris said.

 Even with the discouraging stats, the Chargers believe there are no fundamental issues with McDaniel's scheme. When they watch the film, they grow frustrated with the mistakes they are making that they say they don't see in practice. They'll get a chance to prove themselves this Sunday.

 "There are a lot of plays that we left out there," Herbert said. "I think it's promising to see all the plays that we could have made and how close we are."

title: LaDainian Tomlinson inducted into ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame
summary: LaDainian Tomlinson, author of the single greatest season in fantasy football history, is Week 3's inductee into the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame
full_text:
Fantasy football is all about fun, competition and camaraderie, but it's also another way to appreciate the best of the best in the NFL. For more than three decades, ESPN Fantasy has been here with you, celebrating peak performers and magical moments.

 Presenting the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame   , which honors the best players and acknowledges the most memorable moments since the advent of our game in 1995, the first year fantasy football was available on ESPN.com.

 Take me to the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame 

 Class of 2026 Week 3 Inductee: LaDainian Tomlinson 
 3,451.32 fantasy points 
 13,684 rushing yards, 624 receptions, 4,772 receiving yards, 162 total TDs 

 Tomlinson was one of the most dynamic, versatile running backs of all time, and a thoroughly dominating force in fantasy football. His 3,451.32 fantasy points are the most among running backs during the ESPN fantasy era, and third-most in NFL history. Tomlinson's 2006 MVP campaign was the greatest in fantasy history, his 481.1 points scored and 31 total touchdowns setting single-season records, with an astonishing 28 of those touchdowns being scored across a 10-week span. He was a top-five overall fantasy scorer every year from 2002-07; only five other post-merger players have six or more such total seasons in their careers.

 

 

 Tomlinson will be inducted Sunday during " Fantasy Focus Countdown " (10 a.m. ET on ESPN2). Tune in each week through Week 16 as we reveal all 18 members of the inaugural class of the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame.

title: How has Nakobe Dean reshaped the Raiders' defense?
summary: Nakobe Dean has stepped up in a big way to lead the Raiders' defense through two weeks.
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev. --  Nakobe Dean 's impact on the Las Vegas Raiders ' defense could be summarized by one play in the Week 2 win over the Los Angeles Chargers .

 The Raiders led 17-14 in the fourth quarter and needed to stop the Chargers from converting on third-and-2 from the 28-yard line. Quarterback Justin Herbert handed the ball off to second-year running back Omarion Hampton , hoping he could convert the short-yardage situation. Dean had a different plan.

 Dean maneuvered from the B-gap to the A-gap and met Hampton face-to-face before tackling him for no gain, forcing the Chargers to punt.

 

 Dean's performances through his first two weeks with the Raiders have been filled with clutch moments. He has made plays all over the field, racking up 15 tackles, 1.5 sacks, four pressures and a pair of forced fumbles.

 Over the offseason, the Raiders signed Dean to a three-year, $36 million deal. So far, it was money well spent.

 "He's been the glue to our defense," safety Jeremy Chinn told ESPN. "It's crazy how much a linebacker in the middle of the field can make such a difference in the back end and front end."

 Dean came to Las Vegas after four injury-riddled seasons with the  Philadelphia Eagles , who selected him in the third round of the 2022 draft. Dean played in at least 15 games only twice with the Eagles. But when he was on the field, Dean was effective. He compiled 226 tackles, 7.5 sacks, three forced fumbles and 19 tackles for loss in 47 games (27 starts).

 Las Vegas might have to give credit to Dean's intuition for landing one of the top off-ball linebackers in free agency. After the 2025 season, Dean had a competitive offer from the Dallas Cowboys  along with the Raiders.

 However, Dean thought about and prayed on both offers and ultimately, he couldn't go against his gut, which told him Las Vegas was the right fit.

 Dean and fellow teammate Quay Walker have reshaped the Raiders' inside linebacker room. Last year, Las Vegas filled the room with veterans who were past their prime and signed to one-year deals. The production was inconsistent.

 The Raiders took a new approach with Dean and Walker, both of whom are in the prime of their respective careers. And even though defensive coordinator Rob Leonard has had a strong start as a playcaller, Dean and Walker have been vital for the unit's ability to operate efficiently.

 

 Dean, in particular, has added much-needed support in the passing game. In six pass-rush snaps, Dean recorded a pressure rate of 66.7% and three quarterback hits. He recorded three pressures against the Chargers.

 As a whole, the Raiders have a league-leading sack total (eight) while ranked fifth in pressures (41) and first in pressure rate (50%). Of course, edge rusher Maxx Crosby has played a major role, but Dean has been much-needed support. Similar to Walker, Dean can line up in multiple spots up front. He has played 71 defensive snaps at inside linebacker, 12 at defensive tackle and 16 at outside linebacker.

 "You have guys that can consistently win one-on-one [matchups] or be able to disguise. It's huge for a defense," defensive tackle Thomas Booker IV told ESPN. "When you got guys getting home from blitzes and pressures, it makes everybody else's job easier. So it's great to have those two guys behind us."

 Dean has been just as impactful in stopping the run. He has collected 11 run tackles and two run stuffs. Dean has played in 120 defensive snaps (97%), and the Raiders have allowed 3.7 rushing yards per attempt when he is on the field. However, they have given up 11 yards per carry whenever he is on the sidelines.

 Las Vegas is 15th in rushing yards per game (100.5), 17th in rushing yards per game (four), but first in defensive rush total EPA (17.71).

 

 Dean's leadership has been invaluable. He is responsible for lining his teammates up and making sure everyone is on the same page. Dean's most important trait is his winning pedigree, which is why the Raiders were attracted to him in free agency.

 Dean won a national title during his final season in college at Georgia in 2021. His best season in Philadelphia was 2024, when he and the Eagles ultimately won a Super Bowl over the Kansas City Chiefs .

 His winning mentality has been essential to the Raiders' first 2-0 start since 2021. Another defining moment in the Raiders' matchup against the Chargers came late in the fourth quarter when Dean punched the ball out of Hampton's arm, resulting in a recovery from Chinn to help them secure the win.

 "He's a dog," Crosby said. "...You could rely on him in the biggest moments, and he's been playing his ass off."

title: What to expect from the much-anticipated Giants-Daboll reunion
summary: All eyes will be on former Giants coach Brian Daboll, who returns to New York as the Titans' offensive coordinator.
full_text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- There will be a lot of familiar faces in new places when the Tennessee Titans and New York Giants face off at MetLife Stadium on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, CBS).

 All eyes will be on former Giants head coach Brian Daboll, who returns to New York as the Titans' offensive coordinator. Former Giants assistant coaches Shea Tierney and Carmen Bricillo, along with players Wan'Dale Robinson , Austin Schlottmann , Daniel Bellinger and Cor'Dale Flott , will also make the return to their former team's field. Waiting for Tennessee will be Giants quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan, who was the Titans' head coach before Robert Saleh was hired, and former Titans, now Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. Although there will be so much familiarity scheme-wise, the Titans believe the deciding factor will be the players' execution.

 "It really comes down to the Jimmys and Joes," Robinson told ESPN. "You don't really worry about the X's and the O's so much, it's more about the matchups and who you know you can go after, and I'm sure on their side, they're doing the same thing."

 Daboll said he's grateful for the Giants giving him his first opportunity to be a head coach in 2022. He spent just over three seasons there, leading the Giants to a 20-40-1 record, including a divisional playoff game appearance in his first season. The Giants fired Daboll in November 2025 after a 2-8 record. But Daboll said there are no hard feelings and he's treating this like any other game as he prepares to return to MetLife Stadium.

 "It's a one-week season every week, so you got to put everything you got into it," Daboll said Thursday. "That's what it is every week in the National Football League. I have a ton of respect for the people in that organization. From top down to the bottom, really good people in that building. I've been on a number of teams that played my former teams before. But it's about our players."

 Robinson signed a four-year, $70 million deal to follow Daboll to Tennessee. Robinson echoed Daboll's sentiments, saying there's no bad blood between him and the Giants. Similar to Daboll, Robinson is excited to face his former team but insists it's "just another game at the end of the day."

 

 The Titans' receivers should get opportunities to make plays against a Giants secondary decimated by injuries. Rookie cornerback Colton Hood was thrust into a starting role last week and allowed four completions on five targets for 42 yards and two touchdowns, primarily matching up with Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams , a future Hall of Famer. Under Wilson, New York has resorted to man defense an NFL-high 18.8% of its snaps this season. Regardless of who's in the secondary, Saleh, who's very familiar with Wilson's defenses, is expecting a battle.

 "He [Dennard Wilson] and I have had a lot of conversations," Saleh said. "I think he's a hell of a football coach. His defenses reflect his personality in that they play their tails off. The back end and the detail at which he coaches from a schematic standpoint is up there with anybody in football." 

 Giants safety Tyler Nubin said he has observed similarities in the Titans' offense under Daboll. 

 "You know what type of coach Dabs [Daboll] is," Nubin said. "He wants to be aggressive and likes to use tight ends." 

 Titans quarterback Cam Ward has attempted only one pass that traveled 20 yards or more. The tight ends have a total of seven targets in two games this season.

 One of the main players around whom Wilson's defense in Tennessee revolved was  Jeffery Simmons , who said he's more than willing to be a resource for the offense if the unit wants tips. After watching Wilson's defense on Monday night, Simmons believes the Giants' style of defense hasn't changed from what Wilson did in Tennessee. Daboll said he and some of the coaches joked about watching previous years of Titans film as well as the Giants this year to get tendencies from Wilson's defenses.

 Similar to the Giants, Tennessee's secondary is banged up. CB Flott missed last week's game because of a quad injury. Flott has been a limited participant in practice this week but said he's trending toward playing Sunday, just in time to face his former team. But Flott has no ill will toward the Giants, who he said allowed him to showcase his talent enough to earn a three-year, $45 million deal with the Titans. 

 While with the Giants, Flott got to line up against wide receiver Malik Nabers in practice. Getting to face Nabers in a game when it counts will be one of the highlights of the week for Flott.

 "It's going to be fun," Flott said. "I can't wait to see him talk s---, have fun and compete. That's just what me and Malik do."

 Of course, winning the game will be the biggest goal for everyone traveling to New York. But Schlottman, who spent two years with the Giants, is looking forward to something else.

 "I'm excited to get a bagel from up there," Schlottman said. "That's about the only thing I'm super excited about. This is another opportunity for us to go out there and execute and win. It's nothing more than that, nothing less than that. It's just that's what it is: the next game."

title: Giants' offense about to 'shift' with Jameis Winston
summary: The Giants' offense was starting to take shape with Dart as QB, but now Winston has to take over for the rest of the season.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- It was several weeks into training camp for the New York Giants when offensive coordinator Matt Nagy mentioned that only half the team's plays were installed. At the time it seemed disconcerting, but it makes sense considering the Giants eventually practiced and installed close to 300 plays, according to offensive lineman Jon Runyan .

 All that extensive work is poised to pay off. The offense greenlit by new coach John Harbaugh isn't only Jaxson Dart -specific. 

 "Probably the biggest thing is -- one of the things with this offense when we first got started is we wanted to be able to be prepared to have multiple styles of offense," Nagy said. "And so, if something like this does happen, it doesn't put you in a hole where it changes everything."

 The Giants' offense was starting to take shape with Dart as the quarterback before he suffered a knee injury in Week 2 and was placed on IR. His legs and ability to run were a big part of the run game. He had 54 yards in an impressive season-opening win over the Dallas Cowboys .

 Backup QB Jameis Winston had two rushes for one yard in a Week 2 loss to the Los Angeles Rams and that came trying to escape a sack.

 "All those plays are plays that we have, that we've been practicing and running, it's just kind of more like a shift maybe over a little bit as opposed to ... maybe a lane change as opposed to changing direction or anything like that," Harbaugh said. "More of a lane change."

 The most notable change with Winston at quarterback will be the lack of QB runs. Winston, 32, isn't anywhere near the same threat as a runner as Dart.

 

 The run-pass options are unlikely to be as big a piece of the Giants' offense.

 "We did have a lot more Jaxson-driven-type quarterback runs," Runyan said. "It wasn't necessarily something that we were going to major in like we kind of did last year most of the time. So, unfortunately, a lot of that is out. I mean, could be here and there.

 "Jameis is a gunslinger, obviously. So we're going to run our offense from a run point how I expect we have been through those two games. From a [quarterback] standpoint, I mean a little bit different. I don't think he's going to get the option to run a lot, but you never know."

 Harbaugh has insisted since he arrived that the Giants are going to be a big, physical team. That is what they want to be. They are expected to continue to establish the power run game, try to make it effective and then take shots downfield.

 This is where it could work with Winston.

 "Well, he can throw it," Harbaugh said. "I mean, he's a big, strong, passing quarterback. He can throw the ball. Everybody that follows football has certainly seen Jameis play, and his strengths are evident. So that's what you build around."

 It all bodes well for the Giants' running backs. They are now the focus of the Winston-led offense, beginning with starter Cam Skattebo . He has definitively become the team's No. 1 option while handling 67% of the running back carries the first two weeks.

 The running back pecking order also appears to have taken shape. It's Skattebo followed by Devin Singletary , then Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy Jr .

 Expect to see more Skattebo and fullback Patrick Ricard moving forward.

 "[Ricard] needs to play more. He's a great weapon for us," Nagy said. "Sometimes when you get into these games, whether it's a certain package that you have, none of it's intentional. Some of it just kind of happens.

 

 "It's the same thing, too, with [Skattebo] down inside in the red zone there with carrying the football and stuff."

 This works for Skattebo. He had 16 touches Monday night in the 28-6 loss to the Rams and felt good physically coming out of the game.

 He's open to a bigger workload and more responsibility on his shoulders.

 "I don't look at it as I need to do more," Skattebo said. "It's I get to do more."

 The tight end position could also get affected with Winston at quarterback. Isaiah Likely had quickly become Dart's go-to receiver and security blanket. He caught a team-high eight passes on eight targets in the opener, including a pair on third down on the game-ending drive. It looked to be continuing with a third-down catch on the opening drive against the Rams.

 Likely's targets seem destined to dip with Winston. Tight ends had a target rate of 24% with Dart as the quarterback since he entered the league last season. Winston has targeted the tight end on 19% of his passes over the course of his career.

 "My job remains the same," said Likely, who noted the routes he runs won't change. "Just make the quarterback's life as easy as possible is really my main focus."

 Likely will have to develop chemistry with Winston. He and star wide receiver Malik Nabers spent the entire summer working with Dart to get on the same page. They didn't work at all with Winston.

 It's no wonder that Winston was on the field after practice Thursday getting in extra work with many of his receivers. Among those out there -- Nabers.

 The Giants' No. 1 receiver should be a beneficiary of Winston's desire to push the ball downfield. Speedy wide receiver Darnell Mooney , too. Winston's 9.9 air yards per target is the most by any quarterback since he entered the league as the No. 1 pick of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2014.

 "I mean, he believes in his receivers to go make the plays for him. And we plan out to do that," Nabers said. "And when the opportunity comes, you've just got to go ahead and snatch the opportunity. The fact that he gives us opportunity, that means he believes in the good work that you put in in practice. He believes that you're going to make the play for him, and I trust that he trusts me. So we'll make the play."

title: Seahawks encouraged by Jadarian Price leading RB room
summary: Seattle's running back committee has no touchdowns through two weeks, but there's another opportunity this week at Commanders.
full_text:
RENTON, Wash. -- Three things were apparent with running back Jadarian Price while watching the  Seattle Seahawks ' first-round pick during training camp.

 One, he has plenty of speed, even if not the same fifth gear as the guy he's replacing ( Kenneth Walker III ). Two, he's better in the passing game than his limited college production as a pass catcher would suggest. And three, while he will be the Seahawks' RB1, he has plenty of company in their backfield -- especially once Zach Charbonnet returns.

 So, much of what we've learned about Price during Seattle's 2-0 start has merely been confirmation of what was already assumed.

 After not playing a down in the preseason, the Seahawks limited Price's workload to 24 snaps in Week 1 . He gained 58 yards on 12 touches against the New England Patriots . That included a 13-yard run on the first play of his NFL career. In a Week 2 win over the Arizona Cardinals , Price played 24 snaps and touched the ball 14 times for 60 yards. That included a 25-yard run that set up their second touchdown, as well as an 11-yard run when the Seahawks went right back to the rookie after he lost a fumble on the previous drive.

 "I've thought he's done well," offensive coordinator Brian Fleury said Thursday. "We gave him a little more last week and he showed up, had a couple explosive runs that he was able to break and run through contact. So I'm happy with the development we've seen, and I think it'll just continue to show itself."

 Price was sidelined against the Cardinals after hurting his chest/shoulder late in the third quarter. However, he took part in the first two practices of this week as a limited participant and appears to have a good chance of playing Sunday against the Washington Commanders (1 p.m. ET, Fox).

 

 Through two games, Price leads Seattle's backfield in snaps with 48 and in touches with 26. George Holani has looked like the clear RB2 since the start of the offseason program, and he has out-snapped Emanuel Wilson  41 to 32. But Wilson has 23 touches compared to Holani's 13.

 However, that trio is still looking for its first touchdown. Wilson couldn't find the end zone on three consecutive carries from inside the 5-yard line late in the second quarter against Arizona, leading to a turnover on downs. But he came through on the Seahawks' final possession to help close it out.

 With Price out and Holani briefly joining him on the sideline, Wilson carried the ball 10 times for 48 yards on a 16-play touchdown drive that took more than 10 minutes off the clock. He finished with 92 yards on 21 attempts after playing just three snaps in the opener.

 "It's the things that we saw him do throughout training camp before he had that minor setback," coach Mike Macdonald said of Wilson, who was sidelined for part of the summer with a hamstring injury after signing a one-year deal with Seattle in March. "Glad to see him do his thing. A decisive runner. He gets downhill, not just on the inside run game, it's on the perimeter game, as well. Had a great run on third down where he kept the drive going on the last drive, which is awesome. Lot of great stuff, so we're happy to have him."

 Seattle's backfield equation will change once Charbonnet -- a co-starter last season -- returns from last season's ACL tear in his left knee. He will miss at least two more games while on the physically unable to perform list. The Seahawks did not open his 21-day practice window this week, but Macdonald's comments suggested that should happen in the near future.

 

 As for Seattle's available tailbacks, their roles look defined when all are healthy. Price has started both games, and all of his work has come on first or second down. Holani, an excellent pass blocker, has played 18 of the team's 24 third-down snaps. Wilson, listed at 5-foot-10 and 226 pounds, is the power runner.

 While Holani is the best receiving threat of the three, Price continues to look plenty capable in that regard. After catching only 15 passes over three seasons at Notre Dame -- and backing up No. 4-overall pick  Jeremiyah Love  for much of that time -- Price has three receptions for 14 yards on four targets.

 His last touch against Arizona was a screen pass late in the third quarter that gained 8 yards. While Price was being tackled, his right shoulder hit the turf hard as former Seahawks defensive lineman L.J. Collier landed on him with all 300 pounds of his body weight. Macdonald said X-rays were negative.

 "It's something we'll monitor throughout the week," he said. "Shouldn't be a long-term thing."

 Through two games, Fleury's offense has the NFL's highest designed rush rate (52.2%), a metric in which they also led the league last season (47.6%) under Klint Kubiak. After totaling 162 yards on the ground against Arizona, the Seahawks rank ninth in rushing yards per game (129.5) and 14th in yards per carry (4.2).

 "I think as an offense, I think we have great opportunity for growth to really just get the one more block," Macdonald said. "We have the right mentality -- I'll tell you that -- on offense. I think the guys want that. It's just, when you watch the tape, there's a hunger there for more explosive runs, which is really cool. We've got a great opportunity in front of us."

title: What's next for Jayden Daniels, Commanders after elbow injury?
summary: Experts weigh in on Daniels' latest injury and what it means for him, the Commanders and their collective futures.
full_text:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- For nearly an entire half on Sunday, Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels resembled the player from 2024, the one who was named NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year and mentioned as a future league MVP.

 On the final drive of the first half at the  Dallas Cowboys , Daniels provided reminders of that season: He ran for 24 yards and threw for another 27, including a strike on third-and-6 to Stefon Diggs for 10 yards.

 

 Then, on the final play of the half, the 2025 version of Daniels showed up, the one who missed 10 games with three different injuries. He suffered a dislocated left elbow, leaving the Commanders with plenty of questions about the future -- from his durability to whether they had built a good enough roster to withstand his absence for even a short period.

 After visiting specialists Tuesday through Thursday, Washington general manager Adam Peters told 106.7 The Fan radio that Daniels would not need surgery nor would he be placed on injured reserve.

 Still, his latest injury has left Washington in a familiar spot: wondering what this means for Daniels' future and trying to piece together wins. Last season, the Commanders struggled to do the latter and finished 5-12. Washington is 0-2 now and will face the defending Super Bowl champion  Seattle Seahawks  in its home opener Sunday.

 "0-2 is not where we wanted to be, that's for sure," Quinn said. "But we also are resolute that that's not where we're going to be staying."

 Commanders reporter John Keim, ESPN draft expert Jordan Reid and senior fantasy writer Eric Karabell weigh in on Daniels' latest injury and what it means for him, the Commanders and their collective futures.

 

 

 Is the season lost? 
 It's only two games. But after last season, when injuries -- notably the one to Daniels -- derailed the Commanders, it would require a leap of faith to think otherwise at this point, particularly in the NFC East. Even if Daniels had remained healthy, Washington is now 0-2 in the division. So, the road would have been tough regardless. Also, the Commanders will next face Seattle in their home opener and in the coming six weeks will play the Giants twice, the 49ers, the Rams and the Eagles. However, the Giants' game looks different with quarterback Jaxson Dart out for the season. The Colts in Week 4 in London also is winnable. A bleak picture could change in a hurry.

 But if Daniels is out multiple weeks, that's a steep task - especially because the defense continues to struggle in coverage. But there is still a chance he only misses one week. As one teammate said, the shame of the injury is that he looked terrific in the first half vs. Dallas - and that meant good things for the future. His return and subsequent performance changes everything about their future.

 It's also a big year for Quinn; while ownership values him this is a results-based industry and another bad season wouldn't help him. But any decision for when Daniels' returns will be led by medical personnel.

 

 And this isn't about backup quarterback Marcus Mariota , who will start Sunday, as much as it is about what the Commanders haven't shown in other areas.

 Against Dallas, Daniels was sharp and showed the dynamic ability that made him the No. 2 pick in the 2024 draft, and a player multiple high-profile coaches liked best in that class.

 "I loved everything about the first half, how he was playing," Quinn said of Sunday's performance, as Daniels rushed for 69 yards and threw for 96 yards and a touchdown before the injury.

 But Daniels also covers up a lot of flaws. Those flaws will now be magnified during his absence, and that's the concerning part. Washington's defense has allowed seven touchdowns in two games. A new system always brings growing pains, but the Commanders are faster and more talented in the front seven as compared with 2025's unit, and new coordinator Daronte Jones has a strong reputation. Defensive backs say his scheme requires a lot of preparation and knowledge; that also could lead to early issues in coverage until they have more games in the system.

 On multiple plays Sunday, a cornerback could be seen communicating with a safety right before the ball was snapped. In one case, there appeared to be confusion; and in another, the corner was looking at the safety when the ball was snapped. At other times, it appeared players went to the same coverage area.

 Quinn said they know what it looks like when they do it right, so after two games, "It's not good enough."

 But can that overcome all the issues? The Commanders' defense struggles unless it applies pressure. They don't create turnovers. That's a bad combination. Last season, the Bears' defense ranked 24th in scoring and 29th in yards but led the NFL with 33 takeaways (23 more than Washington).

 Washington has forced only 27 turnovers since the start of the 2024 campaign and hasn't taken the ball away in two games this season.

 If the Commanders had a proven defense and a strong, consistent run game, then they could survive for a few weeks. But their offensive line, already down left tackle Laremy Tunsil , now has right guard Sam Cosmi -- their top remaining lineman -- in concussion protocol. Tunsil and Daniels are Washington's best offensive players. It's tough to survive those absences.

 Could they develop those other aspects? Sure. But when? And will it happen quickly enough for Washington to withstand Daniels' absence? The Commanders have lost 12 of their past 14 games dating to last season, but they changed coordinators and spent heavily on defense in the offseason. If not a new team, it should be a different one. After two games, Washington ranks 27th in yards and 25th in points. The Commanders are 28th in yards per pass attempt.

 After Sunday's game, one player, without prompting, expressed confidence in what the offense and the team could still do. He was encouraged by a lot of what he had seen by the offense, despite the loss. And he remained convinced it could get the season pointed in a better direction. Others share his belief. If that belief doesn't turn into a win real soon, then hope will once more lead to despair for Washington fans. -- Keim 

 

 Should the Commanders have serious concerns about Daniels' viability as their QB of the present and future? 

 If he missed another long stretch, it would be hard not to have those concerns. But even with a short absence there's risk involved that impacts his future.

 What they'll never have to worry about is his approach. Few work harder or study more; he continues to arrive at work by 5:30 a.m. every week. He organized film sessions with the receivers. He picks the brains of athletes in other sports -- Steph Curry, Draymond Green and LeBron James -- and has talked to Lakers general manager Rob Pelinka about Kobe Bryant's mindset.

 Daniels has been focused on improving and winning; he has said he doesn't care about fame and celebrity status.

 However, he has now dislocated his left elbow twice in his past four games and reinjured it in another. He has finished only four games since the start of last season and left four others early. He suffered a knee injury in one game that cost him two weeks and a hamstring in another that sidelined him for one.

 The question is: Can anything be done to prevent another dislocation? One source close to the situation said surgery was never recommended last year and multiple medical experts said surgery is almost never performed after a first one because the risk for recurrence is around 2 percent.

 Indeed, Quinn said surgery was not discussed and after consulting with multiple outside specialists it wasn't recommended this time either. According to Dr. Marc Kowalsky, an orthopedic surgeon with ONS in Connecticut, and an expert on elbow and shoulder injuries the likelihood of another dislocation increases - even if Daniels plays with a brace.
